title: After arriving in David Montgomery trade, Juice Scruggs is Lions' starting center
summary: When the Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Texans in March, Juice Scruggs was viewed as mostly a throw-in along with the fourth-round pick and seventh-round pick Houston had sent to Detroit.
full_text: ''' When the Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Texans in March, Juice Scruggs was viewed as mostly a throw-in along with the fourth-round pick and seventh-round pick Houston had sent to Detroit. Scruggs was a disappointment as a 2023 second-round pick of the Texans, and he was expected to have to compete just to make the Lions' roster. Instead, Scruggs will be the Lions' starting center on Sunday against the Saints. Scruggs was working more at guard than center for most of the offseason, but Cade Mays, who was expected to start at center, injured his wrist a month ago. Mays is now on injured reserve, and Scruggs said he's getting used to his role as the No. 1 center even if it wasn't a role he was expected to play. "A lot more comfortable, for sure. Things have slowed down. When I got thrown in at center at first it was like, kind of overwhelming, but I'm definitely feeling more comfortable and ready to play for sure," Scruggs said. "You've just got to be ready. You never know when your number is going to get called, so you prepare like a starter, always." Although Scruggs played mostly guard for the Texans, he did start eight games at center, so he's not new to his position. Even if he's new in Detroit, and playing a part few saw him playing when he arrived in the Montgomery trade.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ben Johnson sees Bears practicing at a championship level, unlike last year
summary: A year ago, Johnson said his team's practice habits were not yet championship-caliber. He no longer thinks that.
full_text: A year ago, Bears coach Ben Johnson didn't think his team was practicing like a team that wants to win the Super Bowl. He no longer thinks that. Johnson said on Friday that one of his reasons for optimism heading into the season is that he sees better practice habits from his players than he was seeing heading into the 2025 season. "Here's what I'm excited about: How hard they're working on a regular basis right now," Johnson said. "I think I made a comment last year about how we're not practicing at a championship level yet. I'm not saying that this year. These guys, the work they're putting in throughout the week, it doesn't guarantee you a win on Sunday, but it gives you a darn chance. So I'm happy about what I'm seeing from all of those guys, and as a result from that they all get better." Johnson's comments about last year's team came after an 0-2 start, when he said, “ Our practice habits are yet to reflect a championship-caliber team ." After that, the Bears won nine of their next 10 games and ended the season with an 11-6 record and an NFC North title. This year, Johnson's goals for his team are even higher than just winning the division. He thinks his team is practicing like a team that can go all the way.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Caleb Williams is one game from tying the franchise record for multiple TD passes
summary: The Bears have still never had a quarterback with 4,000 passing yards in a single season.
full_text: The Bears have still never had a quarterback with 4,000 passing yards in a single season. They also have had only one quarterback with multiple passing touchdowns in eight straight games. By Sunday evening, they could have two. Via NBC Sports research, Caleb Williams is one game from tying Sid Luckman for the franchise record with eight straight games with two or more touchdown passes. Williams has accomplished that feat in seven straight games, including the 2025 postseason. It's another example of the team's traditionally anemic offense giving way to an era of significant production on that side of the ball, particularly in the passing game. Last year, Williams finished the season with 3,942 passing yards. It was enough to break Erik Kramer's 30-year-old record. It seems inevitable that Williams will get to 4,000 yards — possibly as soon as this year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles send OC to booth, for first time under Nick Sirianni
summary: In five years as the Eagles' head coach, Nick Sirianni has had his offensive coordinator on the field with him during the games.
full_text: In five years as the Eagles' head coach, Nick Sirianni has had his offensive coordinator on the field with him during the games. For the first time in Sirianni's tenure, the man calling the plays on offense will be upstairs. "We want to think through every situation to make sure that we're giving ourselves the best opportunity for us to win the game and be at our best," Sirianni told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to have Sean Mannion be in the booth. "Also understanding that there is no right way to do it or wrong way to do it. There's many different ways to do it. I think we can get caught up so much, it's like, 'This is the only way to do it.' You have conviction in what you believe, but there's many different things that can work and have worked. It's just about making the best decision, what's best for your football team and for you to do your job the best. That's how we went about it." Sirianni was then asked how it will affect him to not have the offensive coordinator by his side during games. "I don't think at all," Sirianni said. "I mean, obviously, there's communication still, right? We're talking on the headset and everything like that. I would say it's the amount of conversations that happen that have to be face-to-face, I think, are very minimal. I don't think that's -- you're being able to communicate and that's something that we stress on our players of how important communication is. We have to lead that as coaches as well. I don't think that affects us at all." The balance continues to be seeing the full field for every play and having the ability to talk directly to the players without using a phone. And there is no magic to it. Nevertheless, it will be a different game-day experience for Sirianni, and for players like quarterback Jalen Hurts. The first test of the new approach comes on Sunday, when the Eagles host the Commanders.
author: Mike Florio

title: Baker Mayfield hopes to extend starting record against Joe Burrow to 4-0
summary: Sunday's game between the Buccaneers and Bengals has an intriguing subplot.
full_text: Sunday's game between the Buccaneers and Bengals has an intriguing subplot. Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield has never lost to Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow. Mayfield is 3-0 against Burrow as a starter. All three matchups happened in 2020 and 2021, when Mayfield played for the Browns. And, yes, Mayfield faced Burrow in 2022, when Mayfield played for the Panthers. In that game, however, P.J. Walker got the start; Mayfield entered the game after halftime, with the Panthers trailing 35-0. The Mayfield-Burrow matchup is also one of two Week 1 games featuring a pair of Heisman Trophy winners. The other one happens in Charlotte, between Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and Panthers quarterback Bryce Young. The Bucs-Bengals game carries greater weight than Mayfield's 3-0 record as a starter against Burrow. Both teams need to get off to a good start if they hope to get back to the playoffs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings convert CB Isaiah Rodgers's playing-time incentives into a signing bonus
summary: Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers had a solid 2025 season for the Vikings.
full_text: Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers had a solid 2025 season for the Vikings. The team has acknowledged it with a tweak to his contract. Via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Vikings have converted $1.5 million in playing-time incentives for 2026 into a signing bonus. To earn that payment, he would have been required to participate in at least 85 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026. Rodgers signed a two-year, $11.045 million deal last year. He's now due to make $5.94 million in 2026. He can make another $250,000 if he qualifies for the Pro Bowl or $350,000 if he's a second-team All-Pro or, if Rodgers becomes a first-team All-Pro, $500,000. A sixth-round pick of the Colts in 2020, Rodgers has 77 regular-season appearances with 28 starts. Last year in Minnesota, he appeared in 17 games with 15 starts. His best game came in Week 3 against the Bengals, when he returned an interception 87 yards for a touchdown and a fumble 66 yards for another touchdown.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills' initial grass field had "major deformations"
summary: In six days, the Bills will host the first regular-season game at their new stadium.
full_text: In six days, the Bills will host the first regular-season game at their new stadium. On the second new field there. The team decided to replace the grass after only two preseason games. Via Tim Graham of The Athletic , NFL field expert Nick Pappas explained what went wrong with the first field installed there. "The aspect of the field that appeared to be an issue was that there were major deformations happening, large divoting outside of what we typically see at many of our NFL grass fields — although not something we haven’t seen before," Pappas told Graham. "That lent itself to say there was an opportunity to improve that surface, and that’s what the Bills have stepped up to do and made that decision to replace it." Pappas explained that, whenever a new stadium is built, "There’s a period before it gets turned over to Bills staff. So, you’re now reliant on the general contractor or the installation company for maintenance over a certain period of time." He attributed the situation to a "combination of the sod quality from the start, the challenges, and maybe the management up until the Bills’ grounds crew were able to take over, and then you couple it with a very new growing environment that needs to be worked through." Pappas said the new sod "will come in thicker" than the prior version. The next challenge becomes preparing the field for three home games in three weeks: Week 2, Week 3, and Week 4. Pappas thinks another replacement will likely happen during the season. "Recovery needs to outpace usage," he said. "But if the weather is great and all goes well over that three-game stand, maybe they’re looking at Week 8 to replace it, or they can look at the weather and say, 'Hey, based on where we are today, we have three weeks to recover. We can bring the grow lights out. We can provide our agronomic program with fertility and grow it back.'" Given the weather challenges in Buffalo, Pappas said he wouldn't be surprised if the Bills need three or four fields per year. That's one of the reasons why some teams prefer artificial turf. It's cheaper. It doesn't require constant evaluation. But if teams and owners care about giving their players the surface they prefer, it's worth the money and the effort. Despite the challenges the Bills are facing, they deserve credit for trying to give the players the best possible surface.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans claim G Atonio Mafi off of waivers
summary: The Titans tweaked their offensive line ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
full_text: The Titans tweaked their offensive line ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets. The NFL's daily transaction report for Friday shows that they have claimed guard Atonio Mafi off of waivers. The Raiders dropped Mafi when they claimed guard Bryce Cabeldue on Thursday. The Titans waived guard Garrett Dellinger to open a roster spot. Mafi was a Patriots fifth-rounder in 2023 and he played for the Colts in 2024 before landing with the Raiders last season. He started five games as a rookie, but has only played in a reserve role over the last two seasons. The Titans plan to start Peter Skoronski at left guard and fifth-round pick Fernando Carmona at right guard this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Free agent LB Xavier Thomas suspended three games
summary: The NFL has suspended free agent linebacker Xavier Thomas for the first three weeks of the season, according to the league's personnel notice.
full_text: The NFL has suspended free agent linebacker Xavier Thomas for the first three weeks of the season, according to the league's personnel notice. It is unclear why the NFL suspended Thomas. Thomas, 26, was waived from injured reserve by the 49ers on Aug. 26. He spent time in the offseason with the Texans before reaching an injury settlement with the team May 20. He signed with the 49ers on Aug. 12. The Cardinals picked Thomas in the fifth round in 2024, and he played 14 games as a rookie and four last season. He has totaled 10 tackles, 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a pass defensed, all in his rookie season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ashton Jeanty off injury report, set to play Week 1 vs. Dolphins
summary: Ashton Jeanty is officially "on the mend" no more.
full_text: Ashton Jeanty is officially "on the mend" no more. Jeanty has no game status and is set to play in Las Vegas' season opener against Miami on Sunday. Jeanty suffered an ankle injury late last month. While the injury initially seemed serious, Jeanty recovered quickly enough to be listed as a full participant for all three practice days this week. The No. 6 overall pick of last year’s draft, Jeanty rushed for 975 yards with five touchdowns and caught 55 passes for 346 yards with five TDs as a rookie. He is expected to be a significant part of Las Vegas’ offense in 2026 under new head coach Klint Kubiak. The only other player on Las Vegas’ injury report this week was tight end Brock Bowers, who is out after undergoing a meniscus trim earlier this week . He reportedly will be sidelined for just 1-2 weeks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Josh Allen hopes to improve 1-4 career record vs. Texans
summary: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a 96-46 record as a starter in regular-season and postseason games.
full_text: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a 96-46 record as a starter in regular-season and postseason games. That's a 67.6-percent success rate. Against Sunday's opponent, he's right on the Mendoza line. Allen holds a sluggish 1-4 career record against the Texans, and 0-4 in Houston. The Week 1 game happens in Houston. Most recently, Allen was sacked a career-high eight times in a 23-19 Thursday night loss in Houston. He had two interceptions and no touchdown passes in the game. Countering his one career win against the Texans are eight playoff victories. Per NBC Sports research, that's the most for any quarterback who did not play in a Super Bowl. As he starts the ninth year of his career, the clock is ticking. The pressure is increasing. While the postseason narrative can't change until January, Allen has a chance to alter his history in Houston by finally getting a win there, in his fifth try.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys RB Malik Davis will miss time with a "pretty serious" hip injury
summary: The Cowboys have ruled out running back Malik Davis for Sunday's season opener, and they are bracing for him to miss significant time.
full_text: The Cowboys have ruled out running back Malik Davis for Sunday's season opener, and they are bracing for him to miss significant time. Executive vice president Stephen Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that Davis was carted off from practice Friday with a "pretty serious" hip injury. "Unfortunately, I think he's looking at a pretty serious injury that could take him out for some period of time," Jones said, via Nick Eatman of the team website. "We don't have the final details, we'll know more, but certainly so disappointed for Malik. Obviously, tough for our team, but like anything, it's next man up." Davis won the backup job to Javonte Williams and was expected to play a significant role in the offense. The Cowboys' initial 53-player roster included only those two running backs before they claimed veteran Emari Demercado off waivers as the third back. Dallas has Israel Abanikanda on the practice squad, and he will likely get a call-up for Sunday's game. The Cowboys, though, could be in the market for another veteran running back. Every other player on the roster had full participation Friday, and no one other than Davis has an injury designation.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chiefs list Chris Jones as limited with a calf injury
summary: Defensive lineman Chris Jones was added to the Chiefs' injury report on Friday.
full_text: Defensive lineman Chris Jones was added to the Chiefs' injury report on Friday. Jones was a limited participant in practice and he is listed with a calf injury. The team will issue their final injury report for Monday night's game against the Broncos on Saturday and that will provide a better idea of Jones's outlook for the opener. The outlook for left tackle Josh Simmons remains dim. He missed practice again with a back injury. Defensive back Chamarri Conner (knee) also remained out of practice. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee), linebacker Jack Cochrane (knee), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (foot), wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee), guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee), defensive end R Mason Thomas (hamstring), and wide receiver Xavier Worthy (shoulder) all remained full participants in practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions release DL Levi Onwuzurike
summary: The Lions dropped a player from their active roster on Friday.
full_text: The Lions dropped a player from their active roster on Friday. They announced that they have released defensive lineman Levi Onwuzurike. Onwuzurike would have been guaranteed his entire salary for the season if he was on the roster for Week 1, so a return after the Lions face the Saints could be in the cards. Onwuzurike was a second-round pick for Detroit in 2021, but he's missed two of the last five seasons with injuries. A back injury kept him out in 2022 and he missed all of last season with a torn ACL. When healthy, Onwuzurike has 68 tackles, 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble in 42 regular season appearances. He also has five tackles in four playoff games. The Lions also announced that they have signed defensive lineman Tyre West to their practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens rule out LB Teddye Buchanan
summary: The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts.
full_text: The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts. Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan will not play. Both are coming off season-ending injuries from 2025. Madubuike's delayed return was previously reported when coach Jesse Minter gave the team's injury update during his news conference. Buchanan was limited in practice all week. He tore the ACL and the meniscus in his right knee on Dec. 14 and sprained his LCL in the same knee. He only returned to the practice field Aug. 17. Trenton Simpson, listed as a co-starter on the depth chart, will start for Buchanan. The Ravens, though, have only three healthy linebackers on their 53-player roster, so they are likely to elevate Carl Jones Jr. from the practice squad. Wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) is questionable after limited practices this week. Wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to full participation on Thursday and has no injury designation. The team added defensive lineman Calais Campbell to the injury report as he took a rest day Friday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants list Malik Nabers as questionable to play Sunday night
summary: Wide receiver Malik Nabers was a full participant in practice again on Friday, but the team isn't ready to say anything definitive about his status for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.
full_text: '' Wide receiver Malik Nabers was a full participant in practice again on Friday, but the team isn't ready to say anything definitive about his status for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys. Nabers has been listed as questionable to play in the team's first game of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh called Nabers " ready to go " on Wednesday, but Nabers said on Thursday that missing the game is a possibility and that the team is " leaving the decision up" to him. Nabers tore his ACL late last September and said earlier in the offseason that he doesn't want to return until he feels able to play an entire game without any limitations due to his knee. The signs from Giants practices of late have been that Nabers is ready for that kind of involvement, but official word isn't going to come until closer to kickoff.
author: Josh Alper

title: Klint Kubiak: I was optimistic Brock Bowers would be able to go, but he's not
summary: On Wednesday, a curious situation came up with the Raiders, head coach Klint Kubiak, tight end Brock Bowers, and the media.
full_text: On Wednesday, a curious situation came up with the Raiders, head coach Klint Kubiak, tight end Brock Bowers, and the media. During his press conference, Kubiak was asked directly if Bowers and edge rusher Maxx Crosby would be available to play the Dolphins to open the season. In response, Kubiak said, "We're expecting to have all of our guys ready for Sunday." But later that day, multiple reporters noted that Bowers will miss 1-2 games after undergoing a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday. Bowers suffered the injury during training camp, and the surgery to address it was scheduled last week. “I was optimistic earlier that Brock would be able to go — he’s not ,” Kubiak said as part of his opening statement in his Friday press conference. “We’ll get him back soon.” Given the discrepancy, that did not cut off Kubiak’s questions about Bowers. “It all happened pretty quick, I don’t remember exactly what day,” Kubiak said on the timeline from finding out about Bowers’ injury to his procedure. “But he got it cleaned up and we’ll get him back soon.” Kubiak added that he’s not going to talk about a timeline, when asked about the report that Bowers will be out for 1-2 weeks. “We’ll hope to get him back as soon as possible,” Kubiak said, adding that he was optimistic the tight end would be back this week even after the procedure. Bowers, the No. 13 overall pick of the 2024 draft, figures to be a significant part of Las Vegas’ offense when he returns. Limited to 12 games due to injury last season, Bowers caught 64 passes for 680 yards with seven touchdowns. As a rookie, he caught 112 passes for 1,194 yards with five TDs.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Klint Kubiak confirms Fernando Mendoza is the No. 2 QB
summary: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed rookie Fernando Mendoza will serve as the backup to Kirk Cousins.
full_text: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed rookie Fernando Mendoza will serve as the backup to Kirk Cousins. Kubiak would not previously say whether it would be Mendoza or Aidan O'Connell, but the team's depth chart released earlier this week showed the No. 1 overall pick as the No. 2. Mendoza is the first quarterback since Baker Mayfield in 2018 not to start Week 1 after being the top overall pick. "I am encouraging him to know his reads and progressions, to know the game plan," Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. "What the guys take off of each other comes through osmosis. So he's just gotta get his butt ready to roll. The people in front of them are there to produce as well. And if he learned something from their preparation, I think that's a good thing. That's why we have [Cousins] there. But most importantly, we have [Cousins] there to go play and go win the game." Mendoza won't get many practice reps, but he has to be ready to play as he is one play away. "That's the life of an NFL backup," Kubiak said. "That's why he's got to be the most mature guy in the room. A guy that can prepare on his own, in the darkness, in the shadows. And then when called upon, go win the game." Kubiak said Jackson Powers-Johnson will start at right guard ahead of Caleb Rogers, but he considers both players to be starters.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chris Johnson unable to travel to Nashville, Titans postpone Ring of Honor ceremony
summary: The Titans' plans to induct Chris Johnson into the Ring of Honor this weekend have been put on hold.
full_text: The Titans' plans to induct Chris Johnson into the Ring of Honor this weekend have been put on hold. The team released a statement on Friday afternoon announcing that they will still celebrate Johnson's career at halftime of the game, but that the official induction ceremony will take place at a later date. "Due to unforeseen circumstances, Chris Johnson and his family are no longer able to travel to Nashville for this Sunday’s game," the statement said. "Knowing how much he and his family desire to be in person at Nissan Stadium for his induction into the Titans Ring of Honor, we will postpone the official induction ceremony and look forward to celebrating the moment with them at a future date." Johnson revealed that he has ALS earlier this year. The 2008 first-round pick spent six seasons with the Titans and also played one season for the Jets, who will be the visiting team in Tennessee this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rome Odunze: I feel ready to go; I plan on playing
summary: Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is listed as questionable to play in the season opener because of a calf injury.
full_text: Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is listed as questionable to play in the season opener because of a calf injury. Odunze questions that. " I feel ready to go ," Odunze said, via video from Jason Liser of the Chicago Sun-Times . "I doubt I'm questionable. I know there's a way everybody goes about things, but I feel pretty good. I was out there today. I plan on playing." Odunze said he strained his right calf, calling it "just a little muscle fatigue" during training camp. "But, yeah, feel great and ready to go," Odunze said. He missed five games last season due to a stress fracture in his foot and finished the season with 44 catches for 661 yards and six touchdowns. "Coming off last year, you hate to have injuries," Odunze said. "Through the offseason, through this training camp, to have been healthy, you can't take those things for granted." Odunze sounds ready for 2026. "I can play football, man," he said. "I've been dreaming of doing this since I was 6. Guaranteed opportunity, and I'm trying to make the most of it every single time I step out there. Be excited to go and start a game away."
author: Charean Williams

title: Eagles rule Jonathan Greenard out for Week 1
summary: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard said on Thursday that he feels "close" to being ready to play after missing all of training camp and the preseason with a pectoral injury, but he's not close enough to be in the lineup this weekend.
full_text: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard said on Thursday that he feels "close" to being ready to play after missing all of training camp and the preseason with a pectoral injury, but he's not close enough to be in the lineup this weekend. Greenard returned to practice this week as a limited participant and the Eagles announced on Friday afternoon that he has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders. If all goes well, Greenard could make his debut for the team against the Titans in Week 2. Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa will be the available outside linebackers for the Eagles. Second-round pick Eli Stowers is the only other Eagle with an injury designation. The tight end is questionable to play due to a hamstring injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Monken on Deshaun Watson: "I really like where he's at"
summary: On Sunday, Deshaun Watson will make his first start in almost two years when the Browns take on the Jaguars.
full_text: ' On Sunday, Deshaun Watson will make his first start in almost two years when the Browns take on the Jaguars. While Cleveland fans have been clear about their displeasure over Watson still being QB1 in 2026, he will have a chance to perhaps change some minds with his play in Week 1. After Watson won the QB competition over Shedeur Sanders, he's been taking all of the first-team snaps. That's made a difference in the preparation, according to head coach Todd Monken. "Watching him get all the reps the last couple of weeks and getting more and more comfortable, how it helped Shedeur in terms of his development by splitting the reps and having a competition, you can see the opposite of that," Monken said in his Friday press conference, via transcript from the team. "He got a lot more of the reps, and you could see him getting more and more comfortable with the concepts, obviously putting the game plan in early and getting him comfortable. "But I really like where he’s at.” Watson's task may become a bit more difficult with an offensive line that features rookies at left tackle and right guard. The Jaguars finished No. 8 in points allowed and No. 11 in yards allowed last season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bears, D'Andre Swift agree to three-year contract extension
summary: Bears running back D'Andre Swift will kick off the new season with a new contract.
full_text: Bears running back D'Andre Swift will kick off the new season with a new contract. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Swift has agreed to a three-year contract extension in Chicago. The deal is worth $33.75 million and includes $27.5 million in guaranteed money. Swift's new deal comes after Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson, and Jonathan Taylor agreed to new deals over the summer. Swift joined the Bears in 2024 and has started 33 regular season games since coming to Chicago. He had 476 carries for 2,046 yards and 15 touchdowns while also catching 76 passes in those appearances. He added 32 carries for 130 yards and a touchdown in the postseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans place second-round pick Kayden McDonald on IR
summary: Texans second-round pick Kayden McDonald won't be making his NFL debut in September.
full_text: Texans second-round pick Kayden McDonald won't be making his NFL debut in September. The team announced that McDonald has been placed on injured reserve on Friday. McDonald missed the last two days of practice with an ankle injury. With McDonald out of commission for four games, the Texans moved to bolster their defensive line options. They announced that they have signed Jaden Crumedy to the 53-man roster. Crumedy was in training camp with the Packers, but did not make it through their final cuts. He had 15 tackles and a half-sack in eight games for the Panthers over the last two seasons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Shemar Stewart doubtful, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins set to play Week 1
summary: The Bengals are unlikely to have defensive end Shemar Stewart for Sunday's season opener against the Buccaneers, but the rest of their 53-man roster is healthy to play — including receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
full_text: The Bengals are unlikely to have defensive end Shemar Stewart for Sunday's season opener against the Buccaneers, but the rest of their 53-man roster is healthy to play — including receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Cincinnati has listed Stewart (knee) as doubtful for the contest. Stewart was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, but was downgraded to limited on Thursday. He was downgraded once again on Friday as he did not participate in the day's session. In eight games as a rookie last season, Stewart recorded 11 total tackles with one sack, two tackles for loss, and four quarterback hits. As has been the expectation all week, Chase (knee) and Higgins (foot) are set to play. Chase did not practice Friday, but it was considered a rest day. Cornerback DJ Turner (hamstring) is also set to play despite being limited in practice over the last two days. Kickoff for Sunday’s matchup between the Bengals and Bucs is set for 1 p.m. ET.
author: Myles Simmons

title: RB Malik Davis carted off at Cowboys practice
summary: The Cowboys may need to pivot to a new plan for their offensive backfield ahead of Sunday night's game against the Giants.
full_text: The Cowboys may need to pivot to a new plan for their offensive backfield ahead of Sunday night's game against the Giants. According to multiple reports, running back Malik Davis had to be carted off the field at Friday's practice after suffering an injury. There's been no word from the team about Davis's condition yet, but the team will issue their final injury report of the week later in the day. Davis is listed as the No. 2 running back behind Javonte Williams. Emari Demercado, who was claimed off of waivers on August 31, is the other back on the 53-man roster. The Cowboys also have Israel Abanikanda on the practice squad and an evaluation of Davis's condition will likely determine if he'll be called up for the opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rome Odunze, Xavier Woods questionable for Bears vs. Panthers
summary: Two Bears starters are questionable for Sunday's opener against the Panthers.
full_text: ''' Two Bears starters are questionable for Sunday's opener against the Panthers. Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is listed as questionable with a calf injury, while free safety Xavier Woods is questionable with a groin injury. Two Bears backups are also injured: No. 2 quarterback Tyson Bagent is questionable with a back injury, and second-string left tackle Ozzy Trapilo is questionable with a knee injury. Bagent's injury could mean Case Keenum will be the No. 2 quarterback behind Caleb Williams. All other Bears practiced fully today and are good to go on Sunday against the Panthers. The Bears are three-point road favorites for the 1 p.m. ET kickoff in Carolina.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Packers release Bo Melton, but will bring him back on practice squad
summary: The Packers have made a surprising roster move on Friday, but there’s more to it than it initially appears.
full_text: The Packers have made a surprising roster move on Friday, but there’s more to it than it initially appears. Green Bay has released receiver Bo Melton, but there’s more to it than it appears. According to multiple reporters on the Packers beat, this is a roster management move, as Melton is expected to re-sign with the club’s practice squad and get elevated to the gameday roster for the Week 1 matchup against the Vikings. Melton, a seventh-round pick in 2022, is now a vested veteran, which means he does not need to clear waivers to go to the practice squad. In 16 games last season, Melton caught four passes for 107 yards with a touchdown. He also took five carries for 35 yards. He was on the field for 47 percent of special teams snaps and 10 percent of offensive snaps in games played.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Nnamdi Madubuike will not play this week
summary: Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike's return to game action will have to wait a little bit longer.
full_text: Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike's return to game action will have to wait a little bit longer. Madubuike has been out since Week 2 of last season because of a neck injury that required surgery and head coach Jesse Minter said on Friday that he will not be playing against the Colts in the season opener. Madubuike had been doing team drills for the last couple of weeks, but Minter said he's not all the way back to where he needs to be. "He is really, really close ," Minter said, via the team's website. "It's been a great process for him to return from the injury that he had. We feel great about where he's at, but we're not going to play him this week." Travis Jones, Calais Campbell, Broderick Washington, John Jenkins, and Aeneas Peebles are the other defensive linemen on the roster in Baltimore heading into Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalen McMillan doubtful for Bucs, but Emeka Egbuka is set to play
summary: The Buccaneers will likely be down one wide receiver when they open the regular season against the Bengals on Sunday.
full_text: The Buccaneers will likely be down one wide receiver when they open the regular season against the Bengals on Sunday. Jalen McMillan is listed as doubtful to play in Cincinnati this weekend. McMillan is dealing with a knee injury and was limited in practice all this week. Emeka Egbuka also missed time during the preseason, but his toe injury was well enough for him to fully participate in practice the last three days. He has no injury designation for Sunday. Running back Sean Tucker (hamstring) returned to practice after sitting out on Wednesday, but is likely to miss the game after being listed as doubtful along with McMillan and offensive tackle Justin Skule (oblique).
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL Week 1 injuries: Giants' Malik Nabers, Bears' Rome Odunze listed as questionable
summary: Malik Nabers and Rome Odunze are questionable for the season opener, while Cameron Jordan is ruled out and Jonathon Brooks is cleared to return for the Panthers
full_text:
Week 1 of the NFL is here, and while that is exciting, several teams are dealing with notable injuries as they enter their first games of the season. The Atlanta Falcons won't have their top two quarterbacks, the Las Vegas Raiders will be without their top weapon, Brock Bowers , and the New York Giants could be without their top wideout, Malik Nabers , for their primetime conference clash with the Dallas Cowboys .
While almost every NFL team will have a player or two listed on their final injury reports, these will likely be the cleanest injury reports all year! Below, we will break down the official injury reports for Week 1 in the NFL.
The Saints won't have veteran defensive end Cameron Jordan for Week 1, as he sat out practice on Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury. Running back Alvin Kamara is officially listed as questionable to play with his MCL sprain, but practiced Friday as a full participant.
The Lions enter Week 1 relatively healthy with only one player with a game status: nickel corner Christian Izien (groin). Izien was a limited practice participant all week.
Baker Mayfield could be without one of his wide receivers, Jalen McMillan, who was limited all week in practice with a knee injury. He's doubtful to suit up. The same is true for backup running back Sean Tucker, who missed practice on Wednesday with a hamstring injury.
For the Bengals, Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and DJ Turner II were all listed on the injury report, but carry no game designations into Week 1 -- which is good. Shemar Stewart, on the other hand, missed practice Friday with a knee injury and is considered doubtful.
Baltimore Ravens two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) only played two games last season before going down with a season-ending neck injury. He practiced as a limited participant all week, but Baltimore isn't rushing him back to action in Week 1. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee) is also out after practicing in a limited fashion all week.
The Indianapolis Colts only have one player with a game status: linebacker Austin Ajiake (hamstring). The injury popped up on Friday, even though he had fully practiced on both Wednesday and Thursday. Wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) doesn't have a game status after being limited all week, so he'll be good to go for Week 1.
Browns starting right guard Teven Jenkins will miss the season opener with a back injury. Rookie Austin Barber will start in his place next to Tytus Howard on the right side.
Jaguars running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) is the only player with a game status on Jacksonville's injury report. He is questionable after not practicing Wednesday and being a limited participant on Thursday and Friday.
The Jets are without free agent addition Joseph Ossai. Rookie slot corner D'Angelo Ponds was limited all week with a calf injury and is considered doubtful. That means Jarvis Brownlee Jr . will see plenty of action against his former team.
The Titans will be without linebacker Cedric Gray because of a concussion. He didn't practice all week. Gray is the only Titans player with a game status.
The Bills have three players questionable: defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (knee), running back Ty Johnson (hamstring) and Jordan Hancock (quad). Sanders was limited in practice on Wednesday and Friday, but did not practice on Thursday. Johnson practiced for the first time all week as a limited participant on Friday, while Hancock has improved throughout the week. He didn't practice on Wednesday, was limited on Thursday, and fully practiced on Friday.
The Houston Texans are incredibly healthy entering Week 1: their injury report lists no one with a game status.
The Falcons will start Week 1 down their top two quarterback with Tua Tagovailoa suffering an oblique injury on Thursday in practice, and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) not ready to return from the torn ACL injury he suffered last season. That has journeyman Cooper Rush in line to start in head coach Kevin Stefanski's team debut. Veteran edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (shoulder) is the only player questionable for Sunday.
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (back) is the only player on the Steelers' injury report after being limited all week. His limited status could somewhat be tied to his ongoing contract negotiations, as he is set to enter the final year of his rookie deal in 2026.
Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is questionable to suit up Sunday after being limited in practice all week with a calf injury. Ozzy Trapilo, who is also questionable, was limited all week with a knee injury, and Xavier Woods was limited Thursday and Friday with a groin injury. He, too, is questionable.
The Panthers had a relatively clean injury report, with Patrick Jones II the only player listed. That also means running back Jonathon Brooks is cleared to play in his first NFL game since Dec. 8, 2024.
No injury designations for the Vikings entering Week 1. Safety Jacob Thomas and offensive tackle Caleb Tiernan were listed on the report earlier this week with ankle injuries, but will play.
The Packers only ruled out defensive lineman Warren Brinson after he didn't practice this week. Starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) are both questionable after both being limited practice participants all week. Linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper is also questionable after practicing for the first time this week on Friday in a limited fashion.
The Miami Dolphins don't have any injury designations for Week 1. Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is good to go for Sunday after practicing fully every day this week and not having a game status on the final injury report. Las Vegas All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers (knee) is out after having a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday.
The Arizona Cardinals ruled out three players: offensive lineman Isaiah Adams (knee), safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (ribs) and cornerback Garrett Williams (Achilles). Adams didn't practice all week while Taylor-Demerson didn't practice on Thursday or Friday. Williams was ruled out after being a limited participant all week. Third overall pick running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is questionable after being a limited practice participant all week.
The Washington Commanders don't have any players listed as game status for their season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles.
The Eagles ruled out edge rusher Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) after he was a limited practice participant all week, and tight end Eli Stowers (hamstring) is questionable after being a limited practice participant all week.
Dallas Cowboys No. 2 running back Malik Davis went down with a hip injury Friday in practice.
Pro Bowl wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) is questionable to play on Sunday despite practicing fully all week. Nabers is working his way back from a torn ACL he suffered last season, and he said the team will l eave the final decision o n when he returns up to him.
"I've been wanting to play for so long now, but at the end of the day, I can't put my career at risk," Nabers said on Thursday . "I gotta take that into account. There's a lot of football that I still have left to play. Making a split decision on when do I think I'm able to go out there and perform rather than just going out there -- I think the coaches know that, I know that I have a lot more football to play. So just being conscious of making sure I'm at the right standpoint of going back out there."
The Denver Broncos just have one player listed on their injury report, and it's wide receiver Marvin Mims (foot). However, he is trending toward playing on Monday after practicing fully on Thursday and Friday.
The Kansas City Chiefs have a number of players on the injury list, but almost all of them practiced fully on both Thursday and Friday, including three-time Super Bowl MVP Patrick Mahomes (knee). Mahomes is in line to start in Week 1 after tearing his ACL last season. Left tackle Josh Simmons (back) and safety Chamarri Conner (knee) both…

title: Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. denies seeking record contract as Week 1 deadline approaches
summary: Contract negotiations remain unresolved, but Porter says the business side of the NFL has not changed his desire to stay in Pittsburgh
full_text:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr . enters Week 1 of the 2026 season in a contract standoff with the Pittsburgh Steelers while being set to begin the final year of his rookie deal. Porter Jr., the No. 32 pick in the 2023 NFL Draft , claims a desire to be the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL isn't what's holding the deal up.
"I don't know where that came from," Porter Jr. said, via ESPN . "Whoever made that up, I really don't pay too much hype into it."
Porter Jr. led the NFL in passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage last season, with a minimum of 60 pass attempts, with a 49.1 rating. No other corner allowed a sub-50 passer rating against. Porter Jr. ranked ahead of other All-Pro and Pro Bowl cornerbacks who have received big paydays in recent years, like Patrick Surtain II (four years, $96 million), Derek Stingley Jr . (three years, $90 million) and Christian Gonzalez (four years, $135 million).
"At the end of the day, it's business. I know what that is, and I got my head straight so I understand that," Porter Jr. said. My dad [Joey Porter] been in this league as a coach and a player, so he has knowledge on that. It's nothing new to me, even though this is my first go around. That's how I look at it."
The Steelers kick off their season at 1 p.m. EST Sunday while hosting the Atlanta Falcons , and Porter Jr. is holding out hope deal gets done before then.
"I hope so, man, that's all I can do is just hope," he said.

title: Bears extend RB D'Andre Swift to three-year, $33.75 million deal, per report
summary: Swift is fresh off producing career highs in scrimmage yards (1,386) and touchdowns (10) under Ben Johnson in 2025
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are taking care of bell cow running back D'Andre Swift before their Week 1 matchup at the Carolina Panthers . Chicago and Swift have agreed to a three-year, $33.75 million contract extension with $27.5 million guaranteed, per ESPN .
Swift was set to enter this season in the final year of his three-year, $24 million contract that he signed in 2024. Instead, he'll now be in Chicago for the next four seasons, including the upcoming 2026 campaign.
Swift produced career highs in rushing yards (1,087), rushing touchdowns (9), rushing yards per game (67.9), scrimmage yards (1,386) and scrimmage touchdowns (10) in 2025, the first season under Bears coach Ben Johnson. Despite this new deal being Swift's third NFL contract, he still has plenty of prime years left at 27. That means Chicago now has its backfield of quarterback Caleb Williams and Swift in place for the foreseeable future.

title: NFL Week 1 picks and score predictions: Broncos edge Chiefs, Raiders over Dolphins
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks for every game as Seattle hosts a Super Bowl rematch and Patrick Mahomes returns from injury
full_text:
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Season 14 of my NFL picks !
I know, I know. I can't believe I'm still around, either. At some point, I'll retire or be forced into retirement, and when that happens, the first thing I'm going to do is buy a 49ers helmet so I can take it with me to the beach.
Why would I need a 49ers helmet at the beach? I think we all know the answer to that.
Fake 49ers player Daejon Love posted practice drills at the beach and always made sure to carry a 49ers helmet with him everywhere. He scammed women out of $1.8 million by pretending to play for the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/HRkxesbQNe
I mean, just look at those routes. If the NFL ever decides to create an entire team out of only fake football players on Instagram, Daejon Love will be a first-round pick. I don't know why anyone would ever create an entire team out of fake football players on Instagram, but I've seen crazier things happen on social media, so I'm not going to pretend like it can't happen.
If the 49ers put as much effort into this season as Daejon Love did into scamming people, they are a lock to win the Super Bowl .
Now, did I actually pick the 49ers to win the Super Bowl this year?
That's a great question, and you can find the answer by clicking here to see my predictions for the entire 2026 NFL season. If you click over, you'll see my final record prediction for all 32 teams, plus who I'm picking to make the playoffs and who I'm taking to win Super Bowl LXI. Spoiler alert: I'm not taking the Browns .
For those you clicking over to read my predictions, we'll wait here until you get back.
All right, welcome back. Let's get to the Week 1 picks.
Wednesday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC)
For just the second time in 75 years, the NFL is opening the season on a Wednesday. I don't think anyone asked for a Wednesday night opener, but after going more than 210 days without having an actual NFL game to watch, I'm not going to complain.
As a matter of fact, I'm going to do the opposite of complain. I'm going to praise the move, if only because it gave NBC an excuse to pull the Hump Day camel out of retirement.
The best way to get over the midweek hump? NFL Kickoff - and it's only three weeks away! 🏈 📺: Patriots vs Seahawks, Wednesday September 9 7ET on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/TRaofO7ff1
If I had to choose any NFL coach to open the season with a game on Hump Day, I probably wouldn't have gone with ... you know what, I'm not going to go there. That's too easy. Let's just get to the pick.
The last time we saw these two teams on the field together was in February, when the Seahawks absolutely destroyed the Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl LX. In that game, the Patriots got blown out on a neutral field, and now, they have to go to Seattle to face a Seahawks team that is 10-1 against the AFC under Mike Macdonald.
Since hiring Macdonald, the Seahawks have made a habit of demoralizing AFC teams, and I'm not sure this game is going to be any different. New England might have gotten better this offseason, but not by 16 points.
The Patriots' two biggest problems heading into Week 1 are both related to the pass rush: on defense, they have no proven pass rush, and on the other side of the ball, I don't think their offensive line can stop Seattle's pass rush.
That feels like a recipe for another blowout. The Patriots did make some major upgrades on offense with the biggest one being the addition A.J. Brown , but it's hard to get him the ball if you don't have time to throw. It's also hard to get him the ball if he's being blanketed by Devon Witherspoon .
As for the Patriots offensive line, Will Campbell is now fully healthy and the unit should look better than it did in the Super Bowl, but that's mostly because I don't think it's possible to be any worse ( Drake Maye got sacked six times in the Super Bowl loss).
Before we get to my pick in the NFL opener, I feel obligated to mention the fact that I picked the Seahawks to win by two touchdowns when these two teams met in Super Bowl LX. I'm only pointing this out so we're all aware that I'm one-for-one picking Patriots-Seahawks games over the past nine months, so we can probably all just assume I'm going to go two-for-two.
The Seahawks might be the most slept-on defending champ in NFL history, and I feel like they're going to come out angry in this opener. I think Seattle sends a message to the rest of the NFL with a double-digit win over a good Patriots team.
THE PICK: Seahawks 27-17 over Patriots
Thursday, 8:35 p.m. ET (Netflix)
For the first time in NFL history, we're getting a regular-season game in Australia, and I have to say, this has already turned into what is possibly the greatest battle of wits that we have ever seen in a Week 1 game. Not only do both teams have to deal with a 17-hour time difference between Australia and California, but they also have to fly 16 hours just to get to Australia.
When you add those two things together, that can lead to some serious jet lag, but both teams think they know how to beat it:
I'm not sure which strategy is better, but I did once make a 36-hour trip to Melbourne, so I at least know what the Rams are up against. And in case you're wondering what I did on my 36-hour trip: I started the day by going to Patricia Coffee for breakfast, which I'm only noting because if you go to Melbourne and don't try Melbourne coffee, they will ban you from making any future visits to the city.
I also went to the Queen Victoria Market for lunch, and I ate at the Biggie Smalls restaurant in the Melbourne Airport for dinner.
If there is one rule I live by in life, it's that I will never pass up an option to eat at a restaurant named after Biggie Smalls.
Although I didn't get to see as much of Melbourne as I would have liked, I wasn't affected by jet lag at all, so I think the Rams might be on to something.
Since Sean McVay was hired in 2017, the Rams have always kept their international trips short and sweet, and it seems to work. Under McVay, the Rams are 3-0 both straight up and against the spread in international games, and they've won those three games by a combined score of 92-17.
Last year, the Rams became the first team to arrive on Saturday for a game in London. The decision to go with their unprecedented plan last season was definitely risky because they were playing a Jaguars team that has played more games in England (14) than anyone. If anyone knows how to handle the travel for a London game, it's the Jags, but the Rams destroyed them anyway.
The Rams created a bold travel plan for Australia and if you're picking against them because you think the plan is crazy, you're making one of the three classic blunders and we all know the three classic blunders:
1. Never get involved in a land war in Asia. 2. Never go in against a Sicilian when death is on the line 3. Never try to outsmart Sean McVay when making a travel itinerary for an international game
And now, let's forget about the actual travel for a second and simply talk about how this game might go.
The first week of the season is usually when most NFL teams are at their healthiest, but not the 49ers. Somehow, they're already banged up. The 49ers are so injured that they might actually have to let Daejon Love play. So you have a beat-up 49ers team traveling halfway across the world to face a Rams super team that has two of the defenders in NFL history ( Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald ) along with the reigning NFL MVP ( Matthew Stafford ).
It's still not a lock that Donald's going to play (SEPT. 8 UPDATE: He definitely won't be playing ), but as long as Garrett and Stafford are both out there, the Rams should be able to play at a high level. And Stafford is going out there as long as his back holds up on the flight over.
Feel like surviving the flight to Australia is going to be half the battle for the Rams and 49ers. Matthew Stafford back in February, "I hope my back isn't too sore afterwards." #Rams #49ers #Australia pic.twitter.com/vwu6ClqJOF
Alright, if you…
