title: Sean McVay defends Rams' travel schedule following ugly loss to 49ers in Australia
summary: McVay says the 49ers were the No. 1 reason why his team fell to 0-1
full_text:
Sean McVay knew questions about the Rams ' travel schedule were coming following his team's ugly 27-7 season-opening loss to the 49ers in the first-ever game played in Australia.
McVay started his postgame press conference by stating that there were going to be "narratives" stemming from the loss and that others would "appropriately, put the blame on me." He accepts responsibility for the loss, but he doesn't (at least publicly) regret his decision to arrive in Australia less than 30 hours prior to kickoff.
"I don't believe that's why we didn't play well enough," he said. "I really don't. I'm more than comfortable with that. I'll always make decisions that I think are best for the football team. It's easy in hindsight to be able to say it was a miss. But those are responsibilities that I'll take and then you try to be able to look at it. I'll always look at myself inside out and figure out where I can improve."
A popular offseason pick to win the Super Bowl , the Rams looked anything like a championship team on Thursday night, while the 49ers did. Los Angeles was outgained by nearly 100 yards, were just 2 of 9 on third down, allowed the 49ers to convert on more than half of their third downs, and had no answers for the 49ers' star players. Brock Purdy threw three touchdown passes that included scores to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Christian McCaffrey had 88 total yards, and Fred Warner recorded 11 tackles and a forced fumble.
The Rams' star players, however, largely failed to show up. Matthew Stafford had his worst game in recent memory. He finished the game with just 155 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Davante Adams didn't have a catch until midway through the third quarter and finished with just three receptions on six targets. Myles Garrett didn't register a sack or a tackle.
McVay shared several other reasons for the loss outside of the team's travel schedule. He pointed out his team's inability to capitalize on some of its momentum early in the game. He said that the Rams did not communicate very well "on either side of the ball." Lastly, McVay acknowledged that the 49ers "outplayed us in every phase."
"They deserve the win," McVay said. "I think that's really what it boils down to. And sometimes sports can have days like that. And like I said, this will only define us if we allow it to. And I'm looking forward to leaning in, going back to work. And today was humbling, but sometimes life can do that to you. We've got a lot of football left, and we're not going to allow this one game to do anything other than help us learn and grow."
McVay said that he felt that his team was ready to play in response to a question about how the Rams slept on the eve of the game after arriving in Australia just hours earlier. Conversely, the 49ers arrived in Australia days in advance.
"I thought we were ready to go, and obviously we just didn't play good enough," he said. "You know, you give the Niners credit; they were sharp in all three phases. They did a really good job, and we were never able to really get any continuity going offensively. When we were able to get some drives going, we weren't able to finish it with points, but again, you know, I look at nobody but myself, and I have to do a much better job. And then defensively, we had some chances and couldn't necessarily get off the grass, and we struggled in the kicking game as well."
As flat as the Rams were, they were in position to make it a one-score game late in the third quarter. But after Stafford was stuffed on fourth-and-goal on the 1-yard-line, the 49ers drove 99 yards on 11 plays and took a 24-7 lead after Purdy hit Samuel on a 15-yard touchdown pass.
At that point, the Rams abandoned their running game (which had been one of their few bright spots), became one dimensional and therefore predictable. The Rams turned the ball over on their ensuring possession, the 49ers tacked on a field goal, and McVay waved the white flag when he pulled Stafford from the game with 3:05 left.
"We got outplayed," McVay said. "They did a good job. We didn't, and you know, there's a lot of football left to be played. And I love that locker room. I love our coaching staff. And today will be an opportunity for us to learn it, and we're going to find out what we're about. And I'm excited to be able to lean in, and certainly I make no excuses. And you know, it starts with me, and I got to do a better job for our group."
McVay then apologized to the large contingent of Rams fans who helped make up what was the seventh largest crowd for a regular-season game in NFL history. He finished his press conference, however, by reiterating that his decision to arrive in Australia so close to kickoff was based solely on football and what he thought was best for his team.
"We thought that was the best plan of attack in terms of our approach," he said. "We didn't have the result that we wanted today, but you know, you could certainly say it was great to be able to get the feel for the culture here. That didn't have anything to do with us not wanting to embrace that. It was just what we thought was best, and unfortunately, we didn't have the result that we wanted and didn't play the way that we were capable of."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Where to watch Colts vs. Ravens: TV channel, live stream, prediction, pick, odds, spread
summary: Lamar Jackson and Daniel Jones look to bounce back from injury-plagued seasons
full_text:
The NFL is back, and so, too, are Super Bowl expectations for the Baltimore Ravens . This time, though, things look a little different. The Jesse Minter era opens Sunday with a visit to the Indianapolis Colts , who are out to prove last season's strong start was no fluke.
Both teams feature quarterbacks hoping to bounce back from up-and-down 2025 seasons. Lamar Jackson struggled with injuries all year, and he rarely looked like himself. He had the highest sack rate of his career and averaged 26.8 rushing yards per game, less than half of his career average. The Ravens' stop-and-start season came to a sudden end when Tyler Loop missed a game-winning field goal attempt in Week 18 against the Steelers , sending Pittsburgh to the playoffs.
Daniel Jones , meanwhile, was playing the best football of his career by far—and some of the best football in the NFL, in fact—before a midseason leg fracture (he played through it) and, a few weeks later, a torn Achilles. Through 10 weeks, Jones led the NFL in passing yards and was fourth in yards per attempt. The Colts fell into disarray after the injuries, slipping from 8-2 to 8-9 and missing the postseason for the fifth straight year.
Both teams have several reasons to be optimistic they'll put their respective disappointing finishes in the past, and that starts Sunday. Here's what you need to know.
Lamar Jackson in a new offense: Each of the two times Jackson's changed offensive coordinators, he's won MVP. Can he make it three for three? Declan Doyle is only 30 and is calling plays for the first time, but he was the Bears ' offensive coordinator under Ben Johnson last year, and Jackson has drawn rave reviews from him. Expect more under-center play-action passes—an area Jackson has excelled—and other notable shifts in the approach.
Superstar running back meeting: Over the past five seasons, Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor rank first and second, respectively, in rushing yards. Sunday, they'll go head to head. Henry is coming off another monster statistical year—1,595 rushing yards, 16 rushing touchdowns—but he had some costly, uncharacteristic fumbles as well. Taylor was averaging 113.9 rushing yards per game through 10 weeks, but Jones' injury threw a wrench into things, and he averaged just 63.9 yards per game over the final seven contests. Still, 1,585 rushing yards and a league-high 18 rushing touchdowns is hardly anything to sneeze at.
Jesse Minter's impact on the defense: Minter will call defensive plays for Baltimore, which makes sense given he was excellent as the Chargers ' defensive coordinator the past two years. He should immediately help patch up a leaky pass defense. The Ravens allowed an NFL-high 64 passes of 20+ yards last year. Minter's Chargers allowed just 37, tied for second-fewest in the league.
By all accounts, Jones has looked outstanding, physically, even after such a major injury. That is crucial in Shane Steichen's offense. Jones' ability to throw on the run via play action and even scramble when needed finally allowed Steichen to run the ideal version of his offense. Adding Taylor into the mix made Indianapolis one of the NFL's most explosive offenses over the first half of the season. Defensively, the healthy returns of DeForest Buckner , Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward cannot be overstated.
But there's simply more talent in Baltimore, where Jackson is finally healthy again and the defense has plenty of individual talent, especially up front. The Colts' excellent offensive line against the Ravens' defensive front should be a terrific battle throughout. Minter's play calls should unlock the best version of Baltimore's secondary, too.
There will be some starts and stops for both offenses, but Henry should be in line for a monster day, and Indianapolis' linebackers could have some trouble against the run and the play-action pass. Minter's coaching debut is a winning one.
Pick: Ravens 23, Colts 20; UNDER 47.5
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 1 best bets: Big days for star running backs, plus what to expect in Patrick Mahomes' return
summary: Plus, picks for all 16 games as the 2026 season begins
full_text:
The NFL is back, and for as much as we've prognosticated and hemmed and hawed and tried to predict what's going to happen, we are flying blind to some extent.
Week 1 in particular tends to produce not only some surprises, but some results that prove to be anomalies. Last year, the Raiders beat the Patriots in Week 1. The Steelers and the Jets (!) played one of the week's most entertaining games, a 34-32 comeback Pittsburgh win. To cap the week, J.J. McCarthy accounted for three fourth-quarter touchdowns to rally the Vikings past the Bears .
Our knowledge will improve as the season does, and hopefully so will this column. Each week, I'll have my best bets heading into the weekend, plus my full slate of picks. Let's do it.
NOTE: All odds via DraftKings .
Here's Saquon Barkley's history in four games as an Eagle against the Commanders :
No player has ever run for 110+ yards in five straight games against Washington, nor has any Eagle run for 110+ yards in five straight games against a single opponent, but Barkley will be the first.
Philadelphia has revamped its run game, and its offensive line is as healthy as it's been in some time, perhaps dating back to two seasons ago, when Barkley ran for 2,005 yards and the Eagles won the Super Bowl . Washington had a bumpy close to training camp/the preseason, and while its starters are OK, there are significant depth questions. Plus, while I am high on Sonny Styles , this is a very tough assignment for a rookie linebacker in his NFL debut.
In a game that could have some stops and starts as both teams debut new offenses, Barkley ripping off a big run or two will give the Eagles a big boost.
While I'm not quite as bullish on Derrick Henry as I am on Barkley, I'm willing to bet on a solid day for the ageless wonder. The Colts do get a major boost in the form of a healthy DeForest Buckner , but this is, again, a spot where I worry about the linebackers. Akeem Davis-Gaither is on his third team in three years. Jaylon Carlies played two defensive snaps last year. Those are the starters. Rookies CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher have talent, but both emerged from the preseason as backups.
The Ravens brought in certified ass-kickers in guards John Simpson and Olaivavega Ioane , which should mitigate the loss of center Tyler Linderbaum . They also have new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who will install more under-center plays. Henry actually averaged more yards per carry out of the shotgun (5.3 compared to 5.1), but he had a higher explosive run rate (10.8% to 8.0%) when the quarterback was under center. And we love explosive plays when chasing yardage totals.
You may look at this and say "duh." After all, Cam Ward struggled as a rookie (though he was actually pretty good at not turning the ball over).
But more importantly, this would mean something that did not happen at all last year: THE JETS WOULD RECORD AN INTERCEPTION!
That's right, in case you forgot amid all the other Jets misery, they became the first team since at least 1933 (when the NFL started tracking interceptions) to not pick off a single pass for an entire season.
The Titans ' passing offense has not looked good this preseason, to put it nicely. The Jets added a ton of veterans to a defense that was basically incompetent at many points last year. It won't be a good unit, necessarily, but it will be functional. There's young talent up front: I'm a big fan of David Bailey , and I liked the T'Vondre Sweat addition a lot. Kingsley Enagbare , Joseph Ossai and Will McDonald IV can all provide pressure. Demario Davis is still getting it done at linebacker. Nahshon Wright had five interceptions last year. Minkah Fitzpatrick is 29 and no longer the All-Pro he once was, but he still has a nose for the ball.
Listen, at some point, the Jets have to pick off a pass, right? And on the other side, Geno Smith led the NFL with 17 interceptions last year. He had 15 the year before. His super aggressive play style leads to a wide variety of outcomes. If we combine the two quarterbacks, we get much tastier odds than betting on just one.
I am going to be interested in Browns unders quite often this season, considering Deshaun Watson was quite literally one of the worst quarterbacks of the 21st century when we last saw him, and that was two Achilles tears ago.
On the other hand, the Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars ' offense went nuclear in the second half of last season, and maybe it will pick up right where it left off. But I'm skeptical. The run game was pretty meh last year, and the offensive line has issues. It can still be good, but I don't think it will run league-leading hot.
More importantly for this game, though, the Browns' defense is still really talented, even without Myles Garrett . Jared Verse is a very good player. Maliek Collins was excellent last year, and Cleveland is hoping 2025 No. 5 overall pick Mason Graham takes a big step in Year 2. Reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger is outstanding. Denzel Ward is, too. I see this being a 24-10 Jacksonville win.
I was surprised to see the Chiefs as a 2.5-point favorite against the Broncos on "Monday Night Football." Denver has won four of the last five meetings, and the defense has given Patrick Mahomes fits for even longer; Kansas City has scored under 20 points in six straight games against Denver. Vance Joseph might just have the secret stop-Mahomes formula. Offensively, the Broncos still have one of the best offensive lines in the game, and Jaylen Waddle adds a much-needed explosive element.
And remember, not only is Mahomes in his first game back from a torn ACL, but left tackle Josh Simmons isn't expected to play. That means undrafted rookie Khalil Benson is tasked with protecting Mahomes' blind side against a team that led the NFL in sacks last year. That's a rough combination.
There's been a ton of roster churn for the Chiefs. Many key contributors from the Super Bowl teams are gone. Many rookies are in. It's a bit of a transition year, though Mahomes is good enough to make any year a winning one. But there are too many questions at left tackle, at wide receiver and in the secondary right now.

This year, Arizona’s coaching staff wants to run the ball effectively. Last year, LA was ranked #5 in overall defense and averaged just 285.2 combined yards per game on average. That breakdown is #5 against the pass and #8 against the run. Let’s look at three things the Cardinals must accomplish to defeat the Chargers. Establish a balanced rushing attack This new offense has several aspects that LaFleur wants to maintain. A short passing game is one. Usage of multiple tight ends is another. And a consistent rushing attack is paramount. That is why Arizona used the third overall draft pick on a stud running back instead of one of the elite pass rushers that were available. LaFleur wants to run the ball. Last year the Cardinals were #31 in rushing, averaging just 93.1 yards a game. They were #22 in red-zone scoring at 54.1%. All of that needs to change. How were the Los Angeles Rams in 2025, the team LaFleur left as their OC? #1 in total offense, #1 in passing, #7 in rushing, #1 in scoring offense, and #7 in Red Zone efficiency. This will not happen overnight, but LaFleur has multiple years of running this offense, and it will get there eventually. For now, the Cardinals need to have their running game produce and become a game manager against the Chargers. Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love returned to practice today in a limited capacity as he continues working back from a high ankle sprain. Love had been sidelined since suffering the injury during the preseason. A positive step for Arizona ahead of Sunday’s Week 1 matchup against the… pic.twitter.com/B05ADRlwsO — The Sports Place (@offsportsplace) September 10, 2026 Arizona’s offense needs a balanced rushing game. The bulk of carries will most likely come from Tyler Allgeier. If rookie Jeremiyah Love is 100% with his ankle issue, he will get his fair share of carries, but don’t expect a full load. A balanced attack will ease the need to pass the ball often and also help control the clock. Now, how will the offensive line react? Already, RG Isaish Adams is ruled out, and rookie RG Chase Bisontis is on IR. This is already a problem. Jon Gaines will take the reins and had a great camp and preseason. LG Isaac Seumalo is also a question mark. So, we’ll see. Keep out the Chargers’ pass rush The Chargers have a very good pass rush, and it comes from various spots and players. They generate a great pass rush with LB Tuli Tuipulotu, who actually lines up as an EDGE rusher, and Khalil Mack, who has returned to California. To counteract these fine athletes, the Cardinals depend greatly on the skills of RT Elijah Wilkinson and LT Paris Johnson on the corners. The Wilkinson vs. Tuipulotu will become a battle and just might determine quite a few things in this ballgame. What is that called? Baptism by fire? Mack is a beast and has been for years. He was the “NFL Defensive Player of the Year” back in 2016 but dislocated an elbow last year, which landed him on IR. Mack finished the 2025 season with 11 starts, 32 total tackles, 5.5 sacks, 11 QB hits, 11 hurries, and 23 pressures. Tuipulotu has a leaner build and was a second-round draft pick. He was exceptional in college at USC and totaled 21 sacks in a tough conference. He led the conference in tackles for loss (22) and sacks (13.5) in his final year. He was a unanimous All-American, a two-time All-Pac-12 recipient, and was named the “Polynesian College Football Player of the Year.” In the 2025 NFL season, Tuipulotu racked up 13.0 sacks and has 26 for his three-year career. His quickness off the edge and a fast first step are his calling cards. 39 tackles for loss, 52 QB hits, and 73 pressures are why he is such a menace. Tuipulotu was limited in practice on Thursday, but is expected to play. Can Johnson contain him? Stay tuned. Attack the Chargers’ receivers Arizona’s defense has to have constant pressure on Chargers QB Justin Herbert every time he drops back to pass. But he will have time to throw. And when he does, the back end of the Cardinals defense has to be ready. Herbert has a good arm and can’t be allowed to set up and go through his progressions and set up the short passing game. If Herbert is able to set his feet at will, it will become a very long day. He can throw into tight windows when he has time to survey the field, and can throw long. Whether the defensive line can rattle Herbert is one issue, but when he does throw, the Cardinals’ defensive backfield has to come through. It is not clear if Garrett Williams will play, or at the very least become limited in his snaps. A guy like Williams is as real as they come and is a critical piece to the pass defense. This would mean that Max Melton will become the default starter on the outside with Will Johnson. Denzel Burke will then be moved to the slot corner position. The coaching staff has complete trust in all four players. Keeping Herbert out of his comfort zone will be a huge plus to this game with containment. The Chargers have a very good receiver corps headed by Ladd McConkey. Also in this group are Quentin Johnston and Tre’ Harris. Rookie WR Brenan Thompson was drafted in Round 4 and is expected to have a decent number of offensive snaps.

title: How Cooper Rush starting at QB changes the Falcons’ offensive game plan
summary: Tua Tagovailoa’s back is tighter than a clam with lockjaw, and Michael Penix Jr. doesn’t trust his knee as far as he can throw it. It’s Cooper Rush time. For some, this feels like the worst-case scenario for the Atlanta Falcons quarterback room, but is the drop-off from Tagovailoa to Rush really all that significant […]
full_text: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tua Tagovailoa’s back is tighter than a clam with lockjaw, and Michael Penix Jr. doesn’t trust his knee as far as he can throw it. It’s Cooper Rush time. For some, this feels like the worst-case scenario for the Atlanta Falcons quarterback room, but is the drop-off from Tagovailoa to Rush really all that significant in 2026? If we are judging who ran the offense more competently during the preseason, the answer is Rush. Yes, he had a rough outing against the Broncos, but Rush joined the roster only 15 days before the game. Since then, he’s shown command and the ability to keep Tommy Rees’ offense on schedule. His ability to pick up the playbook in that short amount of time is why he’s been able to stick as a backup in this league. Rush to Velling! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ibjVS6UxNh — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) August 29, 2026 However, being a quarterback takes more than knowing the calls; when you look at physical ability and skill sets, Rush and Tagovailoa have been indistinguishable this summer. Neither is known for arm strength, and making plays out of the pocket is a crapshoot. Rush did show a slight willingness to push the ball compared to Tua, who had an ADoT (average depth of target) of 3.3, to Rush’s 6.3. Tua has an edge when it comes to processing, but he didn’t do a great job showcasing that during the preseason. If this feels like a Tua slam piece, that’s not my intent, but it’s important that we establish how similar the two players are at this stage in their careers. These similarities are why I believe that Kevin Stefanski won’t have to tweak the game plan much, if at all. The staff clearly believed Tua could execute the offense better, but they can still ask Rush to run the same plan. The 2026 offense was always going to run through Bijan Robinson, not the Falcons quarterback. He is the clear strength of this offense, a true one-of-one talent, and whoever is under center is here to manage the game. The worry for this offense, especially with Tua, is: what do you do when you get behind the chains or trail in the scoring column? Many have been prepared to hold their breath on third-and-long this upcoming Sunday, and that’s not going to change with Rush. So Stefanski and Rees are still focusing on solving the same problem, which is a good thing. If the team had to adjust to a completely different play style at the last minute, I’d be more concerned about the product we’ll get Sunday. To be clear, I am still concerned to a healthy degree. KP down the sideline! With the @DrakeLondon_ block 👀 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/5vQ1gLa0gH — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) August 28, 2026 Rush won’t be expected to win this game with his arm, and neither was Tua before going down. This needs to be the Bijan Robinson show with an overdose of screens and quick-hitting passes. Hopefully, paired with complementary play from the defense, that’s enough to get the Falcons through Week 1.

We learned quite a bit on Friday, so let’s dive into the injury reports. Let’s take a look! Notably, Penix has been clear and is healthy to play, but according to The Falcoholic’s Jeanna Kelley, head coach Kevin Stefanski told the media this week that Penix is not where he feels he needs to be right now. title: Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix Jr. both inactive for Week 1 Falcons vs. Steelers
summary: The official injury report hasn’t been released as I write this, but the team confirmed to onsite media after practice that both Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. will be inactive against the Steelers in Week 1. This, of course, comes on the heels of Tagovailoa being named the starter just this past Monday. The […]
full_text: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The official injury report hasn’t been released as I write this, but the team confirmed to onsite media after practice that both Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. will be inactive against the Steelers in Week 1. This, of course, comes on the heels of Tagovailoa being named the starter just this past Monday. The oblique injury Tua suffered in Tuesday’s practice will officially keep him sidelined. Cooper Rush will be the Falcons’ starter against the Steelers, with rookie UDFA and fan favorite Jack Strand serving as his backup. Billy Bowman and Cam Williams will also be inactive Sunday. Za’Darius Smith is questionable. It’s certainly not the ideal scenario to start the season. But it is an extremely Falcons situation to be stuck in for Week 1. After practice, Stefanski praised Cooper Rush’s preparation, saying the veteran “stays ready so he doesn’t have to get ready.” Stefanski also seemed unphased by the situation — maybe because of his nightmare QB rotation with the Browns last year. “Ideal world, you’d love for one guy to get 17 games plus, but that’s not realistic,” he said. On getting Rush fully up to speed after he’s taken so few first-team snaps to this point, Stefanski said adjusting the game plan isn’t unfamiliar either. “Every game plan known to man has tweaks throughout the work week,” he said. Previously, Stefanski has said they tailor the offensive game plan to maximize a QB’s strength, so I would assume there’s been plenty of tweaking going on since Tua went down in practice on Thursday. As far as Penix, he was going to be inactive whether Tagovailoa was healthy to start or not. Stefanski told us Monday after Tua was announced as the Week 1 starter that Penix would be inactive because he isn’t ready to play. That will not change. God forbid the team needs an emergency QB on Sunday, but if they do, it won’t be either Tua or Penix. Per league rules, to designate a player as an emergency third quarterback, the player has to be a “bona fide” quarterback, and they have to be inactive. So there is no emergency QB for this week. We’ve just gotta hope for the best, I guess. Stefanski wouldn’t guess at a timetable for Tua’s recovery, or for Penix to be ready. He’s going to stay focused on being ready for Pittsburgh. So now we wait to see what Cooper Rush has to offer against the Steelers, and how quickly Tua and or MPJ can get healthy and available.

title: What to know about Falcons – Steelers in Week 1
summary: Season openers can be many different things. They can be trials, making teams test their mettle against terrific opponents, as was the case with the Patriots-Seahawks Wednesday night matchup. They can also be divisional rock fights, like the Thursday night battle in Australia between the 49ers and Rams. They can even be cupcakes, like the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 08: James Daniels #78 of the Pittsburgh Steelers wears a Guardian Cap while making a block during the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 08, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Season openers can be many different things. They can be trials, making teams test their mettle against terrific opponents, as was the case with the Patriots-Seahawks Wednesday night matchup. They can also be divisional rock fights, like the Thursday night battle in Australia between the 49ers and Rams. They can even be cupcakes, like the hapless Browns facing off against a greatly improved Jaguars team. Or they can be an exorcism of sorts, which is where the Falcons land. Atlanta has a long and sorry history against the Steelers that we’ll discuss here and Adnan Ikic will cover in more detail over the weekend, but suffice to say it’s history alone that makes bearing Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh seem borderline impossible. These teams are not so far apart in terms of talent that it should be so, but it’s on the Falcons to prove that they’re not just a Steelers punching bag for eternity. Let’s talk about the matchup ahead. 2026 results for both teams Your Atlanta Falcons went 8-9 in a very familiar way, falling apart in the middle of the season (with a five game losing streak and seven losses in eight games) and rallying late to win their final four games. Arthur Blank looked at the state of the team, which was sloppy and ruinously bad on special teams to go with an underwhelming offense and better-than-expected defense, and launched both Raheem Morris and Terry Fontenot into the sun. That led to the team hiring Ian Cunningham as general manager and Kevin Stefanski as head coach, with Jeff Ulbrich sticking around to run the defense, and an offseason where the team added Tua Tagovailoa to compete with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback and turned over about a third of the 2025 roster. They’ve now put together eight straight losing seasons and are banking on offensive and special teams improvement without significant regression on defense. The Steelers, meanwhile, went 10-7 and snuck into the playoffs in the AFC North before an absolutely miserable playoff loss to the Texans, where the defense limited Houston to just 10 points but saw the offense put up just eight points as Aaron Rodgers put together one of the worst games of his long and illustrious career. Mike Tomlin and the team parted ways in the offseason, bringing Mike McCarthy to town. How the Steelers have changed entering 2026 There’s a familiar core here, particularly in the trenches, but much has changed. Mike Tomlin finally walked away from the Steelers after 19 seasons, and was replaced by Mike McCarthy. Simultaneously overrated and underrated, McCarthy reunites with Aaron Rodgers after many years away and will hope to upgrade a stagnating offense, but isn’t known for significantly raising a team’s floor when it’s already fairly high. The team traded for Michael Pittman Jr. to boost their receiving corps and drafted a fullback—that’s Steelers football, baby—but otherwise have not made substantial changes to their starting lineup on offense. The theory is that McCarthy can get more out of this group, which isn’t a terrible bet; the problem is that there’s still probably not enough talent in the skill positions for this group to be outstanding. Defensively, the Steelers look largely unchanged up front, which makes sense given that they’re typically killer in the front seven. They did turn over their secondary significantly, however, adding safeties Rayshawn Jenkins and Jaquan Brisker and cornerback Jamel Dean to the group. It may take some time for that group to gel and both Jenkins and Brisker are not really coverage assets at this stage of their respective careers, but Dean and Joey Porter Jr. are an excellent pair of starting cornerbacks. Overall, this was not a tear-it-down-to-the-studs offseason because the Steelers don’t really do that. After years of winning seasons that managed to be pretty underwhelming, however, I’m not sure adding McCarthy and a small handful of pieces is going to drag the Steelers to something special in 2026. What you need to know This won’t be easy, because playing the Steelers is never easy for the Atlanta Falcons. They’re 2-16-1 against Pittsburgh all-time, with their last victory coming all the way back in 2006. This is simply not an opponent Atlanta handles well. That said, this is the most vulnerable Steelers team I can remember. Mike McCarthy is new to this team, which features a 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers with one cheek in the podcasting chair, a lackluster supporting cast outside of a couple of killer wide receivers, and a shaky offensive line. The defense is still excellent and special teams is at least solid, even with kicker Chris Boswell coming off a down season by his standards, but the very real question marks around the offense should give the Falcons a fighting chance. To actually win on the road—and they’ve never won in Pittsburgh, by the way—the Falcons will need to take advantage of every Steelers weakness and limit mistakes. Fumbles and interceptions from Tua or Cooper Rush, to say nothing of the indecision and wilting under pressure that were worrying in preseason and last year with the Dolphins for Tua and in the first week of preseason for Rush, will give an anemic offense more chances. They need to get in a rhythm passing the ball and putting pressure on a secondary that has three new starters and may be without Joey Porter Jr., who is limited with a back injury he’s been dealing with all summer. They need to feed Bijan, naturally, but also Kyle Pitts and Austin Hooper, who are capable of taking advantage of matchups against safeties Jaquan Brisker and Rayshawn Jenkins. The key is going to be meshing Tua’s natural ability to deliver quick, accurate short-to-intermediate throws with yards after the catch from Atlanta’s playmakers, limiting the time Tua has to sit in the pocket in the face of a withering Pittsburgh pass rush. If Rush has to start, the Falcons will keep a similar gameplan, looking to limit the quarterback’s mistakes and only take high percentage shots at a tough Steelers defense. Defensively, it’s going to be about effectively stopping Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle—and for what it’s worth, the latter averaged under 3 yards per carry against Atlanta in two games in 2025—and pressuring Rodgers. There’s still a dangerous player in the aging quarterback, but he can really only show that off in stretches and in clean pockets. Pittsburgh’s interior offensive line is their weakness—and has looked quite shaky this preseason—even if it’s not an outsized weakness, and the Falcons happen to have a deep group of defensive linemen to rotate and an attack-first philosophy under defensive line coach Nate Ollie. Rodgers has increasingly struggled under pressure as he’s aged, and he’s particularly susceptible to getting off-rhythm and missing throws when he’s forced to roll out instead of being allowed to step up and put more oomph into his throws. Interior pressure will wreck Pittsburgh’s day, and the Falcons will need it. We have little idea of what to expect from these Falcons with a whole new coaching staff and a lot of new faces, but the keys to winning this game are easy to see: Limit those mistakes, attack Pittsburgh’s outsized weaknesses, and lean heavily on your playmakers. If they can beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh for the first time ever, they’ll certainly have our attention going forward.

full_text: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Hello Falcoholics, and welcome to Friday’s Falcons Opening Drive. Today, of course, is the 25th anniversary of Sept. 11th. Our hearts go out to the survivors, to those who lost their lives that day or as a result, to those who still mourn loved ones they’ve lost, and to all of us who bore witness. I’m on my way to Flowery Branch to see what Friday’s practice has in store for us. Obviously, I’ll be keeping my eye on the quarterback situation, and what Tua Tagovailoa ’s able to do in the portion of practice we’re allowed to watch. As always, I’ll share my reporting from practice in The Falcoholic’s Feed. I’ll dig into the Tua injury situation below, we’ll walk through the Falcons coverage you need to check out before Atlanta takes on the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, and make sure you scroll down to the comments and answer our question of the day: What’s your boldest prediction for Falcons vs. Steelers? Let us know in the comments. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Falcons Opening Drive: When the Falcons named Tua Tagovailoa the Week 1 starting quarterback, I wrote that Atlanta’s QB situation has been a roller coaster ride this summer, and not a particularly fun one. Friends … I want off this ride. The Athletic ’s Josh Kendall reported Thursday that Tua Tagovailoa went down during practice appearing to be experiencing pain in his lower back or side. Reggie Chatman Jr. from 11 Alive News happened to catch the moment Tua went down: #WATCH : I happened to catch the moment #Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa went down briefly during the open portion of #Falcons practice He stood off to the side for the rest of the period we were able to watch. https://t.co/VyzfRrzond pic.twitter.com/sIO2CtmOkF — Reggie Chatman Jr. (@ReggieChatman) September 10, 2026 The team listed Tua as limited on Thursday’s injury report, and Cooper Rush told the media after practice that he took the majority of the first-team snaps. Falcons QB Cooper Rush said he played with starters at practice today after Tua Tagovailoa’s potential injury that occurred during the early portion. He said they’re the first reps he’s taken with the whole starting unit outside one 2-minute scrimmage session in camp. — Joe Patrick (@JoePatrick) September 10, 2026 As Josh Kendall noted, Tua missed some time at the beginning of camp with lower back spasms. We do not know if these issues are related. I don’t know what to expect, but I do know this: I am going to start mentally preparing myself for Cooper Rush, starting Falcons QB if Tua isn’t able to participate in that early part of practice. There are still two days before kickoff, and NFL players have access to extensive treatment options. Maybe limiting Tua so much on Thursday was precautionary and he’ll be fully ready to go on Sunday. We can hope. But after over two decades of following this team, I have a very real concern that the Falcons are, for some cosmic reason beyond my comprehension, not allowed to have nice things. Let’s all hope I’m wrong. And let’s get to the Falcons coverage you need to watch, read, or listen to before the Falcons take on the Steelers this Sunday. Atlanta Falcons news Billy Bowman is back at practice, and he doesn’t take it for granted : Tori McElhaney at AtlantaFalcons.com wrote this insightful piece on the young Falcons DB who can’t wait to get back out on that field. Cooper Rush hasn’t been told he’s starting on Sunday, but did take his first significant reps with the first team on Thursday . Mark Raimondi from ESPN has all the details. Chris Lindstrom said Rush was “great” in Thursday’s practice , and Daniel Flick from the AJC has more on Rush and the possibility he’ll start on Sunday. If Tua is healthy enough to play … can he resurrect his career like Baker Mayfield and Sam Darnold ? D. Led breaks down the situation on Bowtie Sports. Kevin Knight and Adnan Ikic were kind enough to let me join their Week 1 Dirty Birds and Brews extravaganza , along with Dave Choate and TreShon Diaz. Check it out! From the Falcoholic Community NorthernHawksFan said it so well: Cooper Rush isn’t the best the Falcons can do at quarterback in the grand scheme … but he might be the best they can do this week. Throwing an undrafted free agent rookie out of a D2 program to the wolves in Week 1 would be less than ideal for Jack Strand’s development. The Falcoholic’s Question of the Day: What are your boldest predictions for Sunday’s matchup with the Steelers? Here are mine: Brian Robinson scores a TD I’ll curse TJ Watt’s name upwards of 10 times The Falcons win, regardless of who starts at QB. Week 1 is incredibly weird. Anything could happen! Share your boldest predictions in the comments.

title: Ravens-Colts Week 1 predictions: how will Jesse Minter attack Daniel Jones?
summary: Let’s face it: odds probably do not mean much to Ravens fans at this point. Last year, Baltimore entered 14 games as favorites and won just half of them. That pattern is likely to play out once again this year given the Ravens’ early slate of opponents, starting with the Colts in Week 1. Baltimore […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Jesse Minter head coach of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s face it: odds probably do not mean much to Ravens fans at this point. Last year, Baltimore entered 14 games as favorites and won just half of them. That pattern is likely to play out once again this year given the Ravens’ early slate of opponents, starting with the Colts in Week 1. Baltimore is favored by 3.5 points heading into Indianapolis ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ), indicating plenty of confidence in Jesse Minter’s head coaching debut. The Colts are largely running it back with their 2025 squad, so last year’s tendencies can offer some insights into their plans for Sunday. Head coach Shane Steichen’s offense primarily operates out of the shotgun, relying on running back Jonathan Taylor to churn yards in the run game and suck linebackers in for play action shots to the intermediate areas of the field. Quarterback Daniel Jones rarely pushed the ball downfield, throwing deep balls less than 10% of the time ( via Pro Football Focus ). Most of those targets went to wide receiver Alec Pierce, the NFL’s back-to-back leader in yards per reception; beyond him, Indianapolis lacks another deep threat. That should lead the Ravens to deploy some bracket coverage against Pierce to prevent him from taking the top off the defense. Minter’s three-safety looks will also allow the secondary to shift the coverage picture post-snap. Look out for Baltimore to bait Jones by showing a 1-on-1 matchup against Pierce pre-snap only for Malaki Starks or Jaylinn Hawkins to fly back and cover a potential shot downfield. If Indianapolis tries a high-low route combination on the outside, the boundary corner can try to jump the underneath route with safety help overtop. The Colts’ defensive coordinator is a familar foe: Lou Anarumo, who previously held the same position in Cincinnati from 2019 to 2024. The Ravens offense largely found success against his Bengals defenses during his tenure, able to control games on the ground and keep up with Joe Burrow in a shootout when needed. But Anarumo’s ability to disguise his coverages and pressure packages can attack the Ravens offense in two key ways. First, it will demand Jackson to be on the same page with a revamped offensive line that features a brand-new interior trio, including center Jovaughn Gwyn making his first start. He will already have his hands full with Colts defensive tackles DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, but he also has to help Jackson read the defense and communicate adjustments to the rest of the line. Jackson will also have to be careful not to fall into Anarumo’s coverage traps. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has worked to re-establish the Ravens’ quick passing game with an emphasis on Jackson’s footwork and timing as he goes through his progression. But just as Minter will try to bait-and-switch Jones, Anarumo will do the same against Jackson. This could become a particularly interesting battle when the Ravens go under center, which has been another of Doyle’s early focal points. Baltimore will no doubt use running back Derrick Henry to set up play-action shots to wide receiver Zay Flowers on his signature deep dig routes. Anarumo can respond with a two-high safety look but sending one of them to buzz the middle of the field. But that will only be possible if his front can stop the Ravens’ ground game, putting pressure on undersized linebackers Jaylon Carlies and Akeem Davis-Gaither to step up and fit the run. Otherwise, the Colts will have to use their safeties in run support, which should give Flowers more room to operate over the middle. Given that this is his first game in Doyle’s system – and his first game back at 100% after last year’s injuries – the two-time MVP could lean on his legs on Sunday as he gets settled in the offense. Some of his most dazzling extended plays came against Anarumo’s Bengals, partially because the coverage look forced him to hold onto the ball. These are just a few elements of the schematic battle set to take place on Sunday. Steichen and Anarumo will offer a solid first challenge to the Ravens’ new-look coaching staff in a game that could come down to Baltimore’s star power advantage on both sides of the ball.

title: Ravens rule out Nnamdi Madubuike, Teddye Buchanan for Week 1 vs. Colts
summary: The Ravens will have to wait at least one more week to have defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan back on the field. Both were ruled out on Baltimore’s final injury report before their regular-season opener against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Head coach Jesse Minter projected optimism about the progress of both […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 25: Nnamdi Madubuike #92 of the Baltimore Ravens walks off the field after a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 25, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens will have to wait at least one more week to have defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan back on the field. Both were ruled out on Baltimore’s final injury report before their regular-season opener against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Head coach Jesse Minter projected optimism about the progress of both players in recent weeks but made no commitments regarding Week 1. Taking the cautious route is no surprising considering the nature of their injuries. The Ravens have carefully managed Madubuike’s ramp-up since returning from the neck injury that ended his 2025 season. He only began participating in full-team work last Friday; this week, he was listed as limited in all three practices. The two-time Pro Bowler should make his 2026 debut by Week 4 since he was not placed on injured reserve during roster cuts, but he could be on a limited snap count to start. “He is really, really close,” Minter said after Friday’s practive. “It has been a great process for him to return from the injury that he had. Feel great about where he is at, but we are not going to play him this week.” Madubuike himself spoke to the media for the first time since going down in Week 2 last year, expressing his appreciation for the Ravens organization and fans who supported him through his recovery. “Over the past year, it has been definitely one of the hardest points of my life, but I am very grateful to be where I am at right now,” Madubuike said. He declined to go into the details of his injury, but clarified that he never considered ending his career. “There are a lot of rumors out there, but I always knew I was going to be back,“ he explained. ”It was just a process of coming back just like any other injury. This was my time in which I had to deal with it. I went through it, and now we are here.” Minter was not asked about Buchanan’s status, but the second-year linebacker is just shy of nine months removed from the torn ACL he suffered last December. He has also been limited in practice, indicating he still has another step to take before playing in a game. The Ravens did not list wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) with an injury designation, while Devontez Walker (groin) was listed as questionable. His absence could elevate third-round wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane into a significant role in his much-anticipated NFL debut. Fellow rookie Elijah Sarratt would also be active on game day and could see some snaps. The Colts’ cleared all of their players for Sunday’s game except for linebacker Austin Ajiake, who did not practice on Friday due to a hamstring injury. That means wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) will play, giving quarterback Daniel Jones the same complement of weapons that devastated Jesse Minter’s Chargers defense last year.

title: Zay Flowers upgraded on Ravens’ Week 1 injury report
summary: The Baltimore Ravens upgraded star wide receiver Zay Flowers to full participation on their second injury report of the 2026 NFL season. Flowers, 25, was listed as as a limited participant on Wednesday with a hamstring injury. He previously dealt with a minor groin injury during training camp but was quickly back on the field. […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MD - AUGUST 26: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens laughs during the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens joint practice at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on August 26, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens upgraded star wide receiver Zay Flowers to full participation on their second injury report of the 2026 NFL season. Flowers, 25, was listed as as a limited participant on Wednesday with a hamstring injury. He previously dealt with a minor groin injury during training camp but was quickly back on the field. His upgrade should quell any concerns about his availability in Week 1. Baltimore’s injury report was otherwise the same as Wednesday’s. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee), defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck), and wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) were all limited. The Colts had five status changes on their Thursday injury report. Rookie safety A.J. Haulcy (ankle), depth tight end Drew Ogletree (neck), and backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) were all upgraded from limited to full participation. Quarterback Anthony Richardson (illness) was listed as a full participant, while defensive tackle Grover Stewart (rest) did not practice. The only constant for Indianapolis was wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), who remained limited as he works his way back to 100%. Head coach Shane Steichen said earlier in the week that he is expecting the 26-year-old to take the field on Sunday. However, if he is out of the picture, the Colts’ wide receiver corps will be led by Keenan Allen and Josh Downs with former Raven Laquon Treadwell elevated to the No. 3 role. Neither Allen nor Downs particularly impressed in 2025; both averaged just 6.4 yards per target. But the former is still a crafty route-runner who will find the soft spots in zone coverage, and the latter can be a dangerous threat with the ball in his hands. The Colts’ offense was one of the best in the league before Daniel Jones’ injuries last season, including a 38-point, 401-yard outburst against the Chargers’ Jesse Minter-led defense. Pierce had nine catches for 98 yards in that game, so his potential absence could make a difference on Sunday.

title: Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans, Week 1 bold predictions
summary: The wait’s almost over, Bills Mafia! In a couple days’ time, the Buffalo Bills will be on the field at NRG Stadium to take on the Houston Texans. It’s a tall task for the Bills as the road team in Week 1, made more daunting by the fact that quarterback Josh Allen has never won […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills throws a pass against the Houston Texans during the second quarter at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait’s almost over, Bills Mafia! In a couple days’ time, the Buffalo Bills will be on the field at NRG Stadium to take on the Houston Texans. It’s a tall task for the Bills as the road team in Week 1, made more daunting by the fact that quarterback Josh Allen has never won a game (four tries) in the Texans’ home stadium. Overall, Houston leads the all-time series 8-5, dating back to the first matchup in October of 2003. The Texans have six straight home wins over the Bills in that timeframe, which includes a Wild Card playoff win during the 2019 NFL postseason run. Will Buffalo buck history’s trend and find a way to win a game in Houston? You can bet Allen will do all he can to end the suffering in H-Town. It won’t be easy, with a new-but-familiar head coach in Joe Brady and a first-time NFL defensive coordinator in Jim Leonhard. How will all of that affect Buffalo this Sunday? Here are a few predictions I’m willing to bet bear fruit for Josh Allen and company in Week 1. If you feel like getting in on the action with FanDuel Sportsbook , there are lots of ways to take your game-day experience to a new level while cheering on the Buffalo Bills! Bills cover spread (-1.5 | O/U 44.5) for 1st win at NRG There are a few reasons to avoid this line, and most won’t need to look any further than the oddity that NFL Week 1 often is league-wide. There’s also the fact that the Bills have never won in NRG Stadium, with Josh Allen holding onto four such losses. Add in a pair of young first-time lead coaches for Buffalo working their first game, and it feels like there might be too much working against them this weekend. Yet some of those same reasons are why it might makes sense to take these odds. While most will say these should be flipped in Houston’s favor, at some point history has to change course. In many ways, Buffalo was a known entity to much of the league in prior seasons, thanks to the nine-season tenure of prior head coach Sean McDermott. It’s true that the NFL has also seen Brady’s work as the team’s previous offensive coordinator, but it was under the leadership of McDermott. Will Brady operate a different type of system as the new leader? He’s brought in Pete Carmichael as offensive coordinator, who’s also comes from the Sean Payton coaching tree. Together, and with Brady still calling plays, look for Buffalo’s offense to utilize certain principles Payton has made famous in his career — but with a twist perhaps the Texans haven’t yet seen. Add in what’s sure to be a highly motivated Allen and we might see the Bills finally claim a W in Houston. If you’re looking to wager on the O/U of 44.5 (Bills-specific total of O/U 23.5), consider the volatility of the first week, and that every game has equal potential to be a blowout or low-scoring defensive battle. Josh Allen scores 2+TDs (+900) Book it. A motivated Josh Allen is dangerous for the Bills’ opponents. There may be no better game to begin a season if the goal is to have Allen locked in from the start. He wants a win in NRG like little else. To accomplish that, Buffalo will need plenty of end zone production from Allen. I expect Brady to get Allen in a rhythm off the bat, which could play into an afternoon that sees him throwing at least two touchdowns, and perhaps running for another score. In fact, if things go according to plan, Allen could meaningfully flirt with scoring three-plus touchdowns (+5500) Sunday afternoon. Getting off on the right foot in Week 1 means letting Allen take control of things. This is the way. James Cook III gets 100+ yards from scrimmage If you’ve read this far, you might be wondering if I’ve even taken a second to consider the immense talent all over the Texans’ defense. I have. But it’s Week 1 and this is a new season. James Cook is currently -114 at FanDuel O/U 74.5 rushing yards. Cook can get most of that total with one cut to the end zone. At some point, Brady will lean into the running game in an attempt to smash home a proper reminder about who led the league in rushing for 2025. Interestingly, Cook is also -114 (at publishing) to finish O/U 19.5 receiving yards. I say he finishes over that total, perhaps north of 30 yards on the day. Parallels have been drawn between Cook and Alvin Kamara for good reason. Cook came out of college as a premiere dual-threat player, and I expect Brady to better unleash Cook in that role this season. Cook at -105 as an anytime touchdown scorer also feels like a solid bet; while his -165 odds to lead the game in rushing yards feels similarly likely to happen. Those are just a few quick takes, but there are plenty of more bold predictions to make. We really don’t know what to expect out of Leonhard’s defense yet, so that leaves room for a lot of guessing about who claims the first sack in his system, and what an aggressive scheme looks like toward turning the ball over. What are you willing to predict happens during Bills-Texans in Week 1? Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now to put it to the test !

title: Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans, Week 1: Five key questions for both sides
summary: The Buffalo Bills hit the road this weekend to open their 2026 NFL season against the Houston Texans. NRG Stadium has been a veritable house of horrors for quarterback Josh Allen, who’s yet to win a game there in four prior attempts. Each season brings a new version of every NFL team, so the roster […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Danielle Hunter #55 of the Houston Texans runs against Spencer Brown #79 of the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills hit the road this weekend to open their 2026 NFL season against the Houston Texans. NRG Stadium has been a veritable house of horrors for quarterback Josh Allen, who’s yet to win a game there in four prior attempts. Each season brings a new version of every NFL team, so the roster Allen and the Bills battled last season will look a bit different this Sunday. Despite that, the Texans are expected to bring the same level of ferocity on defense, and an offense with plenty of firepower on tap as led by quarterback C.J. Stroud. Many have the Texans among this year’s elite teams in the AFC, and rightfully so. After making the playoffs last season, some see Houston’s ceiling as the Super Bowl. Buffalo gets first crack at these Texans, hoping to show them that they’re not going anywhere. To get us ready for Sunday’s 1 p.m. EDT kickoff, I connected with Scott Barzilla of Battle Red Blog . We chatted all things Bills-Texans this week, but here we’ll focus on Houston’s side of the equation in an effort to learn something new ahead of kickoff. Below, we touch on what’s different about the Texans this season, and who Barzilla sees as the most important addition to Houston’s team in 2026. Plus, if the Texans should find themselves short on defensive firepower, what’s the counter move, and what an opposing coach might target as a weakness of Houston’s on offense and defense. Barzilla also clues us into what it’ll likely take for the Texans to defeat the Bills on Sunday. You can read more about all of this below, and be sure to head over to Battle Red Blog to check out my Bills-centric half of this season’s inaugural Five Questions ! Five Good Texans questions with Buffalo Ramblings 1. Update us on this year’s Texans. What’s different with Houston this season? The Texans have a few new defensive starters in Kayden McDonald and Reed Blankenship. J.D. Clowney should be a major contributor off the bench. On offense, David Montgomery is the major addition as the Texans hope to be a more ball control offense. 2. Who do you see as the most important addition to the Texans this season? It is Montgomery. Joe Mixon gave them zero yards last season, so anything Montgomery gives them is more. In particular, he hopefully will be more effective in the red zone than Woody Marks was. More first downs and time of possession plays right into the Texans hands. 3. If Will Anderson Jr. and Kayden McDonald can’t suit up Sunday, what changes for the Texans (how do they offset those losses)? Both players should be a go, but if they aren’t then Clowney takes over at defensive end and the Texans use a similar tackle rotation as last season on the inside. Obviously, the Texans are better with those two but they should have plenty of depth. 4. If tasked with game-planning to open the season against Houston, what might you try to exploit on offense and defense as an opposing coach? The key to this game will be the running games on both sides. Whoever is able to make the other offense one dimensional will win. I have little faith that the Texans can move it consistently through the air. However, their pass rush could single-handedly wreck the game. Staying in front of the chains will be crucial for both teams. 5. What do the Texans have to do to defeat the Bills on Sunday? Obviously, the same applies to the Texans. They have the added challenge of keeping Josh Allen in the pocket. If they make him beat them with his arm then it will be a great day for them. The Bills led the league in rushing yards last season, so that will be easier said than done. My thanks to Scott Barzilla for taking time to chat Bills-Texans ahead of Sunday! Be sure to check out more of his and the rest of the team’s work over at Battle Red Blog . You can also catch up on my Bills thoughts from this conversation over at BRB . title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. Houston Texans in Week 1
summary: On Sunday afternoon, the Buffalo Bills will square off against the Houston Texans in each squad’s opening game for the 2026 NFL season. Both teams enter with high hopes for their year, just like every NFL team in September. While some of those teams may harbor unrealistic dreams of playing February football, there is a […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 22: Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Deone Walker (96) leaves the field following the National Football League preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns on August 22, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Sunday afternoon, the Buffalo Bills will square off against the Houston Texans in each squad’s opening game for the 2026 NFL season. Both teams enter with high hopes for their year, just like every NFL team in September. While some of those teams may harbor unrealistic dreams of playing February football, there is a clear argument to be made that both teams playing at NRG Stadium on Sunday have a legitimate chance at representing the AFC in Super Bowl LXI on Valentine’s Day. Buffalo has traveled to Houston and lost in each of the last two seasons, dropping a 23-20 decision in 2024 before losing 23-19 last season. In each contest, a tenacious Houston defense prevented Buffalo’s offense from finding its footing. While Buffalo’s defense played well enough in each game, it was ultimately the Texans who were able to make enough plays, executing sound situational football to come out victorious. If the Bills are going to reverse that trend this Sunday, they’ll need some big plays from their top contributors. Here are five Bills players to watch this week as they take on the Texans. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR DJ Moore I’m going to clear the obvious right off the bat: Josh Allen is a player to watch. He is always a player to watch. I’m going to try to skip him as many times as I can this season as a result. With that in mind, though, this is the first chance that we have to see Buffalo’s newest weapon in real action, and Moore’s mere presence is likely to open so much for Allen and the Buffalo passing attack on Sunday and beyond. In last year’s matchup between these two squads, Allen found himself unable to find open receivers against a suffocating Houston defense. Moore is known for his excellent route running ability, and that route running ability makes him the obvious man-beater in the receiver room this season. Moore will have a tough matchup regardless of which corner Houston decides to use against him, but I don’t expect the Bills to anchor him to the outside and force him to fend off Derek Stingley Jr. or Kamari Lassiter exclusively. Look for head coach Joe Brady and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. to move Moore around the formation to create plus matchups for him. Sometimes, teams have to fight strength vs. strength, and while the Texans have excellent corners, Moore is an excellent receiver. Buffalo has to find ways to put the ball in his hands. TE Dalton Kincaid Speaking of players who need to find the football, Buffalo’s top tight end is going to play a huge part in Sunday’s matchup, and he’ll need to perform if the Bills are going to win the game. Kincaid missed last season’s matchup with an injury, and he caught just two of six targets for 34 yards in the 2024 meeting between these clubs. The Bills need their TE1 to find space in the middle of the field, and that space likely needs to come in the short-to-intermediate areas. It’s not wise for Allen to hold the ball for too long against this Texans defense, so uncovering quickly will keep him upright and keep the offense on schedule. Designing some quick looks for Kincaid early to help establish some rhythm is a good plan in the passing game, and if the Bills can run the football effectively, they may be able to use some heavier formations to allow Kincaid to slip out deep via play-action after moving the chains. G Alec Anderson Speaking of the running game, the offensive line is going to be a focal point this week for multiple reasons. First, Josh Allen took eight sacks in the meeting between these two teams last year, a career-high. While I think that many of those sacks were on Allen for trying to make something out of nothing, there were plenty of plays where Buffalo’s offensive line allowed near-immediate pressure. James Cook scored on a 45-yard rushing touchdown early in the game, and he totaled 116 yards on his 17 carries, so the run game worked. Can the offensive line give a better performance in pass protection while clearing space for Cook in the run game with a new configuration this season? The hope is that Anderson will slide right into the left guard spot smoothly, though departed David Edwards was one of Buffalo’s best linemen last season. Anderson is a longtime reserve who has performed well in spot duty, but Sunday will mark the first step towards what will hopefully be a fruitful next phase of his career. He has a tough task ahead of him given Houston propensity for stunts, picks, and games up front, as this defense will test the Buffalo o-line’s ability to communicate. All five of the big boys up front are keys to success, but I’ll be watching Anderson in particular this week. DL Deone Walker Buffalo’s new-look defense has a chance to make a big statement this weekend, and it very well could be the biggest man on the team who makes the biggest statement of all. Walker showed flashes of brilliance in his rookie season, and a change in scheme coupled with a year of experience could lead to a huge breakout for the mammoth interior lineman. Houston’s offensive line is the clear weakest link on the team, and new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard will look to exploit the advantage Buffalo has up front all afternoon. Look for the Bills to move Walker around the line a bit to create positive matchups for him, but as the team’s primary nose guard, don’t be surprised when Walker controls the middle of the line and makes some big plays from arguably the most difficult spot on the field. While I think Buffalo will rotate August acquisition Greg Gaines in the middle as well, it’s primarily going to be Walker’s show in the middle. If he can take another step forward, look out, because that will give the Bills a huge advantage on Sunday. CB Maxwell Hairston After a summer where he fended off a legitimate challenge from rookie Davison Igbinosun on the outside, this is a perfect opportunity for Hairston to show that he belongs as the undisputed CB2 on this roster. Hairston was another rookie who showed promise last season, but he missed a ton of time due to injury and spent much of this summer injured, as well. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is extremely accurate when he has time to throw, and the Bills have been burned by the long ball against him in the past. Hairston has excellent speed, and while he isn’t overly physical, he is a willing tackler who isn’t afraid to mix it up in the run game. A good start on Sunday would go a long way towards solidifying a new-look Buffalo secondary.

title: NFL Power Rankings, Week 1: Buffalo Bills favored to begin 2026 season
summary: Despite the fact the NFL has only played two games of the 2026 season thus far, nothing was going to stop analysts and prognosticators from revealing their first Power Rankings of the regular season. Some call it “Week 0” and use the endeavor as a means to discuss expectations and rank accordingly. Others? It’s it’s […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills scrambles and looks to pass during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite the fact the NFL has only played two games of the 2026 season thus far, nothing was going to stop analysts and prognosticators from revealing their first Power Rankings of the regular season. Some call it “Week 0” and use the endeavor as a means to discuss expectations and rank accordingly. Others? It’s it’s their own version of the wild west borne out of quota needs. That doesn’t mean we should focus only on those that are observably button-up, since sometimes the off-the-beaten-path offerings are far more entertaining. If you’ve followed along with me in prior seasons, you’ll know I try to remain consistent in sharing the same group of “rankers” each week. You may see some outfits join in or drop off, depending on vibes. That’s to be expected because we all know how important it is to give such an opinionated exercise the level of seriousness it deserves. One thing’s clear in looking over this batch: Everyone LOVES the Los Angeles Rams. We get it, they have the reigning NFL MVP in Matthew Stafford, made a massive trade for edge rusher Myles Garrett (injured, mind you), and someone convinced a well-retired Aaron Donald to come back and play defensive tackle. Plus they have some guys who are good at catching the football. Los Angeles is the easy pick. Well, it was until they took a flight just to mail in a game in Australia. Someone has to be crowned the premiere team ( The Athletic crowned them a “superteam”), and the Rams made the most sense. But their Week 1 effort should serve as a reminder that crowning a champion in September is foolish. In a similar way, any success a team finds early in the season should be dealt with in measured praise. Though quick to pass in our timeline, it’s a long season and very little reveals itself until after the Turkey (maybe Tofurkey or even lobsters) is (are) carved. We saw this play out last season when the Bills beat teams the experts didn’t view as a real threat. They wanted to see more out of Buffalo, only content to buy in once the playoffs began. Well, we know what happened on that front. Anyway… power rankings. It’s not that serious. Or is it? Seriously, power rankings are fun! We’re at almost 2,700 words with this one — featuring 20 outlets (plus one) — so this article should help dissolve away some of those Friday office blues in no time. This list may shrink in any given week, but this season’s first at-bat is swinging for the fences. No one aggregates Buffalo Bills power rankings data like Buffalo Rumblings! Let’s get to it, to see where the experts place the Buffalo Bills, shall we? SB Nation NFL 3 via: 2027 Super Bowl Chances by James Dator and Mark Schofield 4 via: Tim Lynch with Mile High Report 4 via: Brandon Lee Gowton with Bleeding Green Nation NFL.com : 4 “The vibes are generally high in Buffalo, although receiver Khalil Shakir’s health status is worth monitoring prior to the season opener in Houston. The potential for a honeymoon campaign with WR DJ Moore — oh, and the commencement of Joe Brady’s first season as a head coach — begins against an elite defense, which should inform us on where the Bills stand offensively.— Nick Shook The Athletic : 3 “ (Austin) Mock’s projected win total: 10.8” The defense is undergoing a significant change, entering a 3-4 scheme with six new starters, and that’s part of the reason for hope. The other is a fresh start with coach Joe Brady that could get this team over the hump and into the Super Bowl. Even if last season didn’t go as planned, it’s hard to keep a Josh Allen-led team out of the top five entering the season.” — Chad Graff/Josh Kendall ESPN : 3 “ Milestone to watch: Josh Allen surpassing Patrick Mahomes for the most combined passing and rushing yards by a quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons.” “This would take Allen close to the end of the season, but it is well within reach. Allen is 3,782 yards away from eclipsing Mahomes (38,604), and Allen has not missed a start since his rookie season. He averages 590.1 rushing yards and 3,762.8 passing yards per season, so he could pass Mahomes with multiple games to spare. Breaking records is a common occurrence for Allen, and with new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore added to the mix, he’s primed to set many marks yet again.” — Alaina Getzenberg Sports Illustrated : 5 “Perpetually a team embodying the Atlas statue, the questions for the Bills are myriad. Can Josh Allen continue to play his style of football and get through a season relatively healthy? Will new head coach Joe Brady represent the right kind of vibe switch for Buffalo? Is Jim Leonhard’s defense finally going to provide Allen with some teeth on the other side of the ball and lessen the burden on his back? This is a team that we can almost assuredly believe will be there at the end of the year, though getting over the hump remains the eternal obstacle.” — Conor Orr FOX Sports : 7 Ralph Vacchiano is smart listing his rankings in descending order, that way you have to scroll all the way down to see who’s the top dog. No one scrolls an entire article to read who’s holding court in the basement, right? You do? Oh. Moving on… Vacchiano’s comments on Buffalo should serve as a warning, at least enough to give you pause about what president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane built. However, most teams can’t endure the amount of injuries to one position that the Bills managed with their wide receivers this summer. “Summer injuries to WRs Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir were a dangerous reminder that receiver is still a problem for this team. Man, if they can properly address that position, look out.” — Ralph Vacchiano Bleacher Report : 5 We’re good with B/R these days, no? I am. They’ve come a long way, and to be clear they offer a very slick power rankings presentation. That’s the most important thing in all of this, yes? Well, it’s close to the most important thing. Remember, we’re having fun, folks! Gary Davenport makes a lot of key points about the Bills that fans of the team are woefully aware of, and which some are fearful may never change. He’s pretty spot on here, revealing that once again that most of this won’t matter if they lose in the postseason. “There isn’t a team east of Los Angeles more in Super Bowl-or-bust mode than the Buffalo Bills. The Bills dismissed their highly successful coach because he couldn’t get the team over the hump. They are led by Josh Allen, who has more playoff wins than any quarterback in NFL history without a Super Bowl appearance. The good news is the team should be in the thick of it in the AFC. The offense has the league’s reigning rushing king and a new No. 1 wide receiver in D.J. Moore. The defense ranked seventh in the league last year. The bad news is that the Bills have been in the thick of it for the better part of a decade, but for whatever reason they come up short in the postseason. — Gary Davenport “ The Ringer : 5 With genuine and obvious applause to SB Nation and Buffalo Rumblings : Find a better overall sports-focused digital website better than The Ringer , I dare you. The Ringer looks and reads like one of those glossy European-specific car magazines short on advertisements, and that cost $30 dollars in a famous bookstore. It’s true that The Athletic ’s playoff odds/playoff simulator can’t be beat ( here are both from last season / if you’re curious ), but that’s about the only place The Ringer comes up short. I get nothing for such endorsements, mind you. I’d be shocked if either outfit even knew I existed. As Dante Lee points out, their rankings will come monthly, which means we won’t see them again in these spaces until October. Lee’s thoughts on Buffalo, should they pan out, would leave little doubt about the Bills’…
