title: Five bold predictions for the Buffalo Bills 2026 season
summary: Josh Allen just finished as the second-highest ranked player on the NFL’s Top 100 list for 2026, trailing only Myles Garrett and sitting ahead of every other offensive player in the league. That alone tells you where the conversation around this team should start. But this year’s Bills are also walking into Week 1 with […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Head Coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills on the sideline during a pre-season game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen just finished as the second-highest ranked player on the NFL’s Top 100 list for 2026, trailing only Myles Garrett and sitting ahead of every other offensive player in the league. That alone tells you where the conversation around this team should start. But this year’s Bills are also walking into Week 1 with a new head coach, a new defensive identity, and a roster that looks meaningfully different than the one that has been bounced from the playoffs six straight times. With training camp in the rearview and Houston up first, here are my five bold predictions for the 2026 Buffalo Bills. Josh Allen wins his second NFL MVP Not so bold, right? The league already told us where it stands on Allen entering this season. He’s the No. 2 overall player on the NFL Top 100, the highest-ranked offensive player in the sport, and Sports Illustrated’s most recent quarterback comparison had him at the top of the position as well, ahead of Patrick Mahomes. Dalton Kincaid even said out loud what a lot of people around the league seem to think — that Allen should have been No. 1. He’s also getting what might become the best supporting cast of his career. DJ Moore arrives via trade to reunite with new head coach Joe Brady, who was Moore’s offensive coordinator in Carolina back in 2020 and 2021 — the two best statistical seasons of Moore’s career. Allen himself has said the fit already feels seamless. Pair that with a difficult schedule that will force Buffalo to play its best football just to stay in the AFC East and wild-card race, and you have every ingredient for an MVP case: the talent, the weapons, the opportunity, and the motivation. Maxwell Hairston finishes with five or more interceptions Hairston’s rookie season was more about flashes than volume, and for a fair reason — a training camp knee injury cost him the first six weeks, and an ankle issue ended his year before the playoffs even started. He still finished with two interceptions and five pass breakups in just 11 games and three starts, good enough to tie for third among all rookie defenders in picks and to land him on both ESPN’s and The Athletic’s All-Rookie teams. The tape backs up the ceiling. In just his second career game, Hairston picked off Patrick Mahomes and led every Bills defender in PFF grade that day at 91.1, the highest mark on the field. His 4.28 40-yard dash gives him the recovery speed to play aggressive, ball-hawking coverage rather than just survive downfield. Now entering year two as an expected full-time starter across from Christian Benford, and hopefully healthy heading into the season, Hairston should get the reps and consistency his rookie year never allowed. I think he takes that leap into being one of the better young corners in football. My friend Raphael Sattamini, from the “SattaMiniCast” , has him leading the league in INTs! Terrel Bernard returns to All-Pro-caliber form Bernard and Hairston share the same theme: talent that hasn’t been able to stay on the field. Bernard’s ceiling isn’t in question — his 143 tackles in 2023 ranked 12th in the entire NFL, and he added 6.5 sacks and three interceptions that year. Even in a lesser 2024 campaign as a team captain, he still posted 104 tackles. But 2025 was a step back across the board, with just 65 tackles, zero sacks, and one interception in 12 games as injuries piled up. Here’s why I think that changes. Buffalo’s move to Jim Leonhard’s 3-4 scheme, with bigger bodies up front designed to occupy blockers, should keep Bernard cleaner than he’s ever been in the NFL. That’s not a new concept for him — he played inside linebacker in a 3-4 under Dave Aranda at Baylor, and Aranda and Leonhard worked together at Wisconsin, sharing a defensive philosophy built around disguised pressure. With the extra defensive linemen and Dorian Williams taking on more of the load absorbing bigger offensive linemen in the new base defense, Bernard gets to play in space again, doing what he does best: making plays sideline to sideline instead of constantly shedding blocks from guards and centers. I think he’s not just healthy this year — I think he’s back to being one of the most disruptive off-ball linebackers in the league, earning a Pro Bowl nod and being in the All-Pro conversation. The Bills finish top three in the NFL in sacks Jim Leonhard isn’t walking into Buffalo without a résumé. He spent the last two seasons on Vance Joseph’s staff in Denver, where the Broncos set a franchise sack record in 2024 and led the entire NFL in sacks again in 2025. Before that, at Wisconsin, Leonhard ran defenses that blitzed on over half of all dropbacks across six seasons, touching nearly 72% in 2020. Aggressive is the baseline, not the exception, for this coordinator. He’s also inheriting more juice than Buffalo’s pass rush has had in years. Bradley Chubb signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal after an 8.5-sack season in Miami and slots in as a starter. T.J. Parker, Buffalo’s second-round pick out of Clemson, adds another true edge threat. Inside, Deone Walker and Ed Oliver give Leonhard real interior push to pair with an outside rotation that also includes Greg Rousseau and Michael Hoecht. After finishing 27th in pass-rush win rate a year ago, this group has the pieces and the coordinator to flip that number completely. I expect it to show up immediately in Week 1 against Houston, and I expect it to hold up over 17 games — this defense finishes top three in the league in sacks. The Buffalo Bills win the Super Bowl Let’s be fair about what actually happened over the last six years. Sean McDermott built a genuinely winning culture in Buffalo, and that part of his legacy is real. But it’s also fair to point out that his defenses collapsed at the worst possible moments, over and over. Six straight playoff losses since 2020 for a combined 199 points allowed — the most in the NFL over that stretch. Four blown fourth-quarter leads in five of those eliminations. Zero sacks and one takeaway in the loss to Denver that got him fired. That’s not all bad luck or bad calls. That’s a pattern. Speaking of bad calls, though — they were real too. The fourth-and-1 spot in the 2025 AFC Championship Game, with Buffalo up 22-21 and 13 minutes left, went against Allen on a quarterback sneak that plenty of people, including cameras from multiple angles, thought he got. Kansas City scored a touchdown on the ensuing drive and won by three. That’s not the only time a Bills season has ended on a coin flip of a spot or a measurement. Sure, Josh Allen had plays he wanted back, which quarterback, EVER, doesn’t? However, his playoff résumé already speaks for itself: a 101.5 passer rating, 3,915 yards, 29 touchdowns, and only six interceptions across 15 career playoff games. He has nine rushing touchdowns in the postseason, second all-time behind only Jalen Hurts. He’s made the playoffs every year of his career except his rookie season, and he’s one win away from tying Tom Brady’s record of eight straight seasons with at least one playoff victory. Allen has done more than enough to get this team to a Super Bowl. What he hasn’t had is a defense that matches his level in December and January, or the racing luck to go with it. That’s what’s different now. Buffalo kept the locker room culture and the professionalism that McDermott built, while removing the parts that kept costing them in January. Joe Brady gives the offense continuity instead of a teardown. Leonhard gives the defense an identity that should hold up under pressure instead of folding. Add a fairer bounce or two along the way, and I think this team finally has everything around Allen that it’s been missing. Get the Bills to the Super Bowl, and I don’t…

title: Buffalo Bills Record Book: What could change vs. Texans in Week 1
summary: A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books. And Week 1 is as good a place as any to get started. So, sharpen your pencils, find your erasers, and let’s get ready to mark up the books.  Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 21: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates a touchdown over the Cleveland Browns in the the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on December 21, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books. And Week 1 is as good a place as any to get started. So, sharpen your pencils, find your erasers, and let’s get ready to mark up the books. Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we will have an entry in every chapter. Other weeks, we may be more selective. Either way, we’ll know which numbers to watch as this version of the Buffalo Bills writes its story. _____________________________________________________________________________ WEEK 1 – September 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things We have just one entry here • Josh Allen’s consecutive-start streak: Allen has started 122 straight regular-season games. When he takes the field Sunday, he will have 123. I know, I impressed you with my math skills there. But here’s why that number matters. Allen already owns the league’s longest streak among active starting quarterbacks. Joe Flacco, who is now serving as Joe Burrow’s understudy, has 122 straight regular season starts (a streak that ended in 2015 due to a knee injury). Number 123 will move Allen into sole possession of eighth place among NFL quarterbacks. Ever. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet Nothing here this week. It’s too early in the season for me to call something a good bet, watch your parlay fall apart, and find myself at the center of a Bills Mafia witch hunt by Sunday night. We’ll fill this chapter when the numbers earn it. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible • Dawson Knox receptions: Knox needs just three catches to go from 229 to 232 (again, I’m good at math). That higher number would move him past wide receiver Cole Beasley on the Bills’ all-time receptions list and slide the tight end into 15th place Sunday. • Dawson Knox touchdown catches: Our next entry is Knox again. Should Allen find him in the end zone Sunday, the Buffalo tight end would tie fan-favorite former wide receiver Stevie Johnson with 28 touchdown catches. If he were to snag a second touchdown catch, his 29th, he would find himself tied with Jerry Butler at seventh all-time on the Bills’ list of touchdown catches. But that’s not so serious. • Khalil Shakir receptions: Next up is the human pinball wizard himself: Khalil Shakir. The Bills wide receiver has bounced, bopped, and weaved his way down the football field for four years, so, obviously, we should expect to find his name scattered throughout the record book. This entry could move him into 17th place in franchise history. Shakir enters the season with 197 catches. Eight more—that’s 205 for those of you keeping up with my math skills—and he would pass Robert Woods and Jay Riemersma. • Josh Allen’s dual-threat record: Allen’s entry comes with a wink because the record is already his. He’s just trying to put it out of reach for every other human. It’s his dual-threat record. The Buffalo quarterback has scored both a passing and a rushing touchdown in the same game 50 times, the most in NFL history. Week after week, he’ll have another chance to add to that number. Or so we hope. • Joe Brady’s Bills debut: We’re putting this one under Not Impossible because calling it anything stronger feels like a good way to upset the football gods. With a win in his regular-season debut, Joe Brady would become the fourth head coach in franchise history to win his first game with the Bills. He would join Marv Levy, Rex Ryan, and Sean McDermott. • Josh Allen keeps chasing running backs: Two rushing touchdowns would bring Allen’s career total to 81 and move him into a tie with Frank Gore and Ottis Anderson for 20th on the NFL’s all-time list. Which is, obviously, a completely normal place to find a quarterback. • Bradley Chubb’s road to 50: Chubb arrives in Buffalo with 48 career sacks. Two against Houston would get the new Bills captain to 50—and give him a pretty memorable way to introduce himself in his first regular-season game wearing red, white, and blue. • Josh Allen on opening day: Allen again. Get used to it. With 300 passing yards Sunday, he would record his third 300-yard season opener and tie Jim Kelly for the most in Bills history. He would also become the first Buffalo quarterback to throw for at least 300 yards in consecutive season-opening games. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman • James Cook rushing yards: James Cook opens the season sixth on the Bills’ all-time rushing list with 4,259 yards. He would need 187 against Houston to pass Joe Cribbs’ 4,445 and break into the top five. That earns Cook a spot in our Superhuman chapter. Except he ran for 216 yards in a game last season, so, apparently, superhuman is something James Cook has already done. _____________________________________________________________________________ For now, all of these numbers stay in pencil. Sunday will tell us which ones earn ink in the Buffalo Record Book, which ones move to a different chapter, and which ones stay right where they are. Then, when we reopen the book next week, we’ll do the math. Again.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 1 Day Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - SEPTEMBER 23: Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton (1) does his signature superman move after scoring a rushing touchdown during the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Carolina Panthers on September 23 2018, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte,NC. (Photo by Dannie Walls/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #1. Cam Newton How fitting that the player that comes in at number one on our countdown also wore the number one on his jersey. Serendipity. It’s Super Man himself, Cam Newton. The Panthers and their fans endured a season of Jimmy Clausen to earn the number one pick in the 2011 NFL Draft. The team was almost guaranteed to take a quarterback, and the debate was between dual threat Cam Newton out of Auburn and the more traditional passer Blaine Gabbert out of Missouri. The Panthers elected to take a shot on Newton, and it couldn’t have worked out better. There were all sorts of questions about Newton’s ability to actually throw the football when he entered the league, and the fact that he got very little runway into his rookie season because of the lockout only added to those concerns. He made his debut against the Arizona Cardinals, who clearly believed he couldn’t beat them with his arm, and lit them up for 422 passing yards and two touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown on what would become his trademark super man dive over the pile on the goal line. He finished that season as the first rookie to ever throw for 4,000 yards, and he simultaneously set the record for rushing touchdowns by a quarterback with 14. Newton continued to redefine the quarterback position throughout his time in Carolina. He paired high difficulty passing productivity with elite rushing efficiency and was one of the best short yardage ball carriers in the league regardless of position. His ascent continued into 2015, where he turned in arguably the greatest season any Panther has put together. He led the team to 15-1 record with the only loss coming just a few days after Newton welcomed his first child into the world. In that season, Newton threw for 3,837 yards and 35 touchdowns against 10 interceptions while adding 636 yards and 10 more touchdowns on the ground. He led a league best four fourth quarter game winning drives. All of that unsurprisingly earned him MVP and Offensive Player of the Year honors. He is the only Panthers in the team’s history to win either award. And all of that happened with Ted Ginn as his number one wide receiver. The Panthers and Newton saw a major regression in 2016 after losing the Super Bowl. Newton missed a game with a concussion and was benched for the start of another because he didn’t wear a tie on the team flight . Derek Anderson started that game, threw an interception on the first play, and the Panthers went on to lose 40-7. The following week, Newton injured his throwing shoulder trying to make a tackle on an interception after wide receiver Kelvin Benjamin made a poor effort to catch the ball and then no effort to tackle the defender . That injury would dramatically impact Newton’s ability to generate velocity on his passes for the rest of his career. Despite his diminishing arm strength, Newton bounced back to lead another hodgepodge offense to an 11-5 record and playoff appearance in 2017, but that season ended with a playoff loss to the Saints. After a strong first half of 2018, Newton took a shot to the shoulder from TJ Watt during a game against the Steelers. His play would rapidly deteriorate from that point through the end of the season before he was deactivated for the final two games to get shoulder surgery. He played just two games in 2019 before a foot injury ended his season. After a year in New England, Newton made a triumphant return to Carolina midway through the 2021 season. He came in for special packages in a game against the Cardinals and was responsible for two touchdowns as the struggling Panthers pulled off a shocking blowout win over the then 8-1 Arizona Cardinals. Newton got more playing time as the season went on, but he was clearly not the player he once was. The Panthers limped to a 5-12 record after losing 12 of their last 14 games. Newton’s contract expired after that season, and he wouldn’t play another down in the NFL. Newton’s career was very enigmatic in a way. On one hand, he redefined the quarterback position and reinforced how much of a weapon the quarterback can be as a runner while still being a threat as a passer. His impact and talent were undeniable. On the other hand, his consistency and counting stats as a passer could fluctuate, though there was a lot of context around that as well. The bulk of Newton’s playing career came with Mike Shula as his offensive coordinator. Shula never received any head coaching interest despite the success of his Newton-led offenses, and he never led successful offenses that didn’t have Cam Newton at quarterback. At the same time, Newton’s best wide receivers were an aging Steve Smith, a rookie DJ Moore, and Ted Ginn Jr. Newton was heavily reliant on Greg Olsen at tight end to be his true number one receiver for most of his career. He rarely if ever had a good supporting cast at the skill positions, and most of his career was marred by subpar offensive coaching. While Newton’s career will go down as far and away the best we’ve seen at quarterback in Carolina, there are still questions about what could have been if the team did more to support him during his prime. Instead, he seemed to carry the weight of the offense on his own while the rest of the organization either did little to help or actively hampered what he was capable of doing. Still, he rose to the level of Most Valuable Player and took the team to a Super Bowl. Cam Newton is the best quarterback the Panthers have ever had, and the best player they have ever had. For that, number one in your programs comes in at number one on our countdown of the top 100 Carolina Panthers of all time.

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 1
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries As the Panthers prepare to kick off the 2026 season, the team had a pretty light injury report as of the latest update from Thursday’s practice. Running back Jonathon Brooks has […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 09: Tyrel Dodson #25 of the Miami Dolphins enters the field prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Hard Rock Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries As the Panthers prepare to kick off the 2026 season, the team had a pretty light injury report as of the latest update from Thursday’s practice. Running back Jonathon Brooks has been limited, outside linebacker Patrick Jones II hasn’t practiced this week, and defensive tackle Bobby Brown III was a full participant yesterday. As far as the injured reserve list goes, there’s more damage there. Right tackle Taylor Moton will need to miss at least the first four games due to a blood clot in his lungs. Fellow offensive lineman Brady Christensen will also miss at least the first four games with a hamstring issue. Running back and return specialist Trevor Etienne is also out to begin the year but designated to return. Regarding season-ending injuries, second-year defensive end Nic Scourton will miss the year with an ACL injury. He was coming off a promising rookie season last year and was poised for a breakout campaign, so this one really hurts. Rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell will miss the entire season with a knee injury, putting a damper on the third-rounder’s first season. Transactions September is usually a fairly quiet period when it comes to transactions, and that’s the case this year with the Panthers. This month there have been a handful of moves impacting the practice squad, and here are the more noteworthy ones: Signed Tyrel Dodson to the practice squad Wow. While most practice squad signings are inconsequential, this one could be a big deal. Tyrel Dodson has appeared in 92 career games with 43 starts. He spent 2019 on the Buffalo Bills practice squad but didn’t appear in any games. Over the next two seasons he cracked the rotation and played a lot of special teams. In 2023 he had a breakout season starting 10 of 17 games with 74 tackles and 2.5 sacks. In 2024 he signed with the Seattle Seahawks and started all nine games in which he appeared with a team-leading 71 tackles and two sacks before getting released. One article called the release “ shocking and unforeseen .” Dodson quickly signed with the Miami Dolphins where he started three of eight games with 36 more tackles, giving him 107 on the season. He remained in Miami last year and started all 16 games in which he appeared with an impressive 129 tackles and five sacks. He returned to Miami this year but was released during final roster cuts after second round rookie Jacob Rodriguez from Texas Tech won the starting job. In summary, Tyrel Dodson is a 28-year-old middle linebacker with 310 tackles and 9.5 sacks over the last three seasons. He has no injury history. While he was suspended for six games during his 2019 rookie season for domestic violence, there are no recent red flags surrounding him. It’s quite shocking Dodson didn’t land on a 53-man roster somewhere, and it’s a luxury for the Panthers to have him on the practice squad. Signed guard Chandler Zavala to the practice squad Chandler Zavala was a Panthers fourth-round pick in 2023. Over the course of three seasons he has appeared in 34 games for Carolina with 14 starts, but his play has been shaky when given the opportunity. The Panthers waived him on August 31st as part of roster cutdowns, then signed him to the practice squad the following day. Signed outside linebacker Jeremiah Moon to the practice squad Jeremiah Moon will be a familiar name to some Panthers fans as he briefly orbited the franchise last year. He spent 2023 with the Baltimore Ravens and in eight games he produced 12 tackles with two forced fumbles. In 2024 he played for the Pittsburgh Steelers and over 13 games with nine tackles. Last year he signed with the Panthers practice squad, got elevated to the 53-man roster, and appeared in one game with no stats. But when Carolina moved him back to the practice squad, the Steelers swooped in and claimed him for their active roster, and he appeared in two games for them last year with two tackles. This seems like a smart move for the Panthers to bring back a 28-year-old vet with at least some familiarity with the franchise.

title: Panthers vs Bears: Round table predictions, odds, and falling skies
summary: The Carolina Panthers are set to have their first home opener since 2022. That was a 24-26 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Matt Rhule’s last (partial) season in Charlotte. A win on Sunday against the Chicago Bears would be their first win an opener, home or away, since their 2021 victory over the New […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 06: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers and Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears embrace after the game at Soldier Field on October 06, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are set to have their first home opener since 2022. That was a 24-26 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Matt Rhule’s last (partial) season in Charlotte. A win on Sunday against the Chicago Bears would be their first win an opener, home or away, since their 2021 victory over the New York Jets in 2021, the Sam Darnold year. If all of this makes you feel sad then congratulations. You understand what it is to be a Panthers fan since 2020. The Panthers most successful stretches of football since Ron Rivera and Cam Newton have left have been Weeks 3-5 of the 2020 season, Weeks 1-3 of the 2021 season, and Weeks 5-7 of the 2025 season. That is three 3-week winning streaks in six seasons. Why am I dwelling on this history now? While the odds are technically against the Panthers— the Bears are -3 road favorites per FanDuel —there is a fresh season afoot. This is technically and traditionally a time for optimism. Yet most Panthers fans I’ve interacted with are wary. Even for those of us who believe that this roster is largely improved over the 2024 and 2025 squads and in a different league, so to speak, from the 2023 disaster, there is a sense of “I’ll believe it when I see it.” That’s perfectly justified. It’s also important to acknowledge that just because we’ve seen everything go off the rails so many times in so many recent seasons that doesn’t mean a Week 1 loss, even a Week 1 blow out loss, means the end of this season. Yes, Lucy, this season could still be different. Trying to prevent over reactions to Week 1 is like trying to stop Chicken Little from fretting, but here were are. Look at how noble we are at the start of a season. Now, on to the predictions. Staff predictions for Week 1 Oh we of middling of faith. Our staff is split 3-3 on which team will win this week. Even our score predictions average out to a scant Panthers win, 23 to 22 over the Bears. Coincidentally, that score has occurred 16 times in NFL history per nflscorigami.com and Pro Football Reference . The Carolina Panthers won one of those games in 2024 against the New Orleans Saints. Walker Clement Panthers 24, Bears 17 – The Panthers manage three difficult scoring drives on offense, but the difference comes when Devin Lloyd picks off a Caleb Williams pass intended for Colston Loveland or Cole Kmet in a fourth quarter attempt to ice the game for the Bears. Jonathan DeLong Bears 16, Panthers 10 – Both teams are rusty after playing over their heads at times last season, and Bryce Young’s Week 1 struggles continue. Brian Beversluis Bears 35, Panthers 31 – It will be a wild duel between the two quarterbacks, but ultimately the Bears pull it out. Daniel Belton Panthers 27, Bears 10 – Bryce Young out gains Caleb Williams by 200 yards and leads the Panthers to a two score victory, permanently ending the “who won the trade” conversation Andrew Sweat Bears 27, Panthers 17 – Both teams have questions on defense, but on offense the Bears have much more honey in the pot than the Panthers do. Eric Buchanon Panthers 31, Bears 27 – A messy first half turns into a second half shootout where 4th quarter chunk plays to Jimmy Horn and Jalen Coker prove the difference in an upset victory.

title: Brian Answers: Bears/Panthers, Bryce Young, Brad Idzik, Fall happenings and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re only days away from the first regular season game, so only one set of questions away from having some clarity, and likely changing the focus of this column going forward depending on how it all goes. Let’s dive […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Jonathon Brooks #25 of the Carolina Panthers scores a touchdown on a run against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re only days away from the first regular season game, so only one set of questions away from having some clarity, and likely changing the focus of this column going forward depending on how it all goes. Let’s dive right into all your questions! PurrDurham: Will we see panthers or kitties vs. Bears? Which team is likely to show up for us? I think the Panthers will show up for this game. But all I have to base that on is vibes. Chef: Hey, Brian. So, I haven’t really seen much concerning the potential Waller impact on the passing game outside of his expected red zone targets. Is it foolish to expect him to be more than that in our passing attack or do you think people are sleeping on him? I don’t think Darren Waller would have been available as late as he was in the off-season if any team could reasonably expect him to be more than a complimentary passing target. I do think his addition reveals that the Panthers want to use more 13 personnel (3 TEs) and I also think he’ll be a decent move the chains option for Bryce Young. But I would temper expectations, he may not even be the leading receiver of the Panthers offense when its all said and done. But the more red zone targets, the better in my opinion. ImOpen: I believe that barring injury, Bryce starts every game….which could lead to them drafting a QB I believe we are one more offseason away from being a very good team….able to drop a QB into a good situation I am going to throw in an upset win and say our win total is 8-10…ehhhh 7-9…ish….kinda. What do you think of those statements? The question of the future of the quarterback position and Bryce Young will likely have a clearer answer following this season. I do tend to agree they may be one more solid off-season away from truly being a team that could compete for a deep run in the playoffs, but stranger things have happened. I have them at 9-8 as their overall record still but a deviation two games in either direction wins wise wouldn’t surprise me at all. If they decide Bryce isn’t the answer in the off-season, they should at least have a pretty good situation for the next guy. But I do hope we don’t have to deal with another reset at the QB position. schrodingersblackcat: I think some variation of this may have come up in this feature before, but what are some of your favorite Fall traditions, football related or otherwise? Food/Drink? Outdoor activities? Movies/shows? Social gatherings? Halloween-related stuff? Other? Maybe I’m jumping the gun here, but now that football is finally back, Oktoberfest beers are on store shelves, and we’ve had a couple cooler days to tease us, I am 100% ready for Fall. I’m definitely a fan of a good Oktoberfest beer. Some good whiskey and a cigar on a nice cool Fall night is also great. And I very much look forward to Thanksgiving dinner (sometimes for me, Friendsgiving on a different weekend). Big bonfire guy. Sitting outside in cool PA weather is great. Halloween films absolutely. Anything horror I’m always down for but October is the greatest time for it. Getting people together for some Rock Band is a year round event, but more common during the Fall. Super Smash Bros also tends to run itself back during this time for social gatherings. Oh yeah, and I’m starting my second or third full Dungeons & Dragons campaign following Panthers games most weekends. Lots of Halloween get togethers. I used to be more into dressing up for Halloween so that may be in the cards this year. Might have to bust out my Tommy Wiseau costume once again. Bruce Guild: What do you see for Cokers future Brian? Do you ever see a Pro Bowl or a year he ends up the top receiver by catch count, receiving yards or TD’s? Do you see him being a 6 to 10 year player for the team, or a guy that had the potential but ended up being very mid or oft injured and is out in 3 years? I am very much on the Jalen Coker train, but I need to see a full season of work from him to make a determination. Its very telling that the Panthers already gave him a 3 year extension, and I think he compliments Tetairoa McMillan well. Not seeing Pro Bowl or top of the league receiving stats in his future just yet, but that could change this season. @WTMealey: If we win the toss defer or take the ball? 1st down of 1st drive run or pass? Obviously I’d like to know the thinking behind your answers as well I’d expect the Panthers to defer on the first possession, give the defense a chance to come out swinging early. I think they’ll run the ball on the first play, but that’s not a solid answer from me because I don’t know what to expect from Brad Idzik just yet. WanderingJanusz: I’m surprising my dad for Christmas and taking him to our week 18 home game against Atlanta. Will this end up being a great gift or depressing gift? Well, Bryce Young always tends to go off against Atlanta, so my instinct here is should be a great gift. The Falcons also may not have a quarterback left standing by then based on their luck with injury there throughout the off-season. Even if the Panthers are mathematically eliminated from the playoffs, the Falcons games are always chaotic and unexpected. positivebob: Idzik. What’s the biggest difference we’ll see between him and DC? Again, very hard to say what the difference will be between Brad Idzik and Dave Canales calling plays, as it will all fall in the same system. I think Idzik may open up the passing game more than Canales was willing to, but that’s all based on conjecture and just general instinct. The Panthers may also be in more games where they have to open the passing game based on their 1st place schedule. Mozzie11: Play action pass on 1st down is the best play to make statistically. So do we get bold and run a pass play on the 1st offensive play of the game – and I do not mean a screen for -2 yd or go semi bold with a run up the middle for a yard and a half. Decisions, decisions…. While I said above I think a rushing play starts it out, I wouldn’t be surprised if the opening drive game script is designed to get Bryce Young into more of a groove early rather than having him rip is first pass on a 3rd down situation. I am hopeful they go this direction rather than the usual run first attempt. Bull123: Is Pat Jones hurt yet again? What are we gonna get from Chuba and Brooks? Pat Jones is not expected to play this Sunday, though this seems to be more of a day-to-day injury rather than anything long term. It sucks to not have him the first week of the season, but Ejiro Evero seems to have a plan. He talked up Princely Umanmielen quite a bit this week. I actually expect them to run the same time share they did with Chuba Hubbard and Rico Dowdle this past season, but I think it will work out better this time. These two have more of a complimentary skill set rather than running similar styles. Jonathon Brooks adds a different element as a pass catcher. That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Enjoy your first game of the season, and KEEP POUNDING!

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 2 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: Dec. 8, 2008; Charlotte, NC, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive end Julius Peppers (90) reacts in the Panthers 38-23 victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #2. Julius Peppers It is the penultimate entry in our list of top 100 Panthers of all time. We’ve hit lots of fan favorites and players that were good to great. Now we’ve reached the best of the best. The best player to ever suit up on the defensive side of the ball for the Panthers comes in at number two on our list, defensive end Julius Peppers. Peppers is a Carolina kid through and through. He grew up in Bailey, North Carolina, about 30 miles east of Raleigh. He didn’t play football growing up, but his sheer size and athleticism caught the eye of the coaching staff of his high school, and he quickly turned into one of the most dominant players in the state on both sides of the ball. He received a scholarship to play football at UNC and also walked on to the basketball team. He was a reserve forward for the basketball team while we was assembling an elite resume as a defensive end for the Tar Heel football team. He was considered a generational talent entering the 2002 NFL Draft. The Panthers had the number two pick in that draft with the first overall pick going to the expansion Houston Texans. Fortunately, the Texans elected to take David Carr with the first overall pick to be their franchise quarterback. That meant Peppers was sitting right there for the Panthers at the second pick. Peppers delivered on the hype. He registered 12 sacks, five force fumbles, and an interception en route to Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2002. He added a modest seven sacks in his sophomore season before fully breaking out as an elite defensive end. He earned his first of six All Pro nominations in his third season with 11 sacks and two interceptions, including a 97 yard pick six. He would spend five more seasons in Carolina after that, accumulating double digit sacks in all but one season in which he was uncharacteristically ineffective. The Panthers elected to let Peppers test free agency after the 2009 season, and Peppers opted to leave to sign with the Chicago Bears. He spent four seasons there before hopping over to the division rival Packers. He spent three years before making a return to his home state. He tallied 11 sacks in his first season back in Carolina despite being 37 years old. He added five more sacks in his age 38 season before announcing his retirement at the end of it. Peppers finished his career with 159.5 sacks, fourth most in NFL history (0.5 sacks behind Kevin Greene for third). 97 of those came with the Panthers, 29.5 more than any other player to wear the black and blue. He scored six defensive touchdowns and blocked 13 kicks, showing just how much of a menace he was in every facet of the game. The two seasons that Peppers spent in Carolina to end his career did a lot to improve his standing with the fan base. During his first stint, there was a perception among parts of the fan base that he wasn’t always giving full effort despite his dominance, and his even keeled persona was often misconstrued as apathy. Those frustrations further boiled over when Peppers refused to re-sign with the team and ultimately left in free agency. Some time apart allowed for a storybook ending, with Peppers returning home to become a fan favorite to end his career and ultimately ending up in the team’s Hall of Honor. Peppers was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2024 and became the first player to spend the majority of his career in Carolina to earn that honor. The end of his career quashed any beef between he and the fan base, leaving him as the inarguable best defensive player to play for the Panthers. For that, he comes in at number two on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Chicago Bears vs Carolina Panthers Preview: Bears need to slow Chuba Hubbard
summary: On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll previews the Week 1 matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Carolina Panthers with two individuals who know these teams inside and out. First, she gets the skinny on Carolina by chatting with Alex Zietlow, who covers the Panthers for the Charlotte Observer. They break down the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 06: T.J. Edwards #53 of the Chicago Bears tackles Chuba Hubbard #30 of the Carolina Panthers in the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 06, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll previews the Week 1 matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Carolina Panthers with two individuals who know these teams inside and out. First, she gets the skinny on Carolina by chatting with Alex Zietlow, who covers the Panthers for the Charlotte Observer. They break down the Panthers’ side of the ball, including the 2026 expectations for Bryce Young and how important the running game will be. Alex also shares thoughts on Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. Next up, she brings on our own Jeff Berkes to cover what Chicago will look to do and how the Bears can bring home a victory. But back to Carolina… Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks (2024 second-round pick) is completely off the injury list, and most assume he’s in line to be RB1, but Alex disagrees. “The general fantasy football fan is like, ‘Well, Jonathon Brooks is like five running backs above Chuba Hubbard in the ESPN fantasy football drafts,’ whatever the case may be, and I’m trying to tell the world Chuba Hubbard is running back one,” Zietlow said. “Chuba Hubbard is a captain of this team. Like, he is probably the most important voice in that locker room outside of Bryce Young and maybe Derrick Brown on the defensive side. He is really important. In 2024, he had a 1000-yard season, and he didn’t even play every game due to injury. So, like, this guy’s really good.” Hubbard and Brooks give Carolina a potent backfield, and in the 90-degree heat, they could be a factor against the Bears’ run defense. title: NFL Week 1 Bears-Panthers Predictions: Which run defense will step up?
summary: The Carolina Panthers have not won a Week 1 game since 2021, but they are coming off a playoff season in 2025. Could they beat the Chicago Bears outright at home or at least cover the spread? Much has been made of the trade that brought Caleb Williams to Chicago and Bryce Young to Carolina. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 06: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears runs the ball against the Carolina Panthers during the second quarter at Soldier Field on October 06, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have not won a Week 1 game since 2021, but they are coming off a playoff season in 2025. Could they beat the Chicago Bears outright at home or at least cover the spread? Much has been made of the trade that brought Caleb Williams to Chicago and Bryce Young to Carolina. Since the two QBs have taken over for their respective squads, the Bears have gone 16-18 (11-6 under Ben Johnson), and the Panthers have gone 15-36. Both teams are coming off strong seasons with playoff appearances led by their run games, and both teams made substantial acquisitions this offseason, especially on defense. Chicago signed S Coby Bryant and LB Devin Bush while Carolina added LB Devin Lloyd and Edge Jaelan Phillips. Obviously, Chicago fans know Bryant will miss most of the year with an injury, but the question remains for both teams. Can they slow down their opponent’s offense this week? For a Chicago defense that allowed the 6th most rushing yards a season ago, the Panthers know they have to establish the run and build off their 2025 season, when they ranked in the top 20 in both rushing yards and attempts per game. Chicago will be leaning heavily on a couple rookies, Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving, and 9th-year pro Kentavius Street, whom Bears DC Dennis Allen said had the strongest camp of any DT on the roster . For the Panthers, the addition of Lloyd and Phillips will most certainly help, but the Panthers defense still relies on the play of All-World DT Derrick Brown to slow down opposing offenses. Especially the run game. That said, the edge for best DL seems to go to Carolina in this one. However, in his first 3 career Week 1 starts, Bryce Young has thrown a combined 2 TDs and 6 INTs and has yet to throw for more than 200 yards. Which leads even more credence to the idea that the Panthers should “ Keep Pounding ” the ball on the ground this week. Our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Bears as 3-point favorites for this week’s contest in Carolina. If you think the Bears will win outright, the moneyline is at -176, with the point total over/under at 47.5. I am predicting a 31-20 Bears win, with both D’Andre Swift and Chuba Hubbard to lead their teams with over 70 yards rushing each – and that’ll hit the over on their betting lines in this one, with Swift currently at 63.5 and Hubbard at 50.5.

title: Bears-Panthers: Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: The Chicago Bears start their 2026 campaign with a trip to Charlotte to take on the Carolina Panthers. Both teams saw surprise playoff berths last season, which included division crowns. Now, the teams face the difficult follow-up act. Regression, one-season wonder, or lucky- these labels are going to stick with them until they can prove […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 6: Running back D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers, at Soldier Field on October 6, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears start their 2026 campaign with a trip to Charlotte to take on the Carolina Panthers. Both teams saw surprise playoff berths last season, which included division crowns. Now, the teams face the difficult follow-up act. Regression, one-season wonder, or lucky- these labels are going to stick with them until they can prove otherwise. What’s it going to take for the Chicago Bears to come home victorious on Sunday? We asked our staff. Sam: It’s a battle of the trenches for me. We know Ben Johnson wants to establish his ground game. The Bears should have a slight edge here. The Panthers already have several key injuries along their offensive line. The Bears’ defensive line will have their hands full, but outside of the shaky left tackle situation, the Bears are established up front. Pound the rock, get pressure on Bryce Young and grind out a win. ECD: Offense: Get into a rhythm early and take that next step in the passing game. It’s going to be super hot and humid while playing against a team that has been coached to take advantage of mistakes. Once a good 2-score lead is built, let the ground game grind their defense to dust. Defense: Do something to put pressure on Bryce Young. A good chunk of their running game may be out of action due to injuries, and their offensive line doesn’t strike fear. This might be their easiest matchup up front for a good while. Special Teams: Use all that speed between to your advantage Kalif Raymond and Zavion Thomas to your advantage. I feel both players are capable of generating explosive returns against a rather soft bunch coverage-wise. Lester: The NFL season is a marathon, so the Bears should lean on the running game in Week 1 to establish their identity. Ground and pound while rotating in the skill players all afternoon to keep everyone fresh in what could he a hot day in Carolina. On defense, the pass rush might be a work in progress, but get those hands up to hamper 5’10” Bryce Young. Josh: The offense just needs to pick up where it left off. A balance of hard running and explosives from Caleb should be enough to rock the Carolina defense. What needs to happen on defense, though, is more important. They have to find a way to force Young off-schedule. That means somehow stifling the run and forcing the Panthers to rely on their quarterback. If they can shut down the easy stuff, they should be able to carry the day. Gary: Offense needs to continue its upward trajectory we saw on the tail end of 2025, Panthers have a revamped defense and should be much better then their bottom 1/3rd finish in 2025. Luckily, we have one of the best offensive minds in the business at HC and a QB hungry to continue his upward trajectory. I think, like most, I’m not sold on the defense until I see it, but if I’m being blunt, Bryce Young is one of the few QBs in the league I don’t necessarily fear. That said he is capable of dropping points and had his Panthers in a dogfight with the Rams in the Wild Card. May need a couple turnovers to help, but I expect a 2-score win. DGooch: Offense: no turnovers, establish the run game, spam the play-action pass to limit the effectiveness of the Panthers’ rush and protect Braxton Jones. I fully expect Ben will have a couple of wow trick plays to flip the field. On defense: STOP THE RUN. That is the key to the entire defense. Stopping the run yields longer down-and-distances where the rush will have a chance to get there. On the back end, the defense needs to gel. So many new faces at both levels and injuries have kept the Bears’ secondary from being on the field much with their starters in camp or in the preseason games. As will be true all year, the defense’s job is not to lose the game. Caleb and the offense will go win it. What are your keys for a Bears victory?

title: 2026 NFL QB Rankings
summary: We are bringing back the QB rankings for the 2nd straight season. These will look pretty close to the final rankings from last season because, of course, there hasn’t been any football played since the end of last season. One important note: even though there are four QBs that have played games so far in […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs kisses his daughter, Sterling Mahomes, prior to the preseason game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are bringing back the QB rankings for the 2nd straight season. These will look pretty close to the final rankings from last season because, of course, there hasn’t been any football played since the end of last season. One important note: even though there are four QBs that have played games so far in 2026, their performances are not taken into account in these rankings. We will update these rankings at the 25%, 50%, 75%, and, of course, end-of-season junctures of the season. Just a reminder as to how we came to these numbers. Their history comes into play. Yes, their current play is heavily weighted (otherwise Aaron Rodgers would be a lot higher), but their past plays into it. Josh Allen played better than Patrick Mahomes in 2025, but Mahomes’ history still gives him the top spot on the list. Without further ado, here are the 2026 preseason NFL QB Rankings. 1. Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs The king still has the top spot, but he’s clinging to it at this point. If Allen starts off hot and Mahomes is slow to recover from his ACL injury, there’s a good chance that Allen grabs the top spot when we update this list after 4 games. 2. Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills He has the gaudy numbers. He has the highlight plays. He has an MVP. He needs some playoff success, including a Super Bowl championship, if he wants to start being discussed as an all-time great. 3. Matthew Stafford, LA Rams Coming to the Rams has been great for Stafford’s career image. No, Dan Orlovsky, if the Rams win a Super Bowl this year, Stafford will not be a top 5 QB, but he will definitely be top 20, and possibly top 15. 4. Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens Jackson is poised to have a big bounce-back year with Declan Doyle. His relationship with John Harbaugh always seemed strained, and some fresh coaching faces should do him good. 5. Joe Burrow, Cincinnati Bengals Burrow needs to start playing more games. He averages missing almost 4 games per season. If he played more games, he could be as high as two on this list. 6. Justin Herbert, LA Chargers Herbert really needs some postseason success to have his image start to change. Right now, he’s a regular season warrior and a postseason dud. 7. Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys See Justin Herbert. The only difference is Herbert gets the ball more often than Dak. A lot of experts think the Cowboys will be back in the playoffs this year, and if they are right, Dak can really change his image. 8. Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks It is really hard for me to accept Sam Darnold as a top-10 QB. Most of the offseason rankings didn’t have him up there, but he won the Super Bowl, played well in the postseason, and has had two excellent regular seasons in a row. You have to give the man some respect. 9. Drake Maye, New England Patriots Maye peaked as high as 6 on the list last year, but his playoff performance has to ding him a little. He was certainly a bum slayer off that weak schedule, but tougher opponents made him look a lot more pedestrian (and no, the performance on the season opener was not considered into this yet). 10. Jared Goff, Detroit Lions To me, right now 7 QBs are the best in the league, and there is going to be a lot of variance between 8 and 15 or so. Goff is still holding this spot, but it’ll be interesting to see how he plays this year with a weaker offensive line. 11. Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears I really wanted to slide him into the top 10, but I can’t do it yet. If he plays well out of the gate this year, he will firmly plant his flag as a top-10 QB in the league. 12. Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia Eagles This is a big year for Jalen Hurts. He needs to play well without AJ Brown and with a new OC; he needs to attack the middle of the field and show that he’s still a field General. 13. Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers Love is a good quarterback. Some people want to put him a notch above that, and I don’t think the numbers and performances back that up. 14. Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars Lawrence has had a really bumpy start to his career but looked much better under Liam Coen. If he can have another strong season, he should be able to climb this list a little. 15. Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers Purdy just gets the job done. If he was drafted in the 2nd round instead of the 7th round, people would probably speak better of him. But as a 7th-round pick, he can’t possibly be that good, right? (Wrong) 16. Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers Baker earned himself another extension in Tampa after a solid season. But Mayfield definitely faded towards the end of the year last year, and he needs to play more like he did the first half of the season if the Bucs are going to win a very winnable division this year. 17. Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders Daniels was probably considered a top-10 QB after his rookie season, but an injury-plagued season with some mediocre performances bumped him down several notches. He needs to stay much healthier and look more like the QB from 2024 to climb back up the list. 18. Bo Nix, Denver Broncos If Broncos fans find this list, they won’t be happy. But Nix needs to show a little more to start pushing towards the top 10. I think his game is limited. 19. CJ Stroud, Houston Texans The Texans have a phenomenal defense and a handful of weapons on offense. Stroud is basically out of excuses. He needs to put that playoff performance behind him and start playing better, or he won’t be on the Texans much longer. 20. Jaxson Dart, NY Giants A new coach that Dart might listen to will hopefully help with his reckless play. He has definitely shown flashes, but he needs his play to even out and be more consistent and make better decisions with the football in his hands and not just lower his head. 21. Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts Jones was having a career year before the injury. Can he do it again this year? I have my doubts, but he has much of the same support and coaching staff around him. 22. Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers Young has improved from where he was a couple of years ago, but he still isn’t playing nearly well enough to get a contract extension. The Panthers punted that decision for at least a year by picking up the 5th-year option, but it’s possible they may not even make that decision for another two years and utilize the franchise tag if they must. 23. Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints Looked the part when he came in late in the year. If that continues this year, the Saints could win the division. If he regresses a little, they won’t manage to surprise many teams. 24. Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers Out of respect for his career, I bumped him back up a few more spots. Rodgers’ playoff performance was dreadful, and he certainly ran out of steam at the end of the year. Hard to figure out at his age whether he can improve at this point. 25. Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans Ward definitely showed improvement during the second half of the season last year, but there are still plenty of questions about Ward and if he can run an offense. It should make for an interesting year with Brian Daboll. 26. Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins Willis has looked outstanding as the Packers QB2 the last couple of years, and that has given him an opportunity to start this year in Miami. This will be his chance to prove he’s more than a backup QB. 27. Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings Murray fell out of good graces in Arizona and lost his job to Jacoby Brissett, but he has a fresh start in Minneapolis with plenty of elite players around him, including Justin Jefferson. If Murray fails here, his career will tank, but this will be a great opportunity with KOC to bounce back. 28. Mac Jones, San Francisco…

(Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The prop plays are back, and hopefully, if you’re a regular reader of this article, you have been placing wagers with me and winning some money. We have hit 68% of our prop bets over the last two seasons (69-33). I am not making that number up; it’s accurate, and believe me, I’m as stunned as you are. Can we keep hitting at roughly a 2-1 weekly clip? Let’s see how we do this week as we kick off the 2026 campaign. Here are 3 props to play (odds and numbers courtesy of FanDuel). Caleb Williams OVER 226.5 Passing Yards -114 Ben Johnson’s goal is to set the scoring record. Peter Schrager thinks Caleb Williams is going to throw for 5,000 yards. I think Caleb (and Ben) also want to leave no doubt with Carolina Panthers fans that the mistake the Panthers made trading away the first-round pick that became Caleb Williams (and so much more) for Bryce Young was a massive mistake. I mean, they already know it, but they will really want them to know it. You keep all that in mind, and in week one, against a defense that is definitely beatable, the Bears aren’t going to try to light up the scoreboard? I think the Bears feature a passing attack that looks clean and crisp, like it did much of the summer, and Williams has no problems clearing this bar and probably pushes past 250, maybe even 260 or 270 yards on Sunday. D’Andre Swift OVER 63.5 Rushing Yards -114 Usually, I stand by the rule of not betting over a QB’s passing yards and over a running back’s rushing yards. It feels like it’s a tall order to go over both, but I do think the Bears offense hums, and we are looking at 64 yards rushing, not 94. Kyle Monangai’s prop is 31.5, and I would leave that one alone. I feel like Swift gets the heavier workload this week, maybe grabbing 75% of the touches out of the backfield. I think the Bears’ excellent guard tandem does a solid job on Derrick Brown, and because of that, they get the ground game going. Swift is out to prove that last season wasn’t a fluke and that he’s arrived as one of the better backs in the league. Colston Loveland OVER 52.5 Receiving Yards -114 This is the only receiving prop I feel good about. Rome Odunze feels like he could have 75 yards or 25 yards. I feel like Luther Burden will go over his 57.5 number, but not nearly confident enough to put money on it. The Bears are going to live in 12 and 13 personnel, and I think Loveland emerges this year as the team’s most targeted weapon. Burden may end up with more yards than Loveland because I think he will have a better yards-per-catch number than Loveland, but I think Loveland ends up with a lot of targets. The Carolina Panthers really struggled against tight ends last year. Yes, they’ve brought in some new faces, but facing off against possibly the best tight end room in the league is a tough place to start to see if you’ve improved.

title: Bears extend D’Andre Swift to three-year, $33.75 million deal
summary: The Bears have extended running back D’Andre Swift to a three-year deal worth $33.75 million with $27.5 million guaranteed. ESPN’s Adam Schefter first reported the news on Friday. With a yearly annual salary of slightly over $11.2 million per year over the course of the deal, Swift will become the No. 14 running back by […]
full_text: The Bears have extended running back D’Andre Swift to a three-year deal worth $33.75 million with $27.5 million guaranteed. ESPN’s Adam Schefter first reported the news on Friday. With a yearly annual salary of slightly over $11.2 million per year over the course of the deal, Swift will become the No. 14 running back by AAV once his new contract kicks in. His current three-year contract was set to expire at the end of the 2026 season, so this new contract locks him down with Chicago through the end of the 2029 campaign. Swift, 27, is coming off his second season with over 1,000 rushing yards in his career. His total of 1,087 rushing yards is the highest he’s had in a single season thus far, and his yards per carry in 2025 jumped to a 4.9 average after a measly 3.8 average with Chicago in 2024. Though he was brought in while Shane Waldron was still the Bears’ offensive coordinator, Swift’s fit in Ben Johnson’s system is obvious. The two overlapped briefly in Detroit with solid results, and Swift put together an impressive campaign under Johnson in 2025. Johnson’s run scheme, which relies heavily on outside-zone runs to stretch out opposing defenses, plays right into the strengths of Swift, who can use his athleticism to either beat defenders to the edge or to bounce inside and cut with ideal explosiveness and decisiveness. From an analytical perspective, Swift is coming off a career year. In addition to reaching his career high in rushing yards, he also ended 2025 with a career-high 79.7 PFN RB Impact Score , ranking No. 10 in the NFL. His 15.4 rushing EPA ranked third among all NFL running backs, which speaks to how efficient the Bears’ offense was when they handed him the ball. He also ranked third among running backs in both boom/bust rate and elusive rate in 2025. Judging by the guarantees, the Bears will likely have a reasonable out in Swift’s contract after the 2028 season. He’ll be 31 years old by the time his new deal comes off the books, so if the dreaded regression after 30 years old hits him, Chicago will have the chance to free his contract up. That said, he was a tremendous performer for the Bears in 2025, and this new contract locks him down as a key part of the team’s offense for the remainder of Caleb Williams’ rookie contract.

title: Bears vs Panthers Q&A: Bryce Young and Caleb Williams go head-to-head
summary: The Chicago Bears head to Charlotte this Sunday to face off against the Carolina Panthers. The Bears are expected to win this game, according to experts and Vegas. But both teams won their respective divisions last year and are looking to repeat that feat this year. We know the Bears well, but we wanted to […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears head to Charlotte this Sunday to face off against the Carolina Panthers. The Bears are expected to win this game, according to experts and Vegas. But both teams won their respective divisions last year and are looking to repeat that feat this year. We know the Bears well, but we wanted to get some insight on their opponent this week, so we spoke with Walker Clement of Cat Scratch Reader (SB Nation’s Carolina Panthers site) to discuss the Panthers and where they are at heading into this season. Here is our Q&A. 1. Let’s start with the coach and Dave Canales with his decision not to call offensive plays this year. Wasn’t that part of the reason he was brought in? What do fans think about this decision to hand play-calling duties to Brad Idzik? The Canales hire was, as best I can tell, a three-part decision. One part was that Tepper was viewed as a volatile owner and no big names wanted the job. A second part was that Canales’ relentless optimism was viewed as necessary change from the dysfunction that was Frank Reich’s brief tenure and the disingenuousness of Matt Rhule. The biggest part that set him apart from the other “up-and-comer” candidates was his success with Geno Smith and Baker Mayfield. Play calling was always, hopefully, secondary to quarterback whispering. Idzik, for his part, is a relative unknown who has shown some promise in limited preseason games as a play caller. I’m optimistic that the team will look a little stronger and a little more coherent under his guidance, whereas Canales would occasionally get stuck digging a hole for himself with a fixation on one idea. 2. Bryce Young has definitely improved under Canales compared to where he was a couple of years ago, but has he improved enough? Do you expect Young to get an extension after this season or will the Panthers just play out the 5th year option? That is the $26.53M question. When Young is good, he’s pretty good. When he’s bad, he wobbles between ineffective and incautious. Unfortunately, his average is far closer to ineffective than even adequate. While ineffective is an improvement over “outright detriment,” it is insufficient to merit an extension and pales in comparison to the draft capital spent to acquire him. You’re welcome on that one. What we don’t know with Young is whether or not he has hit his ceiling. His entrance to the NFL was bumpy. His size is an obvious impediment. Is that his whole story, or is he slowly building the skills and habits he needs to overcome the first act of his NFL career? I think the answer to that question is yes. He is improving and probably has room left to improve. Will he improve enough to earn an extension this season? Or even at a rate that earns a roster spot during his now-guaranteed fifth year? I don’t know. Young has been nothing but questions since he entered the league, and most Panthers fans are tired of asking them. Give us an answer or give us a new quarterback, but one more year of “maybe Young will step up this season” might actually break us. The awkward thing about that, and what is already splitting the fan base, is that it leaves no clear path to root for. The objectively best thing for the Panthers is for Young to put it together and be the quarterback of the future in a way that justifies his draft spot. ‘The quarterback is on the roster’ is always a better statement than ‘a quarterback is on the roster’. It just seems unlikely. So are we hoping for the wheels to fall off, sending the Panthers plummeting towards the number one overall pick again? What a great thing to root for. Are we hoping he shows just enough to entice another team to trade a high pick for him as part of a reclamation project? This also seems unlikely. It would also leave the Panthers with a likely middling draft pick and few options for pursuing their next quarterback. Young will probably have an OK season. I doubt, at this point, that he is going to start the season on fire and keep burning through January. The Panthers will either have the option to eat some of his salary and flip him for a Day 3 draft pick or keep him as a highly paid back up/awkward piece in a quarterback competition. None of those exactly pave the way for the team having their choice of quarterbacks in the 2027 season. Of course, having the ninth overall pick didn’t stop them from getting their guy in 2023. 3. I think I’m contractually obligated to ask about the trade. Where are fans with this trade, and how much do you think it’s hurt the Panthers? I think most Bears fans are still in agreement that this is the best move Ryan Poles has ever made, and with the growth of Caleb Williams, it probably will never be topped during his tenure in Chicago. See above? Pass? Yeah, we’re doing great. Thanks for asking. Ask again after the season. Maybe then we’ll know more, but as I said in the previous question, we just have too many questions around Young to say anything with confidence. The unknown, more than the actual stretches and stretches of bad play, hurts more at this point. 4. How significant are the injuries that plagued the Panthers this summer, and how much will it impact them this Sunday against Chicago and moving forward the rest of the season? The Panthers’ joyous injury fortunes currently stretch back to the 2025 Wildcard game that the 8-9 Carolina Panthers hilariously took down to the wire. It was a great game, but it also cost us our starting left tackle, Ikem Ekwonu (Patellar tendon), for what will likely be most of the 2026 season. Our starting right tackle, Taylor Moton (blood clots), popped up in the offseason with a blood clot in his lung that has him sidelined for at least another month. Then our rising star from the 2025 NFL Draft and starting outside linebacker, Nic Scourton (ACL), went down on the first day of training camp. It hasn’t gotten a whole lot worse from there, but a lot of us are still walking around on eggshells waiting for the next shoe. The good news is that free agent signing Rasheed Walker and our 2026 first-round pick Monroe Freeling make up a well above average pair of second-string offensive tackles. The team’s depth is actually built pretty well to make a good game out of Sunday and a strong push into December if they can actually come out of the gate with some heat. The team has had notoriously cold starts under head coach Dave Canales, so this is probably the story we’re watching the most closely going into Sunday. 5. I don’t think many people expected Carolina to make the playoffs last year, even at 8-9. Do you think it was a fluke season of a below-average team in a weak division, or is this a team that’s building something and could elevate to that next tier in the next year or two? Yes. There are two questions that we hope to answer relatively early in the season. One, has Young taken a step forward? His supporting cast has improved year over year. He is out of excuses with stability, team depth, and adjustment time. This year is on him. Two, does the whole team start with mountains of offseason rust like they have the past two seasons? A cold start and an inconsistent Young put us right back where we were last year, with a roster trending towards above average but with below average leadership in the silliest division in football. That means anything can happen. A hot start and a Young who passes for over 150 yards more often than not (we set the bar high around here) could make for a fun season for Panthers fans. The NFC South is a weird place to be, but a good team should win it. The Panthers have all the pieces in place to beat the Bears in Week 1 and to win the Division by Week 18. Whether or not they can make all those pieces work together comes down to Young,…

title: Drew Brees thinks Bears Caleb Williams is closer to a breakthrough than you think
summary: For all Caleb Williams’ brilliance in his third season with the Chicago Bears, the burgeoning star quarterback can still get that much better as a passer—a frightening prospect for the NFL, if you ask me. In particular, Williams’ 58.1% completion percentage, a year after completing just 62.5% of his passes as a rookie, is due […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears against the Cincinnati Bengals during the preseason game at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images For all Caleb Williams’ brilliance in his third season with the Chicago Bears, the burgeoning star quarterback can still get that much better as a passer—a frightening prospect for the NFL, if you ask me. In particular, Williams’ 58.1% completion percentage, a year after completing just 62.5% of his passes as a rookie, is due for an improvement in Year 3, which will mark his second under Ben Johnson. But for those worried about whether Williams can make meaningful strides in that area, Hall-of-Fame quarterback Drew Brees had some advice for Williams that might put things in perspective. Brees, who is now working as a color analyst for FOX Sports alongside Adam Amin, recently spoke with Williams as part of their preparations for the Bears’ season-opening contest against the Carolina Panthers. Amin shared an especially interesting piece of that conversation on 104.3 The Score yesterday . (Also, don’t forget to check out Adam’s chat with our own Bill Zimmerman when you’re done reading this.) “Drew’s line at the end of our conversation with Caleb—he said, ‘You know what the difference is between a 60% passer and a 70% passer?’ Caleb’s answer was—he was hesitant, but he goes, ‘Is it checkdowns?’ “Drew’s answer was ‘Three completions.’” You get three more completions per game when you’re probably going to throw the ball 30 times per game.” First of all, Williams getting to speak with one of the greatest quarterbacks to ever do it—a man who completed almost 68% of his career pass attempts—is absolutely invaluable. Secondly, what a way to put the task at hand in plain but attainable terms. When you take away the league-leading 40 throwaways Williams made last year—another underrated sign of his growth—you could generally point to two or three passes a game where the ball simply got away from the young quarterback, who had the third-highest “bad-throw” percentage among all quarterbacks according to Pro Football Reference. (Plus, let’s not forget he also suffered from the fourth-highest drop rate from his pass catchers at 5.5%. He also had 18 balls batted at the line of scrimmage, second-most in the NFL.) The good news, Amin said, is that these improvements are a matter of smaller adjustments and fundamental tweaks than wholesale overhauls. “A few adjustments here and there are all it’s going to take to get small plays that lead to extended drives that lead to four extra points instead of having to settle for a field goal. These are the little things that build up and compound over time, and that’s a good entry point to be in Year 2 in an offense,” the broadcaster said. A little bit of positive regression in each of these stats, and it wouldn’t be hard to see Williams’ completion rate jump into the mid-60s, even as he continues to big-game hunt and generate explosive plays. And if he goes even higher than that? We might be talking about an MVP-caliber player sooner rather than later. And all it might take, at least to start with, is three more completions a game. Imagine that.

Both Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams have expressed a desire to field the most productive offense of all-time, so we’ll naturally have to keep one eye on the 2013 Denver Broncos (led by Bears legends John Fox and Adam Gase), who hold that distinction, having scored an average of 37.9 points per game. Even then, there is a ceiling on his production with all of the mouths to feed in this offense. As far as comp players go, I see Rome Odunze lining up similarly to Jameson Williams’ primary deep threat role, while Luther Burden is set to take on the YAC production responsibility of a young Amon-Ra St. Brown. Kalif Raymond is compared to a past version of himself, but one that held a greater role in the Lions’ offense than in his most recent seasons. Finally, Zavion Thomas is hard to pin down, but Luther Burden’s output from last season seems a fitting measuring stick for another incoming rookie who will need to play himself into offensive snaps.
