title: Bucs DB Zyon McCollum gives Joe Burrow and the Bengals some bulletin-board material
summary: Every sport has its unwritten rules, and one of the most universal is simple: Don’t give your opponent “bulletin-board material.” Don’t say something that can be printed out, slapped on a wall, and pointed to by a coach looking for a little extra motivation. Don’t give the other team a reason to make the game […]
full_text: Dec 11, 2025; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Zyon McCollum (27) reacts during player introductions before the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Every sport has its unwritten rules, and one of the most universal is simple: Don’t give your opponent “bulletin-board material.” Don’t say something that can be printed out, slapped on a wall, and pointed to by a coach looking for a little extra motivation. Don’t give the other team a reason to make the game personal. In the end, almost anything can be twisted into locker-room material in one way or another. When Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive back Zyon McCollum was asked how he felt about playing against one of the most talented offenses in the league in Week 1, he had plenty of ways he could have answered. And he made a decision. “We’re going to have opportunities, guaranteed opportunities,” he said when asked about his Week 1 opponents . “I mean, they want to get their season started off right. They want to get in rhythm early, so the ball is guaranteed to go in the air. And a ball in the air belongs to us. You know, that’s the mentality that we have. That’s what we’re going into the game thinking. We know we’re going to get tested early, so it’s an incredible opportunity for us. “There will be no better feeling than when we take away three, four interceptions.” But it’s that last sentence that sticks out. There will be no better feeling than when we take away three, four interceptions. That, to me, sounds like McCollum has already determined Burrow will be turning the ball over several times. While I wouldn’t be shocked by an errant throw here or there—it is Week 1, after all—assuming a quarterback of Joe Burrow’s caliber is going to hand you three or four interceptions is pretty wild and more than a little disrespectful. Maybe. I have a feeling fans take this sort of thing much more personally than the players do. Professional athletes don’t need extra motivation. They’re where they are because they’re the absolute best at what they do. It’s not like NFL players are all Seabiscuit and need someone to dangle a quote in front of them before they’ll run faster. Still, a little bulletin-board material to get the blood pumping never hurt anyone. Well, outside of the guy who provided the material.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are set to make their 2026 debut Sunday when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to kick off what hopes to be a historic season in the Queen City. It also starts with one of the Bengals’ toughest home matchups of the year, as Tampa enters the game favored to win the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are set to make their 2026 debut Sunday when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to kick off what hopes to be a historic season in the Queen City. It also starts with one of the Bengals’ toughest home matchups of the year, as Tampa enters the game favored to win the NFC South for the fifth time in the last six seasons. Now, let’s take a look at the Bengals’ three keys to victory and a 1-0 start. Effective Bengals running game The Bengals are trying to incorporate more under center into their offense this season. While they saw mixed results working it in throughout training camp, the Bengals will have a chance to show how effective it can be on Sunday. The Buccaneers struggled to defend play-action, which is another reason the Bengals will need to stick with more under-center plays in their opening game this week. For it to be effective, the Bengals have to establish and stick with the running game. This will open up play-action passes and keep Joe Burrow from taking too many hits throughout the game. If the Bengals struggle with the running game early, how quickly would they ditch under center? Burrow has always stated he feels most comfortable working from shotgun, with everything laid out in front of him to diagnose. Will this be the year that he evolves his game to cut down on the amount of hits he takes each year? An effective running game would go a long way toward making that a reality. Slow down Bucs’ pass rush The Buccaneers drafted Rueben Bain Jr. with their first round pick this year. They bring back an explosive pass rusher in Yaya Diaby opposite of him. Vita Vea has a brand new contract this offseason, and commands a lot of attention in the middle of the defense. The biggest X-Factor for that Tampa Bay pass rush is Calijah Kancey. He missed 12 games with an injury during the 2025 season, and the Buccaneers’ defense was just not the same because of it. Kancey is one of the most disruptive defensive tackles in the league when he is fully healthy. The Bengals return all five starters to their offensive line. Communication will be a huge factor in the Bengals being able to slow down the Tampa Bay pass rush. This will be a really good early season test for the Bengals offensive line. Limit big runs from Tampa Bay Tampa Bay has a very talented young running back returning in Bucky Irving. They also added Kenneth Gainwell to the running back room. He played well against the Bengals during his time with the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Bengals ranked last in the league as a run defense during the 2025 season. They gave up 147.1 yards per game on the ground last year. To become a more effective defense, they have to start by stopping the run. They went out and made a massive addition in Dexter Lawrence to man the middle of the defense. Alongside him is veteran Jonathan Allen. The two starters at defensive tackle were BJ Hill and TJ Slaton; they will both now become more rotational players for Cincinnati. Bryan Cook is a physical presence on the back end of the defense and is known for his reliability as a tackler. That is the complete opposite of the guy he is replacing in Geno Stone. The Bengals cannot be one of the worst teams in the league when it comes to missed tackles again this year. Their first test will come against Irving, Gainwell, and the rest of the Buccaneers’ rushing attack.

Thirteen touchdown catches give him the franchise record, breaking Johnson’s 66 … It just goes to show how good of a run the Bengals have had at wide receiver. Since the turn of the millennia, We have watched Johnson, Green and now Chase dominate NFL defenses. Even going back to guys like Pickens and Curtis, though, you can tell it has always been something Bengals’ fans have been spoiled with. Now, we may be watching the best of them ascend to the top of the franchise’s record books. Ja’Marr Chase Says He Just Found Out Bengals’ Start Time for Week 1 vs. Bucs in Funny Video “I’m finding out the game is at 1 o’clock, I do not like that,” he said. “To be honest, I do not like playing in 1 o’clock games. So that means I have to wake up a little earlier than usual.” There is a reason the Bengals give Chase his own press conference to talk to the media. The guy is a one-of-one both on and off the field. Just a funny moment prior to the beginning of the season. What I’m hearing about the Bengals: Cashius Howell, extensions and summer risers “Hitting on Cashius,” defensive coordinator Al Golden began, “I can’t underscore how important that is because he’s come through for us in terms of his intellect, his work ethic, his ability to process, and his learning curve.” When it all is said and done, we may look back and wonder how it wasn’t more obvious to everyone that this defense wasn’t going to be good. Howell is the gravy on top of a summer spent attacking the defensive line. Last season, it seemed the defense would be lucky to get pressure on the quarterback at all. This year, they may have quarterbacks rushing into mistakes. NFL News Niners-Rams in Australia: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 27-7 win Week 1 can always be wild to look back on. A few years ago, Zach Wilson led a comeback win over the Buffalo Bills after Aaron Rodgers went down almost immediately. It is good to see a team dubbed as a super team like the Los Angeles Rams get knocked down a peg, but it is only Week 1. NFL Network: Sam Darnold expected to miss Seahawks’ Week 2 game, but avoids major hip injury One of the worst things about this sport is the injuries. Seeing Darnold go down that early was a bit of an early shock to the system for the entire NFL. Just a reminder that any optimism can be lost in a blink of an eye. Happy to see it isn’t one that will leave him missing major time. NFL QB rankings, Week 1: Ranking all 32 starters entering 2026 season It sure didn’t age well putting Drake Maye in Tier 1 with Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford, huh? It will be curious to see how that shifts next week as guys like Joe Burrow, Lamar Jackson and Dak Prescott were left in Tier 2.

For their debut show, they had none other than Joe Burrow, Bengals quarterback and Chase’s best friend. Burrow didn’t hold back while on the show about how he felt […]
full_text: Feb 25, 2024; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Cincinnati Bengals players Ja'Marr Chase (left) and Joe Burrow sit court side of the Phoenix Suns game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Footprint Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Ja’Marr Chase, the Cincinnati Bengals’ superstar wide receiver, has a new podcast called “Chasing No. 1,” starring himself and viral NFL social media influencer Annie Agar. For their debut show, they had none other than Joe Burrow, Bengals quarterback and Chase’s best friend. Burrow didn’t hold back while on the show about how he felt about the Bengals’ 2026 season. “I just want to win this year,” he said. “I just want to win. The rest will take care of itself. I think we’ll break a bunch of records eventually, but I think we’re going to have a really good team that has a chance to win every game that we step foot on the field for. I don’t know about you, but I could really feel it in my bones, in my soul, in OTA’s this year — different from years past.” While the offense managed to keep everyone together, the defense added Dexter Lawrence II, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook. The deep and talented defensive line has shifted from a weakness to a potential strength, which could have a trickle-down effect that benefits even the safeties. Burrow knows the additions of the veteran defenders have increased the odds the Bengals have of going deep in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. “We brought in a lot of the right guys, a lot of the right people with the right mindsets to go and chase this goal of winning a Super Bowl and winning as many games as we can and being the best possible team that we can,” he continued. “I felt it from our D-line. I felt it from our defense. Our offense has the same guys in years past… but these veteran guys that we brought in on defense to be able to help our younger guys.” Hopefully he’s right. If the Bengals’ offense can stay healthy and play like they’re capable, and if the defense is just good—not great, but good—there aren’t many teams that could stand between them and the Lombardi Trophy.

title: Browns’ ceiling for the 2026 season
summary: While there are reasons to be optimistic about the Cleveland Browns heading into the 2026 season, they still have a realistic ceiling on what they can accomplish. The Browns went 5-12 last season largely due to struggles on offense. The team enters this season with plenty of changes, from a new coaching staff and revamped […]
full_text: While there are reasons to be optimistic about the Cleveland Browns heading into the 2026 season, they still have a realistic ceiling on what they can accomplish. The Browns went 5-12 last season largely due to struggles on offense. The team enters this season with plenty of changes, from a new coaching staff and revamped offensive line to the departure of Myles Garrett and the return of Deshaun Watson . Given all of this, what is a realistic ceiling for the team this season? Most projections and betting lines have Cleveland finishing with 4-5 wins, but if things go right, they can certainly outpace that. The Browns have the easiest strength of schedule in 2026 by many metrics. So while there are many questions about the Browns’ offense, many of their opponents have issues on either side of the ball as well. Opponents like the Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, New York Giants, and Indianapolis Colts all have similar questions about their quarterbacks, which allows Cleveland to sneak in some wins. The AFC North is always a competitive division, but even in some of the Browns’ toughest seasons, they have managed to squeak out a few division wins. Given all of these possibilities, it is not out of the question for Cleveland to reach nine wins this season. This best-case scenario could have them in the playoff conversation late into the season, which would be a welcome result for Browns fans. The Cowboys offense suffered another big blow in practice Friday as running back Malik Davis suffered a hip injury that will keep him out of Sunday’s game in New York and likely a lot longer. Cowboys chief operating officer Stephen Jones said on 105.3 “The Fan” on Friday that Davis had a “pretty serious” injury and could be out for a while. “Unfortunately, I think he’s looking at a pretty serious injury that could take him out for some period of time,” Jones said. “We don’t have the final details, we’ll know more, but certainly so disappointed for Malik. Obviously tough for our team, but like anything it’s next man up.” Spann-Ford, Flournoy reaping rewards of climbing NFL ladder with Cowboys – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford and wide receiver Ryan Flournoy have both been grinding to find their place in Dallas for years. This week, they both signed contract extensions. The fact the Cowboys extended both Spann-Ford and Flournoy on the same night is fitting. The two were both part of the 2024 rookie class. He’s earned a very important role before the season starts, and that’s the Green Dot on defense. Overshown prominently wore the green dot throughout training camp and the preseason, and will now carry those responsibilities into the regular season. Mo will be doing a lot of the heavy lifting ,” Schottenheimer revealed. Bass is being called to step up. The good thing for the Cowboys is that this isn’t unfamiliar territory for him. The waters-run-still demeanor of Bass has always worked in his favor, as does the fact that, this time, he’ll be asked to step in at a position he has a lot of experience playing — from his days playing for the University of Oregon. “Yeah, I’m pretty comfortable with it,” Bass said. “I’d say like left guard is a lot easier for me to step in. To keep that going, there’s something specially that he must do. The single biggest storyline for this game comes down to one question: can Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott get the ball out fast? title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 2
summary: It is Day 2 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: PASADENA, CA - JANUARY 31: Defensive lineman Jimmie Jones #97 of the Dallas Cowboys runs over quarterback Jim Kelly #12 of the Buffalo Bills as he runs for a two yard touch down after recovering a fumble after Kelly was sacked by defensive end Charles Haley in Super Bowl XXVII at the Rose Bowl on January 31, 1993 in Pasadena, California. The Cowboys won 52-17. (Photo by Andrew D. Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 2 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Get ready for a big one here on Day 2 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the night the Cowboys dynasty officially arrived. Dallas had already announced itself by beating San Francisco in the NFC Championship Game, but Super Bowl XXVII turned a promising young team into champions. The Cowboys forced a Super Bowl-record nine turnovers, Troy Aikman delivered an MVP performance and Buffalo was simply overwhelmed. Sunday, January 31, 1993 Rose Bowl, Pasadena, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 52, Buffalo Bills 17 It had been 15 years since Dallas last lifted the Lombardi Trophy. The Cowboys had endured the end of the Tom Landry era, the 1-15 season in Jimmy Johnson’s first year and a complete roster rebuild. Now Aikman, Emmitt Smith and Michael Irvin were on football’s biggest stage, facing a Buffalo team appearing in its third consecutive Super Bowl. Things began perfectly for Buffalo. Special-teams star Steve Tasker blocked Mike Saxon’s punt, giving the Bills possession at the Dallas 16. Four plays later, Thurman Thomas scored from two yards out and Buffalo led 7-0. For a few minutes, it looked as though the Bills might finally be ready to change their Super Bowl fortunes. Then the turnovers, and all of Buffalo’s nightmares began. James Washington intercepted Jim Kelly and returned the ball 13 yards to the Buffalo 47. Six plays later, Aikman found Jay Novacek for a 23-yard touchdown to tie the game. On Buffalo’s very next offensive play, Charles Haley sacked Kelly near his own goal line and knocked the football loose. Jimmie Jones scooped it up and went two yards into the end zone. In only 15 seconds, Dallas had turned a 7-0 game into a 14-7 lead. Buffalo had chances to respond. The Bills reached the Dallas goal line later in the first half, but Thomas Everett intercepted Kelly in the end zone on fourth down. Steve Christie eventually converted a 21-yard field goal on another drive, reducing the Cowboys’ advantage to 14-10 with 3:24 remaining before halftime. That was when Dallas exploded. Smith broke loose for a 38-yard run, and Aikman finished the drive by hitting Irvin for a 19-yard touchdown. On Buffalo’s very next offensive play, Thomas caught a short pass before Leon Lett forced a fumble that Jones recovered. Aikman immediately went back to Irvin for an 18-yard touchdown. Irvin had scored twice in just 18 seconds, and Dallas suddenly carried a 28-10 lead into halftime. By then, Buffalo was also without Kelly, who had suffered a knee injury during the second quarter. Frank Reich took over at quarterback, but this was not going to become another miraculous comeback like the one he had engineered against Houston earlier that postseason. Dallas had too much control and continued creating mistakes. Lin Elliott’s 20-yard field goal stretched the lead to 31-10 in the third quarter. Reich then found Don Beebe for a 40-yard touchdown on the final play of the period, cutting the margin to 31-17. It was Buffalo’s last score of the game. The fourth quarter became a coronation. Aikman connected with Alvin Harper for a 45-yard touchdown, his fourth scoring pass of the night. Smith then scored on a 10-yard run before Ken Norton Jr. recovered another Buffalo fumble and returned it nine yards for a touchdown. Dallas had scored three times in only two and a minutes and pushed the score to an astonishing 52-17. Of course, one of the most iconic NFL plays happened in this game, but it was a negative for the Cowboys. Late in the game, Leon Lett recovered a fumble and ran 64 yards for what looked like a sure touchdown. Lett slowed toward the goal line and extended the ball away from his body in celebration. Don Beebe had ben tracking Lett the whole way and finally reached him right before the goal line and swatted the ball away for a touchback keeping the score at the final of 52-17. Aikman’s performance was practically perfect. He completed 22 of 30 passes for 273 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions, earning Super Bowl MVP honors. His 140.7 passer rating reflected just how efficiently he picked apart Buffalo’s defense on the biggest stage of his career. Yet the defense was every bit as responsible for the destruction. Dallas recovered five fumbles and intercepted four passes, turning Buffalo’s nine turnovers into 35 points. Two of those takeaways became defensive touchdowns through Jones and Norton. Remarkably, a Cowboys defense that had finished first in the NFL in yards allowed that season did not have a single player selected to the Pro Bowl. This game belongs at number two because it represents the exact moment a new era of Cowboys football became undeniable. Dallas had gone from the worst team in football only three years earlier to Super Bowl champion. The Cowboys did not sneak past Buffalo or survive a close finish. They dominated every phase and produced one of the most overwhelming championship performances the Super Bowl had seen. #Cowboys vs #Bills 1993 Super Bowl XXVII Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 52, Buffalo Bills 17 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/lOSynSSpdz — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 11, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The Cowboys forced a Super Bowl-record nine turnovers, recovering five fumbles and making four interceptions. title: Cowboys at Giants: The offensive and defensive X-factor for Dallas
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are set to kick off the 2026 NFL season against their division rival, the New York Giants, on Sunday night. The Cowboys have gotten the better of the Giants over the past several years, but there is plenty of new coaches and players this year that it has a slightly different feel. […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are set to kick off the 2026 NFL season against their division rival, the New York Giants, on Sunday night. The Cowboys have gotten the better of the Giants over the past several years, but there is plenty of new coaches and players this year that it has a slightly different feel. Today, we identify one player on both the offensive and defensive side of the ball for the Cowboys who will make a game changing play in Week 1 against the Giants. We call these players X-factors. They can be anyone from someone who makes a huge special teams tackle to someone who makes the game-winning touchdown. Offensive X-factor: WR Ryan Flournoy There’s already been quite a bit of trash talk back and forth between the Giants cornerbacks and the Cowboys receivers, so we expect quite a bit of physical play and trash talk between the two Sunday night. Both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens will naturally draw most of the attention in this matchup, but it’s Ryan Flournoy who should reap the rewards with favorable coverage. He will make some key catches this week, one of which will result in a touchdown. After that, he can celebrate his new contract extension in the end zone. Defensive X-factor: DB Caleb Downs Caleb Downs may be making his NFL debut against the Giants this week, but at no point so far since joining the Cowboys as the eleventh overall pick has he looked as if he’s not ready to live up to everyone’s expectations, including his own. As one of the favorites to win Defensive Rookie of the Year, Downs has already played in some big games in college and seems more than ready to make a difference in his rookie debut. We predict he’ll make some key plays as both a run defender and in pass coverage to alter the outcome of the game. Who are your x-factors for the game?
author: Brian Martin

title: New coaches have brought new feeling to familiar Cowboys-Giants opener
summary: The last time the Dallas Cowboys played at the New York Giants in Week 1 to begin a new season, and on Sunday Night Football just like they will this upcoming Sunday, they had a new offensive coordinator in his first year in that role named Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys won this game 40-0, returning […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants looks on during warm-ups prior to a pre-season game against the Minnesota Vikings at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last time the Dallas Cowboys played at the New York Giants in Week 1 to begin a new season, and on Sunday Night Football just like they will this upcoming Sunday, they had a new offensive coordinator in his first year in that role named Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys won this game 40-0, returning a blocked field goal for a touchdown on the opening possession for the Giants and never looking back. This was the fifth straight win for the Cowboys against the Giants, a streak that would reach eight games under Mike McCarthy through the 2024 season. Fast forward to 2025, and that OC from the 2023 matchup is now the head coach of America’s Team, and extended the win streak against the Giants to nine games in Week 2 of his debut season. Something was different about this win though, as the Cowboys went from beating the Giants by an average of 21 points from the 40-0 game on to needing a dramatic overtime back and forth to beat a Russell Wilson-led New York team 40-37 on a Brandon Aubrey field goal with four seconds left. This game was in week two, and it wasn’t too long after this when Cowboys fans could put their finger directly on what was actually “different” about this game and many others that followed – the Dallas defense was as far away from being competitive as entire generations of fans had ever seen. By Week 18 and the conclusion of the season, the Cowboys defense had the team eliminated from playoff contention, playing on the road at a Giants team that was also eliminated. The game meant nothing, other than the Cowboys keeping their win streak against the Giants alive, but ultimately this didn’t matter in the big picture to coach Schottenheimer. Quarterback Dak Prescott played just the first half, replaced by Joe Milton in the second half. The Giants got their first win against the Cowboys since January of 2021, and a second straight win to end the 2025 campaign with some things to feel good about with rookie Jaxson Dart at the helm. Call it artificial billboard material, a nothingburger, or whatever you want, but Schottenheimer and the Cowboys look to start a new chapter in 2026 at the scene of where the book closed on both the 2025 season and streak against the Giants ended. If this isn’t enough spice from the Dallas side of this matchup to be “waiting all day for Sunday night”, the New York side really kicks things up. Their new chapter for 2026 begins with a new head coach who was the biggest fish in the coaching market pond this offseason, John Harbaugh. After a remarkable 18 years as the head man for the Ravens, Harbaugh has brought an instant dose of confidence to a fanbase that hasn’t had many reasons at all to be excited for far too long. Given the lopsided recent history between these teams, a debut win in primetime against the Cowboys to make it two in a row on home turf for Big Blue is about the best way imaginable for the Harbaugh era to begin if you’re a Giants believer. Both of these teams come into Week 1 with remade defenses and new defensive coordinators, high expectations that continuity at quarterback and running back will carry them, but also concerns on the offensive line. For the Giants, it’s a defense with a flock of former Ravens brought in by Harbaugh, as well as the Ohio State draft pick that started a run on Buckeyes defenders landing in the NFC East, Arvell Reese at fifth overall. Their new defensive coordinator is Dennard Wilson, who spent just one season with the Ravens as defensive backs coach in 2023 and most recently was the Titans defensive coordinator from 2024-25. Dart and Cam Skattebo are the Giants’ battery on offense, and how both players mature within a locker room where the addition of Harbaugh is expected to make a huge cultural difference compared to years past will be interesting. The first thing they can do to help this cause is consistently play well from the jump of this season, and getting to attack a Cowboys defense in game one for Christian Parker as coordinator where the scheme is still new is a golden opportunity for the Giants offense to make a statement. Of course, the offensive scheme for the Giants is totally new as well, going from Brian Daboll as an offensive-minded head coach to former Bears head coach Matt Nagy as OC now. This is Nagy’s first job away from the Andy Reid/Patrick Mahomes environment in Kansas City since being the Bears head coach from 2018-21. The question mark spot on the Giants offensive line that will have a huge say in how this approach will go for them is rookie starter Francis Mauigoa at right guard. Mauigoa was the second of two first-round picks the Giants spent to get better along the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball in April’s draft. No matter who the Cowboys line up against Mauigoa, they’ll have their choice of experienced players to try and win this matchup decisively with Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, Otito Ogbonnia, or even Von Miller and Rashan Gary as pass rushers. The primary buzz around this game has gone far away from the trenches, mainly out to the receiving units for both teams and the potential for big plays on both sides. This was partially the case for the first primetime game of this season as well though, Patriots at Seahawks, yet that game proved again that it all starts up front in this sport. The next primetime game featuring the Cowboys and Giants could be no different, and the road team should be excited they have more than just coaching aura and lip service to be excited about when it comes to how they’ll set the tone at the line of scrimmage. The Cowboys offensive line concern for this game is at the other guard spot, where T.J. Bass starts the season in place of the injured Tyler Smith. Paired with concerns at tackle against a Giants pass rush unit that’s been trying to play up to their expectations forever now, and it’s fair to expect both quarterbacks to be under some heat throughout this game. Which passer can make the right decisions under pressure between Prescott and Dart, and which receivers can help their QBs with run-after-the-catch efforts, will also go a long way in deciding this one. In the Week 2 Cowboys win last year, their defense became the first to allow a pair of Giants receivers to both get over 100 yards since the Falcons in 2018. CeeDee Lamb was the only receiver over 100 yards in the game for the Cowboys. For these two fanbases, it is really, really, really, really hard to make a Week 1 game feel like anything different than what it is – a sequel to a sequel that’s been running forever now. Somehow though, with the coaching matchup at the forefront, Caleb Downs versus Arvell Reese, and so on, this Cowboys-Giants chapter to start 2026 feels refreshed and most importantly, more even-sided than a lot of previous ones. Dallas has not lost two in a row against New York since a three game losing streak between Week 7 of 2015, Week 1 of 2016, and Week 14 of that same season. The Giants have not started a season 1-0 since 2022, and haven’t started off with a divisional win since that 2016 season. Something has to give at the conclusion of the first football Sunday of this new season.
author: Sean Martin

title: Malik Nabers will be good test for Cowboys secondary
summary: For the first time since last September when he sustained a season-ending ACL injury, New York Giants wide receiver was a full participant in a game week practice on Wednesday afternoon, and is expected to be good to go for the 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Facing a young, talented WR of Nabers […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 28: Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants makes a reception against the Dallas Cowboys during an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on November 28, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since last September when he sustained a season-ending ACL injury, New York Giants wide receiver was a full participant in a game week practice on Wednesday afternoon, and is expected to be good to go for the 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Good news: #Giants WR Malik Nabers, returning from a torn ACL, was a full participant in practice today — the team’s first official practice of the 2026 regular season, per HC John Harbaugh. The Giants host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night. pic.twitter.com/mahl4sZvdT — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 9, 2026 Facing a young, talented WR of Nabers caliber will be a good test for Dallas’ revamped secondary; he is someone who’s had quite a bit of success against them in the past. In the three games Nabers has played against the Cowboys in his young career, he is averaging nearly 100 receiving yards per game. As a rookie he caught 12 passes for 115 yards in their first meeting and eight catches for 69 yards in the second. Then in 2025 he caught nine passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns against the Cowboys in Week 2 before his season was cut short to just four games. Now back to playing status, Nabers will be looking to restart his dominance against the Cowboys in Week 1. The question is, will he be able to do so against a secondary that has been revamped in new defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s image? Highly regarded for his ability to develop defensive backs in his young coaching career, the 34-year-old Parker wasted no time rebuilding the Cowboys secondary after replacing Matt Eberflus. He added free agents Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke to pair with Malik Hooker on the backend, drafted Caleb Downs to play the ever-important nickel/safety position, and signed Cobie Durant to solidify things at CB with DaRon Bland and Shavon Revel. Will it pay off though? From the defensive front to the back end of the secondary, we’ve seen signs of improvement throughout the offseason in organized team activities, training camp practices, and during preseason games from the defense. But, as of yet, we haven’t seen them do it in a meaningful game. That’s going to change when the Cowboys square off against the Giants in Week 1. Things are expected to improve in New York under John Harbaugh’s tutelage as the new head coach, but it’s unlikely they will be a high-powered offensive unit this season. Still, they are talented enough on the offensive side of the ball to give the Cowboys some problems. Especially with Nabers back in the mix. That is where the test comes in for Parker’s new defense and their new scheme.
author: Brian Martin

title: 5 points: The important Cowboys-Giants storylines
summary: Football is back, and so is the five points column. Last year, this article came after the Dallas Cowboys played to break down what went right or wrong, and boy, a lot went wrong last year. I’m sorry if a lot of it came off as complaining. This year will hopefully be different. Instead, this […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants is tackled by Donovan Wilson #6 of the Dallas Cowboys during their game at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is back, and so is the five points column. Last year, this article came after the Dallas Cowboys played to break down what went right or wrong, and boy, a lot went wrong last year. I’m sorry if a lot of it came off as complaining. This year will hopefully be different. Instead, this year it will come before each matchup to help set the table on both sides and highlight the key factors to watch for each week. Some points will be a little more on the nose, while others may be a little more obscure. This will be the 13th season the Cowboys will begin the year with a game against the New York Giants . The Cowboys are 11-1 in the previous 12 games. History would dictate Dallas walking out of MetLife Stadium with a win, but the Giants have overhauled their team the same way the Cowboys have. It should be a game that’s more competitive than people think. Here are five points to watch for on Sunday. First Point: Did Dallas build their wall with sticks or bricks? If you don’t believe in an over-the-hill Odell Beckham Jr., or Jaxson Dart to take the next step as a quarterback, be fearful of what the Giants defensive line can do to the Cowboys offense. Headlined by Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Abdul Carter, and rookie first-round pick Arvell Reese, New York has reimagined a slew of pass rushers that mirror how they won their Super Bowl matchups against the New England Patriots. Dallas’ offensive line is young but growing quickly through continuity. However, Tyler Guyton needs to carry over his offseason bump to the regular season, Terence Steele needs to hold off Broderick Jones, and T.J. Bass has to fill in for All-Pro Tyler Smith for the next month or more. A second-year leap from Carter could be the key to the Giants’ pass rush Sunday night, especially if they move him all over the defense similar to how Micah Parsons played in Dallas. When Carter was on the field, the Giants generated quick pressure on 18.6% of opponent dropbacks , which would have been the second-highest mark of any defense on the season, per NFL Pro. How Dallas neutralizes the Giants’ pass rush will unlock whatever they want to do on offense. They can do that early by establishing the run and limiting the damage on the outside. Second Point: Jaxson Dart prefers his eggs scrambled If you have watched enough Cowboys football over the last decade, you understand the problem that’s plagued the Dallas defense has been the mobile quarterback. Rob Marinelli’s old saying of “keep the quarterback in the well” echoes every time an opposing QB scrambles for seven yards a carry. New York’s second-year signal caller was one of the best at getting out of the pocket last year. Dart had 18 explosive runs last year, tied with Patrick Mahomes for most in the league, and a 61.6% rushing success rate, per NFL Pro. That was the highest among QBs with at least 35 carries last season, and the fourth-highest career mark among QBs with at least 75 carries in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). The Cowboys’ defense gave up the third-most rush yards per game (23.4) and the most touchdowns (8) in the league to quarterbacks running. Having the league’s worst defense will do that. If Christian Parker wants to put his stamp on this defense, it’ll be keeping them disciplined and not allowing Dart to run all over the field for first downs. Maybe someone like Caleb Downs can be used as a spy on Dart to make sure that if he leaves the pocket, he’s there to clean it up before it reaches seven to ten yards downfield. Dallas no longer has a Micah Parsons on the outside to put Dart in pressure situations. Collapsing the pocket from the inside will bode well for Dallas’ defense. They need a big night from Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Third Point: Calling your Schott Brian Schottenheimer defied expectations placed on him last season as a play-caller. The Cowboys had a top-ten offense in almost every major category, along with career seasons from Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, and George Pickens. The one black mark against the unit was how they fared in the red zone. Dallas finished 18th in red zone efficiency at 56.9 percent . Still middle of the league, but not good enough for an offense with this much talent. How Schottenheimer responds with his play-calling in year two, especially in the red zone, could be what puts Dallas over the top as a true NFC contender. The Giants’ pass rushers can be mitigated Sunday night by how Schottenheimer calls the game, so the sequence of play calls and how in tune he is with Prescott will matter in Dallas winning Week 1. Fourth Point: Passing the buck(eye) Before the NFL draft, Cowboys fans had sugar plums dancing in their heads of what life could be like with Caleb Downs falling to them and pairing him with Christian Parker. All along, it felt like a pipe dream. There’s no way Downs would not fall past the New York Giants, who picked twice in the top ten. John Harbaugh called Downs a generational talent at safety, almost tipping the internal feelings around the national champion. Then the unexpected happened. The Giants didn’t pass on Downs just once, but twice. The Cowboys traded up with the Miami Dolphins to pick 11, and the rest is history. Schottenheimer talked about how they felt heading into draft weekend; there was no chance they would be lucky enough to land their No. 1 player, but that’s what makes it so fun—the unknown. #Cowboys Brian Schottenheimer said Dallas had a deal in place with the Kansas City Chiefs to trade up and get Caleb Downs. Of course that all changed when the Chiefs moved up to get Mansoor Delane. “…we had four guys targeted that we really felt strongly about that would fit… pic.twitter.com/uu3qjtBUX9 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) July 5, 2026 Downs will be making his professional debut as a member of the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football with all the eyes of the world on him—and yet he seems unfazed by it all. You wonder if there will be any extra motivation for someone who already plays with a chip on his shoulder, facing the team that passed on him twice. Players have talked in the past about how things like this can give them extra motivation in a game. Hopefully, for the Cowboys’ sake, it could bring out the very best in Downs in primetime. Fifth Point: Under-the-radar players There are a few guys who have not been talked about as much this offseason that could be key to a Cowboys victory: Cooper Beebe – The Cowboys center has had a quiet offseason. For the center position, that’s a great thing. Dexter Lawrence is no longer in the picture for the Giants, leaving veterans DJ Reader and Shelby Harris to fill the void. Both players are nowhere near the same level as Lawrence, so Beebe should have some favorable matchups. How he fares against some of the edge rushers who line up on the inside will be the biggest challenge. Javonte Williams – The $24 million man is looking to carry the success from a breakout 2025 season into this year. Williams had 1,201 yards rushing and 13 total touchdowns. From a fantasy angle and production angle, his career year flew under the radar over the offseason. As the unquestioned bell cow for Dallas’ offense, Williams should have success running up the middle without Lawrence on defense. Tyler Booker – The second-year man out of Alabama had a great rookie season. He should be even better in his second year, with a full offseason and NFL acclimation under his belt. There’s a chance he could earn Pro Bowl honors when it’s all said and done. Jalen Thompson – It’s not often a team’s most expensive outside free-agent acquisition goes unnoticed, but Thompson has done just that. Unfortunately, he dealt with a lot of nagging injuries from mini-camp to…

title: Cowboys news: Rising stars get new contracts before start of the season
summary: We are just days away from the Dallas Cowboys kicking off their 2026 season on the road, taking on a division rival, the New York Giants. Before the Cowboys go wheels up to New York, they took care of some business, inking tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year contract extension to remain in Dallas. […]
full_text: We are just days away from the Dallas Cowboys kicking off their 2026 season on the road, taking on a division rival, the New York Giants. Before the Cowboys go wheels up to New York, they took care of some business, inking tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year contract extension to remain in Dallas. Spann-Ford has been one of the biggest risers for the Cowboys over the offseason, and his development was rewarded with a brand new three-year extension. They also took care of wide receiver Ryan Flournoy with a 1-year extension. Brevyn Spann-Ford agrees to terms on extension with Cowboys – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Brevyn Spann-Ford is expected to make a big leap in 2026. Before doing so, the Cowboys lock him in for three more years ahead of week one. FRISCO, Texas — The Cowboys and tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford have agreed to terms on an extension. Spann-Ford, who was set to be a restricted free agent after the 2026 season, will now stay in Dallas through 2029. During training camp, Spann-Ford grew into Dallas’ TE2 role behind Jake Ferguson, contributing as one of the offense’s best in-line blockers at the position and a key player on special teams. With three days to go until the Cowboys kick off the NFL season, Spann-Ford now gets added comfort long-term with Dallas being confident in what he can bring to the offense. Cowboys, WR Ryan Flournoy agree on 1-year extension worth up to $6M – RJ Ochoa, BloggingTheBoys.com Another deal indeed. Just before the league’s second game of the season kicked off in Australia, it was reported that Dallas agreed to a 3-year extension with tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford . That was great to see. About 5 minutes after the San Francisco 49ers polished off the Los Angeles Rams… news of the same variety broke. This time it is Ryan Flournoy. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . For Cowboys rookie Caleb Downs, opener vs. Giants offers opportunity for extra motivation – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News The Dallas Cowboys first-round pick Caleb Downs is ready to make his NFL debut. From the sounds of it, it seems like he has a little extra motivation heading into New York. Now, instead of playing for the Giants, Downs will play against them in his NFL debut when the Cowboys open the season against New York on Sunday Night Football . There’s already a lot of excitement for Downs about getting the chance to live his NFL dream. Considering the Giants’ interest and their decision to pass on him not once, but twice, is there also some added motivation? Downs downplayed the notion when asked Thursday. “I’m just trying to win on Sunday,” Downs said. “That’s about it.” The Dallas Cowboys are getting mixed signals from the Giants as star player’s availability is getting seriously confusing – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports One of the biggest questions coming into Sunday Night Football is will Malik Nabers play? The Giants are doing a great job of keeping that information all in house ahead of their home opener. The Dallas Cowboys got hit by major injury news when they were forced to place All-Pro guard Tyler Smith on Injured Reserve . But other than that, their starting lineup looks ready to go. The biggest injury mystery ahead of Sunday Night Football is on the New York Giants’ side of things. That’s because Giants top wide receiver Malik Nabers is raising questions about his Week 1 availability despite being a full participant in practice in back-to-back days. Despite Nabers’ participation in practice, the Giants have been non-committal on his status for Sunday. That’s mostly because of Nabers, who claims the organization is letting him make the call. “I’m just focusing on today, had a really good day at practice,” Nabers told reporters. “I’ll let God tell me [when it’s time to return].” How the Cowboys offensive line matches up with the Giants front The Cowboys offensive line was going to have it’s hands full with the Giants pass rush before the Tyler Smith injury. With T.J. Bass in and Tyler Smith out, those problems could get louder on Sunday Night Football. The biggest concern for the Cowboys offensive line this week is not difficult to find. New York can send Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux after Dak Prescott, and Dallas enters the season with questions at offensive tackle. That matters most on the right side. Terence Steele allowed 52 pressures last season, the most among qualifying offensive tackles according to PFF, while his 54.9 pass-blocking grade ranked 76th out of 89 tackles. Dallas trading for Broderick Jones just before the season and immediately putting him into competition with Steele tells its own story about how the Cowboys view the position. Daily discussion question: Are you more confident or nervous about this week?
author: Connor Livesay

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 2 of 2026 NCAA Football season
summary: Week 1 of the NCAA Football season in the books. Last week, we took a look at a trio of potential first-round prospects that could be of interest to the Denver Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week we will cover three more players, with varying degrees of potential round placement, for the Week […]
full_text: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - SEPTEMBER 27: Will Echoles #52 of the Mississippi Rebels reacts against the Louisiana State Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on September 27, 2025 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Randy J. Williams/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 of the NCAA Football season in the books. Last week, we took a look at a trio of potential first-round prospects that could be of interest to the Denver Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week we will cover three more players, with varying degrees of potential round placement, for the Week 2 slate of games. Will Echoles — Defensive Tackle — Ole Miss The defensive line is a key of the Denver Broncos. It’s a position they have acquired quality free agents such as Zach Allen, Malcolm Roach, D.J. Jones. Additionally, the have utilized some early round draft picks (Sai’vion Jones, Tyler Onyedim) the couple of years to address long-term. It’s certainly not a primary need for the Broncos. However, Eyioma Uwazurike is in a contract season and D.J. Jones will be 32 next year and carries over a $14.5 million cap hit. With that in mind, taking a look at this year’s class of defensive tackles is worth considering. Fortifying the defensive line is always a smart move, which makes it potentially in play if the right player is on the clock when the Broncos are picking next April. One player I’m bullish on is Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles. After a quiet freshman campaign, the former four-star recruit was a fifteen-game starter for the Rebels last season and notched 68 tackles, 11.5 tackles for loss, and 5 sacks. For his efforts, he earned AP first-team All-SEC honors and topped all P4 conference players with 39 quarterback pressures and 35 defensive stops. He just turned 20 years old and there is no doubt his best football is ahead of him. He is a force against the run and shows great upside as an interior pass rusher. While had a bit of a rough outing in the Rebels’ close Week 1 victory over Louisville, Echoles should have a chance to dominate against Charlotte tonight. If he can put it all together this season, I would not be surprised if he wound up being a Top 15 pick next April. Peyton Bowen — Safety — Oklahoma The Broncos enter their 2026 season with Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga slated as their starting duo. It’s an underrated group, and they also brought back Taylor Rapp who will eventually see time as a depth player for them this season. Though it’s important to note Jones will be a free agent at the end of the season, with Hufanga following suit in 2027. As far as the rest of the players at the position, their roster is rounded out by Tycen Anderson, Devon Key, and J.L. Skinner. That trio has largely been career contributors on special teams—with their potential as foundational starters in the future unlikely. The team also has ‘26 NFL Draft selection Miles Scott on their practice squad. I’ll admit that safety isn’t a premium position to address in the draft. History shows you can find quality starters at the position on Day 2, even as well as Day 3. One layer I think who will wind up hearing his name called a lot earlier than you think is Oklahoma Sooners standout Peyton Bowen. After spending his first two years in Norman as mostly a backup contributor and special teams’ player, Bowen became a full-time starter in ’25 and was a second-team All-SEC selection. He posted 47 tackles, 7 pass breakups, and 2 interceptions. His size (5’11 and 200 pounds) doesn’t stand out, but his football play on the field does. Bowen’s football intelligence and positional versatility are huge positives. I feel he has true potential as a single-high player but is also someone who has the chops to man down the nickel position in the NFL. That duality will be highly coveted by scouts and general managers in the coming months looking to bolster their franchise’s secondary. He’s just consistent with most everything he does, which is a reason I’ll be keeping a close eye on him as the collegiate season continues. You can catch Bowen in action against the Michigan Wolverines in today’s early slate of games. Vicari Swain — Cornerback — South Carolina Fans might not want me to talk about the potential of Denver opting to use an early round selection on a cornerback in the 2027 NFL Draft, but here we are. I do expect one of Ja’Quan McMillian or Riley Moss to get an extension with the team. However, it seems unlikely both will earn well-deserved extensions. The good thing is they have 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron already as an in-house replacement option for one of them. He has been cross trained at both the slot and boundary spots. While some were down on his lack of impact as a rookie, I’m optimistic about his NFL potential. The Broncos are facing a situation where their All-Pro return specialist Marvin Mims Jr. may depart in free agency after this season. Finding players with his dynamic return ability are rare. That’s why I thought I’d bring up South Carolina cornerback Vicari Swain—who is an impressive cover corner who makes big plays on defense but is also one of the nation’s elite punt return specialists. During his first two seasons with the Gamecocks, Swain (6’0”, 193 pounds) was primarily a backup player. Last season, he appeared in every game and had three starts. Even though he wasn’t a full-time starter, his impact (especially at slot) was evident with 28 tackles, 1 sack, 2 forced fumbles, along with 2 interceptions and 5 pass breakups. He also had 19 punt returns for 302 yards and three touchdowns. This season he is poised to make a greater impact for his team. As of now, most outlets have Swain as Day 2 selection. While he doesn’t have a tough matchup this week, you can catch him this evening when South Carolina hosts Towson.

title: Broncos at Chiefs 5 questions: What are the expectations in KC?
summary: For the first time in nine seasons, the Kansas City Chiefs failed to win the AFC West. If that wasn’t enough, the Chiefs didn’t even make the AFC Playoffs. To pour a little salt in the wounds, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL. After nearly a decade of success, the 2025 season was a nightmare for […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs attempts to evade Tuli Tuipulotu #45 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in nine seasons, the Kansas City Chiefs failed to win the AFC West. If that wasn’t enough, the Chiefs didn’t even make the AFC Playoffs. To pour a little salt in the wounds, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL. After nearly a decade of success, the 2025 season was a nightmare for Kansas City. Now comes the opener on Monday Night Football against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium. To get a feel for the expectations Chiefs Kingdom has (and what the reality is), plus why this season will be different, we go “behind enemy lines” with Maurice Elston from Arrowhead Pride . MHR: How is Chiefs Kingdom feeling heading into the season? What are the expectations for the team, and what is the reality? Maurice : I think Chiefs Kingdom will always lean toward the overly optimistic side of things as long as Andy Reid is the head coach and, more importantly, Patrick Mahomes is the quarterback. With those two here, it will always be Super Bowl or bust, unfortunately. I don’t think that expectation is far from reality, though. If the Chiefs can find a way to be more efficient in one-score games this season, I believe they will be a playoff team. And if Mahomes gets into the playoffs, he immediately becomes the quarterback no other team wants to face. MHR: Why will this season be different for KC? Tied into that is Patrick Mahomes going to be Patrick Mahomes? Maurice : I don’t believe Mahomes would be on the field if the Chiefs’ leadership and training staff didn’t believe he could play like his normal self. The Chiefs understand what he means to the franchise, so they aren’t going to jeopardize his long-term health just to get him on the field for opening night. What should make this season different is the supporting cast around him. The Chiefs added reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III, giving the offense an explosive running back who can take some of the pressure off Mahomes. He should also finally have his full wide receiver room healthy and on the field together—something that never happened last season. If Mahomes is healthy and Kansas City can pair its complete receiving corps with a legitimate running game, this offense should look much different. MHR: What do the Chiefs need to do offensively and defensively against Denver on Monday night? Maurice : Offensively, the Chiefs need to run the ball effectively enough to keep Denver’s defensive front honest. Kansas City may also need to provide additional help on the left side of the offensive line to give Mahomes time against a Broncos defense that led the NFL in sacks last season. I expect Andy Reid to be prepared for that and use the running game, quick passes, and different protections to slow down Denver’s pressure. Defensively, Kansas City’s first priority should be stopping the run and forcing Denver into a pass-heavy game. If the Chiefs can put Bo Nix in obvious passing situations, I like Steve Spagnuolo’s chances of creating pressure and disguising coverages against him. MHR: What do you make of the current spread at FanDuel Sportsbook? And what is your best bet? Maurice : As of now, the Chiefs are 2.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook, and I think that spread is right where it should be. These teams are evenly matched, but Kansas City is playing at Arrowhead with Mahomes back under center. My best bet is Chiefs -2.5 because I expect Kansas City to squeeze out a victory with a late field goal, winning by three points. MHR: How does the opener play out, and what are your expectations? Maurice : I expect this game to remain tight throughout. Neither team’s starters played many preseason snaps together, so I anticipate some early rust—particularly from both offenses. The defenses could control the first half before the quarterbacks and play-callers begin settling into the game. Ultimately, I believe the opener will be decided late in the fourth quarter. Mahomes leads one final drive, Kansas City kicks the winning field goal, and the Chiefs open the season with a three-point victory.

title: Scouting the Enemy: Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The Denver Broncos kickoff their 2026 gridiron campaign defending their AFC West title against their longtime rival Kansas City Chiefs. For the first installment of Scouting the Enemy this year, we will take a look at how the Chiefs performed in 2025, their key offseason additions and departures, as well as their X-Factor players on […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Tight end Travis Kelce #87 of the Kansas City Chiefs signals to stay in the game during the first quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos kickoff their 2026 gridiron campaign defending their AFC West title against their longtime rival Kansas City Chiefs. For the first installment of Scouting the Enemy this year, we will take a look at how the Chiefs performed in 2025, their key offseason additions and departures, as well as their X-Factor players on offense and defense for Monday Night Football . 2025 Kansas City Chiefs Season Review The Chiefs finished last season with a 6-11 record . It was the first time they had missed the playoffs since 2014 and their first losing season since 2012 when Romeo Crennel was head coach. 2026 Kansas City Chiefs Offseason Additions and Departures The big addition for the Chiefs over the offseason was signing running back Kenneth Walker III in free agency. They also brought back cornerback L’Jarius Sneed, who had spent the past two years with the Tennessee Titans. Kansas City also traded a late 2027 draft selection to bring in former first-round quarterback Justin Fields to be the backup to Patrick Mahomes. The biggest departure came via trade, with the GM Brett Veach trading two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams. Additionally, cornerback Jaylen Watson and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu both signed with the Washington Commanders in free agency. With extra selections after the McDuffie trade, the Chiefs focused on shoring up their defense. Kansas City moved up to get Mansoor Delane at the six slot in 2006 NFL Draft. The former LSU standout was touted as the best cover corner last April. Additionally, they added versatile Clemson defensive lineman Peter Woods late in the first round. To bolster their pass rush productivity, the Chiefs picked R Mason Thomas out of Oklahoma in the second round. I also liked their fourth-round selection, Oregon slot cornerback Jadon Canady. Their fifth-round picks, running back Emmett Johnson and wide receiver Cyrus Allen could be situational players for them as rookies. Offensive X-Factor: Running Back Kenneth Walker III All eyes are on the health of Patrick Mahomes and how he will return from an ACL injury last season. If he can revert to prior form, the Chiefs are likely title contenders. However, my X-Factor for them in Week 1 is free agent addition Kenneth Walker III. Last year’s Super Bowl MVP, Walker inked a 3-year, $34 million dollar deal this offseason to bolster their rushing attack. Walker had a productive 2025 season with 221 rushes for 1,027 yards, and 5 touchdowns. He added 31 receptions for 282 yards as a receiver out of the backfield. The creative playcalling of Andy Reid coupled with Walker’s skillset will be a big challenge for the Broncos. Limiting his impact will be critical to not only win the time of possession battle but also come out of Arrowhead with a victory. The Broncos can’t afford to let Walker run wild. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his defensive front seven certainly have a tough challenge in the opening game. Defensive X-Factor: Cornerback Mansoor Delane The Chiefs opted to do a little bit of reshuffling in their defensive backfield this offseason. Their general manager has a history of trading away cornerbacks right before they are set to earn mega-extensions. Sending off McDuffie to the Rams was emblematic of that. That means rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane will have to play a huge role for them this season. On Monday night against the Broncos, he will certainly have his hands full. With Denver adding Jaylen Waddle into the mix, Delane will be tasked with not just covering him, but also having to battle longtime veteran Courtland Sutton as well. Both wide receivers have unique skill sets which will certainly test his abilities. Delane’s talented merited such an early selection, but I don’t see Bo Nix and the Broncos being shy about throwing in his direction. I expect them to test Delane early and often. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Chiefs The Chiefs are a tough draw for the Broncos in Week 1, but I’m confident the Broncos can find a way to victory. As noted above, slowing down Walker will be a huge part of that. With it being a road game, slowing him down and finding a way to win the time of possession battle will be crucial. Not only that, but finding a way to force some turnovers on defense will be huge if Denver wants to earn a victory. That’s been a focal point of theirs over the course of the summer. Now it’s time to put their plan in action on Monday Night Football . On offense, the Broncos will need to limit their miscues and be efficient on the ground and through the air. The team’s rushing attack needs to hit the ground running, and Bo Nix needs to dial up a good game and find a way to get some explosive plays against their defense. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 24, Chiefs 17.

title: Broncos coaches face major test against the Chiefs
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! When you face the Kansas City Chiefs, there are always built-in challenges. Andy Reid. Patrick Mahomes. Steve Spagnuolo. And that’s just to name a few. The last one may not get as much attention as the other two, but it doesn’t lessen the task in front of Bo Nix, Davis Webb, […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - August 18 : Denver Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph answers questions from reporters at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! When you face the Kansas City Chiefs, there are always built-in challenges. Andy Reid. Patrick Mahomes. Steve Spagnuolo. And that’s just to name a few. The last one may not get as much attention as the other two, but it doesn’t lessen the task in front of Bo Nix, Davis Webb, Sean Payton, and the Denver Broncos offense. Summit White helmets 🔛 pic.twitter.com/AWpem3F3Ft — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 10, 2026 Spagnuolo is one of the best defensive coordinators ever, and his defenses are always difficult to go against, especially at home. Welcome to your first game of calling plays, Mr. Webb. “My mind has gone back a few times,” Webb said to the media on Thursday after practice. “In Buffalo, we played him often. We were usually on the losing end of that. Then he was our interim head coach for the last four or five weeks of the season, I believe, back in the day (with the New York Giants in 2017). I was like a scout-team quarterback, so back in the day, only the defensive players and myself got banana pudding from his wife. I miss ‘Spags.’ He’s a great dude and one of the best defensive coordinators in this game’s history. He’ll be a tough challenge for us out of the gate.” It’s similar to what Vance Joseph will face in going against Reid, Mahomes, and Eric Bieniemy. What adds to all of this is Mahomes’s return from a knee injury and a season in which the Chiefs failed to make the playoffs. “I think Patrick is going to be Patrick,” Joseph said to the media on Thursday. “In my opinion, he wouldn’t play if he couldn’t be himself. He’s had a good summer and spring to kind of rehab, and from what I hear and from what I read, he’s feeling great. So we expect Patrick to be Patrick, and he is obviously the guy in the league who wins an awful lot. He’s obviously motivated, and it’s a big game for them; it’s a big game for us, obviously. It’s Week 1, so everyone’s healthy and excited to play, so we’ll get his best shot.” What helps with all of this is having a head coach like Sean Payton. Joseph and Webb know they have someone who has tons of experience and knowledge. “I think gameday will be similar to what it has been in the preseason,” Webb said. “He’s been awesome throughout the game. He has his few pointers here and there, and they are all productive pointers. He’s 62 years old, and I’m 31. It is what it is. He has a lot more experience than me. Even the last few nights, he’s given us five to 10 nuggets that have really benefitted us going through the game plan meetings. It’s still a Sean Payton offense, and that is how we want to operate it.” Added Joseph: “He is fabulous in front of the team. He can paint a picture each week for each opponent that we’re playing. That Wednesday meeting is interesting because he can paint a picture, and most of the time, that’s the picture that happens. That’s his strength. He can explain opponents, he can explain the keys to victory, things we have to do to win games, and he’s usually right. So I think for him, he can spend more time doing that. Obviously, he’s still involved with the offense, and the defense and special teams because he’s responsible for all of it, but he has more time now to do his thing. “That’s his best trait, in my opinion, is team building, keeping guys on edge, and keeping everybody humble and moving forward. When it’s really good, he’s hard. He keeps you going. That’s old school (Pro Football Hall of Fame) Coach (Bill) Parcells. When it’s bad, he shows grace, and that’s also old school in Coach Parcells. So he’s in his element, he’s happy, he’s getting rest. So it’s been fun to watch him work.”

title: Detroit Lions release Levi Onwuzurike and rookie DL
summary: The Detroit Lions announced on Friday that they’ve released veteran defensive tackle Levi Onwuzurike from the 53-man roster and rookie defensive lineman Tyre West from the practice squad. It’s a bit of a surprise with Onwuzurike, who was the team’s second-round pick in 2021. The defensive lineman has struggled with injuries for most of his […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - AUGUST 29: Detroit Lions defensive end Levi Onwuzurike (95) during a NFL preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on August 29, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced on Friday that they’ve released veteran defensive tackle Levi Onwuzurike from the 53-man roster and rookie defensive lineman Tyre West from the practice squad. It’s a bit of a surprise with Onwuzurike, who was the team’s second-round pick in 2021. The defensive lineman has struggled with injuries for most of his NFL career—a back injury for the first few years before an ACL injury zapped all of his 2025 season. In total, he’s played in just 42 games and made only 10 starts. Over that time, he’s tallied 68 tackles, 3.5 sacks, and 16 quarterback hits. That said, his 2024 season was very promising: 28 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 45 pressures, and 13 quarterback hits. It’s unclear why the Lions made the move, but there is a rational explanation that could involve Onwuzurike coming back to the team as soon as next week—or even on Saturday on the practice squad. There is a rule in the NFL that any veteran who is on the Week 1 53-man roster will see his annual salary become fully guaranteed for the year. Given Onwuzurike’s injury history, the Lions may have wanted to avoid this, and therefore will add him back to the 53-man roster next week. There’s even a chance Onwuzurike signs to the practice squad on Saturday, gets elevated using one of the team’s two standard elevations, and plays on Sunday vs. the Saints without having his salary guaranteed. Or, it’s entirely possible the Lions have opted to move on. We’ll have to wait and see. As for West, he struggled to make an impact during training camp and barely got any playing time during the preseason. It’s possible the Lions bring him back to further his development after some roster shuffling. Detroit will likely have one more set of roster moves before Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. On Saturday, the team will announce any more moves and practice squad elevations by 4 p.m. ET.

title: Best Detroit Lions content of the week: Jack Campbell’s personal, professional growth

It’s as if he was born to be an off-ball linebacker in the National Football League. From his physical attributes on the field, to how […]
full_text: Sometimes when you hear certain people speak, you can quickly understand why they are great at what they do. Such is the case with Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. It’s as if he was born to be an off-ball linebacker in the National Football League. From his physical attributes on the field, to how he wired between the ears, Campbell is a special player. Colton Pouncy of The Athletic sat down with the Cedar Falls, Iowa native and wrote a fantastic piece that details Campbell’s unique perspective on not only football, but on life, too. “He’s doing Hall of Fame stuff now,” Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill told The Athletic . “He’s trying to reach that type of level now because he’s already one of those guys. He’s on his way there, in my opinion.” Originally the 18th overall selection in the 2023 NFL Draft, many (including myself) were confused by the Lions’ decision to take Campbell. With that said, sometimes it feels really good to be so incorrect. On top of earning his first All-Pro honors in 2025, Campbell has also established himself as one of the leaders on the defensive side of the ball. “Anything that Jack says, people listen,” Dan Campbell said of his middle linebacker. “He’s earned that.” Jack Campbell remembers what you said about him, back in 2023. “F.” “Reach.” Something about positional value, right? And yet here he is, fresh off the year that changed everything, proving his people right. He’s ready to talk about it. Story, unlocked and free to read ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/s0Nssv2eF9 — Colton Pouncy (@colton_pouncy) September 11, 2026 You can read the entire article from Pouncy right here . And now onto the rest of the best Lions content from this week. Without spoiling the direction in which this interview with Brad Galli and Lions right guard Tate Ratledge goes, it involves how easy it has been for Lions All-Pro left tackle Penei Sewell to make the change. Will Burchfield of 97.1 with another excellent piece where he examines whether or not Lions quarterback Jared Goff will ever get the respect that he is due? Jared Goff answered his critics. Will he ever get the respect he's due? "For me and him, we just gotta win the Super Bowl. If Jared wins the Super Bowl, it’ll shut a lot of people up, and I can’t wait. I want that for him so bad," says Amon-Ra St. Brown: https://t.co/V9pCgdZX34 — Will Burchfield (@burchie_kid) September 11, 2026 Justin Rogers of the Detroit Football Network talked with Lions left guard Christian Mahogany about what he needs to work on in order to earn and keep the starting job. A lot of players won't talk when dealing with adversity. I appreciate that Christian Mahogany was willing to chat today about the ongoing battle for his starting job and what he needs to clean up to win it: https://t.co/xqK7Os3H6c — Justin Rogers | Detroit Football Network (@Justin_Rogers) September 10, 2026 Just by listening to who Goff remembers as his veterans reminds you how long he has been in the league now. Love for the OGs pic.twitter.com/imqrA8uOs4 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) September 10, 2026 For our Canadian friends, you can now download the SB Nation app! For those not in Metro Detroit or Michigan, shoutout to TiredOfFL for posting the broadcast map into The Feed. And lastly, in case you somehow missed it earlier in the week, Lions coach Dan Campbell joined the, “St. Brown Brother Podcast,” and it was as awesome as you would think.
