title: Jaguars vs. Browns: Predictions, picks, odds
summary: I don’t know about y’all, but I’ve been buzzing ever since the NFL’s season opener on Wednesday. I missed this sport so much. The mind-bending athleticism. The schematic wrinkles. The dumb penalties. The momentum swings. The cringy announcing. Inject all of it into my veins. WE’RE BACK! Everyone’s preseason predictions are about to be turned […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 15: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns runs with the ball during the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at TrEver Bank Stadium on September 15, 2024 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images I don’t know about y’all, but I’ve been buzzing ever since the NFL’s season opener on Wednesday. I missed this sport so much. The mind-bending athleticism. The schematic wrinkles. The dumb penalties. The momentum swings. The cringy announcing. Inject all of it into my veins. WE’RE BACK! Everyone’s preseason predictions are about to be turned upside down, if they haven’t been already. The undisputed Super Bowl favorites have already dropped a game. The reigning champions are vulnerable with their starting quarterback now hurt. Drake Maye is suddenly a fraud. Allow me to lean on my priors one more time before the Jacksonville Jaguars kick off their 2026 season and reshape our opinions. The Jags are 8.5-point favorites against the Cleveland Browns, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and you can find my score prediction in our staff roundtable preview . (Spoiler: I like the Jags to cover.) Let’s get to some predictions. Deshaun Watson commits multiple turnovers Watson has a 7-0 all-time record against the Jaguars — including an upset win at TrEverBank Stadium in the 2024 home opener — but today’s version is not the same quarterback who once led the NFL in passing yards and hoisted a national championship trophy. Checking in on Deshaun Watson pic.twitter.com/2kHZtPYmmH — McNeil (@REFLOG18) August 22, 2026 Checking in again on Watson pic.twitter.com/EoK7SkkRHU — McNeil (@REFLOG18) August 22, 2026 Anthony Campanile has to be salivating. As eager as his Jaguars defense is to hunt down bigger game, they’ll attack this lame duck of a Week 1 opposing quarterback with full intensity. The game plan probably states, “1) Stop the run. 2) Wreck their shit.” Jacksonville will feel the absence of Devin Lloyd and may take time to adjust to a scheme shift. “Campanile tweaked his coverage plan this offseason: Instead of leaning on traditional zone, the Jaguars will play more match concepts with man principles,” Bucky Brooks detailed . “This plays to [Travis] Hunter’s strengths as an athletic cover man with supreme ball skills. The decision to place him at left cornerback makes perfect sense, putting a bona fide ballhawk on the more-targeted side of the field.” Cleveland also has some real-deal talent in its skill group. Harold Fannin Jr. arguably poses the biggest threat to the Jaguars as an uber-athletic target hog, but touches will also be manufactured to first-round pick KC Concepion. Fellow rookie receiver Denzel Boston has reportedly been outstanding in training camp, and Quinshon Judkins profiles as one of the league’s next premier rushers. These guys are all proven playmakers… but how many plays can they realistically make with a laughable quarterback and hodgepodge offensive line? I’m guessing not many. The biggest mismatch of the game is Jaguars DL > Browns OL. By about 1:26 p.m. on Sunday, the questions around Hunter’s role and Lloyd’s departure — and the regression allegations facing the Jaguars defense — will be totally forgotten by Jaguars fans. Watson’s passing over/unders on FanDuel are set at 178.5 yards and 0.5 touchdowns. YEESH. Trevor Lawrence leads all Week 1 passers in yards/attempt If there was one turning point in the Jaguars’ 2025 season, it had to be the embarrassing Week 10 loss against Davis Mills and the division rival Texans. Inside the building, it’s simply referred to as “the Houston game.” After the L, first-time head coach Liam Coen implored his quarterback to “let it rip,” and as offensive pieces clicked into place around him, Trevor Lawrence refound himself. Jacksonville won eight straight games. Weeks 1-10 Weeks 11-18 Air yards/attempt 8.8 10.2 Yards/attempt 6.4 8.0 Passer rating 79.7 102.5 PFF grade 71.2 90.9 Big-time throw rate 3.4% 6.9% Total touchdowns 10 25 Now entering his sixth pro season, Lawrence is set to not just reach expectations, but reset them. And the Browns defense is probably weaker along the edges than down the middle. Denzel Ward remains one of the best cover defenders in the sport, but Jacksonville traded away Tyson Campbell for a reason, and Cleveland’s cornerback depth behind those two is uninspiring. Meanwhile, the Jags boast one of the league’s deeper pass-catching cores. Lawrence should have plenty of places to throw the football, and hopefully, plenty of time now that Myles Garrett has been freed. Lawrence’s passing over/unders on FanDuel are set at 236.5 yards and 1.5 touchdowns. His rushing prop of 16.5 yards is even more tempting; Lawrence had 16+ rushing yards in 10 of his final 12 games last season, and we know the Jaguars want him to keep that up . Jaguars lead by 10+ by halftime There’s a collection of Jags fans who are scared to be hurt again — and that’s okay. We understand. But personally, after a full year of watching this new regime’s process, I’m bought in. They have my trust, dammit! I do believe they’ll take care of business on Sunday. “You always want to start off fast,” Coen said at Wednesday’s presser. “You want to win for momentum purposes, whatever the next steps are. But, there’s so many teams that have poor starts and end up having really good years. So it’s like trying not to live and die by every game, especially not the first one. There’s enough on these guys as it is. “It’s wild to, to say that we’re here. It’s here, it’s now, we want to try to stay in the moment, but yeah, it’s important to have a fast start and to set the tone of kind of how you want these guys to play. You hope that your play style does show up in Week 1 because, that gives you the best chance to win, is when we play the way that we have proven to be able to do so at times.” The Jaguars are 5.5-point first-half favorites on FanDuel. title: Jaguars vs Browns: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 1
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 1’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Cleveland Browns at EverBank Stadium. Question 1: Before we get to the season opener, what are your overarching expectations for the 2026 Jaguars? Dillon Appleman: My expectations probably aren’t quite as sky-high as a lot of fans, but I certainly […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars scrambles against the Cleveland Browns during the game at EverBank Field on September 15, 2024 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 1’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Cleveland Browns at EverBank Stadium. Question 1: Before we get to the season opener, what are your overarching expectations for the 2026 Jaguars? Dillon Appleman : My expectations probably aren’t quite as sky-high as a lot of fans, but I certainly expect a playoff berth. Considering this year’s schedule and roster construction, I am comfortable predicting a 10-7 record and a Wild Card spot in the playoffs. I don’t expect a deep run at this point, but that could easily change after the first few weeks of the season. Travis Holmes : Whether the floor of the roster has been raised or maintained remains a question in the fanbase, but one thing seems clear: the front office seems to believe they’re in a stable position for continued success, and I somewhat agree. Sans an injury at the quarterback position or an extended injury in the defensive front four, I expect Jacksonville to repeat as back-to-back AFC South Champions for the first time since 1998-99. My prediction for the 2026 Jaguars is a 12-5 record to earn another home playoff game (at a limited-capacity EverBank Stadium). Gus Logue : I’ll stick to my original prediction of a 12-5 record. I really don’t see how the Jaguars could miss the playoffs unless Trevor Lawrence misses significant time. While they may not have the blue-chip talent to compete for a Super Bowl this season, they have plenty of ascending young players who could take another jump. The team is highly adaptable and ultra-competitive, equipped to solve any potential problem on game days. Few other teams can be reasonably projected to field top-12 units in offense, defense, and special teams. The best thing I can say about the Jaguars is that they are balanced — and I expect that to go a very long way in a division/conference there for the taking. Henry Zimmer : I think the Jaguars can continue the shape they were in last year for a push at another AFC South title and a playoff run. The Houston Texans seem to be a big obstacle this year, especially with Will Anderson Jr. predicted by many to be the DPOTY, but it takes a whole team effort to win the division and beyond. Trevor Lawrence continues to excel in an actual offense built around him, and we truly get to see how best to use Travis Hunter. There should be a “playoffs or bust” mentality in Duval County moving forward. Question 2: What’s the biggest question you have about the Jaguars as we enter the season? Dillon : We still don’t know what the backfield workload is going to look like between Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, so it’s hard to really envision what game plans will look like, seeing as those two provide very different skill sets. So my biggest question is: What is our identity in the run game? Travis : Can Anthony Campanile’s defense again be a top unit with Devin Lloyd’s 5 interceptions now residing in the Carolinas? A team that exited 2025 ranked second in the NFL in turnovers, losing its top defender for interceptions, poses the clear risk of a huge offseason loss. More importantly, the lack of a clear Week 1 answer in Lloyd’s vacated linebacker role presents another level of intrigue, as the team could potentially be facing a roster weakness in a spot that was previously a strength. With Jacksonville’s 2025 offense benefiting tremendously over their difficult opening five weeks from those increased turnovers, to the tune of a 4-1 record, this is no small question. Gus : Can they hang with the big boys? The Jaguars were mollywhopped last season by the Rams and Seahawks, a.k.a. the NFL’s very best pass rushes and overall teams. Do they have the guys to win big-time games against powerhouse opponents? With three primetime matchups and two international games, Jacksonville will have several opportunities in the regular season to earn some respect. Henry : The offensive line and subsequent run game might be my biggest concern. That concern is by no means breaking new ground, but it will be quite different not having Travis Etienne in the backfield, especially with his ability to catch passes. Can this offensive line keep Lawrence upright and get the ground game going, and can these backs support a healthy offensive attack? Question 3: What are you hoping to learn about the Jaguars in Week 1? Dillon : That Trevor Lawrence has mastered Liam Coen’s offense. Lawrence has never entered a season with quite the expectations as he has this season, and to live up to those, he will need to show that the system is muscle memory to him in Week 1. I’m hoping to see an effortlessness to the passing game above all else. Travis : What will this 2026 Jacksonville run-game blocking, and the associated running back rotation, resemble? In a Week 1 matchup that most expect Jacksonville to handle easily, the run game should be present and active throughout the day on Sunday. Will we get any clarity on the Bhayshul Tuten/Chris Rodriguez timeshare questions? And will this offensive line be able to better open lanes than the unit seen in late 2025? Gus : What will the spine of the defense look like? As Travis mentioned earlier, linebacker is a big question mark for the Jaguars. We can probably assume that Ventrell Miller will start opposite Foye Oluokun, but how often will he be taken off the field for Branson Combs? Will Oluokun himself be an every-down player? How often will the personnel adjust to field more defensive backs? What will the usage look like for CBs Jourdan Lewis and Jarrian Jones? Up front, what will DTs Albert Regis and Ruke Orhorhoro show in their first game as a Jaguar? Henry : The Cleveland Browns are a lesser opponent. I want to see the Jags win in all three phases, not play with their food and just win a 60-minute football game outright. There should be no reason they cannot do that. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 24, Browns 14 Travis : Jaguars 27, Browns 13 Gus : Jaguars 20, Browns 0 Henry : Jaguars 35, Browns 10 What are your Week 1 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! title: 5 Questions with Dawgs By Nature: Containing KC Concepcion is Priority No. 1
summary: As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, we exchanged questions with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Browns have a brutal QB situation and traded away a legendary defender. Do you expect Cleveland to still be competitive this season, […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - MAY 27: KC Concepcion #1 of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on May 27, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, we exchanged questions with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Browns have a brutal QB situation and traded away a legendary defender. Do you expect Cleveland to still be competitive this season, or has the race for Arch Manning already begun? If the Browns had just received draft picks only, then it would have been a clear signal that the race for Arch Manning (or whatever quarterback) has already begun. But, the fact that Jared Verse was part of the deal was huge, and reportedly the only reason Cleveland agreed to it. Granted, Myles Garrett is in a league of his own as a two-time defensive MVP, but the fact of the matter is that Cleveland consistently had losing seasons even with his talent. Verse allows the team to still maintain a solid presence at his vacancy, and the defense in general still has the rest of the pieces that has made it successful over the years, including not allowing a 300+ yard passer in…I think it’s been 45 games? Cleveland’s defense will allow them to be competitive on any given Sunday, but the big question mark is how the offense will perform, which I’ll try to touch on more in your other questions below. With a couple of clicks you can visit Dawgs By Nature and learn everything you need to know about this week’s opponent! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Question 2: If we disregard final standings/draft order, what would a successful 2026 season look like for the Browns? A successful season for Cleveland would be if the offensive line builds some chemistry together, the young wide receivers look worthy of the draft spots they were taken, and the team has crystal-clear clarity as to how their quarterback situation will be handled next offseason. That could involve Shedeur Sanders (at some point) getting a chance to start and blowing people away, or it could involve Deshaun Watson continuing to be a liability and everyone confirming that “Cleveland is right there in terms of contention, but now we can use as many draft assets as we need to for drafting a quarterback in 2027.” Question 3: What are your expectations for first-time head coach Todd Monken? Have there been any positive or negative signs this offseason? Todd Monken seems to be in a unique position where this is going to be his only shot at being a head coach in the NFL. Even if he doesn’t say it, he knows that Cleveland could be transformed with a new quarterback next year, so if he wants to be part of that, the team needs to play relatively well. The quarterback play holding the team back will not be a red mark on him. If he makes dumb coaching decisions and the team loses motivation quickly, then he’ll be kicked to the curb and there will be no qualms about starting over next offseason. In general, he’s been fine this offseason. We’ve seen elements of the Ravens’ offense incorporated, and he’s inheriting a solid defense. He often talks candidly and has fun stories to listen to. The only thing that somewhat irked me earlier this offseason was during the quarterback competition, Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders would alternate first-team reps every other practice. Prior to one practice, Monken clearly said Sanders was going to get the first-team reps that day, but then when practice started, Watson got all of the reps instead, which made the media go into a frenzy about what it meant. The next day, when Monken was asked about it, he essentially said he changed his mind to balance things out and didn’t need to update the media. Which, on one hand I understand, but it just seems weird to switch it up so close to practice starting — like, shouldn’t that have been well-decided already? Question 4: What problems could the Browns pose for the Jaguars this week? The Swiss Army knife utilization of KC Concepcion can be a problem. Taken in the first round, we heard some good and bad things about him. But, through all of training camp and the preseason, this guy looks like he has that “it” factor. He has caught everything . He is effective on jet sweeps. He can be used on any route, he can stretch the field, he can return punts. He looks like the type of player who could be an instant Pro Bowler, and he was having success in camp regardless of what quarterback is throwing him the ball. Watching him is by far the No. 1 thing I’m eager to see at the beginning of the regular season, because we’ve seen this tremendous offseason, and now I want to see that it transforms to regular season action. Cleveland’s defense is also poised to remain a problem. Their defensive front has several top-tier players, and their secondary remains consistent. Having a new defensive coordinator, we still don’t know if the unit will suffer any dropoff from that, but I’m banking on them remaining a well-oiled machine. Question 5: Do you expect the Browns to cover as 8.5-point underdogs , and do you have a favorite player prop for the game? There are times when Cleveland can fall apart later in games from a snowball effect of negativity, but for as bad as they were last year, they still remained highly competitive in a lot of games. The Browns’ entire offensive line from last year is either retired, out of the league, or a backup on other teams in 2026, and the Browns went out and got five new starters. That could be a disaster in terms of chemistry, but also, it can’t get any worse than last year. With that improvement, plus a significant upgrade at wide receiver, the Browns have more pieces to be a better team than they were a year ago. The quarterback position might continue to hold them back from being a playoff team, but they should easily be right in these games, so I’d take the Browns to cover the 8.5-point spread. With how much I hyped up WR KC Concepcion above, I think it’s a solid bet to take the over on the 33.5 receiving yards for him. Thanks to Chris for taking the time to answer our questions. title: Chiefs readying to play Broncos in an ‘old-school AFC West blood match’
summary: It’s an early rivalry week in the football season for the Kansas City area, apparently. On Friday night, the Kansas Jayhawks are hosting the Missouri Tigers to write the latest chapter in a historic rivalry. Three days later, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos to do the same. To open his press […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s an early rivalry week in the football season for the Kansas City area, apparently. On Friday night, the Kansas Jayhawks are hosting the Missouri Tigers to write the latest chapter in a historic rivalry. Three days later, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos to do the same. To open his press conference Friday afternoon, offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy appropriately labeled the Chiefs-Broncos matchup ahead of his first game on the Kansas City sidelines since 2022. “Chiefs versus the Broncos, an old-school AFC West blood match here,” Bieniemy said. "We want to establish a physical presence…It's about having an attitude and a focused, determined mindset to go out there and inflict your will." – Coach Bieniemy on the mentality he wants to set offensively on Monday night pic.twitter.com/sM3guX0Jpn — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) September 11, 2026 There’s plenty to focus on in the game, but the Chiefs’ offense — led by quarterback Patrick Mahomes in his first game back from knee surgery — has an especially stiff challenge to begin the season. The Broncos were a top-3 defense last year in points and yards allowed. Both Bieniemy and head coach Andy Reid understand why the Denver defense has been one of the NFL’s best. It starts with defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. “Vance is a sharp guy, and he’s got a nice package full of blitzes that he has,“ Reid told reporters during his press conference on Thursday. ”I’m sure he’ll unload a few of them.“ According to Pro Football Reference , the Broncos blitzed 29% of the time last season, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. “You want to be able to play fast and not stagger yourself down to where you can’t function with a ghost,” Reid continued. “He’s got plenty of things he can throw at you for sure.” Up front, the Broncos deploy a talented group of pass rushers led by outside linebacker Nik Bonitto; he has 27.5 sacks over the last two regular seasons. Bonitto will be joined by defensive lineman Zach Allen and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss as priorities for the Chiefs to handle on pass downs. Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who totaled eight sacks last year, is currently on the Commissioner’s Exempt List . For Bieniemy, one word stands out above all else this week. “Protect, protect, protect,” Bieniemy said. “We know [Bonitto] can get after it; we know Zach Allen can get after it… I know the kid, Cooper, is not playing, who is an outstanding player. The kid, Elliss, is pretty damn good… They’re good on the line; they’re good on the second level with the backers and, obviously, they have some guys in the back end that can play.” “We will be challenged,” Bieniemy stated. “VJ does a great job, but we want to find a way to make sure we can secure victory, any which way we can.”
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Alohi Gilman knows the Chiefs’ defense will grow throughout this season
summary: As he prepares to take the field for his first game as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs, safety Alohi Gilman says that he’s feeling good about where he’s at in regard to learning a new defense under coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and defensive backs coach Dave Merritt. “I feel really good, really comfortable,” Gilman […]
full_text: As he prepares to take the field for his first game as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs , safety Alohi Gilman says that he’s feeling good about where he’s at in regard to learning a new defense under coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and defensive backs coach Dave Merritt. “I feel really good, really comfortable,” Gilman told reporters as he stood at the podium on Thursday. “They do a great job here. Just preparing us. Training camp was necessary for me to get those reps, to make mistakes, and to build and stack days… It’s never going to be perfect. But, you know, I feel really comfortable where I’m at.” Chiefs FS Alohi Gilman says his back feels better and it’s responded well to the rehab. He says he’s ready for Week 1. pic.twitter.com/zUQ6H9fJe8 — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) September 10, 2026 One hallmark of the Chiefs over the last few years has been their ability to lock down opposing teams’ top wide receivers. Last season, the Chiefs held opposing quarterbacks to under 200 yards passing per game and ranked in the top 10 in points allowed, giving up just 19.3 points per game. Part of the reason the Chiefs brought Gilman in this past offseason was to attempt to take the next step forward. “I’ve always respected the way that Coach Spags [coaches],” Gilman said. “I think it’s a good challenge for us to continue to build and to get to the place where we want to be, to be a dominant defense.” In a game where defensive backs are rewarded for turnovers above all else, and often trade off physicality for interceptions, a Dave Merritt secondary will be physical and will tackle, whether it’s on a disguised blitz or in run defense; Chiefs corners and safeties have never been afraid to lay the wood. Gilman said this isn’t by accident and is a byproduct of how the Chiefs go about business. “Just being really detailed about it. Intentional about what we do in practice,” Gilman elaborated. “Just being physical out there. They’re just going out there and playing fast. And I think that helps, getting everyone to the football.” That said, Gilman also acknowledged that with a couple of new pieces in this secondary, it may take time for everything to gel, but he’s confident it will come together. “We have a lot of good, talented guys,” Gilman reflected. “I think it’s just about staying together. Staying connected. That’s what good secondaries do. So I look forward to doing that and building on that every day. Takes time. It’s a process. But it’ll be fun down the line as we continue to grow and as we all get better as a group.” And to that point, Gilman highlighted that a defense is “Never a finished product.” “People think… you figure it out in OTAs and camp, and then you have this beautiful product,” Gilman said. “It’s an ongoing product for everyone. Obviously, a lot of new faces in the secondary. You’re going to keep growing. You don’t want to be the best player in September. You want to be the best unit defense when it’s, when it counts, all the way at the end.” The defense gets its first test right out of the gate in Week 1 as they host the defending division champions, the Denver Broncos, at home on Monday Night Football. Like a fine wine, the defense may not be fully mature yet, but we will know pretty quickly how strong it is and if the product is drinkable and gets the job done.
author: Rocky Magaña

title: The Chiefs’ 2026 season, starting Week 1, is all on Andy Reid
summary: I love Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. I think he is the second-best coach of this generation, and a top-5 coach of all time. He will likely finish his career as one of the three winningest coaches in NFL history. His future is in Canton, Ohio, at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 21: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs in action against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 21, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chiefs defeated the Giants 22-9. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images I love Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. I think he is the second-best coach of this generation, and a top-5 coach of all time. He will likely finish his career as one of the three winningest coaches in NFL history. His future is in Canton, Ohio, at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. His history is unimpeachable. But his place in the modern game? That’s very much up for debate. The Chiefs have finished 15th, 15th, and 21st in scoring offense over the past three seasons. The passing game has ranked 13th, 21st and 24th in net yards per attempt over that same span. This all took place after the Chiefs ranked among the top six in scoring and the top nine in net yards per attempt in each of the previous six seasons. What changed? Well, everything. I’m not smart enough to give you a detailed breakdown of how much the league has changed since the 2021 season, but plenty of high-brow NFL analysts can and have. My layman’s understanding of those think pieces is that defenses have become more sophisticated and, as a result, run-pass options are no longer as effective; old-school West Coast concepts have become outdated, and abandoning the running game is now a death wish. It’s almost as if the rest of the league designed their defense to shut down the Chiefs’ offense. Wait, that’s exactly what happened. The league has shifted. The Chiefs have struggled to adapt. An elite defense and an all-time great quarterback were still enough to carry Kansas City to back-to-back Super Bowl appearances in 2023 and 2024. The dam finally broke in 2025. The response will tell us a lot in 2026. Not only for the team, but for the coach. Does Reid still have it? Or has the game passed him by? This brings us to the news of the week. Left tackle Josh Simmons is not expected to play Monday night against the Denver Broncos . That’s problematic. He’s one of the three most indispensable players on the Chiefs, in my opinion. His absence doesn’t come as much of a surprise after hearing the recent reporting about his lingering back issues. What is surprising is how the Chiefs plan to replace him along the offensive line. Reid suggested earlier this week that Kansas City expects to start undrafted rookie free agent Kahlil Benson at left tackle with Jaylon Moore slotting in on the right side. Benson played his entire college career on the right side of the line, while Moore has received most of his NFL starts on the left side. It would be a puzzling decision if it’s the direction the Chiefs ultimately go. It could also work. Kansas City has more information about Benson and Moore than we do. Maybe Reid plans to go all-in on the running game, and he believes Benson makes more sense in combo blocks with left guard Kingsley Suamataia than he does spending his time cut blocking on the backside of run plays while right guard Trey Smith pulls as a lead blocker. Or maybe Reid believes this is a one-week absence for Simmons and doesn’t want to play Moore out of position for a one week spot start. Regardless of the reason, the decision will come under scrutiny. As it should. The Chiefs are entering a pivotal season in the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes. If the offseason decisions are indicative of anything, it’s this: Brett Veach and Reid believe an influx of youth on the defensive side of the ball, turnover of the offensive coaching staff, and the addition of running back Kenneth Walker are enough to get this team back into contention. Plenty of otherwise rational analysts have their doubts about that plan. We’ll see who is right. That’s why we play the games. This season is about a lot of things, but really it’s about one thing: Is Andy Reid still the elite coach he’s been for the better part of the last 25 years? If he is, the Chiefs should be just fine in his steady hands. If he’s not, we might look back at this week’s offensive line decisions as the first indication of what’s to come. All eyes will be focused on the left side of the line Monday night, but the spotlight is still on Reid.
author: Brandon Kiley

title: Chiefs-Broncos: 5 Questions with the Enemy before Week 1 battle
summary: On Monday Night, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Denver Broncos. We welcome Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report — our sister SB Nation site covering the Broncos— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Make sure you’re following Mile High Report in the SB Nation App in the lead-up to the Week 1 bout. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) meets Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) on the field after a game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. Although Nix has said that he feels normal and has no limitations, how has he looked throughout training camp and the preseason? Do you expect him to be 100% against Kansas City, particularly when using his mobility outside the pocket? Based on reports from Broncos training camp and the limited action he played in the preseason against the Green Bay Packers , Nix looks fantastic. Nix will be 100% for the Monday night opener with zero limitations in anything he does, in the pocket or his mobility out of it. He’s going to be incredibly motivated for this game. Download SB Nation’s new app for game day! Game-day discussions are so much smoother in SB Nation’s new app. Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 2. Was last season the beginning of a championship window the Broncos can sustain, or did it raise expectations to the point that anything short of a Super Bowl appearance would feel disappointing? It’s both. Denver returns 21 of 22 starters from that team, while adding Jaylen Waddle on offense. The Broncos have one of the best defenses in the NFL, and adding Waddle and Davis Webb as the new offensive play caller will help Nix and the offense be better and more consistent this season. The championship window is open in Denver, but anything less than a Super Bowl appearance will feel disappointing. The fact that the Broncos were so close will motivate this year’s team to take the next step. 3. Denver’s defense ranked second in total defense and third in scoring defense last season while leading the NFL in sacks for the second consecutive year. With most of the core returning under Vance Joseph, do you expect this unit to maintain that standard, take another step forward, or experience some regression in 2026? Look for the Broncos defense to take another step forward and be even more dominant. Creating turnovers is one area they struggled with last season. Joseph has made that an offseason emphasis. Denver will always be able to get after the quarterback; adding turnovers to the equation will make that unit even tougher and, in return, make the offense better. 4. Despite last season’s 14-3 record and deep playoff run, what is your biggest concern about the Broncos entering 2026—and why could that issue prevent them from returning to the AFC Championship Game? The biggest concern remains what it’s been the last few seasons: middle linebacker. I’m just not sold on either Alex Singleton or Justin Strnad. These guys are glorified special teamers. The reason they’re not exposed more is because of how deep and talented the rest of Denver’s defense is. Clearly, Sean Payton and George Paton feel differently. As long as these two don’t get in the way, it won’t prevent the defense from being one of the NFL’s best or the Broncos from returning to the AFC Championship Game. 5. Kansas City has made a clear commitment to improving its running game, headlined by the addition of reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. How well equipped is Denver’s defense to handle a more physical and balanced Chiefs offense, and what will be the key to containing Walker without giving Patrick Mahomes favorable opportunities through play action? The Chiefs bring serious questions at both tackle positions to a game where Denver can bring consistent pressure up the middle and on the edges. Add in that Denver has the best secondary in the NFL, led by the best cornerback in the league, and it comes down to the trenches. The Broncos know that if they stop the run, it limits what KC can do offensively.

title: Andy Reid reaffirms the Chiefs’ confidence in rookie Kahlil Benson
summary: When the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on the season opener of “Monday Night Football” to close Week 1, all indications are that rookie Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle. Starter Josh Simmons has been out of action since midway through training camp with a lower back ailment. Simmons missed this week’s […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Offensive tackle Kahlil Benson #70 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches NFL preseason game action in the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on the season opener of “Monday Night Football” to close Week 1, all indications are that rookie Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle. Starter Josh Simmons has been out of action since midway through training camp with a lower back ailment. Simmons missed this week’s initial practice on Thursday. The decision is curious in that Benson went undrafted in April — and only signed with Kansas City after trying out at the team’s rookie camp. Also, the former Indiana and Colorado talent never took a snap at left tackle in college. Benson has played almost exclusively on the right side both at tackle and guard. Speaking before Thursday’s practice, head coach Andy Reid expressed confidence in Benson’s ability to hold down the fort for Simmons. Reid also defers to his own years of experience and that of the coaching staff. “He’s done a nice job for us,” Reid remarked of the rookie. “He’s obviously shown us that he has the ability to play, and we wouldn’t put him in there if we didn’t think that. “We’ve all been through that. I think when we first got hired, we thought we probably were pretty good at it. So, I want his confidence to be that and go out and play and just use his abilities and write a good story.” "Kahlil Benson has proven, at least in preseason up against what Spags has put out there in training camp, that he's held up pretty good." – @BaldyNFL on the undrafted rookie potentially starting at left tackle for the Chiefs (via @PatMcAfeeShow ) pic.twitter.com/UGnwbK95h6 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) September 10, 2026 Benson will be tasked with protecting star quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who is expected to see his first game action on Monday since tearing multiple knee ligaments in December. A decade of NFL experience has taught Mahomes to be ready when backups are on the field. He trusts that Benson will get the job done — and the possible downgrade on the offensive line does not change his own responsibilities. “Either way,” said Mahomes on Thursday, “you’ve got to roll. That’s the beauty of football is that it’s next man up, and you have to go up there and compete. These guys have gotten a ton of reps in training camp. They’ve gotten a ton of reps throughout their entire life, and they’re going out and living their dream as well. “So, I’ve got trust in anyone that the coaches put out there, because I know that they’ve worked their tail off to be at that spot. There’ll be mistakes here and there, but at the end of the day, you’ve got to go out there and trust those guys and make the plays whenever the plays need to be made.”

title: Predicting the Chargers 2026 win record: Recent history says Bolts will be fine
summary: With the Chargers kicking off against the Cardinals in little more than 48 hours as I’m typing this, it’s about time I throw my hat in the ring with a season record prediction for 2026. After winning 11 games in each of the last two seasons, the Chargers rightfully deserve some more respect. They have […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh prior to the game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers on August 20, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. (Photo by David Dennis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the Chargers kicking off against the Cardinals in little more than 48 hours as I’m typing this, it’s about time I throw my hat in the ring with a season record prediction for 2026. After winning 11 games in each of the last two seasons, the Chargers rightfully deserve some more respect. They have shown some level of consistency and that’s something I want to give them credit for, but MAN this schedule looks daunting. Outlooks have changed ever-s0 slightly after Patriots-Seahawks and 49ers-Rams, but overall it’s still one heck of slate to get through. Let’s go ahead and dive in. Week 1: Vs. Cardinals The Chargers get one of the worst teams in the NFL to begin the season with the Cardinals coming to town. Veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett was named their starting quarterback which immediately puts a cap on their ceiling. There’s notable names strung throughout the rest of the roster, from Michael Wilson to Trey McBride and 2026 third-overall pick Jeremiyah Love, but I just don’t see how Arizona competes well week-in and week-out. The Bolts should win this one handedly if they come in as prepared as they should be. Arizona’s defense was the 27th-ranked unit in 2025 with a bottom-10 group in both pass and run defense. This should be a really good “show us what you got” moment for Mike McDaniel in his first real game as offensive coordinator. Result: Win (1-0) Week 2: Vs. Raiders Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers just underwent a surgery to clean up his meniscus and is expected to miss “at least one game, maybe two” according to multiple reports. Most meniscus procedures lead to more than just one to two games missed and I believe that means it could be a safe conclusion that the Chargers will avoid having to game plan for Bowers in this one. The Raiders are better at quarterback this year having traded Geno Smith for Kirk Cousins, but exactly how much better is that? The last time Cousins faced the Chargers defense, he was picked off four times and threw zero touchdowns. In that game, he had a MUCH better cast of skill players around him compared to who he is throwing to this year. Aside from Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty, you’d be hard-pressed to find a casual fan who could name a single Raiders wideout. This should be another dominant win by the Chargers. Result: Win (2-0) Week 3: @ Bills Traveling to Buffalo to face the Bills is just the first step in a long journey through an absolute gauntlet for the Chargers. From Week Three to 10, the Chargers will have four former NFL MVPs and the reigning Super Bowl champions, plus two other teams that have won a Lombardi Trophy this decade. This stretch will make or break the 2026 season. It will tell us exactly where the Chargers sit in the pantheon of the NFL’s best. Their first road game coming against Josh Allen is a heck of a task and I don’t see the Chargers being up to challenge coming off two cupcake matchups. I think they compete, but Allen’s experience in tight games against other AFC powerhouses will ultimately be the difference here. Result: Loss (2-1) Week 4: @ Seahawks There’s a real chance the Chargers do not have to face the Seahawks with Sam Darnold at quarterback if his hip injury ends up being severe enough. Initial X-rays did not show a fracture, but don’t be surprised if Seattle plays it cautiously with their quarterback. They need him later in the year much more than they do now, especially after they escaped the Patriots in Week One. If Drew Lock is their quarterback, I think the offense will do enough to get the job done. That is, as long as the LA defense can keep a lid on explosive plays which played a big role in Seattle’s win on Wednesday night. Result: Win (3-1) Week 5: Vs. Broncos There’s been a ton of discourse on the Broncos this offseason centered around just how good Bo Nix really is compared to some of the other veteran and elite passers. In my opinion, he’s found the best way his game translates to the NFL and it helps to have an elite defense behind him. However, the Broncos were not as dominant last year as their record made it look like and regression will come. The pass rush was near historic levels and Nix’s offensive line played out of their minds compared to how they look on paper. I think the Chargers utilize home-field advantage and pull out a close one in another AFC West showdown. Result: Win (4-1) Week 6: Vs. @ Chiefs I expect the Chiefs to rebound in some fashion this year, but I can’t imagine it being a massive one. Patrick Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL and Travis Kelce is one year older. The offense did not get that much better, even with the addition of running back Kenneth Walker. The wide receiver room is still fast, but that’s about it. Andy Reid is still a top-three coach in the NFL and Mahomes is arguably still the best quarterback in the NFL (for now.) Those two will yank and drag the Chiefs to a better record than their roster suggests they should have, but I don’t see them being the same monolithic threat they were before the 2025 season. These two teams always play it close until the end and I see the Chargers getting that final bounce their way at home. Result: Loss (4-2) Week 7: Bye Holding a 4-2 record at the bye is honestly a miracle. Several things went their way luck-wise and the team managed to take care of business when they needed to against some tough opponents. This record gives them much more room for error down the stretch. Week 8: @ Rams Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald — the latter of which is probably up and running at full speed by this point in the season — are the only reasons I need to foresee a Chargers loss here. The interior of the offensive line is nowhere near good enough to handle Donald, even at this age, and Garrett is just him. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year in the NFL. The Chargers will have to hold onto their seats no matter which unit is on the field. If the offense isn’t having its hands full with their pass rush, the defense will be tasked with stopping Matthew Stafford (reigning MVP) while he’s throwing it around the yard to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Even while technically playing at home, I think Sean McVay will be too much to handle for defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary. Result: Loss (4-3) Week 9: Vs. Texans That defense is going to be great. It’s going to terrorize offense all season long. My confidence here resides in Slater and Alt being healthy on top of McDaniel being able to call a much better game than Greg Roman did two years ago. McDaniel will have a much better plan getting the ball out of Herbert’s hands safely. That playoff game was still in reach despite the interceptions thanks to the LA defense. They only allowed two touchdowns to the Houston offense and mainly hunkered down and held them to field goals despite the numerous sudden change situations. The Texans defense also scored nine points on their own (pick-six, 2-point conversion return) which is a rarity. I think this matchup showed a fluky cocktail of bad decisions and miscues and that leads me to believe this game will be much closer this time. And yes, I’m mainly ignoring their matchup last December when the team’s otherwise elite defense allowed two massive passing touchdowns on back-to-back drives due to wildly-blown coverages. Result: Win (5-3) Week 10: @ Ravens Jesse Minter got a head-coaching job for a reason. He’s going to have this unit ready to go and the Chargers need to be ready. Offseason additions of of Trey Hendrickson and Calais Campbell have this front seven looking very strong. That’s not even naming the likes of linebacker Roquan Smith and defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike who looks like he’s getting…

title: Chargers-Cardinals Game Preview: 3 things to watch in Week 1
summary: We’ve finally hit the regular season of what was a long and hyped offseason. The Chargers will finally take the field inside SoFi Stadium on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, bringing in the start of a new era for the Bolts as they trot out two new coordinators. Mike McDaniel is bringing his explosive and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 20: Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers carries the ball against the San Francisco 49ers in a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve finally hit the regular season of what was a long and hyped offseason. The Chargers will finally take the field inside SoFi Stadium on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, bringing in the start of a new era for the Bolts as they trot out two new coordinators. Mike McDaniel is bringing his explosive and dynamic offense from his time in Miami to the Bolts and quarterback Justin Herbert. Chris O’Leary, a former understudy of Jesse Minter, will look to keep his unit amongst the best in the NFL while putting his own spin on things. While the Cardinals are not the most intimidating of opponents to open your schedule with, they’re nonetheless a team who could surprised if not taken seriously enough. The Chargers must button up and inflict their will on Arizona to show they’re still the same team who won 11 games in each of the last two seasons. With that said, here are three things to watch for when these teams take the field on Sunday afternoon. 1.) Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt get tough task in season opener Sunday’s game against the Cardinals will be the first time Rashawn Slater will step on the field for the Chargers since January of 2025 (wild card loss to the Texans). That was the last time both him and Alt were on the field together, as well. In Week One, they’ll get a tough draw in edge rusher Josh Sweat who is coming off a career-high 12 sacks last season. That number may be a bit of an outlier as Sweat only accumulated 47 total pressures on the year which was his lowest since the 2021 campaign. Whether that means he has simply gotten better at finishing or not, it’s still an excellent opportunity to show just how dominant this duo is when healthy. 2.) How will Chris O’Leary look in his debut as an NFL play-caller? After one season calling the defense for Western Michigan, O’Leary is entering his first season of any kind as a NFL coordinator. He is also following in the footsteps of Jesse Minter who made the Chargers a top-five defense in each of his two seasons in Los Angeles. In his first game as DC, O’Leary gets the pleasure of putting a game plan together to stop the likes of tight end Trey McBride, wide receivers Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr., and running back Jeremiyah Love. McBride is coming off a historic season for a tight end where he caught a single-season record 126 passes. Wilson also just got extended after his first 1,000-yard season. Love is a little bit of an X-factor here. He missed most of August with an ankle injury and recent reports have not been confident that he will be 100 percent in time for Sunday’s game. Mike LaFleur said he will play, but how many snaps remains to be seen. Either way, Love went third overall in the draft for a reason. He’s equally dangerous as a runner and a receiver. Here’s to hoping O’Leary has his front seven locked in. 3.) Which skill players will show out in Mike McDaniels’ first game as OC? It’s been a long offseason of hype for McDaniel and what his offense will do for guys like Quentin Johnston, Ladd McConkey, and Omarion Hampton. Now, it’s finally time to see which will come to fruition. Hampton stands to gain the most in his second year after injuries took most of what was otherwise a very promising rookie campaign when you look at his per-game numbers. If Hampton truly gets the lion’s share of the opportunities, a massive season is seemingly assured. Reaching 1,000 yards of total offense seems like a given, but what about 1,500+? Not a crazy prediction if he manages to play all 17 games. As for McConkey, he will look to get back to his rookie form where he recorded 82 receptions for 1,149 yards during the regular season, on top of the 197 he posted against the Texans in the wild card round. Reaching 100 receptions for the first time is in the realm of possibility. When it comes to Johnston, he has back-to-back eight-touchdown seasons while posting no more than 735 yards in a season. Depending on his exact role week-to-week, he could also be one to either push for 1,000 yards or make it to double-digit receiving touchdowns. The latter of which hasn’t been done since Mike Williams caught 10 touchdowns (11 total scores) during the 2018 campaign.

title: I wouldn’t want to be Jaxson Dart next week
summary: Myles Garrett is still the best defensive player in football and that makes the New York Giants the unfortunate team that has to face him when he’s as pissed off and motivated as he’s ever been. With as many factors working in Garrett’s favor as were working against him in Week 1, that makes Giants […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Myles Garrett is still the best defensive player in football and that makes the New York Giants the unfortunate team that has to face him when he’s as pissed off and motivated as he’s ever been. With as many factors working in Garrett’s favor as were working against him in Week 1, that makes Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart the unlucky person who is likely to be desperately trying to evade the reigning Defensive Player of the Year next week. I wouldn’t want to be Dart on September 20. Ignore the Box Score This was the fourth time in Garrett’s career that he recorded no tackles and no sacks, but it doesn’t mean that he was sluggish. In fact, Garrett recorded a get-off of 0.59 seconds, per Next Gen Stats , which isn’t just “elite”. It’s more elite than elite. Garrett, the NFL’s top pass rusher, had a get-off of .70 seconds in 2025. This was significantly quicker than that. Likely one of the best marks of his career for a single game. He also had five pressures, according to NGS. If you’re worried about Garrett because he didn’t get a sack, that’s absurd. He had two games in 2024 when he recorded zero tackles, and then the next season he had 23 sacks. He had 14 sacks in 2024. Trent Williams vs Andrew Thomas Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas is a great tackle, but he’s not Trent Williams. Garrett’s first assignment as a Ram was to go against the best left tackle in the NFL, a first ballot Hall of Famer. Credit to both players, as giving up zero sacks to Garrett is an accomplishment few tackles will enjoy, but Trent Williams is one of them. Myles Garrett vs. Trent Williams all 1v1 reps from Week 1 pic.twitter.com/8htoDUHCYs — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 11, 2026 Expect Chris Shula to find additional ways to get Garrett free to the quarterback next week, like finding opportunities to match him against right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor. Brock Purdy vs Jaxson Dart Purdy had a sack rate of 3.73% last season, which is elite. Dart had a sack rate of 9.36%, which is not. Jaxson Dart might be sacked 10+ next times next week. Australia vs Los Angeles Garrett had to travel across the world for his first game with the Rams. He’ll still have to travel across the world before this game, but he’ll have about 10 days to prepare in the same place, and the drive to work might only take 45 minutes or an hour depending on traffic. Addition of Aaron Donald? Week 2 could see the return of Aaron Donald, another player worthy of double-teams alongside Myles Garrett. If Donald is 80% of the player he once was, that’s about 80% greater than Braden Fiske. Healthier vs Less Healthy When Turf Show Times reported that Garrett was missing practices due to his knee, there were times when those articles were met with a lot of pushback that this wasn’t real news. Come to Thursday, and now Garrett’s saying that he needs to “get back to the player I know I can be”… That’s one hell of a statement about his health. Myles Garrett said his knee didn't feel 100%, via @sarahbarshop : "This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there. And I've got to be better. I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before." — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 11, 2026 If Garrett gets his knee back up to 100% and starts practicing in full again, watch out. Myles Garrett will be just fine I wouldn’t worry about Garrett, he’s going to be one of the top players in the NFL again. I might worry about Jaylen Watson. I wouldn’t get your hopes up too high for Terrance Ferguson. But Garrett had so many things working against him in Week 1 — and so many things working for him in Week 2 — that I wouldn’t be surprised if he’s the NFL’s sack leader by October 1.

title: Rams fans react to 49ers loss: ‘Is Davante Adams washed?’
summary: In the wake of the L.A. Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, hot and lukewarm takes about the state of the franchise have been rolling in like California wildfires. full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams attempts to catch a pass in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , hot and lukewarm takes about the state of the franchise have been rolling in like California wildfires. The people at the center of those opinions are mostly the stars of the team like Matthew Stafford, Sean McVay, Myles Garrett, and Davante Adams. Is it a blip or an omen? That’s an answer to unwrap over the course of the next four games, at least, but in the meantime the best place to go for explanations is to the people who know the Rams the best: Rams fans. The Turf Show Times THE FEED section has been red hot over the past day as Rams fans have been compelled to express their feelings about the loss on Thursday. From “Good, bad, and ugly” to “Takeaways” and criticisms about the coaching, these are the voices I’d be listening to right now. To keep up with fan FEED posts, and to create your own, check out THE FEED on the right side of the home page or right here . Here are a few highlights from the FEED that I know you should check out for yourself. “My Takeaways” by BrandonHanson Is Davante Adams washed? Here’s just a snippet of Brandon’s thoughts on the game, but click the link for the FEED post itself to read the entire post. “-Warren McClendon got beat like a bongo drum repeatedly -Davante Adams is maybe washed? -Stafford looked like a QB who hasn’t played since the end of last season, couldn’t hit a pass to save his life” Do you think any of the players who looked washed on Thursday are actually washed? And who? “The good, the bad, and the ugly!!” by PARamsfan1972 What do you think is The “GOOD” this week? “ UGLY Stafford did NOT look comfortable RAMS were bullied from the opening kickoff and never fought back Garrett currently is a liability RAMS looked uninspired Analytics are great… but sometimes the human element is better” “Who’s to blame?“ – AntmanGee Is it Chris Shula? Sean McVay? Matthew Stafford? Welcome, Canada! The SB Nation App is now available in Canada. Find SB Nation app sign-up details here . How is your app experience going so far? Tell us in the comments. “Rams postmortem by Ghost” “Here’s something else about player execution: every single fan on this site could be a hall of fame coach if the players on the field perfectly executed the called play every single time. Actual good coaches are able to recognize the probability of success of the plays they call so that they can maximize their team’s chances of successfully pulling off a play. If its 3rd down with 2 yards to go, and a running play has an 80% chance of success and a passing play has a 40% chance of success, the running play should be called. If the coach calls the passing play, and the play doesn’t succeed, he shouldn’t excuse the bad call by blaming the players for not executing.” Well said. “Shula can’t gameplan: Change my mind” – RamSince68 Chris Shula couldn’t get a head coaching job last year, while several other defensive coordinators did. This season is a make or break for his future. “Hot take…” by JoolzMF Do you find it hot or cold? “The best, most complete game I watched the Rams play last season was against the Jaguars. Why? Because Puka was out, which forced McVay to look at using other players. And formations. Which worked. He finally went deeper into the playbook. So much so that, later on, 13 personnel started trending everywhere within the world of the NFL. And yet, when push comes to shove, he’ll go back to his predictable play-calling the first chance he gets.“ Great point about the Jaguars game. There’s more in the FEED. Go check it out and share your thoughts with other Rams fans.

title: Rams’ travel plan was a bust, never to be repeated
summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ travel plan for their game against the 49ers in Australia on Thursday proved a massive bust. LA’s plan was risky from the start and should never be repeated by a team traveling to the continent again. Both the Rams and 49ers had different strategies for going down under (hate how that […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Sean McVay head coach of the Los Angeles Rams looks on in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams’ travel plan for their game against the 49ers in Australia on Thursday proved a massive bust. LA’s plan was risky from the start and should never be repeated by a team traveling to the continent again. Both the Rams and 49ers had different strategies for going down under (hate how that was phrased, but I guess I’ll allow it). San Francisco got there a week before the game, while Los Angeles arrived in Melbourne just over a day before kickoff. The Rams apparently thought they had figured out jet lag, consulting experts beforehand to figure out what to do. View this post on Instagram Regardless of the thought put into their plan, it failed mightily, with a humbling and embarrassing 27-7 final on the scoreboard once the clocks hit triple zeroes. While no NFL team had ever traveled to Australia before this season, the Rams weren’t strangers to the international scene. They should have known better, even if the destination was uncharted territory for the league. In their previous three overseas games, the team was 3-0, including a win over the Jaguars in London last October, where they deployed a similar travel plan. That worked to perfection as they blew out the eventual AFC South champs by 28 points. However, the Rams had an easier time on that trip in particular because they flew directly from Baltimore to London, since they played the Ravens the week before, according to ESPN . By doing that, LA cut an 11-hour flight to seven hours. For those of you who don’t know geography well — clearly the Rams’ coaching staff didn’t — Melbourne, Australia is quite a trek from the West Coast. The flight was over double what the team flew from Baltimore to London. To illustrate how baffling the plan was from the get-go, new 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans had a priceless reaction upon learning when LA arrived. View this post on Instagram Putting a travel plan together is one thing, and executing it is another. Even with all the backing and research beforehand, all that added stress on the body from the extra-long flight clearly caught up with them. The Rams appeared sluggish throughout the game, and even an apparent super team couldn’t overcome the added challenges. When I flew to Hawaii from Chicago a few years ago, I felt incredibly off from the moment I stepped off the plane. So, I cannot imagine traveling as far as the Rams did and playing a football game in such a short window. During his postgame press conference, Sean McVay said the plan wasn’t the reason why the team “didn’t play well enough,” even if it were easy to pin the blame. View this post on Instagram Hopefully the Rams learned something valuable about international travel following this debacle. One bone-headed travel plan shouldn’t define the rest of the season. Being outclassed by a bitter rival right out of the gate is about the worst possible way to start a season, but LA still has a great team that should be fine once it returns to play on American soil. The Rams served as guinea pigs for their travel plan to Australia in the opener and were on the wrong side of things. Unfortunately, LA is now the poster child for what not to do whenever the league plays in Australia next.
author: Evan Craig

title: Sean McVay says ‘put the blame on me’ after Rams loss
summary: In the NFL, when a team loses, the head coach often gets plenty of credit, whether that’s fair or not. In a loss, the head coach typically gets heaps of blame, whether that’s fair or not. In Sean McVay’s latest press conference after his team’s latest loss to the San Francisco 49ers he makes one […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 10: Sean McVay, Head Coach of the Rams speaks to media following a Los Angeles Rams NFL media availability at Marvel Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the NFL, when a team loses, the head coach often gets plenty of credit, whether that’s fair or not. In a loss, the head coach typically gets heaps of blame, whether that’s fair or not. In Sean McVay’s latest press conference after his team’s latest loss to the San Francisco 49ers he makes one thing clear, “Put the blame on me.” Don’t worry, Coach, people will. But to be fair, McVay and his boys also get the chance to get right. This loss on Thursday night is one game out of 17. There’s plenty of time to correct the course. McVay knows that, but he also knows things don’t get corrected by just talking about it. Action, work, diligence and more will be needed to get back in the win column. Despite however tired McVay was or wasn’t, he gave a solid presser after the loss to the 49ers, and his words alone won’t fix all that the Rams need, but his intentions seem like a solid start. Said McVay, “You know there was a lot of things that didn’t go well. I think the first thing I look at is, ‘Where can I improve? Where can I put our players in better positions to have successful outcomes?’ I love that locker room, I love those guys, and this story is far from written. And I know there’s gonna be a lot of narratives that appropriately, you know, put the blame on me , and then we’ll move forward the right way.” At a certain point, only taking accountability and only saying that you will improve isn’t enough. You need to put your words into action. But after one contest into the season, taking the blame for a loss is likely the best thing McVay can do. Coach speak, wishful thinking, saying a whole lot of nothing, call McVay’s response what you want, but what else can he say after that loss? That the season is over? That one loss defines 2026 for the Rams? That the Rams stand no chance against the 49ers in their second matchup? That the Rams should leave the NFC West? When you lose and your season is over, it’s time to start looking at next year. When you lose and your season is still going, it’s time to start preparing for the next game. The Rams need to show-up much improved for their next contest against the New York Giants, and they’ll need to find a way to win, or else McVay will be taking even more blame. Now, the Rams will get back to work, and everyone will wait to see how this team responds. Put the blame on McVay after this defeat, but be ready to give the young head coach plenty of credit, if he can turn this ship around. We’ll all be watching.
author: Danny Stone

title: The Rams have invited a QB controversy
summary: It was fair to expect regression from Matthew Stafford’s MVP season heights. It’s rare to see a quarterback play at such a high level into his late 30’s—and even more rare for them to accomplish such a feat for the first time a decade and a half into their career. No one saw a total […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams laughs with Ty Simpson #15 and Stetson Bennett IV #13 on the sidelines during a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was fair to expect regression from Matthew Stafford’s MVP season heights. It’s rare to see a quarterback play at such a high level into his late 30’s—and even more rare for them to accomplish such a feat for the first time a decade and a half into their career. No one saw a total collapse coming for Stafford. He was the primary reason the Los Angeles Rams mustered only seven points in a stunning Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Because the Rams do not participate in the preseason, this is all the information we have on Stafford so far. The burden of proof that this was an isolated bad game sits atop his shoulders. We can also assume the potential of significant decline until he shows otherwise. In the same vein, most viewed Brock Osweiler earning starts over Peyton Manning as a remote chance ahead of the 2015 season. Manning was benched around Week 10 after battling injuries and losing significant power in his arm. Osweiler obviously wasn’t the Denver Broncos’ long-term solution at quarterback. The team still felt it was worth exploring alternatives. So how many more bad games will it take before the Rams entertain the idea of pulling their Cadillac—Ty Simpson—out of the showroom and taking it for a test drive? Simpson is a direct solution to many of the issues we saw from Stafford on Thursday night. Can’t score on a one-yard quarterback sneak? Well, Simpson’s mobility would be a huge advantage at the goal line. Having trouble mitigating pressure? Simpson made some of his best preseason throws on the run. Struggling with accuracy? Simpson boasted an accuracy rate over 80% in his exhibition games. For every fit Brock Purdy gave the Rams’ defense, Simpson is capable of the same. Stafford is the prototypical quarterback for an era that no longer exists. Mobility isn’t a bonus—it’s a requirement. The Rams are leaving significant meat on the bone by trotting out an immobile quarterback. Realistically Stafford could bounce back in the next three games and prove that the Week 1 disaster was attributable to jet lag or rust. We could also look back in early October and say this was the first sign he was no longer capable of performing at a high level. The Rams have invited a quarterback controversy. Simpson was drafted for 2027 and beyond. His team may need him sooner than that.
author: JB Scott

title: 3 Sean McVay philosophies that could be holding the Rams back
summary: The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a rough 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and though that can feel deflating in the moment, just keep in mind that last year’s Super Bowl champions lost to the 49ers at home in Week 1. That being said, the Rams have now incurred at […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a rough 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and though that can feel deflating in the moment, just keep in mind that last year’s Super Bowl champions lost to the 49ers at home in Week 1. That being said, the Rams have now incurred at least one loss in their first three games in five consecutive seasons. The last time that the Rams started 3-0, they won the Super Bowl and no that is not a coincidence . The most important goal for every team should be earning the number one seed. It’s just too powerful of a playoff advantage, but Sean McVay’s teams consistently fall a game or two shy of those aspirations and it’s because of slow starts: 2022: 2-3 2023: 3-6 2024: 1-4 2025: 3-2 The Rams have made the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, but they have been seeds 4, 5, and 6. That’s simply not good enough and it’s a large part of the reason why L.A. hasn’t reached the Super Bowl since 2021 and McVay has just a 3-3 postseason record since then despite Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and plenty of other stars. He even has Sean McVay . Well, at times that — the McVay effect — feels like both a blessing and a curse. I’m not saying that these are “flaws” necessarily, but with a 20-point loss to start a season in which a strong start feels imperative, these are McVay philosophies that the team refuses to even address as potential setbacks in need of re-thinking. Will anything convince McVay or the Rams to look in the mirror if they fall short of expectations again in 2026? 1 – Not playing the preseason McVay has consistently sat starters and key players in the preseason since 2018. Could this be a factor in L.A.’s consistently poor openings to the season, looking “flat” and unprepared for Weeks 1-5 ? Compare this philosophy to the victorious 49ers: Kyle Shanahan doesn’t give his starters many preseason reps, but he doesn’t seem as fearful of preseason injuries as McVay does. Brock Purdy, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, Kaelon Black, Marquis Sigle, and others were all active at points in the preseason this season. Yes, they are cautious, but not afraid. The 49ers do seem to have consistent injury problems, but none of these players got injured in preseason action. And Purdy looked far better in Week 1 than Matthew Stafford did. Tom Brady told the rookies in the nfl that he treated his preseason games like if they were superbowl games 🎥: @michaelrubin pic.twitter.com/jeV6DvNLuC — Shannonnn sharpes Burner (PARODY Account) (@shannonsharpeee) May 20, 2024 Is that less surprising than it should be given that Stafford also sits out at least half of the training camp and offseason practices? What if he wasn’t fully prepared for Week 1, regardless of how many seasons of football he’s played before. He’s never played with this exact team before. I often compare football players, especially quarterbacks, to Tom Brady and how he handled his business. Why not? He’s won seven Super Bowls. I’d pay attention. Here’s what Brady recently said about the preseason: “Preseason… Regular season… I never wanted to be taken off the field. Practice makes perfect,” the retired quarterback wrote. “Too many people looking for easy ways out these days. When you’re a football player, and it’s football season, your job is to play football.” Yikes. Sorry, that’s not how I’d want to be seen by players in the Hall of Fame. Like I was too afraid of getting hurt or too good for additional reps. Sean McVay has refused to consider if his preseason philosophy is a flawed one and I doubt that’s going to change in 2027. But if the Rams lose another game or two in the next few weeks, they absolutely should change it. 2 – “Rookies don’t matter” Let’s see: First round pick was used on a QB the team knew would be third string and inactive Second round pick was used on a TE the team knew would be fifth string and inactive Third round pick was used on a OL they team knew would be a backup this season You can definitely justify using a third round pick on Keagen Trost, especially given L.A.’s major free agency problem with the offensive line coming up in 2027. You can probably justify drafting Ty Simpson because Matthew Stafford is old for an NFL player and maybe this would be McVay’s only chance to get a decent prospect at the position to develop. Rams 2026 Draft Picks R1 – QB – Ty Simpson – Inactive R2 – TE – Max Klare – Inactive R3 – OT – Keagen Trost – Injured Reserve R6 – WR – CJ Daniels – Inactive R7 – DT – Tim Keenan III – Raiders Practice Squad — Nathan Jahnke (@FFNateJahnke) September 10, 2026 And yes, the Rams traded a first round pick for Trent McDuffie, which means Les Snead did get some immediate value out of the team’s 2026 draft capital. However, at what cost: L.A.’s extra first round pick didn’t come out of thin air. The team willingly traded out of the 2025 first round in order to acquire an additional first round pick in 2026. They don’t have a developing second-year first round talent on the roster because the Rams traded the pick to use a pick on Ty Simpson…a player who doesn’t play and won’t play any time soon. People always say “Ty Simpson or Makai Lemon” but that’s NOT the comparison you should be making! The comparison is Simpson or safety Malaki Starks? Simpson or tackle Josh Conerly? Simpson or linebacker Carson Schwesinger? Simpson or safety Nick Emmanwori? The Rams could be going into year two with the reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year (Schwesinger) instead of Omar Speights. But because the team does not value their rookie class , they have Terrance Ferguson (who had zero catches on one target) and Simpson (inactive). Flip this around on San Francisco and you’ll see that their first pick was Stribling, who is set to have a huge role but was injured in Week 1 before he got targeted; third round pick Romello Height, a defensive end who is at least in the rotation a bit; third round running back Kaelon Black, who had 70 total yards on Thursday; and fifth round pick Jaden Dugger, who had five tackles against the Rams. 49ers rookie RB Kaelon Black: · Played 44% of snaps with CMC healthy · Out-carried CMC 14-10 · Averaged 4.6 yards per carry · Most valuable handcuff in fantasy if CMC goes down And he's available in 74% of Yahoo leagues. pic.twitter.com/EHkoW4CcpO — Yahoo Fantasy Sports (@YahooFantasy) September 11, 2026 Injuries have taken a toll on San Francisco’s 2025 class and even then they had Sigle, CJ West, and Upton Stout contributing to their defense on Thursday. L.A.‘s 2025 class includes Ferguson, Josaiah Stewart (six tackles), Jarquez Hunter (traded), Ty Hamilton (one tackle), Chris Paul (released last preseason), and Konata Mumpfield (0 catches on 1 target). Any franchise that feels “F them picks” is banking heavily on their pro scouting department and their ability to find diamonds in the rough like Puka Nacua every year. However, in the past three drafts, the Rams’ best picks who are currently on the roster are: Braden Fiske (not a standout recently) Blake Corum (now half of the backfield) Kam Kinchens (maybe right now an above-average safety) Tyler Davis (a rising name at DT, but will Aaron Donald steal snaps?) And … that’s it. The team has traded Jared Verse and Hunter, and they’ve released five others (Paul, Josh Karty, Brennan Jackson, KT Leveston, and Tim Keenan). Jordan Whittington, Terrance Ferguson, Hamilton, and Stewart are still pretty irrelevant in the grand scheme of things. Beaux Limmer is a backup. And every 2026 rookie was unavailable on Thursday. Teams that make picks “for the future” can only justify that philosophy if they’re being carried by picks “from the past” and the Rams…
