title: 49ers receiver pokes fun at Rams’ travel plans
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were mauled on Thursday by the San Francisco 49ers and many are wondering if Sean McVay’s “drop in and get out” travel itinerary is the reason for their sluggishness. Even 49ers receiver Mike Evans, who said after the game: “You’ve got to give your body time to adjust, I mean obviously […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 08: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on during a San Fransisco 49ers NFL media availability at AAMI Park on September 08, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images T he Los Angeles Rams were mauled on Thursday by the San Francisco 49ers and many are wondering if Sean McVay’s “drop in and get out” travel itinerary is the reason for their sluggishness. Even 49ers receiver Mike Evans, who said after the game: “You’ve got to give your body time to adjust, I mean obviously whenever the game is scheduled you’ve got to be ready to play,” Evans said. “Maybe a few days earlier would’ve been ideal.” Evans had himself a strong 49ers debut, catching six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 27-7 49ers win. It was a humbling loss if you want to put it kindly, it was embarrassing if you want to use another adjective. A silver lining is the Rams have 16 more games to go, but their season is far from over. Matthew Stafford was off, Myles Garrett didn’t make a tangible impact, Sean McVay was out-coached and the better team, the 49ers, won. For the Niners, this is a great start to the season (minus all the injuries). For the Rams, they clearly aren’t going to walk into the Super Bowl in February as so many preseason talking heads predicted. Did it have anything to do with traveling? Maybe. But the season is a marathon, not a sprint. Oh, and rumor has it some player who wears #99 may be coming back. The Rams season isn’t done, yet. Top moments, highlights as 49ers beat Rams in Australia (espn.com) “The 49ers handled their division rivals in a statement victory, putting up 379 yards of offense. After the Rams went up 7-3 early in the second quarter, they were outscored 24-0 the rest of the way. Los Angeles had a fumble, an interception and two turnovers on downs during that span. Brock Purdy threw for 205 yards with three touchdowns, becoming the first San Francisco quarterback with three passing scores in a season opener since Colin Kaepernick in 2013, according to ESPN Research. In his debut with the 49ers, wide receiver Mike Evans had six receptions for 49 yards and a score.“ Even 49ers poked fun at Rams’ Australian travel plan after 27-7 blowout — ‘Maybe a few days earlier would’ve been ideal’ (sports.yahoo) “The 49ers deserve credit for executing well and beating the Rams. The 49ers also deserve credit for a plan that had them spend a week in Melbourne acclimating themselves for Thursday’s game, which was actually on Friday morning in Australia. The Rams showed up the day before the game and looked very little like the Super Bowl favorite they had been touted to be all offseason. They looked tired. “Sometimes sports can humble you and today was one of those days,” Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters postgame. “I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it’s about travel, or whatever, we just weren’t good enough in that window. I didn’t coach good enough.” Rams’ lopsided loss to 49ers had nothing to do with Australia travel (ramswire) “We could spend all day dissecting the issues with the defense, as there are plenty. The bigger issue was the pedestrian nature of an offense that led the league in passing efficiency and scoring a year ago. Matthew Stafford looked out of his element, as if he’s forcing throws again because he can’t figure out the defensive puzzle.” NFL draft: Rams watch starts out great for Browns fans as Myles Garrett has his ‘worst’ game in years (dawgsbynature) “The Jaguars watch has ended; long live “Rams watch” for the 2026 season. Much like Jacksonville ended up being in 2025, the Los Angeles Rams are predicted to be very good this year after the Myles Garrett trade with the Browns. Unlike with the Jaguars, Cleveland fans will be on Rams watch for a few years moving forward.“ Rams’ disaster in Australia raises the question: Should the team have followed the 49ers there earlier? (foxnews) “Let’s be clear: This is no slight to the 49ers, a team many believe will earn a playoff berth in a loaded division. Rather, the noise and astronomical expectations for the Rams made this Week 1 performance a shocker to say the least. While the “overrated” talk has already begun for football fans on social media, the question must be asked: were the Rams right to fly to Melbourne less than two days before kickoff? The Rams arrived in Melbourne on Thursday morning local time, with 28 hours until kickoff to begin their season. On the other hand, the 49ers spent close to a week getting adjusted to Melbourne time, practicing multiple times and making sure the team was ready to play a Friday morning game.“ What we learned from Rams’ ugly opening loss vs. 49ers (usatoday.com) ““I know there’s gonna be a lot of narratives that appropriately put the blame on me, and then we’ll move forward the right way,” Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. “… I don’t believe (the travel plan) is why we didn’t play well enough. I really don’t.” The travel decisions will continue to be a topic of discussion in the coming days, but there are several other factors that could be attributed to the loss. Myles Garrett will benefit from Aaron Donald’s return Garrett has proven throughout his career that he can be the primary focus on a defense and still produce. He spent some time matched up against 49ers standout lineman Trent Williams and did not have a good showing by the defenders’ standards, finishing the game without a sack or tackle.“ NFL Week 1 statistical review: San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams (pff.com) “While the 49ers were clearly the better team, the game wasn’t quite as lopsided as the final score suggests. The Rams failed to capitalize on several opportunities, with Matthew Stafford throwing an interception in scoring range and failing to convert a fourth-down quarterback sneak at the goal line. Los Angeles also gave San Francisco a short field after fumbling in its own territory.“ In Australia, the NFL’s Super Bowl favorite looked a world away from its potential (nbcsports) “The Los Angeles Rams built a star-studded roster, only to sleepwalk through a “humbling experience” in a season-opening loss.“ Rams’ Garrett, without a tackle in loss to 49ers, cites knee (espn.com) “Garrett missed most of training camp while dealing with what Rams coach Sean McVay called swelling in his knee. Garrett declined to say which knee is injured but wore a sleeve on his left leg during several practices. “I’ve got to be better,” Garrett said. “I’ve got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I’ve shown that I’ve been before.” Asked what his focus was going into Week 2, Garrett said, “Getting healthy.” “When I was out there, I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed,” Garrett said. “I wasn’t who I needed to be for my team.” Niners-Rams in Australia: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 27-7 win (nfl.com) “ Niners burst Rams’ bubble. Lying in wait for an upset in Australia, the 49ers stunned the NFL’s most-hyped squad — and their division rivals. New faces ( Mike Evans ), returning talents ( Fred Warner ) and familiar standouts ( Brock Purdy ) came to play and make a statement. Kyle Shanahan largely carved up the Rams’ revarnished defense with Purdy throwing three touchdowns passes and for 205 yards in front of 100,021 fans attending the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Australia. Though they only collected three points, the 49ers’ opening drive set a stellar tone, with Purdy guiding them 65 yards on 15 plays, completing 9 of 12 passes with Christian McCaffrey , rookie Kaelon Black , George Kittle (returning from an Achilles injury), Deebo Samuel (returning after spending 2025 with the Commanders) and Evans all catching balls. An absolute beauty of a 39-yard TD pass to former Rams WR Demarcus Robinson led to a precarious 10-7 halftime lead for the 49ers, but in the…

title: Rams Reacts: Fans were very confident about team’s direction before loss
summary: Ahead of the Los Angeles Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, many fans expressed their confidence in the team’s direction. Following a 20-point loss to begin the season, it’s fair to wonder how those fans feel now, especially when the Rams were perceived as a heavy Super Bowl contender entering the […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of the Los Angeles Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, many fans expressed their confidence in the team’s direction. Following a 20-point loss to begin the season, it’s fair to wonder how those fans feel now, especially when the Rams were perceived as a heavy Super Bowl contender entering the game. In the most recent SB Nation reacts poll, which was conducted just ahead of the season opener, a sizable chunk of the fanbase (93%) expressed confidence that the team was moving in the right direction. Heading into the season, that shouldn’t have surprised anyone, considering LA has the reigning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year on its roster. This offseason, the front office had seemingly put the team in position to make another potential Super Bowl run, or so many around the league expected. Now, a horrible loss in the first game of the season has undoubtedly dampened things. Remember, it’s a long season, and on the plus side, the Rams have yet to lose on American soil. Joking aside, there are reasons for optimism amid the darkness cast by the Week 1 loss. For starters, some fans believe the team is positioned for long-term success even after the front office’s blockbuster moves this offseason, signifying a desire to win immediately. With the post- Matthew Stafford world approaching in the near future, one fan shared that the team seems well-built to succeed whenever the veteran quarterback calls it a career. Ty Simpson will have enough solid, young pieces around him on offense and defense to find success in the post-Stafford era. Players like Puka Nacua, Kobie Turner, Terrance Ferguson, Byron Young and several others should grow alongside him as he develops. In theory, they should also keep the team in contention for quite some time, as long as the front office continues to hit on those late-stage draft picks and those key pieces are re-signed. In the survey’s comment section, fans believed the team should always be in good shape as long as Sean McVay roams the sidelines. And they should be, considering the Rams have won a Super Bowl under his watch and LA has finished with one losing record since he took over in 2017. Yes, losing in blowout fashion, to a division rival no less, is a rough way to begin the season, but that shouldn’t cause the fanbase to lose hope. The Rams still have McVay and an array of young talent to move past most challenges in their way. LA is still a Super Bowl contender and has 16 more games to live up to those lofty expectations and regain the fans’ confidence. title: Las Vegas Raiders-Miami Dolphins FEED topic: How much has offensive line improved?
summary: Silver and Black Pride is bringing back the game-day discussions on The FEED this season, where we’ll focus on and talk about a specific topic for each Las Vegas Raiders game. This won’t replace our open thread on game days, which is designed to focus on the game as a whole. For the Raiders’ Week […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Silver and Black Pride is bringing back the game-day discussions on The FEED this season, where we’ll focus on and talk about a specific topic for each Las Vegas Raiders game. This won’t replace our open thread on game days, which is designed to focus on the game as a whole. For the Raiders’ Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins , we’ll be paying close attention to how much Las Vegas’ offensive line has actually improved from last year. It’s no secret that the Raiders’ offensive line was downright putrid during the 2025 season. Hence why the front office made Tyler Linderbaum the highest-paid center in NFL history by $9 million per year , and why head coach Klint Kubiak brought over long-time offensive line coach Rich Dennison this offseason. The Silver and Black will also get Kolton Miller back after Miller missed 13 out of 17 games with an ankle injury a year ago. All of that, plus a solid showing in the preseason, gives reason for optimism when it comes to the trenches in Las Vegas. However, now it’s time to prove it by getting results on the field when the competition level rises and the games actually count. And there are still plenty of question marks within the unit. Free-agent signing Spencer Burford was never challenged for the starting left guard spot despite struggling to stick as a starter during his last two seasons with the San Francisco 49ers. Burford likely knows Kubiak’s offense better than anyone else on the line, having worked with Kubiak in San Francisco for a year (2023) and playing in a similar system under 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. But is that enough to justify a starting spot, and has the fifth-year pro turned the corner? Meanwhile, 2024 draftees Jackson Powers-Johnson and DJ Glaze are slated to man the right guard and right tackle spots, respectively. Both players have shown flashes, primarily during their rookie campaigns, but have struggled to be consistent so far. Powers-Johnson even had to fend off Caleb Rogers to keep his spot in the starting lineup. There was a moment when it seemed rookie Trey Zuhn III might push Glaze, but the latter took most, if not all, of the first-team reps at right tackle during training camp. So, it’s certainly worth keeping tabs on the right side of the line to see how the third-year pros look. Granted, the Dolphins don’t have many defensive linemen who should keep opposing offenses up at night. Like the Raiders, they hit the reset button in the offseason and moved on several notable players. Edge rusher Bradley Chubb led Miami with 8.5 sacks in 2025 , three more than anyone else, but the 30-year-old was a salary cap casualty. However, that creates an opportunity for 2024 first-round pick Chop Robinson to take on a bigger role. Robinson battled injuries and regressed last season with just four sacks, but he had six sacks and was one of the best rookie pass-rushers just two years ago. The Penn State product is known for his speed and athleticism on the edge, which has been one of Glaze’s issues. In the running game and on the interior, Burford and Powers-Johnson will be tested by Miami’s defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The nine-year pro doesn’t get a ton of attention in the media, but he’s posted double-digit TFLs in each of the last three seasons and four out of the last six. Also, Sieler is coming off a down year as a pass rusher, but he’s been plenty productive in that department, too. Having Linderbaum at center can help stabilize the interior offensive line, but the guards also have to hold up their end of the bargain. So, we’ll be focusing on how the Raiders’ offensive line performs against the Dolphins in this week’s game day discussion over on The FEED . The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on FOX (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

title: Ashton Jeanty’s availability allows Klint Kubiak to use full playbook
summary: To Jeanty or not to Jeanty? That’s the ultimate question ever since the Las Vegas Raiders’ prized sixth-0verall pick from the 2025 NFL Draft went down with a right ankle injury during a practice back on August 23. It was a collective gasp moment for the team and Raider Nation as Jeanty reportedly had to […]
full_text: (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images To Jeanty or not to Jeanty? That’s the ultimate question ever since the Las Vegas Raiders’ prized sixth-0verall pick from the 2025 NFL Draft went down with a right ankle injury during a practice back on August 23. It was a collective gasp moment for the team and Raider Nation as Jeanty reportedly had to be helped off the field and couldn’t put any weight on his right leg after he dove for a low pass and got hurt. But no fret. Jeanty is roaring to go and the Silver & Black couldn’t be happier as Las Vegas preps for it’s season-opening home date with the visiting Miami Dolphins this Sunday. Having their RB1 Week 1 is certainly a a jolt of good news for a a Raiders team needing one. Jeanty having a clean bill of health, playing, and contributing much like he did during his rookie season last year — 975 yards rushing with five touchdowns alongside 346 yards receiving for another five end zone visits as a 17-game starter in Year 1 — is much needed after a gut-punch of a loss tight end Brock Bowers is . The Raiders elite tight end reportedly hurt his knee in practice late last week which facilitated a meniscus trim this past Tuesday in Dallas. While reports surfaced Bowers is expected to miss one to two games, former NFL safety Su’a Cravens provided his personal insight on his own meniscus injury and end result , to provide an example of a longer timeframe for recovery. Not to say this is what Bowers’ timeline will be, but an example of timing and end result. Balancing Bowers’ want to return and his health will be key for Las Vegas going forward. Jeanty’s return, play time, and production can help offset the blow of losing Bowers a bit, however. “I feel really good.” Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty talks about his health heading into Week 1 against the Dolphins and the injury scare he went through during a preseason practice. 🎥: By @Sean_Zittel , Vegas Sports Today pic.twitter.com/AS7VefIbIe — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) September 10, 2026 The 22-year-old Boise State product is equal parts effective runner and receiver and with head coach Klint Kubiak now the primary offensive architect and play caller, the expectation is for Jeanty to become an all-around weapon for the Raiders going forward. And based on Wednesday footage of Jeanty practicing , there’s no noticeable limp or wrapping around his right ankle, and he’s able to burst and cut as he normally would. Las Vegas undoubtedly lost a dynamic weapon in Bowers but Jeanty provides a versatile weapon that can be a centerpiece-type. And having the 5-foot-8 and 208-pound back listed as a full participant during practices Wednesday and Thursday, per the daily injury report teams must produce, is a fortuitous turn of events for the Silver & Black. “We’re happy to have Ashton back on the field, get him ready to go,” Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said on Thursday. “He comes out with that big smile on his face, the energy he brings to this offense and to this organization is undeniable. So, just happy to have him back out working.” We’ll see if there are any limitations to Jeanty’s snap counts and usage this Sunday but a hampered RB1 would — without questions — affect Kubiak’s Raiders offense. It’s a system that is heavily predicated on the run which requires the ground game to be not on in-sync but productive to open up the rest of Kubiak’s playbook. The ability to plant and explode is vital in both the ground game and air attack and if Jeanty is limited in that fashion in any way or if the Raiders decide to be cautious and quell his snaps, the offensive strategy is going to be altered. Those sharp cuts Jeanty can make running routes as a receiver and making defenders miss or dashing through a hole as a runner is what makes the tailback dynamic and difficult to defend and we’ll see how prolonged repetition affects his ankle. It may or may not. But what’s unquestioned is Jeanty’s value as a safety valve for quarterback Kirk Cousins on check downs and as a pass protector in the backfield. However, the Raiders drafting Arkansas tailback Mike Washington Jr. in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft can mitigate that. "He's gonna be one of those 'under the radar' type of running backs" 🕵️‍♂️ @RMos_8Ball on @Raiders rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. pic.twitter.com/bg44RMRx9X — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) September 7, 2026 A much bigger running back at 6-foot-2 and 228 pounds along with 4.33-second 40-yard dash timed speed, the 122nd overall pick in the draft dazzled with 168 yards rushing on 23 carries in preseason play. While it remains to be seen how Washington operates as a receiver and pass protector in the backfield, he has the requisite size, speed, and willingness to do both — which are vital aspects in a Kubiak offense. “I’d say Mike’s done a lot of good things well. He’s come in here, he’s competed every single day,” Janocko said of the rookie. “We’ve put a lot of stress on him, whether it be physically, mentally, different things we’re asking about him. So, excited to see how that translates to a real ball game. But Mike works his butt off every day, so want to see what happens on Sunday.” Head-to-Head Sunday’s matchup marks the 44th meeting between the Raiders and Dolphins. The overall series is knotted up at 21-21-1 but Miami holds the regular season advantage with Las Vegas trailing 18-20-1. The Silver & Black are 3-1 all-time against the Dolphins in playoff play, though. The Raiders have lost the last two meetings — 34-19 in 2024 and 20-13 in 2023. And the last time the team toppled the Dolphins was in 2021 a 31-28 victory. In the last 11 matchups between the two teams (since 2008), the Raiders have only two wins in that span (the 2021 win and a 27-24 victory in 2017). Quote of Note: “A lot. I felt like all of a sudden, he (Treydan Stukes) was playing with more confidence. He was playing faster and communicating loudly. I think even he mentioned the other day, it was somewhere in middle of training camp, but those are the decisions that they make to carry themselves a certain way.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard on 2026 second-round pick Treydan Stukes

title: Ashton Jeanty will play, Fernando Mendoza No. 2  Sunday against Miami
summary: It was looked questionable weeks ago, but became apparent in recent days, the Las Vegas Raiders expect starting running back Ashton Jeanty to play Sunday in the Week 1 season opener against Miami Dolphins. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 draft practiced fully all week and he indicated Thursday he feels ready to […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images)r | Getty Images It was looked questionable weeks ago, but became apparent in recent days, the Las Vegas Raiders expect starting running back Ashton Jeanty to play Sunday in the Week 1 season opener against Miami Dolphins. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 draft practiced fully all week and he indicated Thursday he feels ready to go. Jeanty didn’t practice until this week after he injured his ankle August 23 in practice. Initially, the team was concerned the injury was serious. Now, Jeanty is primed to start the season opener. Expect Jeanty to share some of the running-back load with rookie Mike Washington. The fourth-round pick from Arkansas was a standout in the preseason and in training camp. Meanwhile, as expected, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be the No. 2 quarterback behind Kirk Cousins. Veteran Aidan O’Connell will be the No. 3. this was expected, but ESPN did reprot recently O’Connell could be the backup. This is an indication the Raiders feel strongly about where Mendoza is in his development and are confident he can pay if needed. Also, as expected, Jackson Powers-Johnson will start at right guard ahead of Caleb Rogers. Coach Klint Kubiak had said both will play this season. It appears the only player on Las Vegas’ 53-man roster who won’t play Sunday is superstar tight end Brock Bowers. He is reportedly going to be out 1-2 weeks (that is just an estimate) after having knee surgery this week. Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas will fill the tight end roles. Kubiak would not discuss Bowers’ injury timeline, but he said he will should be back soon. Thus, the Raiders’ other inactive players Sunday will all be based on coach’s decisions and for not medical reasons.

title: Dolphins vs Raiders predictions, prop bets, and odds in Week 1
summary: The Miami Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday to open the 2026 NFL season. The Dolphins are expected to struggle this year, with most predictions ranging from an 0-17 season to somewhere around three or four wins. Will Miami be that bad of a team as they reset the franchise with an eye […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins scrambles against the Washington Commanders during the first half of the preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday to open the 2026 NFL season. The Dolphins are expected to struggle this year, with most predictions ranging from an 0-17 season to somewhere around three or four wins. Will Miami be that bad of a team as they reset the franchise with an eye toward consistent winning in the future? Everything starts with Sunday’s game. Miami enters the weekend as 3-point underdog, which might be a little closer than anticipated for a team that is expected to struggle. The Raiders are similar to Miami in they are resetting their team with a new head coach and a systematic change, which does explain the spread to some degree and may make this week the closest spread the Dolphins have early this year. Here are some predictions for Sunday’s game: All odds provides by FanDuel Sportsbook . Dolphins (+3) at Raiders If Miami is going to find early success this year, they have to get off to a fast start against the Raiders. There are a lot of unknowns for the Dolphins, including reliance on younger, unproven players on the roster, a first-time head coach with a new defensive system being established, a first-time full-time starter at quarterback, and an offense trying to modify previous elements into a system run under a new offensive coordinator. A lot has to come together for Miami, and it has to do it quickly. The three-point spread indicates FanDuel sees these two teams about equal, with Las Vegas receiving the home field advantage bump. The Dolphins only used their starting offense for one series in the preseason and did not show anything but their basic plays. The playbook may not be fully open, given how many younger players the team has and not wanting to overwhelm them, but Miami should have an attack that they have not shown yet. Running back De’Von Achane will be the focus of the Dolphins’ offense, but they have pieces that can alleviate some of the pressure on him, and quarterback Malik Willis has the dual-threat ability to run on any play, adding a complexity to Miami’s offense that has not been present the last several seasons. The Dolphins may be underdogs, but I will have them come away with the upset win here. Prop Bets De’Von Achane rushing yards: 68.5 Over: -114 Under: -114 This feels like an easy over in Week 1. The Dolphins are going to run Achane down the throats of the Raiders to see if they can stop him. Until they do, he is going to keep attacking. Achane should have enough carries to top 100 yards this week, even if Las Vegas tries to stack the box against him. Malik Willis passing touchdowns: 0.5 Over : -215 Under: +158 This feels like another easy over. Assuming the Dolphins’ offense has any success on Sunday, Willis should be in position to throw a touchdown pass. I could see a short pass in the flat to Achane or a pass in the middle of the end zone to tight end Greg Dulcich as possibilities. If this were 1.5 touchdown passes, I probably would go under, but I think Willis has one touchdown pass in his Dolphins debut. Caleb Douglas receptions: 2.5 Over: +120 Under: -160 I might have to go under here. How the Dolphins balance their wide receiver corps, with Douglas, Malik Washington, and Chris Bell all factoring into the passing attack along with Achane and Dulcich, we will all have to wait to see. Douglas could have a monster day, especially if the Raiders sell out against the run and Willis can get quick passes out to the receivers, or he could have a quiet start to his NFL career. I think it is more likely it is a quiet start, but we will see on Sunday. Dolphins’ first drive result Punt : -125 Field goal attempt: +370 Touchdown: +440 Any other: +500 I am going to go with the favorite in this group and think Miami punts on their opening drive. Of course that is not ideal, and they were able to march down the field fairly effectively in their one preseason drive, but with the number of rookies starting and the emotions of the first game of the season, I think they press to hard on their opening drive and have to punt. Hopefully it will get better after that.

We took a look at new head coach Klint Kubiak; the debut timeline for first-overall draft pick, quarterback Fernando Mendoza; how Miami can have success against the Raiders’ defense; and, what the future for Las Vegas may be. You can check out the Raiders’ side of our discussion below. My answers to Holder’s Dolphins question will publish on Silver and Black Pride soon. How well has the Raiders’ offense transitioned out of Chip Kelly’s system and into Klint Kubiak’s? What do you expect from the Las Vegas offense on Sunday? It was just the preseason, but the offense looked much more functional in the three drives that Kirk Cousins and the starting offense were on the field, coming away with points (one touchdown and two field goals) each time. The running game was dramatically different, with the offensive line actually getting push, and the offense was able to stay on schedule. Kubiak also used a good amount of personnel packages, going from three-wide to two tight-end sets and even mixing in a fullback to shake things up throughout the drive. In the passing game, there was a lot more play action, bootlegs and pick/rub routes to scheme pass-catchers open and make life easier for the quarterback. Expectations for Sunday are hard to nail down with the recent news that Brock Bowers will be out . The offense was expected to run through Bowers, as he’s hands down their best weapon in the passing game and overall player on that side of the ball. Now, I expect Kubiak to shift the focus to the rushing attack with backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr., especially since the latter looked really good in the preseason. I also imagine wide receiver Tre Tucker will have a much bigger role since he was expected to be the No. 2 pass-catcher behind Bowers. As far as a point or yardage total, I’m in a “wait and see” mode because my expectations were already rather low with the dynamic tight end in the lineup. The Raiders’ offensive line last year was rough, but they seem to have been very deliberate in addressing the group this offseason, including signing center Tyler Linerbaum and guard Spencer Buford. How comfortable are you with the line this year? Is there a spot you think Miami can successfully create backfield pressure? Honestly, I think the biggest offseason addition when it comes to the offensive line was well-tenured o-line coach Rick Dennison. Linderbaum was a great addition, and I’m excited to see how he can improve the running game. But a big part of the Raiders’ problem in 2025 was that Pete Carroll hired his unqualified son, Brennan Carroll, to coach the unit. There were plenty of whispers that Brennan was in over his head during the season, and those have turned into loud roars over the last few months. There have been several reports that last year’s linemen felt unprepared and like they weren’t being coached properly . Meanwhile, Dennison comes in with about 30 years of NFL experience, and the difference was noticeable with the second- and third-string offenses during the preseason. After last season, it was weird to see the Raiders’ offensive line actually moving people in the running game, LOL! So, I’m definitely more comfortable with the line heading into the season. Linderbaum was a necessary addition and a dramatic improvement over last year’s starting center, Jordan Merdith, who was on the roster bubble and got traded for a sixth-, seventh-round pick swap at the end of training camp. Also, this technically isn’t an “addition”, but starting left tackle Kolton Miller only played four games last year after suffering a high-ankle sprain and hairline fracture in the same ankle. Having him back is a huge boost because Stone Forsythe, Miller’s replacement last year, has literally been one of the worst left tackles in the league over the last several years. One matchup in the trenches that has me worried is Chop Robinson against right tackle DJ Glaze. One matchup in the trenches that has me worried is Chop Robinson against right tackle DJ Glaze. I know Robinson is coming off a down season where he battled injuries, but his speed and athleticism when fully healthy could give Glaze some issues. The latter has struggled with that in pass protection throughout his career, and Robinson got the best of him a few years ago when they faced off against each other in college. Penn State’s athletic pass-rushers always gave the Maryland product trouble. Another spot I’d test is Las Vegas’ guards with defensive tackle Zach Sieler, who I think is one of the most underrated interior defenders in the league. I think the main reason Burford is starting is that he knows the offense; he and Kubiak worked together in San Francisco three years ago. But Burford was bad for the 49ers and ended up being a backup during his last two seasons there. At right guard, Jackson Powers-Johnson has shown flashes but has been inconsistent so far. He had to win his starting spot back during training camp and managed to do so, but at this point, you never know what you’re going to get from JPJ. What do you think is a reasonable timeline for the transition from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza as the team’s starting quarterback? What did you see from Mendoza this summer? It’s funny, I originally said Week 6 for Mendoza’s first start. However, the schedule came out with the Rams slated for Week 7, and they added two first-ballot Hall of Fame pass-rushers over the summer. It’s probably not a good idea to put the future of the franchise behind an offensive line that has question marks when Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald are on the other side. Now, I’m thinking Week 8 makes a little more sense. That gives the o-line enough time to gel together and the rookie quarterback a grace period to get more comfortable in the offense and the NFL as a whole. I’d say Mendoza met expectations during training camp and the preseason. I like that he showed growth in working under center, going through his reads and throwing into tight windows over the middle. Those were three “knocks” on him coming out of Indiana, and I think he at least showed enough to make Raider Nation feel comfortable about the direction he is heading in. However, it was pretty clear that the offense functioned more smoothly with Cousins leading it versus the No. 1 pick. In other words, Mendoza passed the test, but there was nothing that stood out enough to make Kubiak and Co. feel the need to deviate from the plan of being patient with him. How would you attack the Raiders’ defense if you were designing Miami’s offensive game plan? What do you expect to see in Rob Leonard’s defense in his first year as a defensive coordinator? And, bonus question, do you expect Maxx Crosby to be traded (and stay traded) this year? Miami’s offensive game plan should be simple: run the ball right up the middle and make the young secondary prove they can cover. General manager John Spytek wasn’t going to be able to address all of the Raiders’ needs in one offseason because there were so many of them. But defensive tackle was widely considered to be one of the biggest holes on the roster, and Spytek didn’t add anyone until the seventh round of the draft with NC State’s Brandon Cleveland, who didn’t make the 53-man roster and is on the practice squad. title: Giving Props: Vikings Player Bets for This Sunday
summary: With the (real) start of the 2026 regular season in the National Football League now just a day away, we know that a lot of you are getting excited to see our favorite team take the field. We also know. . .because we’re not completely naive. . .that at least some of you are excited […]

The Broncos won the game 34-6. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the (real) start of the 2026 regular season in the National Football League now just a day away, we know that a lot of you are getting excited to see our favorite team take the field. We also know. . .because we’re not completely naive. . .that at least some of you are excited for some other reasons that have to do with the money that you may or may not be wagering on games around the league, whether they involve the Minnesota Vikings or not. In conjunction with our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook , we’re going to be attempting to lend a hand on that front, as yours truly will be looking at a couple of the prop bets available for the game the purple are involved in each week. You can take these with as many grains of salt as you deem necessary. . .after all, you’ve watched me pick games for the last few years. But, hopefully, if you do decide to take my advice on any of these it will work out in a positive way for you. You can find all of these figures at the link above. First Touchdown : Jauan Jennings (+1700) I’m sure a lot of people are going to be leaning toward Justin Jefferson or Jordan Mason or something like that, and I wouldn’t blame you if you wanted to look in that direction, too. But Jennings did have nine touchdowns for San Francisco last season, and seven of those nine came from inside of 20 yards. He’s a significant red zone threat, and with the extra attention that Jefferson is almost certainly going to receive from the Green Bay defense, he could very easily take advantage. Or, if you’re feeling extra spicy, Max Bredeson is there at +10000. The Vikings’ last touchdown of 2025 was scored by C.J. Ham. You tell me that a fullback run is completely off the table if this offense gets the ball to the 1-yard line. Justin Jefferson Receiving Yardage : Over 73.5 (-114) What. . .you mean by, like, halftime? I know that the one thing anyone is concerned with is whether or not this offense gets the ball to #18. I’m sure the Packers are concerned about it, too. I’m just not sure how much the Packers are going to be able to do about it. The expectations are high for Jefferson this season, so why not get it off to a high-flying start? Spread/Points Parlay : Vikings -1.5 and Under 45.5 points (+280) The Vikings are favored to win this one at home, and they should be. I don’t see them winning in blowout fashion or anything, but they should certainly be able to cover a spread that’s less than a field goal. As far as the point total, the Packers have some injury issues on the offensive line, they won’t have Josh Jacobs for this one, and their receivers. . .well, they don’t exactly frighten anyone. I think the point total should stay under that 45.5 number it’s currently sitting at. Those are my takes for this one, folks. Are there any wagers that you’ve currently got your eye on?

full_text: The Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers released their injury final reports, along with injury designations, after Friday’s practice in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at US Bank Stadium. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jakobe Thomas S Illness DNP LP FP — Jacob Thomas S Ankle LP LP FP — Caleb Tiernan T Ankle LP LP FP — Harrison Smith S NIR LP — Christian Darrisaw LT NIR DNP — Green Bay Packers Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Micah Parsons* Edge Knee DNP DNP DNP PUP – OUT Josh Jacobs* RB NIR DNP DNP DNP CE LIST- OUT Luke Musgrave TE Neck DNP DNP DNP PUP – OUT Jordan Riley DT Achilles DNP DNP DNP PUP – OUT Aaron Banks* LG Knee LP LP LP QUESTIONABLE Zach Bako-Bewele* RT Knee LP LP LP QUESTIONABLE Warren Brinson DT Calf DNP DNP DNP OUT Ty’Ron Hopper LB Achilles DNP DNP LP QUESTIONABLE Javon Hargrave* DT Knee LP LP LP — Jordan Morgan* LT Knee LP FP FP — Devonte Wyatt* DT Ankle LP LP LP — Barryn Sorrell EDGE Foot LP LP LP — Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. CE List = Commissioner’s exempt list. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Packers, Micah Parsons, Luke Musgrave, and Jordan Riley are all on the PUP list and will miss the first four games of the season. Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner’s Exempt list following an offseason incident until further notice. Zach Bako-Bewele (formerly Tom) is recovering from offseason knee surgery to repair a partially torn patellar tendon and has been limited all week in practice. He said he plans to start on Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable. Aaron Banks has been dealing with chronic tendinitis in his knee and has missed practice time because of it during training camp. It’s unclear if he’ll be able to go on Sunday or not, but Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick, would be the likely starter at left guard if he can’t go. He continues to be limited and is listed as questionable. He seems less likely to be active than Bako-Bewele, but still could be. Ty’Ron Hopper is also listed as questionable after missing the first two days of practice this week, but was upgraded to limited on Friday. Defensive tackle Warren Brinson, who rotates as a backup, is officially out for Sunday’s game. For the Vikings, Harrison Smith and Christian Darrisaw were given planned veteran days off. But there are no players with injury designations. Let’s hope that continues all season! Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

Our Minnesota Vikings will have the pleasure of hosting the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. It’s a late afternoon game, so there will be a lot of eyes. (Week 1, 2022) Jefferson has averaged 105 yards and has 4 TDs in 6 games at home against the Packers. This will be a fascinating game for both sides. The Vikings QB carosel has stopped on Kyler Murray’s name and the Packers will be a good team for him to get his feet wet with the team. The Packers defense will be without it’s best player in Micah Parsons. Their offense will also be without Josh Jacobs, who is on the Commission’s Exempt List. Jordan Love hasn’t had the best games against Brian Flores’ defenses. Love is 2-3 against the Vikings averaging 258 YPG with 9 TDs and 4 INTs. Love does thrive against pressure and the Vikings will be bringing the house with Green Bay’s RB woes. The Vikings have the better play makers and are at home. Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (Vikings 1st & SKOL / Bleav) preview Minnesota’s Week 1 home opener against Green Bay at 3:25 p.m. CT. The hook is the unknown: a Kyler Murray debut against former Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon, a light Vikings injury report, and a Packers front missing Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs. “Kyler Murray could come out, throw for 400 yards and five touchdowns on Sunday, and it wouldn’t surprise anyone,” Forness said. “He also could throw for like 180, a touchdown, and two picks.” The offensive plan, as they sketched it, is incremental, not a full holster dump. Forness cited Murray’s 2024 split: 0.08 EPA per play in the pocket, 0.16 outside it. Expect bootlegs, floods, and half-rolls so Kevin O’Connell can “get him those confident reps.” Frank Smith’s motion is the other lever. Forness argued O’Connell’s run game has been too bland and that Smith’s Dolphins-style motions can change the math against a Packers edge group without Parsons. Dave wants to see Christian Darrisaw and Blake Brandel (and the whole O-Line) in wide zone. On Justin Jefferson, Stefano’s call was blunt: feature him early “to get Gannon to declare.” Forness’s caution: Gannon may simply refuse to let Jefferson beat him and live with Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, and T.J. Hockenson. Defense is one job. “You gotta stop Jordan Love.” Fantasy Points data they aired: Love’s intermediate-right window (10–20 yards, right of the hashes) was 96th percentile and 99th percentile in EPA per dropback at 1.105. Favorite concepts were outs and hitches. The counter: interior pressure, cross-dog linebacker games, contain from Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner so Love cannot escape and hit the scramble drill. “Get pressure up the middle, keep him in the pocket, and collapse on him.” Harrison Smith’s communication is the back-end glue. Forness’s bottom line: “This feels like a game that the Vikings should be able to win rather convincingly.” Will they? That’s the variable. title: 3-Point Stance: Undisciplined football derailed the Patriots’ chances against the Seahawks
summary: Seven second-half penalties and three fourth-quarter Drake Maye interceptions don’t comprise a winning recipe. And on Wednesday night, despite holding a third-quarter 10-0 lead over the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field, the New England Patriots did just that, collapsing from self-inflicted errors. As a result, the Seahawks climbed back from the deficit to secure a […]
full_text: Seven second-half penalties and three fourth-quarter Drake Maye interceptions don’t comprise a winning recipe. And on Wednesday night, despite holding a third-quarter 10-0 lead over the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field, the New England Patriots did just that, collapsing from self-inflicted errors. As a result, the Seahawks climbed back from the deficit to secure a 13-10 victory in the NFL’s season-opening Super Bowl rematch . New England losing its advantage boils down to one overarching factor: undisciplined play. Week One isn’t always an indicator of a team’s season-long performance, however. In 2025, the Patriots fell to the Las Vegas Raiders, who finished the year with the No. 1 pick in the NFL Draft and a 3-14 record, en route to a Super Bowl appearance. Still, they’ll have their work cut out for them, getting back on track and planning around the loss of A.J. Brown, who will miss at least four weeks on short-term injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. Ineffective execution The team’s final offensive play stood out above the rest when examining the numerous poorly executed assignments. Those errors ranged from overall plays and coaching decisions to single-player performances. With 26 seconds remaining on the game clock and trailing by a field goal, Maye forced a pass to Mack Hollins in the end zone, floating the target short, allowing Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe to haul in the game-sealing turnover. According to the Boston Herald, multiple Patriots revealed in the locker room that the late-game play was supposed to be a quick-game concept. Both offensive tackles cut-blocked Seattle’s pass rushers to promptly eliminate them on the play. Instead, the plan broke down. Maye, under duress from right-side pressure and shuffling his feet for three seconds, missed an open DeMario Douglas for a first down and potential score, committing the takeaway. Ultimately, in that crucial situation with a chance to kick a short field goal to send the contest to overtime, protecting the football is most important. “Everything in the passing game is built on timing and built on protection,” Vrabel said on Thursday. “So, if [the play] is not where you want it and the timing of that particular play and protection, you just have to throw it away and say, ‘We can’t win it on this throw.’” After an aggressive-minded play-calling approach that captured the 10-0 lead, New England shifted to a more conservative, bully-ball approach. The offense ran the ball 16 times on first downs and stuck with that strategy despite a 24% success rate in doing so. On an individual scale, facing a long second-down snap, receiver Romeo Doubs dropped a wide-open pass in space that would have cemented a new set of downs during a critical fourth-quarter drive. One play later, Maye threw his second interception of the evening. Doubs concluded the outing without a single reception, drawing three targets. “I just wasn’t locked in enough on the football,” the former Green Bay Packer said after the matchup about whether confidence is a current issue for him. “The results speak for themselves. I’ll be better moving forward.” The Patriots’ coaching staff is now tasked with regrouping and shifting the team’s focus towards what’s next. How the team responds to the loss will be pivotal. “You either move past [the loss], or you go 0 and 17,” Mack Hollins said after the game. “I’d rather move past it.” Drake Maye’s poor decision-making That unsteady execution also extended into Maye’s performance, notably with his end-of-game struggles. Possessing a two-score lead, Maye believed the offense had a “good” plan in place to chip away at the remaining time on the clock, thus limiting the Seahawks’ scoring opportunities. But the 24-year-old’s turnovers allowed Seattle to take its eventual lead. It was a sequence not expected of New England’s young signal-caller. “I lost patience, and it cost us,” Maye said after the defeat. “[They were] decisions that cost us the game on my part. I’ve asked myself to be better and realize it’s a long season, but at the same time (you) can’t have those [plays]. It was unacceptable … That wasn’t how I play football or how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots.” Maye attempted to connect with receiver DeMario Douglas over the middle of the field in a third-and-long situation as just over nine minutes were left. However, Maye threw late and forced an interception directly into the arms of Seahawks safety Julian Love, setting Seattle up for a drive resulting in its go-ahead field goal. His first turnover of the quarter came after another forced deep ball down the left sideline intended for Doubs in heavy coverage. The pass was tipped and fell into the hands of opposing cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett. The quarterback’s errant passes may have stemmed from discomfort in the pocket. Even when the offensive line provided strong protection, Maye often appeared less settled than he did throughout last season, prematurely leaving the pocket occasionally instead of working around pressure. Regaining his poise in the pocket is essential for the Patriots to replicate their 2025 offensive success. Nonetheless, New England already has a foundation to regroup this upcoming week: a persistent belief in their young quarterback. “We’re going to hold our head up high, and we have nothing but the utmost confidence in [Maye],” Vrabel said Wednesday night. Stacking penalties late And when the team prepares for its home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week Two, improving on-the-field discipline should be another priority. Penalties contributed to the team’s collapse. Before the seven they were called for, the Patriots hadn’t been flagged in the first half. Originally, New England took advantage of Seattle’s four penalties in the second quarter; that said, as the Seahawks cleaned up their play in the final frame, the Patriots evidently lost their focus. After Seattle tied the contest at 10 apiece, rookie Gabe Jacas called for an illegal block on the ensuing kick return, pushing New England back 10 yards from its original spot. Then, on the following drive, Will Campbell was flagged for holding on the first play, forcing the Patriots into a first-and-20 situation. The Patriots had control of the game but couldn’t maintain it or make the proper adjustments as momentum shifted. Now, they’ll have to prove that Wednesday won’t be a season-long trend.

title: What placing A.J. Brown on IR, signing DaQuan Jones means for the Patriots
summary: Two days after he left their season opener with what was later diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain, the New England Patriots have decided to place wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve. The 29-year-old will therefore have to sit out at least the next four games before being eligible to return. Taking Brown’s spot on […]
full_text: Two days after he left their season opener with what was later diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain , the New England Patriots have decided to place wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve. The 29-year-old will therefore have to sit out at least the next four games before being eligible to return. Taking Brown’s spot on the 53-man roster will not be a wide receiver but rather a defensive lineman. DaQuan Jones, a 34-year-old free agent who most recently played in Buffalo, joined the club on a reported one-year, $3.5 million contract . Let’s asses what the two moves mean for the Patriots. WR A.J. Brown: Placed on injured reserve Unsurprising outcome: Depending on their severity and whether or not the rehabilitation process goes smoothly, high-ankle sprains such as the one suffered by Brown typically come with a recovery time of around four to six weeks. Even in the best-case scenario of him falling on the lower end of that spectrum, a move to short-term injured reserve immediately seemed like a realistic possibility. After all, there is no need to rush Brown back. Even in the unlikely case he beats the prognostications and is ready for football activity after only three weeks, the risk of returning him to game action quickly would outweigh the potential reward. The goal, after all, is to have him ready for the most important games down the stretch as well as the playoffs. Keeping him on the 53-man roster on the off-chance of having him available against the Raiders in Week 5 would therefore be a questionable decision. And so, Brown landing on IR should not be a surprise. Four-week absence: As noted above, injured reserve requires players to sit out at least four games. In Brown’s case, this means he will miss some challenging contests — including three straight against teams that qualified for the playoffs last season: Week 2: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Week 3: at Jacksonville Jaguars Week 4: at Buffalo Bills Week 5: vs. Las Vegas Raiders Whereas the Raiders did draft first overall back in April, the other three opponents listed here all played in the postseason tournament in 2025. That includes the Bills, who once again should be in contention for the AFC East title this season. Playing them in their new stadium would have been a challenge to begin with; Brown’s absence makes the task even taller. Pressure on the wide receivers: The most concrete impact of Brown’s injury will be felt on the field, where the Patriots suddenly will be without their high-prized No. 1 wide receiver. Naturally, this puts pressure on the entire operation and especially the other wideouts on the roster: 53-man roster (5): Romeo Doubs (87), DeMario Douglas (3), Mack Hollins (13), Kyle Williams (18), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad (2): Kyle Dixon (83), Cameron Dorner (88) IR (2): A.J. Brown (1 | short-term), Jeremiah Webb (29) The biggest remaining name on the active list is Romeo Doubs, who arrived in Foxborough on a four-year, $68 million deal in March. Doubs had a good training camp and showed some promising chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye over the summer, but he had a disappointing regular season debut: his three targets ended as an interception, a drop, and an incompletion. He, possibly more so than any other player, will need to quickly step up now that Brown is out. Doubs is a candidate to move to the X-receiver spot typically occupied by Brown, but the more likely outcome is backup Kyle Williams seeing increased action. The second-year man, who flashed his deep speed repeatedly in preseason, played 12 offensive snaps versus Seattle without registering any statistics. Without Brown in the lineup, Maye also might be giving slot receiver DeMario Douglas and inside/out option Mack Hollins some increased looks. Between the, they were targeted 12 times on Wednesday. Hollins alone was the target of four throws on the final drive, including on the ill-fated interception that sealed the game. In addition, Efton Chism should be able to shed the healthy scratch status he held in Week 1. While not the same type of player as Brown, his presence as a rotational depth and possible kickoff return option will be valuable. DT DaQuan Jones: Signed to 1-year contract Deliberate timing: Jones originally entered the NFL in 2014, meaning that 2026 will be his 13th season in the league. Due to his experience, he falls in the so-called “vested veteran” category of players with four or more accrued seasons under their belt. This makes it that the Patriots signing him now makes perfect sense. After all, any vested veteran signed before the start of the regular season who remains on the 53-man roster through Week 1 sees his base salary become fully guaranteed. If, however, a vested veteran is signed after Week 1, his base salary will not be fully guaranteed. Jones, joining the Patriots two days after their season opener in Seattle, falls in the second category. This means that the reported $3.5 million base value of his pact is not required to include any salary guarantees. There could still be some as well as a signing bonus, but the Patriots still get more flexibility by making the move now as opposed to, for example, a week ago. More depth, size up front: Unless they make a follow-up move along their interior D-line, the Patriots will be heading toward Week 2 with six defensive tackles on their active roster and eight under contract overall: 53-man roster (6): Milton Williams (97), Christian Barmore (90), Cory Durden (94), Joshua Farmer (92), Leonard Taylor III (93), DaQuan Jones (—) Practice squad (2): Eric Gregory (95), Jeremiah Pharms Jr. (98) Jones does not just add another body to the mix, though. At 6-foot-4, 320 pounds, he will become the heaviest player in the room — somebody well-suited to take the field on early downs and help complement the existing group of players. Whether or not he will take over for Cory Durden as the primary nose tackle will be seen, but he does have extensive experience at that particular spot and others along the line. Immense, versatile experience: Jones’ first 12 seasons in the NFL saw him play in Tennessee, Carolina and Buffalo, where he accumulated a combined 179 in-game appearances and 6,779 total defensive snaps. This makes him by far the most experienced defensive tackle in New England at the moment, and one of now seven players on the roster above the age of 30. His experience is not uniform, though. While offering the size to serve as a 0-technique on the nose, as mentioned earlier, he also has moved all over the formation. In addition, he is more than just a big-bodied gap-controller either: even at his relatively advanced age, he has a quick get-off and is able to shoot gaps. On paper, this should make him a perfect fit in New England’s aggressive downhill attack. Another ex-Titan in the fold: The Patriots sure love familiarity, and the Jones signing is the latest proof of that. After all, he spent the final three of his seven total seasons as a Titan working under head coach Mike Vrabel. This makes him one of seven players on New England’s current payroll to have played for Vrabel in Tennessee: RB Hassan Haskins (PS) WR A.J. Brown (IR) DT DaQuan Jones ED Harold Landry III (PUP) CB Kindle Vildor (PS) S Kevin Byard III S Mike Brown (PS) In addition to those players, Vrabel also spent time in Cleveland in 2024 working with tight end Cameron Latu.

title: Patriots place A.J. Brown on injured reserve, per report
summary: For at least the next four games, the New England Patriots will not have A.J. Brown available. After suffering a high-ankle sprain in Wednesday’s season opener, the team has decided to place the veteran wide receiver on injured reserve. Adam Schefter of ESPN was first to report the news. Brown, 29, joined the Patriots via […]
full_text: For at least the next four games, the New England Patriots will not have A.J. Brown available. After suffering a high-ankle sprain in Wednesday’s season opener, the team has decided to place the veteran wide receiver on injured reserve. Adam Schefter of ESPN was first to report the news. Brown, 29, joined the Patriots via trade from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason. He was immediately installed in the starting offense as a perimeter receiver, and throughout training camp showed some solid chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye. On Wednesday night against the Seattle Seahawks, he caught three passes for 26 yards while playing 30 of the team’s first 34 offensive snaps. On his 31st snap, however, he remained on the ground following an incomplete pass. The team’s medical staff and head coach Mike Vrabel quickly entered the field to check on him before he gingerly walked into the blue medical tent. Shortly thereafter, Brown exited for the locker room and was ruled out for the remainder of the eventual 13-10 loss. Brown underwent additional testing on Thursday, confirming the initial diagnosis of a high-ankle sprain and putting his projected recovery timeline somewhere between four and six weeks. “He’s going to fight hard to get back and whatever it is, I know he’s going to want to get back out there quick,” said quarterback Drake Maye after the game in Seattle. “I think he’s a competitor and he’s going to help this football team for a lot of this year.” Now on injured reserve, Brown will at least miss New England’s games against the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills and Raiders. In a follow-up move, the team signed defensive tackle DaQuan Jones to fill his spot on the 53-man roster.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots sign DT DaQuan Jones to reported 1-year contract
summary: The New England Patriots are adding some size to their defensive line. Veteran tackle DaQuan Jones, who is listed at 6-foot-4 and 320 pounds, is set to join the team on a one-year contract. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jones will sign a deal worth $3.5 million with a maximum […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are adding some size to their defensive line. Veteran tackle DaQuan Jones, who is listed at 6-foot-4 and 320 pounds, is set to join the team on a one-year contract. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jones will sign a deal worth $3.5 million with a maximum value of $6 million. Jones, 34, started his career as a fourth-round draft pick with the Tennessee Titans in 2014. Over the next seven seasons, including three under head coach Mike Vrabel, he started 97 of a combined 103 regular season and playoff games for the team. After spending the 2021 season as a 17-game starter in Carolina, he joined the Bills to add 59 more games — all of them starts — to his career totals. In his 179 games, Jones registered 394 tackles including 35 for loss, 21.5 sacks, and four forced fumbles. He also scored a touchdown on one of his three fumble recoveries, and caught the first interception of his career last season. The Penn State product has remained a free agent since his contract in Buffalo expired in March. He visited the Patriots in mid-August but was not signed at the time. Adding Jones to the mix will put the Patriots above the 53-man roster limit and forces a follow-up transaction. At the moment, the team has five defensive tackles on its roster in Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer and Leonard Taylor. The Patriots, who opened their regular season on Wednesday night with a 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, will return to practice on Monday. They will host the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium in Week 2.

title: Gabe Jacas shows improvement in regular season debut
summary: New England Patriots second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas played 19 defensive snaps in his NFL debut Wednesday night. For the most part, head coach Mike Vrabel liked what he saw. “Continues to improve. I thought he was active, set some good edges in the run game. Good to see him make a nice play for […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Gabe Jacas #50 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a play during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas played 19 defensive snaps in his NFL debut Wednesday night. For the most part, head coach Mike Vrabel liked what he saw. “Continues to improve. I thought he was active, set some good edges in the run game. Good to see him make a nice play for a tackle for a loss,” Vrabel said. “Some good things. Some things we’ll have to coach and correct, and fix things on special teams. Thought it was an improvement.” Jacas showed his motor by chasing down Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock for his first career sack in the second quarter. Coming out of halftime, Jacas flashed his athleticism by getting into the backfield for a tackle for loss. But another play caught the eye of his head coach, with Jacas diagnosing a run play against an unbalanced look and chasing down the ball carrier to record a tackle. “Thought his most instinctive play since he’s been here was the unbalanced play in the red zone,” Vrabel explained. “They went for a speed break, tackle over in a little bunch to the boundary. They tried to block down on him and he just kind of reacted across the guys’ face and made a tackle for just a few yard gain. “That was probably the play I was most pleased with. Said this a guy just out here playing.” Mike Vrabel on Gabe Jacas: “Continues to improve. He was active, set some good edges in the run game… Thought it was an improvement.” Calls the play vs. unbalanced look (1:05) the most instinctual play he’s made since being here. https://t.co/LIqVE0a3H3 — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) September 10, 2026 After missing the entire spring and start of training camp due to a procedure and contract dispute, things were expectedly moving quickly for Jacas upon his return. That included some consistent issues in the preseason when it came to play recognition. The struggles left many wondering if Jacas’ Week 1 role would be diminished. But those inside the building noted that the extra preparation time ahead of the season opener was beneficial to Jacas and other younger players across the roster. Jacas felt similarly. “The preseason definitely helped. Then coming into the game, the preparation that we had, like a week or two to prepare for this game. I was comfortable out there and just playing football,” he said post game. The Patriots edge group — which currently features just four players on the active roster — was the position with the most question marks on the roster ahead of the season. The group got off to an overall strong start as free agent addition Dre’Mont Jones impressed in his Patriots’ debut, leading the team with seven pressures. The early flashes from Jacas were then promising, and the 23-year building on that performance would be a welcomed development for the edge group. “Not bad. I mean, there’s a lot of stuff I can clean up,” Jacas said of his performance. “First sack, first game. Not too bad, just look at the film when I get back and work on the things I need to work on. You know, just continue to improve as weeks go on.”

title: Patriots injury analysis after season opener vs. Seahawks
summary: Their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks did not go the way the New England Patriots would have hoped. Not only did they let a 10-0 lead slip out of their grasp behind a three-interception performance from their starting quarterback, they also lost one of their most important offensive skill position players to what projects […]
full_text: Their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks did not go the way the New England Patriots would have hoped. Not only did they let a 10-0 lead slip out of their grasp behind a three-interception performance from their starting quarterback, they also lost one of their most important offensive skill position players to what projects as a multi-week injury. Obviously, all eyes are on A.J. Brown and his sprained ankle coming out of the game. But as a look at our weekly injury analysis shows, he was not the only Patriot to get banged up during the 13-10 defeat on Wednesday night . Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 1 CB Carlton Davis III: Davis was shaken up midway through the first quarter while helping to blow up a run play. He remained down on one knee, but jogged off with members of New England’s training staff shortly thereafter. Following a brief stay in the blue medical tent, he returned to the sidelines and eventually reentered. the contest on the next defensive series. TE Hunter Henry: Henry took a hard hit on the first play from scrimmage in the second half, landing on his back after a 13-yard reception. He left the field under his own power and entered the medical tent for further evaluation, but returned to the game a short time later. WR A.J. Brown: The big one. Brown remained on the ground after an incomplete third-down attempt, with medical personnel and even head coach Mike Vrabel checking in on him on the field. He limped off the field into the medical tent, and later gingerly walked back to the locker room albeit under his own power. Follow-up evaluation done on Thursday found out that he had suffered a high-ankle sprain . C Jared Wilson: The Patriots’ starting center had to be evaluated on the sideline after suffering an apparent cut on his right snapping hand during the first series of the second half, the same that saw Henry and Brown get shaken up. He ended up playing all 71 offensive snaps. RT Morgan Moses: During his Monday press conference, head coach Mike Vrabel listed Moses among other players suffering injuries in the game. There was no obvious moment an injury might have occurred, however, and he did end up playing 100% of New England’s offensive snaps. What this means for the Patriots Losing A.J. Brown just 31 snaps into his Patriots debut is an obvious blow to an offense that already had a hard time stringing consistent plays together versus the Seahawks with him on the field. Now, the unit will have to find a way to operate with Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism as its primary wide receivers — a group that will be in the spotlight over the coming games. Based on Wednesday and his role throughout the summer, Williams in particular should see an uptick in reps as the primary X-receiver. Hollins, who does have some good chemistry with Drake Maye, also will continue to be heavily involved. For how long Brown will be out remains to be seen. According to reports, the expected recovery range for his type of sprain is somewhere between four and six weeks. This means that short-term injured reserve, which would sideline him for a minimum of four weeks, appears to be a realistic if ultimately disappointing possibility. As for the other players listed above, they do not appear to have suffered any long-term issues. “Morgan Moses was able to return. Hunter Henry was able to return. Carlton Davis III was able to return,” said Mike Vrabel on Thursday. “Probably some bumps and bruises, but I do not think anything that would keep anybody out. A.J. Brown is one we will have to monitor.” Coming off their season opener, the Patriots will enjoy a 10-day break before their home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Saints vs. Lions: Quarterback Matchup
summary: Week 1 of the NFL is finally here, and the Saints are set to visit the Detroit Lions to begin the season. This will feature a very interesting QB matchup: veteran Jared Goff, who is entering his 11th season, versus the up-and-coming face of the Saints, Tyler Shough, who is entering Year 2 but his […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 18: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints runs during joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 18, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 of the NFL is finally here, and the Saints are set to visit the Detroit Lions to begin the season. This will feature a very interesting QB matchup: veteran Jared Goff, who is entering his 11th season, versus the up-and-coming face of the Saints, Tyler Shough, who is entering Year 2 but his first season as the full-time starter. Goff and the Lions are looking to bounce back after a disappointing 9-8 season. Talk about a changing of the times. The Lions used to be an organization that would celebrate a nine-win season, but after reaching the NFC Divisional Round in 2024 and falling short to then-rookie QB Jayden Daniels, the Lions had high expectations for the 2025 season. But there were some substantial losses on the coaching staff that really affected the overall play of the team. In 2024, Jared Goff had a fantastic season when the Lions finished 15-2. He completed 72.4% of his passes for 4,629 yards, 37 TDs, and 12 INTs. He was sacked 31 times. But what truly set the offense apart in 2024 was the running game. The Lions rushed for 146.4 yards per game that season, and following Ben Johnson’s departure to become the head coach of the Bears, the Lions would drop that number to 120.1 yards per game, which was virtually middle of the pack. As for Goff, his production in 2025 remained virtually the same. The veteran QB is a prolific pocket passer. He finished the season with a 68% completion rate, 4,564 passing yards, 34 TDs, and only eight INTs. Since Goff was traded to the Lions for Matthew Stafford, there’s been a consensus that he’s just been an average QB, but that’s not really the case. He has been a really good QB and is a major reason why the Lions have been a relevant franchise since he and his head coach arrived. Goff is a rhythm passer. He is excellent with ball placement and accuracy, which is why his completion percentage has hovered around 70% over the past two seasons. In 2025, Goff was tied for the lead in the NFL for the quickest time to throw at 2.57 seconds. Goff will also play within the structure, and this is aided by his pre-snap and post-snap processing. He is entering the 11th season of his career. It is hard for a defense to confuse a QB with his level of experience at this stage of his career. Add to that the fact that he has the physical tools to make every throw across the entire field. But the intermediate area of the field is where he excels the most. His average depth of target is seven yards. What does Goff not do well? Two areas stand out the most: mobility and Big-Time Throws. Big-Time Throws are throws that are further downfield and have tighter windows to complete. Goff will not consistently challenge downfield. In 623 dropbacks, he had 16 BTTs. That ranked 23rd among qualified QBs. His mobility is an issue as well. He scrambled just five times in all of 2025. He will not run away if the pocket collapses. The Saints will have to play sound defense and get Goff off schedule. They need to challenge him in the intermediate areas of the field without giving up wide-open shots to big-time playmakers like Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Saints are coming in featuring the young Tyler Shough, and Shough represents the hope for a brighter future in New Orleans. Statistically, Goff and Shough are very similar. The difference between the two is that Shough will actually run the ball. Goff had zero rushing TDs in 2025. Shough had three in nine starts. Tyler comes in after finishing the 2025 season with a strong close to his rookie campaign. He finished with a 5-4 record in nine starts, but he also had 2,384 passing yards, a 67.6% completion rate, 10 touchdowns through the air, and six INTs. Shough also had 186 yards on the ground to go along with the aforementioned three TDs. Shough had a very impressive 91.3 passer rating for his rookie season. Shough is also very comparable to Goff in that they both finished around a 68% completion rate and seven yards per attempt. Now, where Shough shines is when the play breaks down. He can still find success. He is very good off-script, extending plays and even scrambling for yards. Shough is also not afraid to put the ball into tight windows. In a little more than half the number of dropbacks Goff had, Shough had nearly the same number of BTTs. Goff had 16 in 623 dropbacks. Shough had 13 in 378. Shough also had an 8.7-yard average depth of target, showcasing his ability to push the ball downfield. Shough was able to achieve this level of success without having the same level of weapons around him as Goff. The Saints retooled the wide receiver room this offseason and added an explosive threat to the running back room that should aid in the growth of their young QB. Sunday’s matchup will be a fun one to watch, and it will be a game that could showcase whether the Saints are truly putting themselves on the path toward becoming a playoff team or if the Lions have healed from the shortcomings of last season and can once again become a team to beat in the NFC. What do you think of this QB matchup, and what are your expectations for the game on Sunday? Share your thoughts in the comments.
