Both teams were 3-14 in 2025. The Jets have won four of the five meetings between these teams since 2013, including a 24-17 win in their last […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Head Coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to Week 2 of the preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets get their season underway against their former head coach’s new team, as they will face Robert Saleh’s Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday afternoon. Both teams were 3-14 in 2025. The Jets have won four of the five meetings between these teams since 2013, including a 24-17 win in their last matchup in 2024 which saw rookie Braelon Allen scoring two touchdowns including the late game winner. Let’s break down the Titans’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Last year’s first overall pick, Cam Ward, didn’t do too badly as a rookie given his lack of a supporting cast. He passed for over 3,000 yards and had 15 touchdown passes and two more on the ground. However, he completed under 60 percent of his passes and never passed for more than 265 in any game, although he was over 250 five times. He was also the most sacked quarterback in the league. While Ward looks to take a step forward this year, Mitchell Trubisky waits in the wings. The veteran has 57 career starts, although only seven of those came over the past five years. In the Jets’ final game of 2025 in Buffalo, Trubisky came off the bench and threw for four touchdown passes, so his confidence will be high if called upon. Offensive Line The Titans’ offensive line is built around the veteran Dan Moore at left tackle and two recent first round picks on the right side. Peter Skoronski, the right guard, was a first round pick in 2023 and right tackle JC Latham was the Titans’ top selection in 2024. These three were mainstays last year, missing just five games between them. At center, former Giants backup Austin Schlottmann comes in as the new starter. He has 18 career starts but never more than four in a season, so this is his first chance to be a full-time starter. The other starter is a rookie – fifth round right guard Fernando Carmona. The Jets will no doubt be looking to test the 316-pounder. The two starting tackles gave up eight sacks each last season and Latham led the team with 14 offensive penalties, so there are potential flaws. Pro Football Focus recently ranked the starting group as as a bottom-five unit. Tennessee also has a new-look bench, headlined by the veteran James Hudson, who has 19 career starts. Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, Garrett Dellinger and Jackson Slater were all rookies last year and started just one game between them. Sixth round rookie Pat Coogan, the number two center, rounds out this unit. Running Backs Tony Pollard was a bright spot last season, as he rushed for over 1,000 yards with five touchdowns and added 33 receptions for Tennessee. He’ll provide a good test for the Jets’ reinforced defensive front. Behind Pollard, Tyjae Spears is the third down back. He caught 45 passes last season but averaged less than four yards per carry and six yards per catch. Julius Chestnut had a minor role last season and the Titans drafted Nicholas Singleton in the fifth round to add to this group. Pass catchers The Titans’ wide receivers should be dramatically improved this season. They brought in Wan’Dale Robinson in free agency, drafted Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick and will get a healthy Calvin Ridley back after the veteran was limited to six starts and 17 receptions last year. Robinson reunites with new Titans offensive coordinator in Tennessee and the former Giants head coach will know how to get good production from him due to their time together with New York. Robinson caught 92 passes last season, and surpassed 1,000 receiving yards. Ridley has obviously been a thousand-yard receiver in the past and Tate is expected to be one in the future, so Ward has much better weapons at his disposal this year. Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike can now move back into reserve roles, which may suit them better, although they combined to catch 89 passes last season. At tight end, the Titans lost Chig Okonkwo, their leading pass catcher from last season, so they’ll need Gunnar Helm to step up. Helm had 44 receptions last year but averaged just eight yards per catch with two touchdowns. Another ex-Giant, Daniel Bellinger, will also bring production to this group but David Martin-Robinson is more of a role player and Kylen Granson is a journeyman with just one touchdown in five seasons. Defensive Line The defensive line looks very familiar, as three of the starters and one of the reserves were recent Jets under Saleh. Jermaine Johnson will play his first NFL game since being traded against his former team, with John Franklin-Myers, who already played well in two games for the Broncos since leaving the Jets, lined up inside. The other starting edge is Jacob Martin, who is with his seventh team since the start of the 2021 season, but coming off a bit of a breakout year where he had a career-best 5.5 sacks. Martin is reunited with Saleh, whose Jets traded him for a mid-round pick swap midway through his only year with them. Tennessee’s other starter is their talisman defensive tackle, Jeffery Simmons. The four-time pro bowler is coming off an all-pro season where he racked up 11 sacks. One more ex-Jet comes off the bench in the form of Solomon Thomas, who is joined by former 49ers starter Jordan Elliott, recent waiver claim Nazir Stackhouse and fifth round rookie Jackie Marshall in providing depth on the interior. Thomas can, of course, also play outside. The backups on the edge include the Titans’ second first round pick, Keldric Faulk and two reserves from last year in Truman Jones and Oluwafemi Oladejo. Oladejo was a second round pick but had no sacks in six games as a rookie. Linebackers The Titans’ linebacking unit is led by Cedric Gray, who had a team-high 164 tackles last season and wears the defensive headset. Tennessee will need to play without Gray this week though, because he hasn’t cleared concussion protocol following a recent UTV accident. In Gray’s absence, the Titans will lean on veteran Cody Barton to anchor this unit. He had 81 tackles, 11 pass breakups and three interceptions as a starter last year. As for who will replace Gray’s role, Saleh downplayed it by lauding the depth of their unit. In particular, he said he was interested to see how second round pick Anthony Hill will develop, so the rookie might get an earlier than expected shot at a full-time workload. The other options are Owen Pappoe, who started two games in three years in Arizona, and James Williams, who is listed as a starter but was in a rotational role last season. Tennessee will also elevate Mohamoud Diabate from the practice squad for additional depth. Diabate started 18 games over the past three seasons with the Browns. Defensive Backs Tennessee signed L’Jarius Sneed to a massive contract in 2024, but that hasn’t worked out and he was released in March, forcing the Titans to restock their cornerback position. They raised eyebrows by signing Cor’Dale Flott and Alontae Taylor to free agent deals worth $15 million a year and over $17 million per year respectively, so it will be interesting to see whether either or both can live up to that in the long run. Marcus Harris returns in the slot, while Amani Hooker and Kevin Winston will start at safety. Hooker had 81 tackles and eight pass breakups as a starter last year, while Winston started six games as a third round rookie. Another ex-Jet, Tony Adams, provides depth at safety, along with journeyman former third round pick Terrell Burgess. In terms of depth at cornerback, Jaylon Jones started every game for the Colts in 2024 and had 100 tackles and 12 pass breakups. In addition, Micah Robinson was poached from Green Bay’s practice squad last season. Special Teams The Titans should have a solid kicking game with kicker Joey Slye, punter Tommy Townsend and…

We all held our collective breath when Hall went down with a non-contact injury back in August. Now we can breathe a sigh of relief. The talented tailback has been a full participant for the last two days of practice. “I feel great,” Hall told the media on Thursday, September 10. “It was actually a very good, like two-week vacation. Yeah, so I could have been out there a little earlier, but the team thankfully was very cautious with me, and it was a really good vacation. I feel really fresh now.” The Jets will be running the football a ton in 2026. Hall is a straw that stirs the drink. He got paid like one of the top running backs in football. Now it’s time for him to play like one. Coming off this injury, the Jets will likely be cautious with Hall’s usage, as they should be. The Kryptonite of Saleh’s aggressive attack-style defense is their over-pursuit, which makes them vulnerable to the screen game. After the Jets got killed by it for years, it’s only right to return serve and kill Saleh and the Titans with that same strategy. title: Eagles-Commanders Final Injury Report: Jonathan Greenard ruled OUT
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles ruled one player OUT: Jonathan Greenard. Greenard returned to practice earlier this week after missing all of training camp due to a pec strain he suffered […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 27: Jonathan Greenard #52 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on May 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles ruled one player OUT: Jonathan Greenard. Greenard returned to practice earlier this week after missing all of training camp due to a pec strain he suffered while weight training. Speaking after practice on Thursday, Greenard admitted that he’s not yet 100%. That much is reflected by him only being a limited participant in practice all week. Ideally, the Eagles would have a healthy Greenard available for them on Sunday. But it’s good to see they’re not necessarily rushing him back before he’s ready. The Eagles should have enough talent and depth at edge rusher to still win their matchup against an entirely exploitable Commanders offensive line. Greenard might be ready for Week 2? The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Eli Stowers. Speaking to reporters after practice on Friday, Stowers said he’ll be playing. But the injury report suggest otherwise since he was limited all week due to a hamstring issue. And even if Stowers is healthy enough to play, he might be a healthy scratch anyway as the Eagles’ fourth tight end. The rest of the active roster is healthy and ready to play. title: Vic Fangio talks about the Eagles’ plan at edge rusher while Jonathan Greenard ramps up
summary: The Eagles defense will have a challenge ahead of them on Sunday as they face the Commanders with a new offensive coordinator. Vic Fangio spoke to reporters ahead of the matchup, and talked about how they’ll approach the edge rush group with Jonathan Greenard still working his way back. He also spoke about the safety […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 30: Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 30th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles defense will have a challenge ahead of them on Sunday as they face the Commanders with a new offensive coordinator. Vic Fangio spoke to reporters ahead of the matchup, and talked about how they’ll approach the edge rush group with Jonathan Greenard still working his way back. He also spoke about the safety position, and why preparing for a new OC is a little different. Here’s what the DC had to say: On Jonathan Greenard Fangio mentioned that Greenard’s return is day-by-day, and noted that the edge rusher hasn’t practiced much yet, so that’s something they want to be careful with. As for how Greenard did on Wednesday in his first practice back, the DC said he did, “Okay.” “There’s a minimal amount of practice, real practice, that you have to go through, especially for a guy coming off an injury. It’s like the guy, [Aaron] Donald did with the Rams, he’s just coming off rustiness, no injury, and wasn’t ready this week. So, we’ll see.” The DC later mentioned that it’ll be a little bit before Greenard is game ready for a full load, so until then, it’ll be a pretty good rotation of rushers. Still, Fangio said he has confidence in guys like OLB Arnold Ebiketie and OLB A.J. Epenesa dropping back into coverage. He noted that Ebiketie and Epenesa have made a lot of improvement during camp, and he feels good about it. On Week 1 prep He talked a bit about how he prepares for facing a new offensive coordinator who he doesn’t have history with — like in Week 1 against the Commanders OC David Blough. “It’s a little different than normal. You really don’t know a whole lot about the offense either way, what it might [or] might not be, you make the assumption, right or wrong. They’ll still do some of the stuff that [Jayden] Daniels was good at and comfortable with, they’ll do some stuff the new guy wants to do. So, it’s a little bit of a crapshoot.” Later on, Fangio admitted that they might need to rotate guys, especially up front, earlier in the season, but it’s less about having a set number of snaps and more about the flow of the game. He explained that if they’re out on the field for 8-10 plays and then the offense goes three-and-out, that stresses things more, and they’ll rotate more. On the safety position Fangio confirmed that Marcus Epps will get the start against Washington on Sunday. “[Epps] was just solid the whole way through, but we still like Michael [Carter III], and we have the ability to play him there some, too.” He later was clear that they still have a role carved out of Carter , and he’s someone they value for his versatility. “Michael’s very versatile, can play nickel, can play dime, can play safety, and we plan on using him.” On having the most light boxes in the NFL “That’s a credit to the front guys because if that is true, we’re holding up good enough to be able to do that. There’s been times in certain games where it’s hurt us some. There’s pluses and minuses to everything you do. The minus is you’re stressing your run defense a little bit, so we have to be able to play to run when we’re not having a safety down that linebacker depth in the box.” Other notables The DC said that he expects Moro Ojomo to have a similarly impressive year to last season, and hopes that he elevates his game even further. He noted that Ojomo has already been a good player for the team the past two years, so hopefully he just builds on that, but doesn’t feel like the DT needs to prove anything. Fangio talked about Jihaad Campbell heading into his second season and said that the LB is coming along, while also noting he isn’t a finished product yet. He pointed to missing time the past two seasons due to injuries have held him back a bit, but he continues to work. Fangio was asked about Riq Woolen working to be more consistent from snap to snap, and the DC shared that he likes the CB and his attitude, and he’s working hard. He was asked about how they handled mobile quarterbacks last year, and Fangio took a shot at ProFootball Focus (PFF), suggesting they have some “phony stat” to look up about it. But then he explained that it’s a hard thing to rate because overall they might do a good job, but the plays they don’t that go long, that stand out.

title: Jalen Hurts talks about his relationship with Philadelphia
summary: As we get closer to the Eagles season opener, Jalen Hurts has been making the rounds and giving interviews, but his recent sit-down with Jason Dumas for 6abc Philadelphia showed that the QB will open up if asked the right questions. Fans want to hear Hurts appreciate the city, and he revealed that he would […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we get closer to the Eagles season opener, Jalen Hurts has been making the rounds and giving interviews, but his recent sit-down with Jason Dumas for 6abc Philadelphia showed that the QB will open up if asked the right questions. Fans want to hear Hurts appreciate the city, and he revealed that he would have a hard time finding the words to explain just how special it is. “It’s a special place. I don’t think my words could — I don’t think I could even find the words to explain right now what the city is, and how valuable it is for sports, and sports culture. It has a special edge, and as a player, I just try to carry my edge, carry my competitiveness, carry my love and drive with me wherever I am. So, it’s been great to be able to grow and learn the things that I have in this city, and to build and experience special moments like we have. And so, its just a start of a new journey now, and I’m excited for that.” Hurts also talked about how he wants to honor the platform that football gives him, and said he’s very intentional with his time and making sure to show up for the communities looking up to him. He also gave a little insight into his game day routine, which isn’t too structured, but is filled with good music. The QB said he doesn’t have a specific song he puts on as he heads to the game, and instead lets the music find him. Still, Hurts pointed out that one of the best parts of game day is getting to listen to so much good music up until kick-off.

full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders players scuffle during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Maltepes, known as “The Philly Godfather,” will impart his gambling wisdom on the Eagles and where the smart money is going on various pro football games each weekend this season. Maltepes is one of the nation’s hottest sports betting experts who appears weekly on national radio and has his own website, www.thephillygodfather.com [thephillygodfather.com] . Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles, 4:35 p.m. Sunday The Line: Eagles minus-5.5/Total: 44.5 What is the line telling you: There’s a lot of uncertainty surrounding this Eagles offense with A.J. Brown being shipped to the Patriots and Sean Mannion taking over as the new offensive coordinator. Normally, I’d shy away from laying more than a field goal with a team playing a division opponent in Week 1. But let’s be honest—this Commanders team has plenty of problems of its own. Washington will be without offensive lineman Laremy Tunsil, which means Jayden Daniels could be running for his life against an Eagles defensive line that I believe is arguably the best in the NFL. That’s a bad recipe for Washington and should lead to fewer scoring opportunities. The expectations are pretty damn low for Washington in the betting market this season, with Vegas setting their regular-season win total at just 7.5 games . Even without A.J. Brown, the Eagles should be able to move the football by doing what Philly does best— putting Saquon Barkley in the backfield and running the ball right down Washington’s throat. The Eagles have a top-five-rated offensive line, while Washington ranked 27th in the NFL last season in opponent yards per rushing attempt and didn’t do much in the offseason to convince me they’ve fixed that problem. The new offensive coordinator in Philadelphia does concern me a little, and this is still a nasty NFC East rivalry game. But the Eagles are tough, physical, and protect the football, while the Commanders had the second-worst turnover differential in the NFL last season . Bottom line: At -5.5 , I like the Eagles, but I think the better bet is the total. Give me the Under 44.5. I expect the Commanders’ offensive line to get bullied by Vic Fangio’s defense , and I also expect some growing pains from the Birds’ offense with a new offensive coordinator. This has the feel of one of those old-school Philly games: defense, Saquon, field position, and make the other team earn every damn yard. Prop bets for the game: Saquon Barkley anytime TD -130 Dallas Goedert anytime TD +220 Jayden Daniels over 30 rushing yards -175 (Betting lines are subject to change.)

title: A.J. Brown injury: Patriots place former Eagles receiver on IR
summary: A big part of the Patriots offense is going to miss (at least) the first quarter of the season, with the team placing A.J. Brown on IR after the WR suffered a high-ankle sprain in the NFL season opener. The former Eagles receiver will automatically miss games against the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills, and Raiders. Brown […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots is assisted off the field after being injured in a play against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images A big part of the Patriots offense is going to miss (at least) the first quarter of the season, with the team placing A.J. Brown on IR after the WR suffered a high-ankle sprain in the NFL season opener. The former Eagles receiver will automatically miss games against the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills, and Raiders. Brown went down against the Seahawks on Wednesday, and while he was able to limp to the sideline and then to the locker room, he was seen post-game with a boot on his foot. An MRI on Thursday confirmed a high-ankle sprain, and initial thoughts were that he could miss 3-6 weeks. Before leaving the game, the WR had three catches for 26 total yards, and missed getting into the endzone thanks to an underthrown pass by Drake Maye. BGN’s Brandon Lee Gowton explained why Brown’s injury and missed time was of interest to the Eagles and their future draft plans. “His missed time is of interest to the Eagles not only because he used to play for the team … but because, via the Brown trade, Philly owns the most favorable of two 2027 fifth-round picks from either the Pats or the Chicago Bears. If Brown has to miss time and the Patriots struggle further, the Eagles could benefit in the form of improved draft pick compensation.“ With Brown out at least through Week 5, the Patriots will have to figure out a way to turn things around for their offense with WR1. They just traded away Kayshon Boutte, but maybe Mack Hollins is the answer — or maybe the Eagles will have a better draft pick next year.

summary: The Eagles are kicking off their season with a showdown against the Washington Commanders. The preseason cuts landed a lot of Eagles rookies on the practice squad or on other teams, meaning Philly only has a few first-year players in contributing positions at this point in the season. Here is what I will be watching […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on from the sideline during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are kicking off their season with a showdown against the Washington Commanders. The preseason cuts landed a lot of Eagles rookies on the practice squad or on other teams, meaning Philly only has a few first-year players in contributing positions at this point in the season. Here is what I will be watching for in Week 1. How much does Makai Lemon even see the field? Makai Lemon missed a ton of time this summer due to a hamstring injury. Despite getting some snaps in the final preseason game, it is fair to wonder how much he is involved in the Eagles’ offense at these early stages. Lemon has been listed as the Eagles’ starting WR3 and punt returner on the team-issued depth chart , but it is fair to wonder how much that status is actually reflected in his snap count. The Eagles have a handful of experienced receivers between DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and fan-favorite Darius Cooper. Even as a listed starter, it’s possible Lemon is rotated in and out a lot as he continues to get his feet wet. In Week 1, I am less focused on what he actually does while on the field versus how much he is playing or not. Speaking of which… Does the Eagles coaching staff trust Eli Stowers at all? I have been really bummed to see how rough Eli Stowers’ transition to the NFL has been. He was a prospect I was really excited about. While his story is far from written, it is evident that Stowers has to do a lot of work to get on the field for the Eagles. He is currently buried on the depth chart, likely as the fourth tight end. If he even dresses for the game, Stowers needs to make the absolute most out of every time he sees the field on offense or special teams.

title: Eagles News: Saquon Barkley poised for another big season
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Saquon Barkley looked pretty good in training camp this summer. The Eagles’ offense was uneven as a whole but they looked their best when they leaned into the running game. It’s not hard for me to envision Barkley having another big […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Saquon Barkley looked pretty good in training camp this summer. The Eagles’ offense was uneven as a whole but they looked their best when they leaned into the running game. It’s not hard for me to envision Barkley having another big season. Obviously not easy to project him to reach his 2024 numbers. And him looking good won’t matter if the blocking doesn’t hold up, as we saw last season. But I tend to think things will come together in the run game more than they did in 2025. Can Saquon Barkley recapture his 2024 dominance? – ESPN Not only is the offensive line in a better place but Barkley is as well. He shot past his career high in carries (345) during the regular season in 2024 and added 91 more rushes in the postseason. That number fell to 280 last season. And while the wild-card playoff exit against the San Francisco 49ers was disappointing for the Eagles, it gave everyone more of a physical and mental break this offseason, including the 29-year-old Barkley. “Huge,” said running backs coach Jemal Singleton, on the benefits of the longer layoff. “He could take the time from the offseason and get his rest but then come back and start working. So I feel like he’s in a really, really good place now. … It’s going to be exciting to kind of see him go.” Singleton can see it most in the conditioning part of it where Barkley, who shares a backfield this season with a pair of capable backs in Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, has stayed on the field for more plays during long drives while looking “explosive.” Put the fresh legs with a revitalized offensive front in this run scheme, and there is optimism Barkley can ascend to the top of the running back class once again. “Being a better playmaker,” Barkley said on what he wants to improve from last season. “That’s why I was brought here, that’s what I feel I’m one of the best in the league [at] and just bringing that back.” Can Saquon Barkley defy the RB age curve? His favorite back’s best season came at 29 – The Athletic The Eagles made a major scheme change this offseason that will be apparent in the running game. Quarterback Jalen Hurts will more frequently line up under center. The Eagles installed a wide-zone running scheme. Barkley said he’s “always been intrigued with this kind of system” while observing the success of players from afar. He spoke to Peterson about the depth he should align before the snap, ranging from six yards to eight yards. The landmarks in the running game are different. Barkley said he must be more of a one-cut runner. He believes the protection is friendly to a running back. “I feel like I have a chance to be really good in this system,” Barkley said. “I feel like it’s going to open things that I may have not been able to show in my career.” “He can be good in any system, let’s be honest,” running backs coach Jemal Singleton added. “But I think this is one that allows him to do some things that I think is going to be fun. It’ll be fun to watch him work, and he’s one of those guys that dives into everything. He reaches out to former players that have played in the system like this.” Barkley connected with Todd Gurley, who was offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s teammate in Los Angeles. Gurley’s two best seasons came in this offense, making first-team All-Pro both years. (Gurley is also an example of a running back who did not age as Barkley intends; Gurley’s final season was at age 26.) Singleton, who coached in this system elsewhere, raved about Barkley’s offseason. Barkley has made cuts in practice that left new teammates dumbfounded. For old teammates, it’s a reminder of Barkley’s 2024 greatness. “We kind of take that stuff for granted a little bit,” Singleton said. “It’s like the ‘wow’ factor. It’s Saquon Barkley. Let’s not forget, and he’s done some amazing things, and he still can.” Eagles vs. Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 1 enemy – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles are beginning their 2026 season with a home game against the Washington Commanders. Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts are aiming to reach 6-0 in Week 1 games together. In order to preview this NFC East matchup , I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The affable Andrew Y kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 188: Week 1 Preview – NFC East Mixtape We have FINALLY reached Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season and to start things off we have all four NFC East teams taking on another member of the division. Which two will emerge as winners? Which two will hate everything and want to start over? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Gowton discuss in true Mixtape fashion… plus Big Blue View’s Ed Valentine joins for perspective on the G-Men! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. Lots of Questions – Iggles Blitz So the experts have the Eagles missing the playoffs, as a wild card team or making it back to the Super Bowl. That’s quite a range of outcomes. The lack of faith in the Eagles is all about the offense. AJ Brown is out and a new scheme is in. People have doubts about how good Jalen Hurts will be in the new scheme. It is absolutely fair to have concerns about the offense. I’m buying the Eagles as a contender because of Saquon Barkley, better OL play and an elite defense. That is a winning formula. Hurts should have time to grow into the new offense and for his receivers to work into their roles. Why Sean Mannion decided to call plays from the booth this season – NBCSP While Mannion explained that there are pros and cons of both locations, the 34-year-old ultimately decided to head up to the booth as he enters his first season as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator. “When you’re in the box, obviously you have a little bit more space,” Mannion explained on Thursday afternoon. “You’re not pacing around. You have the tablet. It’s a little bit like sitting at a desk, but I think just the vision is a little bit unique there, the higher vantage point. “Honestly, I felt comfortable with both, and really, I just felt like the vision type of thing really led me to the decision. Ultimately, the other part of it is we have a great staff. They communicate really well on the sideline. There’s been constant lines of communication, and I think all of that led to the decision.” This decision is a departure from the way the Eagles have done things for a long time. Franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts noted earlier this week that this will be his first time with a play caller upstairs since his days in college. It can make communication a bit tricky between Hurts and Mannion because it’ll have to be over the red phone on the sideline. Is Sean Mannion ready for his big moment with the Eagles? He’s been preparing for it for years. – Inquirer Mike Riley and Sean Mannion were having one of their catch-up calls when Mannion, who played quarterback at Oregon State under Riley, told his former coach the latest project he was working on during the nascent days of his own coaching career. Mannion, the most prolific passer in Oregon State history, told Riley that he was putting together and digitizing all of the passing concepts he could find dating back to the 1960s. “This is what he does in his spare time,” Riley explained recently. Mannion is just 34 years old and only three years removed from his playing career. He has never called plays in the NFL before and now is tasked with turning around an Eagles offense that was too stagnant in 2025 under another…

summary: Mike Tomlin revealed the best team he ever coached in a recent interview with the Today Show — and according to the former Steelers head coach, it’s not the 2008-09 team that won Super Bowl XLIII. “The best team I coached, probably, didn’t win,” Tomlin said. “Probably in the mid-teens, 2015-16. Denver won it that […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - DECEMBER 20: Antonio Brown #84 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks into the stands after scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at Heinz Field on December 20, 2015 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Tomlin revealed the best team he ever coached in a recent interview with the Today Show — and according to the former Steelers head coach, it’s not the 2008-09 team that won Super Bowl XLIII. “The best team I coached, probably, didn’t win,” Tomlin said. “Probably in the mid-teens, 2015-16. Denver won it that year with Peyton (Manning).” Former #Steelers HC Mike Tomlin says the best team he coached was the 2015 Steelers, who went 10-6 and lost to the eventual Super Bowl champion #Broncos in the Divisional Round. Pittsburgh played that day without Antonio Brown & Le’Veon Bell. (📽️ 'Glass Half Full', Today Show) https://t.co/7EnJLEeZkQ pic.twitter.com/MStmCatoS2 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 8, 2026 The 2015 Steelers went 10-6, led by the league’s fourth-best scoring offense averaging 26.4 points per game. The team finished second in the AFC North, winning in the wild card round over the Cincinnati Bengals but falling in the divisional round to the eventual Super Bowl Champion Broncos. The Steelers fell in Denver, 23-16, in a game wide receiver Antonio Brown, running back Le’Veon Bell, and offensive linemen Kelvin Beachum and Maurkice Pouncey missed with injury. “Sometimes, man, things don’t come together for you,” Tomlin said. The Pittsburgh offense put up strong numbers that year. Quarterback Ben Roethlisberger recorded 3,938 passing yards with 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions in just 11 starts. Wide receiver Antonio Brown put up a 136-catch, 1,834-yard season with 10 touchdowns. Wide receivers Markus Wheaton and Martavis Bryant each recorded well over 700 receiving yards each, with tight end Heath Miller adding another 535. The Pittsburgh run game that year was led by DeAngelo Williams (907 rushing yards in 10 starts) and Bell (556 yards in six starts). The starting offensive line was made up of Beachum, Ramon Foster, Pouncey, David DeCastro and Marcus Gilbert. On defense, the 2015 Steelers finished 11th in the NFL that year in scoring, led by a core of Cam Heyward, Stephon Tuitt, Lawrence Timmons, James Harrison and Ryan Shazier. Tomlin was reportedly more emotional than usual following the loss in Denver. “That team? That team was as talented as any team I’ve ever been around,” Tomlin told the Today Show. “We had the goods. But that’s what I love and respect about football, man. It’s a single elimination tournament. It’s not best out of seven. We went into that stadium that day without our No. 1 running back and without our No. 1 wideout, and we suffered the consequences of it. That’s life. “But if you ask me the best team I’ve been around, it would probably be that team.”

title: 5 questions about the Falcons for Steelers fans ahead of Week 1
summary: Both the Steelers and the Falcons have new coaching staffs heading into Week 1. It’s safe to say both franchises will be looking to start their new era off on the right foot with a victory. I spoke with Kevin Knight of The Falcoholic to learn a bit about what’s new with the Atlanta Falcons. […]
full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) attempts to make a catch over New Orleans Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry (4) during the second half at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Both the Steelers and the Falcons have new coaching staffs heading into Week 1. It’s safe to say both franchises will be looking to start their new era off on the right foot with a victory. I spoke with Kevin Knight of The Falcoholic to learn a bit about what’s new with the Atlanta Falcons. 1. The Falcons have three exciting skill players in Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts, but have one of the rougher QB situations right now, with Tua Tagovailoa slated to start after a disappointing preseason. Or potentially Cooper Rush? What can we reasonably expect to see from the Atlanta offense? Kevin Knight: Well, now even Tua Tagovailoa is out of the lineup thanks to an oblique injury suffered during individual drills on Thursday. That means Cooper Rush at the helm (who, in truth, may not be any worse than Tua based on the aforementioned preseason). What you’re going to see is a lot of quick game, and as much Bijan Robinson as the team can muster. If Atlanta can run the ball well and get Bijan going, they can score points. So that’ll be the plan, with the passing game largely taking a complementary role until Michael Penix Jr. returns. 2. Likewise, a promising Falcons defense is starting the year shorthanded on pass rush with Jalon Walker out for the year due to injury and James Pearce Jr. serving a suspension for off-field conduct. How does the team plan to replace their production? Kevin Knight: This is a good defense that will have to find ways to manufacture pass rush. Thankfully, Jeff Ulbrich is an evil genius with his blitz packages, and he’s got a lot of interesting looks planned. Expect to see a lot of linebacker and slot blitzes to supplement their weaker edge rusher room, along with a lot of emphasis on interior pass rush. Atlanta has a really nice interior duo with Brandon Dorlus (who was leading all interior defensive linemen in the NFC with 8.5 sacks last season before injury) and trade acquisition Gervon Dexter Sr. They’re hoping the interior can offset some of their weaknesses outside. 3. The Falcons hired Kevin Stefanski this offseason, a coach Steelers fans are familiar with thanks to his years with the Browns. It’s still early, but what are your initial reactions to what he’s brought to the team, and what are your expectations of him long-term? Kevin Knight: I like Kevin Stefanski and think it pretty much takes a miracle worker to extract any amount of success from the Cleveland Browns organization. It does seem like there’s a coherent, forward-thinking plan in place for this Falcons team for the first time in years. I don’t necessarily expect a lot of success in 2026 based on the moves made to this point and the way the team is structured, but I do expect Atlanta to be one of the most aggressive teams in free agency and the draft in 2027. 4. Who are some under-the-radar players on the Falcons that could make an impact in this game against the Steelers? Kevin Knight: As I mentioned before, Brandon Dorlus is a borderline-elite interior pass rusher who may also get some run on the edge. Linebacker Divine Deablo was the biggest surprise in last year’s free agent class and completely transformed the defense when he was on the field. Second-year safety Xavier Watts was a DROY candidate in 2025 and forms a dynamic duo with veteran Jessie Bates III. Atlanta will be starting two rookies on defense: Avieon Terrell (brother of A.J. Terrell) in the slot, and Kendal Daniels at linebacker. Both impressed in training camp, with Daniels being a particularly pleasant surprise given his Day 3 selection. 5. What will the keys to the game have been if the Falcons come away with the victory? Give us your final score prediction. Kevin Knight: Atlanta will need a dominant day on defense and special teams, and will probably need to benefit from some short fields thanks to turnovers or good returns. Cooper Rush must play efficient, mistake-free football, even if it’s not particularly flashy. And Bijan Robinson is going to have to take over the game. If all that happens, maybe the Falcons have a shot to take down the Steelers in Pittsburgh for the first time in history. Not holding my breath though. Thinking Steelers, 20-10. title: Steelers-Falcons preview: What to expect from Atlanta’s offense, defense in Week 1
summary: The regular season is back, and so are Read & React’s game previews. This week, we’ll take a look at the Atlanta Falcons, who finished 2025 with an 8-9 record and third place in the NFC South. Atlanta, like Pittsburgh, will be debuting a new head coach in Week 1. The Falcons fired Raheem Morris […]
full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) runs the ball against the New Orleans Saints in the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The regular season is back, and so are Read & React’s game previews. This week, we’ll take a look at the Atlanta Falcons, who finished 2025 with an 8-9 record and third place in the NFC South. Atlanta, like Pittsburgh, will be debuting a new head coach in Week 1. The Falcons fired Raheem Morris after the team’s disappointing finish last year, hiring former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski to lead the team in 2026. It’s a new era for the Falcons. What can the Steelers expect to face in their season opener? What to expect from the Falcons’ offense Rushing YPG 2025: 125.8 (8th) Passing YPG 2025: 207.2 (19th) PPG 2025: 20.8 (24th) RP : The Atlanta Falcons are a strange offense to wrap your head around. On the one hand, they have three first-round talents that most of the football-watching community agrees are supremely talented. There’s Bijan Robinson, the do-it-all running back the Falcons selected eighth overall in 2023 and whom they just made one of the league’s richest ball carriers with an extension this offseason. Falcons also boast two highly drafted pass catchers: receiver Drake London (2022’s eighth overall selection) and Kyle Pitts (2021’s fourth overall selection). Both London and Pitts signed big-money extensions this summer as well. That collection of talent alone makes them a team you can’t afford to sleep on. However, outside of the Browns — whose coach last year is now the head coach in Atlanta —the Falcons might have the worst quarterback situation in the NFL. Another former eighth-overall selection, Michael Penix Jr., is still not healthy enough to take the field. That meant the Steelers were supposed to see former Dolphin Tua Tagovailoa, a player who just had a brutal preseason and whom Miami is paying just under $52.8 million to play anywhere else. Things were so bad for Tua this summer, NBC had this report ahead of the Patriots-Seahawks game yesterday: “If it doesn’t go well for Tua and he gets benched again, I’m told there is a strong possibility the Falcons will do what the Dolphins did and cut Tua Tagovailoa.” We haven’t even played yet. 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/h1I7xbbOhR — Carrie (@Carrie_ATL) September 10, 2026 Things took another turn Thursday when, less than 24 hours later, Tua seemed to suffer an oblique injury that has put his availability into question. Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa appeared to suffer discomfort during individual throwing drills Thursday and briefly went to the ground. Tagovailoa missed the first week of training camp due to lower back spasms. — Josh Kendall (@JoshTheAthletic) September 10, 2026 As I mentioned before, ESPN’s Adam Schefter already reported that Penix would be inactive Sunday , so he isn’t an option should Tua have to miss this. That means the Falcons might be forced to turn to a player Mike McCarthy should be quite familiar with, having coached him in Dallas. Cooper Rush said he took all the reps with the 1s today. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) September 10, 2026 All this is to say that the offensive situation for Atlanta is messy, and while that should set the Steelers up for success, it can make projecting the exact offense we’ll see a muddled picture. Still, Steelers fans should recognize elements of what the Falcons are likely to run Sunday. Stefanski was Cleveland’s head coach for six seasons. His offensive coordinator, Tommy Rees, was with the Browns the past two seasons as well, growing from passing game coordinator in 2024 to OC in 2025. As such, we should expect to see a run game featuring wide zone runs, a healthy dose of play-action and bootlegs from under center, and formations with multiple tight ends on the field. With that and the Falcons’ quarterback situation in mind, focus number one should be shutting down Robinson and the run game. Robinson is the most talented player on that offense, and he’s got the production to match. In three seasons, Robinson’s produced 3,910 rushing yards, 198 receptions for 1,738 yards, and 34 total touchdowns. He is the engine behind the Falcons’ attack, and he’s difficult to bring down. In 2025, Robinson was second in the league in average yards after contact (3.9) while the Steelers were 10th worst in that stat (3.10) as a defense. No. 3 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @AtlantaFalcons RB Bijan Robinson! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/seqOFrSuVx — NFL (@NFL) September 2, 2026 With a backup quarterback in, there’s a strong chance Robinson leads both the Falcons’ rushing and passing attack on Sunday. As for the more traditional pass catchers, London and Pitts might arguably be more effective with Rush under center than they might have been with Tagovailoa. London is a traditional possession receiver who primarily lines up outside, but he also moonlights as a power slot, with 30.7% of his career snaps coming inside. London isn’t a player who creates a ton of separation with his routes, but he knows how to box out opposing defensive backs to secure the ball and has a 52% conversion rate on contested balls. 3 Minutes of @DrakeLondon_ jump balls #DirtyBirds https://t.co/eTBsfsQKRz pic.twitter.com/yBzjquRwWD — 𝙁𝙖𝙡𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙨 𝙈𝙪𝙨𝙚 (@ATLFalconsMuse) January 23, 2026 Meanwhile, Pitts had a return to form in 2025. After eclipsing 1,000 yards as a rookie, he battled injuries and inconsistent quarterback play in the three seasons that followed. Last year, he looked fully healthy again, totaling 928 yards and setting career highs in receptions (88), touchdowns (5), and yards after the catch (399). Knowing about Stefanski’s proclivity for featuring tight ends in his offense, I would circle Pitts as the player the Steelers should be most focused on stopping after Robinson. Kyle Pitts Sr. 11 REC, 166 YDS, 3 TDs vs TB Tonight. HAVE A NIGHT KYLE PITTS. pic.twitter.com/l2ZAHeFwQx https://t.co/nesfyquOpL — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) December 12, 2025 Outside of Atlanta’s big three, the Falcons receiving corps is a bit of a hodgepodge of role players. Jahan Dotson might be familiar to the Penn State fans in Steeler Nation, but he’s on his third team in five seasons and has struggled to match the promise of his rookie season when he scored seven touchdowns for Washington. He was held under 20 receptions and under 275 yards in each of the past two seasons while playing for the Eagles. Likewise, Olamide Zaccheaus is an eighth-year NFL journeyman on his second stint with the Falcons. He has just 2,311 career yards and 15 touchdowns, and is more known for doing the dirty work offenses need from a complementary receiver. If there is one wild card I’d keep an eye on, it’s rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch. Branch is a smaller receiver (5’10, 180 pounds) with a limited route tree, but a reputation for creating yards after the catch on designed touches near the line of scrimmage. Whether it’s Tagovailoa or Rush — who also has a spotty track record throwing deep with a career completion percentage of just 33.3% on throws 20+ yards downfield — I wouldn’t be surprised to see a few plays designed for Branch to try to create some easy-button looks that might still result in explosive gains, even with a limited quarterback. title: Enemy Reaction 2026: New England Patriots (with bonus Rams meltdown!)
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks lost to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1 of last season, they held a late 13-10 lead and gave up a game-winning touchdown in the final two minutes of regulation. Similar scenario in 2026 against the New England Patriots, and ‘The Dark Side’ wrote a different, happier ending to turn […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after intercepting a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks lost to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1 of last season, they held a late 13-10 lead and gave up a game-winning touchdown in the final two minutes of regulation. Similar scenario in 2026 against the New England Patriots, and ‘The Dark Side’ wrote a different, happier ending to turn what could’ve been a disastrous opening night into a thrilling victory. No Sam Darnold? No problem. Drew Lock came through with some timely, tough plays despite having no first-team practice reps all week, while the Seahawks defense showcased their dominance even without Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada available. It’s time for Enemy Reaction! If you’re new to this series, which I’ve done for the last 15 years (!!) on Field Gulls, we relive the game highlights through the real-time lenses of both our game thread and the opposition game thread. This week we’re not just including Pats Pulpit , we’re also giving cameos to Niners Nation , Turf Show Times , and the new SB Nation NFL Community page where every fanbase can congregate and talk ball. Note : It’s hard to fit game thread images into this article without them automatically shrinking. Whether on mobile or a tablet or desktop, you may have to tap the screenshots twice to get the full image dimensions. If you’re on the SB Nation app, you can tap on an image and zoom in. Sam Darnold sacked by Dre’Mont Jones, gets up limping (0-0) Josh Jobe commits pass interference on A.J. Brown (0-0) Eli Raridon scores first touchdown of 2026 season (7-0 NE) Chazz Surratt roughing the passer penalty results in Patriots field goal (10-0 NE) Cooper Kupp’s one-handed catch sets up Jason Myers field goal (10-3 NE) Nehemiah Pritchett picks off Drake Maye! (10-3 SEA) Jaxon Smith-Njigba takes a 4th-and-1 pass to the house for a tying touchdown! (10-10) Julian Love gets Drake Maye again, setting up go-ahead field goal (13-10 SEA) Drake Maye throws the game to Josh Jobe, Seahawks win! (13-10 SEA FINAL) Bonus reaction from the SB Nation NFL community game thread Bonus reaction from 49ers and Ram s fans Post-game recap: Stock down on Drake Maye ( Phil Perry, NBC Sports Boston ) Growth for Drake Maye in his third season, his second in Josh McDaniels’ offense, was going to be measured not by how much more he could do. He proved last season he could carry a less-than-star-studded offense and look like arguably the best quarterback in football. Growth, rather, would be measured by how consistently he could pare down his mistakes. After shaky performances against high-end defenses throughout last year’s postseason, the expectation was that that four-game reality check would spur change. But questions lingered prior to the start of the season. How frequently could he tamp down his playmaking, gun-slinging mindset when the situation called for it? How often could he make the patient, prudent choice when chaos reigned? How quickly, in essence, could his game mature? While Maye kept the Patriots in Seattle with his scrambling and the occasional timely throw — a 19-yarder to Mack Hollins in the final drive kept their chances alive in a second-and-21 situation — he, by his own admission, got impatient and failed his first test against another top-tier defense. Post-game recap: Patriots lose rematch in frustrating fashion ( Bob George, Patsfans.com ) Defensively, when you can hold Seattle to 13 points at home, that’s a good job. Other than the JSN touchdown, the defense did well. They were gashed a couple of times by rookie running back Jadarian Price, but they sealed that up as the game went on. Both teams lost top offensive weapons along the way. Sam Darnold was hurt on the fifth play of the game and did not return, putting Lock into the game. A.J. Brown hurt his ankle on the fourth play of the third quarter and also did not return. Lock clearly outplayed Maye. Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards and one touchdown. His rating was 113.3. If there was one other issue you might have had with the Patriots, it was in their overuse of Stevenson. This may have been because Lock was in as quarterback for Seattle instead of Darnold. Stevenson finished with 51 yards rushing but averaged only 2.8 yards per carry. He did lead the Patriots with five pass catches, while Hollins led the team with 51 receiving yards. Given that this was a road game against the defending champs in one of the toughest road venues, the Patriots played well enough to win and simply could not close the deal. The Patriots have time to correct things, and come out better against Pittsburgh a week from Sunday. Highlights of Seattle’s comeback as called by Patriots announcers Bob Socci and Scott Zolak Patriots announcers lament the greatness of the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks pic.twitter.com/wg3GYefOuY — 📽️ Red Tribe Cinema (@ClayWendler) September 10, 2026 Post-game video: Drake Maye comes unglued ( NBC Sports Boston ) Bonus Reaction: Los Angeles Rams disaster Mike Evans said MINE 🏈 SFvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/XONVPkC08v — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 . @49ers WITH A BIG STOP ON 4TH DOWN 🔥 SFvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/UHGJ5anrgX — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 PURDY CONNECTS WITH DEEBO FOR THE TD!! SFvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/XKrxUtmLzI — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 Alright, that’s a hell of a way to start Enemy Reaction this season! We’ll see if the good times can keep rolling with Drew Lock and company down in Glendale against the Arizona Cardinals. Yes, the Cardinals are expected to be awful, but we’ll be able to sit back and relax all day on Sunday to see how the Mike LaFleur era begins against the Los Angeles Chargers. Thanks for reading and go ‘Hawks!

title: 8 snap count observations from Seahawks win over Patriots
summary: It’s usually not all that notable when a team comes back from 10 points in the second half to win a game, but the Seattle Seahawks overcoming a 10-0 third quarter deficit to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 to start the 2026 NFL season is one of those exceptions. Sam Darnold was lost to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball against the New England Patriots during the first half of the NFL football game at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s usually not all that notable when a team comes back from 10 points in the second half to win a game, but the Seattle Seahawks overcoming a 10-0 third quarter deficit to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 to start the 2026 NFL season is one of those exceptions. Sam Darnold was lost to injury on the fifth play of the game, the Seahawks defense was already missing starters Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada, penalties were killing Seattle in all three phases, and the offense was struggling to sustain drives for most of the night. In the blink of an eye, the penalties stopped, the defense created three massive interceptions, and Drew Lock and company did just enough to score the game’s final 13 points. We now have the snap count data from last night, so let’s take a look at what stands out on offense and defense. Seattle Seahawks offensive snap counts The Seahawks essentially rolled with four targets from the WR and TE position . Montorie Foster Jr was the team’s fourth WR on the depth chart with no Tory Horton available, and the Seahawks opted to limit him to special teams. It was all about Jaxon Smith-Njigba, A.J. Barner, Cooper Kupp, and Rashid Shaheed. Elijah Arroyo and Eric Saubert had just 21 snaps combined and only 10 of them were on passing downs. Losing Sam Darnold early likely junked the gameplan and therefore changed the snap counts on the fly. Brady Russell gets his heaviest offensive workload to date . With Robbie Ouzts out for the season, it’s Brady Russell (or is it George Holani, Mike Tirico?) who will be the fullback this year. He played a career-high 17 offensive snaps, catching the first two passes of his NFL career. Jadarian Price and George Holani split RB1 duties for the night . How would the Seahawks handle their rookie running back’s snaps? Well, out of his 11 snaps on passing plays, Price did not have a single rep in pass protection. Not even a chip. Holani had 23 snaps, and several of his passing down reps involved taking on a pass rusher. This probably isn’t changing for as long as Zach Charbonnet is out, or until the coaching staff feels Price can take some of those responsibilities in the passing game. Emanuel Wilson only had three snaps, one of which was on the failed 3rd and 1 (with Josh Jones’ only snap coming in this same play) . The next play was a touchdown to Jaxon Smith-Njigba so Wilson can say he was on the field for Seattle’s only TD. Seattle Seahawks defensive snap counts Rodney Thomas II plays almost every snap . The former Indianapolis Colts starter was called up from the practice squad to replace Ty Okada, and while A.J. Finley was directly signed to the active roster, Finley was basically a healthy scratch without being an official inactive. Rodney’s only snap missed was the Patriots touchdown at the goal line, which was so stacked with linebackers and d-lineman that the only secondary player on the field was Julian Love. Thomas helped spark Seattle’s comeback with the tip drill interception alongside Nehemiah Pritchett. Dante Fowler Jr didn’t feature much in his Seahawks debut , and there were a few occasions in which he was lined up alongside two other edge rushers, kicking one of them to the inside. Mike Macdonald twice had Fowler line up as a “Wide 9” beyond the tight end. He only had six pass rushing snaps based on my initial charting. Tyrice Knight did not play a single snap on third down , which is unsurprising given Seattle’s default is 5+ DBs in these scenarios. Nearly every snap he had was a running play, but he at least got on the field. Josh Jobe takes a firmer CB2 role in Week 1, but Nehemiah Pritchett plays plenty . When Josh Jobe increased his role in last season’s defense, he didn’t really wrest the CB2 spot away from Riq Woolen. Some weeks Jobe played more, other weeks Woolen played more, and Woolen outsnapped Jobe throughout the playoffs. For Week 1 of 2026, Jobe solidified himself as the clear CB2 on the team, but don’t discount Nehemiah Pritchett being that nickel corner. Pritchett had a great performance and played 53 snaps, more or less coming out of the game when they put Tyrice Knight in as a third linebacker. And that’s a wrap for Week 1. The champs can rest and recover before a Week 2 road trip to Glendale to face the Arizona Cardinals.

full_text: San Francisco 49ers' wide receivers #5 Mike Evans and #7 De'Zhaun Stribling talk to a member of the coaching staff during a training session at AAMI Park in Melbourne on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / -- IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE -- | AFP via Getty Images “Waiting for injury update” news days are the worst. At least this particular situation is 1) a Saturday after a big Thursday win 2) has plenty of exciting highlights from said win to dig through. I’ve been enjoying reading more about how Shanahan is using “rounded motions” with Kyle Juszczyk, all the ways he was sending random players to chip Myles Garrett, and the different superhero plays that Fred Warner was making all game. 49ers vs. Rams PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Right tackle Colton McKivitz’s 75.1 offensive grade was the highest among 49ers offensive linemen, while left guard Connor Colby’s 53.5 offensive grade was the lowest.” Kawakami: The 49ers’ obsession, commitment, and triumphant Australia Plan (paywall) “We’ll see what happens next; maybe the 49ers will fall into a funk after spending so much time in Australia and expending so much energy to get this win. But they’ve got two extremely winnable home games in the next two weeks (Miami and Arizona) before the season starts to get serious again. I’d imagine that we probably won’t really know much more about the 49ers’ full-season biorhythms until the Oct. 11 game in Seattle. That’s when we’ll probably really know if the 49ers played this 100% right or are set to go through some body-clock payback.” 49ers enjoy family reunion in rout of Rams: ‘It felt like I never left’ (paywall) “During the 16-hour flight to Australia, the 49ers had strict instructions on when to sleep, how many ounces of fluids to drink, when to put their window shades up and how often to slip on blue-light glasses. After rolling over their division rivals, the plan for the flight back was more simple. “Party it up,” Warner said.” 49ers’ game review: How Kyle Shanahan dinked, dunked and KO’d the Rams’ vaunted defense (paywall) “Shanahan uses Juszczyk in motion creatively. On Thursday, Juszczyk was often aligned as a tight end before he looped across the line of scrimmage, often running a half circle, allowing him to have a running head start as a 235-pound lead blocker. On the 49ers’ first offensive snap, Juszczyk lined up outside Williams, went in motion and led the way for a running back Christian McCaffrey’s 6-yard burst up the middle. Six plays later, Juszczyk on the right side, ran across the formation and cleared out safety Kam Curl on a 5-yard screen to running back Kaelon Black on the left side. Juszczyk’s banana-shaped motions created social-media buzz. But they aren’t new. In fact, Juszczyk was doing it against the Rams last season in a loss in November. After the in-motion Juszczyk looped around QB Mac Jones, who was in shotgun formation, to serve a full-speed lead blocker on an 11-yard run, Fox analyst Tom Brady commented on Shanahan’s play design. “In 25 years of watching football, I’ve never seen that exact concept,” Brady said.” 49ers signed Kyle Shanahan to an extension this offseason “The previously unreported move was revealed by Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix on Friday following the 49ers’ win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne.”

title: 49ers Snap Counts and Grades: Nick Bosa and Fred Warner return and dominate
summary: The San Francisco 49ers kicked off the 2026 season with a convincing and dominant win over the Los Angeles Rams Thursday night. The travel plans were discussed the entire week, but ultimately, the 49ers were sharper and executed better. Now, the Rams have a long, long flight back to figure out what went wrong in […]
full_text: Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers kicked off the 2026 season with a convincing and dominant win over the Los Angeles Rams Thursday night. The travel plans were discussed the entire week, but ultimately, the 49ers were sharper and executed better. Now, the Rams have a long, long flight back to figure out what went wrong in their quest to become more than paper champions. The 49ers will have time before the home opener against Miami to reacclimate to the time zone. Here are the 49ers’ snap counts and grades, according to PFF. Offense Quarterback – Brock Purdy 65 (63.3) The only blemish on Purdy’s record was an interception to Quinton Lake. Following the interception, Purdy was masterful and in command. Finishing with a stat line of 25/34 (73.5%), 205 yards, and three touchdowns would have been even more impressive, as PFF credited Purdy with three drops by his receivers. Purdy was under pressure on 22.2% of his dropbacks. That’s only eight dropbacks out of 36. The biggest play for the offense was the deep shot to Demarcus Robinson. Running back – Christian McCaffrey 36 (61.4), Kaelon Black 28 (57.2), Kyle Juszczyk 33 (44.7) Well, what do we have here now? Jordan James was inactive, and that ends any debate about who the RB2 of this team is, but Kaelon Black out-carried Christian McCaffrey 14 to 10. The rushing attack looked back on track from years past, and McCaffrey finished with 68 yards to Black’s 65. We have a one-two punch here, folks; one of the biggest surprises to come from this game. Wide Receiver – Mike Evans 49 (77.9), Demarcus Robinson 41 (68.2), Deebo Samuel 27 (69.6), De’Zhaun Stribling 21 (46.8), Jacob Cowing 5 (44.6), KhaDarel Hodge 1 (58.3) De’Zhaun Stribling’s injury dampened the win, and we are waiting for more information on his injury and timetable. Mike Evans looked every bit the Hall of Famer in his first action as a 49er. Six catches, five for first downs, and a touchdown grab on a fade in the end zone. Three contested catch opportunities, three contested catches. Robinson made sure to get revenge on his former team with his long touchdown catch, and look who continued to give the Rams that belt? Deebo Samuel. Six grabs for 48 yards and a touchdown, and jump started a 49ers drive with a long kickoff return. Tight End – Luke Farrell 46 (57.1), George Kittle 30 (47.0), Jake Tonges 8 (53.4) Unfortunately, Jake Tonges left the game with an injury, and the hope is it isn’t very serious. George Kittle returned on a bit of a pitch count, but overall he looked great. It’s not hyperbole to say this was Luke Farrell’s best game as a 49er, too. Offensive Line – Dominick Puni 65 (65.4), Connor Colby 65 (53.5), Colton McKivitz 65 (75.1), Jake Brendel 65 (69.0), Trent Williams 65 (68.8) It’s a shame Myles Garrett couldn’t make the trip to Australia. Wait, Garrett played last night? Interesting. Trent Williams and Dominick Puni led the team with 75.1 and 82.7 pass-blocking grades, respectively. Much was made of the left guard situation, but Connor Colby was very good as a run blocker, and the results showed for the two running backs. Just a very solid showing from the offensive line as a whole. Very encouraging. Defense Defensive Line – Osa Odighizuwa 36 (59.9), Nick Bosa 36 (86.2), Gracen Halton 31 (30.4), Romello Height 30 (53.2), Keion White 30 (69.4), Cj West 23 (33.2), James Thompson Jr 21 (29.1), Khalid Kareem 19 (60.8), Ogbo Okoronkwo 18 (59.9) There were times when the 49ers’ defensive line was getting blown off the football facing the run, but Nick Bosa looked just like the DPOY version. Bosa single-handedly was shoring up the run defense, and Osa Odighizuwa made his presence felt multiple times. The good news is there is room for improvement for the rookies, but the anchors will be Bosa and Osa, and that feels great. Five total pressures for the former Cowboy. Mykel Williams returning after Week 4 only improves the depth and flexibility. Linebacker – Fred Warner 53 (91.1), Dre Greenlaw 40 (35.4), Jaden Dugger 34 (60.3), Garret Wallow 13 (46.1) This just in: Fred Warner is still the best in the world. A forced fumble was the cherry on top for the returning linebacker. Warner almost came away with a pick on the first play of the game, but my goodness, Warner is back, and who would have thought bringing back Bosa and Warner would be beneficial for the defense. Secondary – Marques Sigle 61 (80.2), Renardo Green 61 (68.9), Deommodore Lenoir 61 (54.0), Ji’Ayir Brown 55 (61.9), Upton Stout 36 (80.4), Jack Jones 8 (70.6), Malik Mustapha 6 (67.1) This was a huge game for Marques Sigle. Without a target in coverage, Sigle was physical and finished with four tackles, five assists, and a defensive stop. Renardo Green made an incredible play on his interception and sank perfectly underneath the route for his first of the season. Raheem Morris had some interesting wrinkles, and one is his dime package with Jack Jones on the field. Early returns are great for creativity, and you have to wonder if his plans are opponent-dependent.
