full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Kyle Shanahan head coach of the San Francisco 49ers looks on following the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyle Shanahan will remain the 49ers head coach for the long term after signing an extension this offseason. The previously unreported move was revealed by Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix on Friday following the 49ers’ win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne. Shanahan, per Pelissero, was previously believed to be signed through 2027. Pelissero did not confirm the length of his new deal, but it will take him well beyond a decade as San Francisco’s head coach. It is noteworthy that there have, as yet, been no simultaneous reports of a contract extension for general manager John Lynch. Lynch is signed through the end of this current season having last signed an extension back in 2023. Shanahan and Lynch came as a package way back in 2017 when the latter was recruited as GM after Shanahan agreed to become the head coach. Lynch has previously had offers to return to broadcasting, reportedly turning down one from Amazon back in 2022. Of course, given how Shanahan’s extension went unreported in the offseason, there’s a chance the 49ers have already made a similar move with Lynch that has not yet been made public. However, at this moment, Shanahan’s contract being announced on its own raises the possibility of an end to their partnership. The 49ers’ dominant 27-7 win over the Rams took Shanahan to 83-67 in the regular season. He is 9-5 in the postseason, with last season’s divisional round loss to the Seattle Seahawks his first playoff defeat before the Conference Championship stage. Shanahan moved level with former 49ers coach Buck Shaw with his 92nd combined win. He will surpass Shaw and move into 53rd on the all-time combined wins list when the 49ers claim their next victory.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 3 stars from the 49ers’ blowout win over the Rams: All hail, Trent Williams
summary: One team on Thursday night looked like they were used to all the circumstances around playing on the other side of the world, while the other looked like they hobbled into Australia a little too close to game time. The San Francisco 49ers decimated the Los Angeles Rams to the tune of a 27-7 rout […]
full_text: Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images One team on Thursday night looked like they were used to all the circumstances around playing on the other side of the world, while the other looked like they hobbled into Australia a little too close to game time. The San Francisco 49ers decimated the Los Angeles Rams to the tune of a 27-7 rout in Melbourne, Australia. There might have been some moments where the game felt close early on, but once the 49ers got rolling, there was no stopping them. A handful of players deserve a spot on the season’s first-three stars list, but unfortunately only three can make it (it’s kind of in the title). Mike Evans had six receptions, all six resulting in a first down or a touchdown. Deebo Samuel wasn’t too far behind with six receptions of his own. Renardo Green hauled in the first interception of his career. The 49ers had a two-headed running back room with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. But despite how those honorable mentions looked, here are the three stars from the 49ers’ opening-night win over the Rams: 3rd star: LT Trent Williams Myles Garrett this. Myles Garrett that. People were so wrapped up in the former Cleveland Brown that they forgot the 49ers have the greatest offensive tackle to ever play the game. The 49ers offensive line as a whole dominated the coveted Rams front four all Thursday night but it was Trent Williams who had to deal with the NFL single-season sack record holder. The 49ers line held the Rams pass rush to just six pressures, five quarterback hurries, and kept Brock Purdy clean with no sacks. But let’s focus on the left side of the line. Williams allowed two pressures and two hurries, but when Garrett was against him, it was lights out for the defending Defensive Player of the Year. Garrett finished with just one pressure, one hurry, and one sack, not exactly the stat line he was expecting for his debut with Los Angeles. Oh, and did I mention Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (1) finished with more tackles than Garrett (0)? All we heard entering this game was how could the 49ers middling offensive line ever stop Garrett? Well, the answer was big Trent Williams. I believe we are watching the greatest run blocking tackle of all-time in Trent Williams, who at 38 is still elite. His consistency, longevity and length of dominance is what a first-ballot HOF OL career looks like. pic.twitter.com/C9iPTVoaTh — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 11, 2026 2nd star: WR Brock Purdy It was an ugly start. Purdy’s second-quarter interception was about as bad as interceptions can get. But from there, Purdy settled in and was as close to perfect as you could ask. The interception came when Quentin Lake dropped back into coverage off the line of scrimmage, something Purdy obviously didn’t notice, handing Lake maybe the easiest interception of his career. It came with the Rams up 7-3 and could have been a turning point in the game, but Matthew Stafford followed with an interception of his own, and the threat was wiped out. Purdy would go 12-for-14 with three touchdowns from that point on. He would make the Rams pay almost instantly, dropping a dime on the following drive on a deep shot to Demarcus Robinson for a 39-yard touchdown, for what proved to be the game-winning score that gave the 49ers a 10-7 lead. San Francisco would get the ball to start the second half and Purdy would get back to work. Christian McCaffrey would help move the ball with a pair of good runs, but Purdy wouldn’t throw an incomplete pass with his three attempts on the drive. He would close the drive with a beautifully thrown fade route ball (one Jim Harbaugh would have been proud of) to Mike Evans for his second touchdown pass of the evening. Then would come Purdy’s pièce de résistance of the evening. With the 49ers offense starting at its own 1-yard-line and their backs against the wall, Purdy would cook. The drive started with a quick 14-yard gain to Luke Farrell to get San Francisco out of the shade of their own goalposts. Then another 13-yard gain to Deebo Samuel to get the ball near midfield. A few plays later, Purdy would connect with Samuel again for a 15-yard score, his third and final touchdown pass of the game. Back against the goal line, and Purdy goes four-for-four for 48 yards (including two runs combining for 26 yards) for a dagger 99-yard drive. An insane bounceback from his sluggish start. 1st star: LB Fred Warner How much better does the 49ers defense feel with No. 54 at the heart of it? After his 2025 ended prematurely because of injury, Warner wasted no time to remind everybody who the best linebacker in the league is. On the opening play of the game, Stafford tried to force a pass to Nacua to get his star receiver going, but Warner was there, nearly making a diving interception, settling for a pass breakup to start a three-and-out drive for Los Angeles. If you know anything about Warner, he might have a near-miss play here and there, but at some point he will make that big play, and Thursday night was no different. His first big play set up the 49ers’ 99-yard touchdown-scoring drive. With the Rams at the half-yard line still trailing by 10, Sean McVay decided the best course of action would be a quarterback sneak with the 38-year-old Stafford. Unfortunately for the Rams quarterback, Warner was there waiting (with the help of Gracen Halton and Osa Odighizuwa) to stuff the attempt and force the turnover on downs. If Purdy’s 99-yard drive wasn’t the killshot, Warner went for the Rams’ neck to ensure it was over. With Los Angeles in desperation mode down 17, Stafford and company would get the ball near midfield when Warner would strike again. Stafford would find Tyler Higbee but the tight end would be slowed by Dre Greenlaw, before Warner would come in to knock the ball free with a peanut punch, recovered by Keion White, ending any Los Angeles comeback hopes. Oh, and Warner led the 49ers with 11 total tackles and five solo. Just a complete and dominating performance from No. 54. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 1, the standings are: LB Fred Warner – 3 points QB Brock Purdy – 2 points LT Trent Williams – 1 point
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 49ers run game finds elusive balance in dominant Week 1 display
summary: The 49ers’ run game has long since been a one-man show. Save for the 2024 season when he spent most of the season on the shelf through injury, the fortunes of the ground attack have hinged almost squarely on Christian McCaffrey. With McCaffrey now 30 years old, that did not seem like a sensible approach […]
full_text: (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The 49ers’ run game has long since been a one-man show. Save for the 2024 season when he spent most of the season on the shelf through injury, the fortunes of the ground attack have hinged almost squarely on Christian McCaffrey. With McCaffrey now 30 years old, that did not seem like a sensible approach heading into 2026 and, in their season-opening demolition of the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, the Niners changed course to devastating effect. San Francisco has spent years investing draft capital in the running back position with little return on investment. Though the Niners had Elijah Mitchell and Jordan Mason behind McCaffrey in 2023, no back has been able to command something approaching an equal share of the workload with the four-time first-team All-Pro. But on Thursday — or Friday local time — McCaffrey was actually in the rare position of having fewer carries than the man behind him on the depth chart. Rookie Kaelon Black had 14 carries to McCaffrey’s 10. Though that was partially due to McCaffrey dealing with cramps, Kyle Shanahan confirmed after the game that having a balanced approach was the plan. “I thought they both ran really hard and really well,” Shanahan said. “I’ll see on the plane exactly how good it was, but it felt like it out there. That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more, whether it was with Kaelon or getting Deebo some carries.” Kaelon Black has a great feel for reading and cutting on these zone runs. Really nice hit here on the 49ers Toss Zorro version. pic.twitter.com/a3FgeWCTp2 — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 11, 2026 Last season, there was little balance as McCaffrey had 311 rush attempts, the highest amount of his career, but averaged just 3.9 yards per carry in one of his least efficient seasons. His backup, Brian Robinson Jr, had just 92 carries. But with McCaffrey and Black sharing the workload more evenly, the 49ers’ run game was outstandingly efficient as San Francisco — aided by some typically nifty scrambling from Brock Purdy — racked up 174 yards. Black had 65 yards on his 14 rushes, an average of 4.6 yards, showing explosiveness through the hole on zone runs that illustrated why Shanahan was convinced to use a third-round selection on a player most had pegged going much later in this year’s draft. 49ers' running game tonight: 5.9 yards per carry 56.7% success rate 0.19 EPA per carry All would have been the best game of the 49ers' season last year — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 11, 2026 The performance of Black drew praise from McCaffrey, who said after the game: “He did incredible. Oh, he’s an awesome back, man. I said this earlier, but he’s a force and he’s someone who’s going to help our team a whole lot. It was really cool to see him go out there and just do what he does.” Yet just as eye-opening as Black’s showing was the impact the rest had on McCaffrey, who, despite the cramps had 68 yards on 10 carries, his average of 6.8 yards his best since his final game of that disrupted 2024 campaign, when he put up 7.6 yards per rush against the Buffalo Bills before suffering a season-ending knee injury. As a team, the 49ers averaged 5.9 yards per rush and 0.19 EPA per carry while putting up a 56.7% success rate on the ground. Both running backs finished the game with positive EPA per rush numbers (Black 0.02 and McCaffrey 0.27). Of course, great credit must go to the offensive line, which got better as the game went on and did an excellent job of demolishing the edges and creating lanes for both backs. But Black’s usage and impact on the game was one of the stories of Week 1 for the 49ers. Having clearly earned the trust of Shanahan, Black justified that faith, with the rest he afforded McCaffrey critical to the most efficient performance in over 20 months for San Francisco’s starter. McCaffrey’s level of usage from past season was never going to be sustainable. For him to avoid the infamous cliff that running backs often hit once they reach 30, McCaffrey needs somebody to share the burden. It is only one game, but the early signs are that, in Black, the 49ers have found a back worthy of doing so. For an offense as focused on the run as that of the 49ers, that may be the biggest development from their hugely impressive blowout win.

title: Rapoport: De’Zhaun Stribling likely to miss some time; tests on hold until the weekend
summary: The San Francisco 49ers cruised their way to a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in Week 1, putting their stamp on the NFL’s favorite to win the Super Bowl in a game where everything went right for them. Well, almost everything. San Francisco lost De’Zhaun Stribling early to an ankle injury, […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: De'Zhaun Stribling #7 of the San Francisco 49ers is attended to by trainers after an injury in the second quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers cruised their way to a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in Week 1, putting their stamp on the NFL’s favorite to win the Super Bowl in a game where everything went right for them. Well, almost everything. San Francisco lost De’Zhaun Stribling early to an ankle injury, and he appeared to re-aggravate the issue shortly after re-entering the field, although the initial outlook seemed far worse with the non-contact nature of the injury. Following the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan eased worries, noting that it was an ankle injury and that Stribling’s Achilles was intact after being carted off the field. Ian Rapoport shared some details on the injury on Friday morning, noting the good news, while mentioning that Stribling will likely miss some time now and that the tests will have to wait until after the 49ers’ flight back from Australia. “We were excited about the debut of De’Zhaun Stribling, one of the more exciting rookies in the NFL this year,” Rapoport said. “Certainly someone who’s going to be a big part of the 49ers offense. That seemed to hit a little bit of a pause after last night. Early in the game, you could see him limping on the field, left with an ankle injury, came back, and ends up exiting with what seemed to be the same ankle injury. “Good news: it’s not an Achilles. He went down kind of like it was, but it is not. That’s what Kyle Shanahan postgame did say. It is an ankle injury. They’re going to see what kind of ankle injury it is. He’s going to have tests but, I don’t know if you guys know this, but they’ve got about a 16-hour flight now, so those tests will have to wait a little bit, but it seems based on the injury that Stribling will likely miss time for the 49ers.” Stribling’s usage prior to his injury was quite notable. While he didn’t get a target in his debut, Stribling was actually the receiver with the most snaps through the time of his injury, being the clear wideout next to Mike Evans in two-receiver sets. 49ers WR snap count as of 7:30 in the 2nd quarter (just in case this is Stribling's last snap) De'Zhaun Stribling 21 Mike Evans 17 Deebo Samuel Sr. 9 Demarcus Robinson 7 Jacob Cowing 3 KhaDarel Hodge 1 Out of 26 plays — Nathan Jahnke (@FFNateJahnke) September 11, 2026 Even after Stribling went out, Deebo Samuel saw a limited snap share, playing only 27 of 65 snaps on Thursday, while Demarcus Robinson stepped into Stribling’s role with 41 snaps. It could be a high-ankle sprain for Stribling, which might cost him a few weeks, but it’s a good sign that he’s not dealing with a significant injury like initially suspected.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 3 quick takeaways from the 49ers dominant Week 1 win: Is this a true Super Bowl contender?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers dominated the Los Angeles Rams in every facet of the game on Thursday evening, winning 27-7 in Australia as they were in control for all of the second half in a strong opener. The 49ers entered the game as 3.5-point underdogs with rep questions about Nick Bosa and George Kittle, who […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers dominated the Los Angeles Rams in every facet of the game on Thursday evening, winning 27-7 in Australia as they were in control for all of the second half in a strong opener. The 49ers entered the game as 3.5-point underdogs with rep questions about Nick Bosa and George Kittle, who were both coming off injuries, while the Rams were ready to debut their new-look addition on defense. They turned out not to be much of a factor, as San Francisco cruised on offense, aside from a Brock Purdy interception, and started off Week 1 on a great note. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers Week 1 win over the Rams on Thursday. Run game flourishes Entering the game, one of the questions I had was about the run game for the 49ers, which was quite inefficient with Christian McCaffrey last year. A lot of the same infrastructure was returning, apart from the addition of Kaelon Black, and it wasn’t clear how much of a timeshare there’d be at running back. Well, the 49ers showed their comfort level with Black, getting him in early and often in the first half, as he led the team with 14 carries. The duo combined for 133 yards on 24 carries, while Brock Purdy and Deebo Samuel added 29 and 12 yards on their own, respectively. The 49ers ran the ball 30 times for 174 yards on a very respectable 5.8 yards per carry. And they did so against one of the NFL’s best defensive lines. I thought the 49ers offensive line played extremely well. And both of their backs looked explosive, as McCaffrey looked very fresh with the running back split. It was a real good day on the ground for the 49ers. Linebackers lead physicality charge on defense Fred Warner had a heck of a game, recording 11 tackles and really making his presence known everywhere on defense, but especially in the run game. Warner flew into lanes, didn’t miss a tackle, and brought the physicality to a rivalry game on defense. But the 49ers as a whole exceeded my expectations in a big way on defense. I thought they’d struggle to defend the run, which happened at times. But the Rams finished with 122 yards on 4.2 yards per carry, as Kyren Williams had just 3.7 yards per carry on 11 attempts, while Blake Corum had 5.4 yards per carry on 10 rushes. I thought San Francisco’s cornerbacks were also quite physical with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, as Matthew Stafford looked quite off. It was a very good showing from the players, and a very quality start for Raheem Morris. Money down The 49ers were the NFL’s best on third downs offensively last year, and they picked up where they left off on Thursday, extending that to both sides of the ball. San Francisco went 7-of-12 on third downs on offense, which led to scoring drives of 15, 9, and 11 plays. Meanwhile, the Rams were just 2-of-9, as they had just one drive over seven plays outside of the final drive in garbage time. The 49ers controlled the time of possession and felt in control throughout the second half as they extended drives and played their style of football. I also thought they did a great job on 1st and 2nd downs to make 3rd downs much more manageable. They had just one third down with a to-go distance of more than five yards, which they converted. It was a good sign for Kyle Shanahan’s offense, as the Niners consistently won in big situations.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers News: Nothing more grouse than a Victory Friday
summary: No matter what happens, I’m just hoping that De’Zhaun Stribling is able to come back strong and still go on with his career at a high level after this injury. I don’t even care that he’ll miss time, I just saw such a talented dude that seemed super smart and committed to the game. You […]
full_text: Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images No matter what happens, I’m just hoping that De’Zhaun Stribling is able to come back strong and still go on with his career at a high level after this injury. I don’t even care that he’ll miss time, I just saw such a talented dude that seemed super smart and committed to the game. You always want to see people like that win. He had an interview with his high school paper that I found on the internet one time and even at that age you’re like, how could you not root for the guy? Prayers up man. That being said… My favorite part of the game was the feeling of going to war with Brock freaking Purdy. He had this Ben Shelton-like intense look in his eyes in the second half, coming back from the pick, and he just started dealing in the third quarter. I don’t know if it’s the play calling or how well the other players executed, but he just looked so locked in, so dialed, just flow state quarterbacking and did what he wanted. The Rams are a good defense on paper and I’m curious if he keeps it up the next few games and later on against the Broncos. The Broncos will have similarly bad linebackers in the passing game but also some absurd talent elsewhere. Defense also looked solid. You love to see it. Happy Friday y’all! Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 49ers’ Brock Purdy looked like a quarterback out to silence his critics “I thought Brock played so well,” Shanahan said after the game. “He had one play I know he wants to take back, the interception to [Rams S Quentin] Lake, but he made some big-time plays, some big-time throws.” ….Purdy said, “…I think Kyle was doing a great job with dialing up the right play calls, and obviously not being aware of when we want to take a shot and go deep and stuff, but the [Rams] defense was giving us our ones and twos in the progression. So, just trying to take that….And then, obviously, when it wasn’t there, I think that was the time in the game where I started using my legs a little bit. And then guys did a great job on the scramble drill, obviously hitting Deebo late.” … Shanahan said,. “The 99-yard drive, there were so many plays there that he had to take off-schedule, where there wasn’t an answer, and he moved the chains with his legs. And I think he found Deebo on one—that was a big off-schedule for the touchdown. So Brock was unbelievable today.” Hutchinson: The 49ers needed this a lot more than the Rams (paywall) “Los Angeles was able to Duo the hell out of the 49ers. They employed double-team runs through their gut while CJ West frequently flailed around and forgot he is not meant to be used as a bowling ball for the opposing team. Despite this issue — one I felt would be crucial to defining the 49ers’ success — the secondary was tremendous. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner were omnipresent. Raheem Morris decided he’d rather trust his four best corners than dare go to big nickel. He used dime more than nickel! The 49ers got rewarded for it against a team that should have theoretically demolished the 49ers with their love of heavy personnel. But the Rams used 13 personnel as a changeup, not as a primary mode of extracting pain. They overwhelmingly stuck to 11 personnel despite their success (5-for-5, 96 yards, +1.06 EPA per SumerSports) in 13….On the other side, the Rams barely ran any man coverage despite having Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie, who … bodybagged Deebo Samuel and the 49ers in the 2023 Super Bowl with a heavy dose of man. The 49ers played more man than they did!….They suddenly have a No. 2 back in Kaelon Black who is a human pistol shrimp. He may not have any interest in reading the flow of the offensive line. But he will shoot through a hole and get positive yardage. If you give him an inch, he’ll take a yard. Shanahan used unique wrinkles from the last few seasons — dash, jet, bump and ghost motions — and bizarre, offset alignments, including a few pre-snap bumps and shuffles to put receivers in the slot, but about 5 yards of depth. He created opportunities for easy throws for Purdy.” Maoicco: What we learned as Purdy, Evans fuel 49ers’ opening win over Rams in Australia “Odighizuwa pressured Stafford relentlessly in the first half with three quarterback hits. Bosa, in his first game back after tearing his right ACL in Week 3 last season, turned up some pressure, too. Cornerback Renardo Green came up with a big play in the first half when he intercepted Stafford’s pass intended for Puka Nacua. But when the 49ers needed a big goal-line stand near the end of the third quarter, it was rookie Gracen Halton and Warner who stopped Stafford for no gain on a push up the middle….And, even more surprising, Aaron Donald had about as much impact on the game as Myles Garrett. Through three quarters of action, Garrett was completely shut out from the stat sheet. He had no tackles, no sacks, no nothing. Donald, who recently came out of retirement and stayed back in California for the Week 1 game, had the same stat line. The 49ers game-planned around Garrett to do their best to make sure he did not wreck the game. Garrett was the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year last season while with the Cleveland Browns. The Rams acquired him in an offseason trade following his 23-sack season.” Cohn: Grading the 49ers After Their 27-7 Win Over the Rams in Australia “First, let’s praise defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. He didn’t sell out to stop the Rams’ running game. He conceded 5.1 yards per carry, which seemed risky, but he was making sure that Stafford wouldn’t beat him. In fact, Morris owned Stafford, just like last season when Morris was the Falcons head coach and they beat the Rams in Week 17. Morris used to be the Rams’ defensive coordinator, so he has faced Stafford countless times in practice and clearly has his number. What a hire for the 49ers. Next, let’s praise Kyle Shanahan. He made all the right calls on this trip. He was right to bring his players out to Australia more than a week before the game. He was right to stop calling passes for Kittle after giving him a chance to show he was ready. He was right to feature Evans. He was right to split carries between McCaffrey and Black. And he was right to hire Morris. As a result, the 49ers just destroyed the team that lots of people predicted to win the Super Bowl. Of course, this one game doesn’t mean the 49ers will win the Super Bowl. Remember, they beat the Seahawks Week 1 last season, and then the Seahawks went on to win the Super Bowl. But that Week 1 win was fluky and close. This one was decisive and embarrassing for the Rams. They deserved every bit of the humiliation the 49ers gave them. They cheated the process of preparation and disrespected the 49ers and Australia by showing up yesterday. Enjoy that long flight home tonight. The 49ers sure will.” ’ Shanahan, McVay brush off travel plans as factor in Niners’ win over Rams “It was definitely worth it coming a little bit early,” receiver Mike Evans said. “I felt like we got acclimated. … We didn’t complain. We actually enjoyed being out here in Melbourne.” The 49ers landed in Melbourne on Sept. 4. They stayed at the Park Hyatt Hotel, where the team arranged for everything from meeting and film rooms, and the 49ers’ chefs prepared meals at the restaurant. The players had access to a nearby spa for various recovery tools such as a cold plunge and red light therapy. When they weren’t planning for the game, the Niners explored the city, trying the various coffee shops and going to group dinners at local restaurants. Running back Christian McCaffrey even got a haircut and was told that his hair “looks cracker,” which he was then informed means it looks good. “Melbourne was sick,” tight end George Kittle said. “I had a great time here. I’m real excited, the fact that we came out early and were here for the whole…

title: Titans vs. Jets picks and predictions
summary: I heard on the radio earlier this week that this is the biggest game in Tennessee Titans history. That’s an absurd statement, but it is one of the biggest Week 1 games that I can remember. The fanbase is standing on the edge of a cliff, ready to jump. Some of them even want to […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to an NFL preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images I heard on the radio earlier this week that this is the biggest game in Tennessee Titans history. That’s an absurd statement, but it is one of the biggest Week 1 games that I can remember. The fanbase is standing on the edge of a cliff, ready to jump. Some of them even want to jump. That is exactly what everyone will do if the Titans lose here. There are a million things we can talk about surrounding this game, but all eyes are going to be on Cam Ward. The jury is still out on what he will be as an NFL quarterback. Don’t let anyone convince you otherwise on that. This one game can’t change that, but it sure would be nice to see him come out and have a really good game here. Ward playing well in a win is about the only thing that can make the fanbase take a step away from that cliff. I’m going to be the optimist here and predict that Ward is going to come out and have his best game as a pro. The New York Jets led the league in passing touchdowns allowed last season and didn’t have an interception all season. Their defense should be better this season with the additions of EDGE David Bailey and CB D’Angelo Ponds in the 2026 NFL Draft, but the Titans should still be able to move the ball through the air. Give me Ward for 275 yards and 2 passing touchdowns. The Titans defense didn’t look great in the preseason, but this is a matchup they should be able to take advantage of. The Jets have some weapons, but they also have Geno Smith. The Titans’ front should be able to get enough pressure on Smith to force him into a couple of bad decisions. The best way to jump start an offense is to give them a short field to work with. This game will probably be close for most of the afternoon, but I think the Titans pull out a 24-17 win. What’s your prediction? The Titans opened as a 3-point favorite, but the line has moved all the way down to Titans -1.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook . Is that a number you are willing to take?

title: Commanders season preview: Stakes are high for Washington, Jayden Daniels
summary: Editor’s note: After posting some insightful stories in The Feed, Hogs Haven’s ShogunofHarlem93 has put together his first story for the main site. He breaks down why this Commanders season is so important for Jayden Daniels, new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones (and those that hired them). Every season, I try to set realistic […]
full_text: Editor’s note: After posting some insightful stories in The Feed, Hogs Haven’s ShogunofHarlem93 has put together his first story for the main site. He breaks down why this Commanders season is so important for Jayden Daniels, new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones (and those that hired them). Every season, I try to set realistic expectations for this Washington Commanders team. In 2024, my only hope was that Jayden Daniels would prove to be Washington’s franchise quarterback. And boy, did he deliver, leading the Commanders all the way to the NFC championship game. After an offseason of adding talent to a barebones roster, I had incredibly high hopes for 2025. Instead, the season was completely gutted. Injuries, poor decision making and uncompetitive games dragged Washington down to a massive low point, erasing a decade’s worth of renewed optimism. It made last year incredibly hard to stomach. Head coach Dan Quinn saw the writing on the wall and let both of his coordinators go. While most head coaches in his position would hire experienced retreads to save their own skins, Quinn took a massive gamble. He brought in two newcomers: Daronte Jones and David Blough. We have absolutely no clue how this will translate when the games actually matter. The stakes are incredibly high, and every single storyline this year feels like an unprecedented gamble. Will the real Jayden Daniels stand up Jayden Daniels entered the league with a clear mission statement: prove he was the best quarterback in the 2024 NFL draft class. He shattered records and dragged this franchise somewhere it hadn’t been in over 30 years — the NFC Championship Game . Even though they were ultimately handled by a dominant Philly team that went on to win the Super Bowl, the foundation seemed set. Yet, despite the optimism surrounding his progression, the “sophomore slump” narrative still loomed. I blindly dismissed it at the time, firmly believing a slump was impossible because his rookie year was a tale of two entirely different Jaydens. Early in 2024, then-offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury relied heavily on first-down screens, RPOs and vertical concepts. At one point, Washington ran an absurd 35% of their first-down plays as screens to protect a highly suspect offensive line. The faster Jayden got the ball out, the better. But in Week 11, the Eagles completely exposed the game plan. Philly squeezed the offense’s lateral spacing and dared Daniels to attack the intermediate middle of the field. While most rookie quarterbacks could’ve hit a wall and coordinators could’ve waited until the offseason to adjust, Washington adapted immediately. Over the following weeks, they challenged the toughest part of the field — the 6-to-10-yard intermediate middle. Their screen frequency plummeted from 35% to 21%, the vertical deep shots were scaled back and they completely rebuilt the offense on the fly without losing momentum. It is impossible to overstate how impressive it was for a rookie to handle that mental adjustment. That mid-season pivot is exactly what made 2025 so incredibly frustrating. We can talk about the injuries and the lackluster supporting cast — points that have been discussed ad nauseam — but when he was on the field, the performance simply wasn’t there. His completion percentage tanked by an alarming 9%. There were costly underthrows, balls skipped into the dirt and while the playmakers around him offered little help, the regression from his rookie brilliance was surreal. To put a 9% completion percentage drop into historical perspective, look at how similar drop-offs impacted other notable quarterbacks: Quarterback Season 1 (Cmp %) Season 2 (Cmp %) Percentage Drop The Following Season (Year 3) Context / Rationale Carson Wentz 2018: 69.6% 2020: 57.4% -12.20% 2021 (IND): 62.4% Lost his job in Philadelphia due to mechanical breakdown; bounced back slightly under Frank Reich in Indy. Kurt Warner 2001: 68.7% 2003: 56.5% -12.20% 2004 (NYG): 62.8% Hand fractures and sudden fumbling issues led to a severe multi-year downward spiral before his Arizona resurgence. Deshaun Watson 2020: 70.2% 2022: 58.2% -12.00% 2023 (CLE): 61.4% A full year away from football followed by a team change to Cleveland severely disrupted his pocket rhythm. Cam Newton 2018: 67.9% 2019: 56.2% -11.70% 2020 (NNE): 65.8% A Lisfranc foot injury limited his 2019 run to just two games, severely skewing his active consecutive volume. Joe Burrow 2022: 70.5% 2023: 59.3% -11.20% 2024 (CIN): 68.3% A severe pre-season calf strain and subsequent torn wrist ligament caused his accurate throw rate to tank temporarily in 2023. Cam Newton 2020: 65.8% 2021: 54.8% -11.00% 2022: Out of NFL Rejoined a highly unstable Carolina offensive structure mid-season, leading to structural accuracy regression. Daniels faces an uphill battle, but history shows a recovery isn’t impossible — especially when you look at guys like Joe Burrow or Kurt Warner who weathered the storm. What makes his current situation so fascinating is that he is learning a brand-new offense simultaneously. Transitioning to a true pro-style system after years in spread and RPO-heavy schemes is a massive hurdle, but the buzz out of training camp has been incredibly positive regarding his mental processing. He took over 500 snaps in camp, an intensive workload designed to fast-track his comfort level. Whether that practice volume translates to wins remains to be seen, but the foundation is there. If JD5 can bounce back and replicate or surpass his rookie efficiency, watch out: he’ll vault right back into the top-10, if not the top-5 quarterback conversation. Defense? DEFENSE!! I can join the crowd and rag on former defensive coordinator Joe Whitt Jr. all day, but let’s be real — he wasn’t the sole reason this defense was completely awful. When your best pass rusher is a nearly 40-year-old Von Miller, you have fundamental problems. The personnel was a total mess. An old, slow defense will get absolutely ripped to shreds in today’s NFL. Even when Quinn took over the defensive play-calling duties they were still getting dismantled, proving a massive overhaul was needed. To Quinn’s credit, he recognized his own limitations, stepped back and brought in a defensive coordinator whose system is a complete departure from the scheme Quinn ran his entire career. Enter Daronte Jones. Outside of his brief stint calling plays at LSU , he’s a first-time NFL coordinator tasked with bringing a chaotic, Brian Flores-style scheme to Washington. To give him a fighting chance, management went all-in, injecting $165.8 million into that side of the ball — the sixth-highest defensive spend in the league. They completely reshaped the roster by signing Odafe Oweh, Tim Settle, K’Lavon Chaisson, Nick Cross and Leo Chenal, while using the draft to secure young talent like Sonny Styles and Joshua Josephs. With up to eight new starters, this unit simply has to outperform the disasters of the past three defensive seasons. Everything will live and die with the defensive line. For the last two years, this team was hellbent on blitzing heavy on first and second down to force third-and-long situations. The fatal flaw? They kept giving up first downs anyway, not to mention working with a completely awful run defense. The new additions must restore order in the trenches and finally unlock the underperforming duo of Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw. With a brand-new scheme and a completely reconstructed starting lineup, this defense is one of the biggest mysteries in the league. New -ish Sheriff in Town When Kliff Kingsbury was initially hired, I wasn’t a fan. I believed his offense was inherently predictable and destined to hit a proverbial wall every season. While his explosive 2024 campaign proved me wrong, he unfortunately reverted to those same stubborn play-calling habits in 2025. His firing wasn’t a shock, though I did assume he’d get one final year to redeem himself. Instead, Quinn opted for a…

No corresponding move was immediately announced. Humphries was signed the last week of the […]
full_text: The Commanders have released veteran offensive tackle D.J. Humprhies, the team announced on Friday morning. This cut comes but a few weeks after the former Pro Bowl standout was signed and just days before Sunday’s season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles. No corresponding move was immediately announced. Humphries was signed the last week of the preseason, on Aug. 26 , and was active during a joint pracitce against Baltimore and the subsequent preseason game against the Ravens. He was an option to back up left tackle Brandon Coleman, thrust into a starter’s role after star Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps early in training camp. The Commanders are currently set to go with Andrew Wylie as the primary swing tackle , unless an option is promoted from the practice squad. Washington could add an offensive tackle from the practice squad with the open roster spot, which is possible with just eight offensive linemen currently on the roster. Or, with that whole group healthy, they could leave the 53rd spot open and earmark it for Dorance Armstrong, who will come off suspension after the Eagles game. Or, they could keep him off the roster for a week and bring him back to avoid a full-season base salary guarantee. Time will tell what the Commanders do here.

While he was shut down for the final three games , the staff put together a tape that showed every play where he scrambled in 2025. He’d played just seven games because of various injuries, and his homework assignment was to determine which plays he should’ve given up on to avoid an unnecessary hit. “The first order of business was to say, ‘Of these, which play is it time to move on to the next play?’” Coach Dan Quinn told The Post. “As a competitor, that wasn’t so easy for him in his first two years.” The Commanders still want Daniels to use his speed and athleticism to extend plays and scramble when needed, but they intend for it to be a feature of the offense, not a primary weapon. In practice, Daniels became more discerning about taking risks. A couple of weeks ago, Quinn praised Daniels on a play where he escaped the pocket and threw the ball away. “I was like, ‘Man, that was a great decision,’” Quinn said. “For him, it’s knowing when to go to the next play. … I don’t think he had that part of his game in order, and he does now.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Every Jayden Daniels touchdown from his historic rookie season 🔥 Will he return to form this season? pic.twitter.com/UOLHKnBW3f — Kalshi Football (@KalshiFB) September 6, 2026 Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) How will Jayden Daniels handle throwing over the middle more often? Kingsbury’s offense worked a lot more outside the numbers, asking receivers to win one-on-one matchups. Blough’s offense will likely look to attack the middle of the field more often. Throwing over the middle was something people had questions about regarding Daniels when he entered the draft. At LSU, Daniels had receivers like Malik Nabers and Brian Thomas Jr., so he could trust them to win one-on-ones outside as they were just better than most college cornerbacks they faced. That meant in college, he wasn’t asked to throw over the middle very often. Kingsbury’s offense leaned into that philosophy too, but the offense Blough is likely to try and replicate is very different. title: Washington Commanders vs Philadelphia Eagles Week 1: Five Questions with Bleeding Green Nation
summary: It’s week 1 of the NFL season and the Washington Commanders will be facing an Eagles team on the road at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Eagles have now done the improbable and won the NFC East Championship two years in a row, though they flamed out […]
full_text: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley celebrates a first down against Washington Commanders safety Will Harris (3) during the first half of an NFL football game, Saturday, Dec. 20, 2025, in Landover, Md. | AP Photo - Nick Wass It’s week 1 of the NFL season and the Washington Commanders will be facing an Eagles team on the road at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Eagles have now done the improbable and won the NFC East Championship two years in a row, though they flamed out of the playoffs last postseason to an injury-riddled 49ers team in the Wild Card round. Still, the Eagles are the most accomplished team in the division in recent years and the betting favorites to win the division . On offense, the Eagles have switched OC again after an underwhelming stint from OC Kevin Patullo last year. The Eagles offense this year will be helmed by OC Sean Mannion, formerly of the Packers. Similar to Washington’s OC David Blough, Mannion was a player as recently as 2023 and only served a couple of years coaching QBs for the Packers before being hired by the Eagles to run their offense. Mannion is expected to run a Shanahan-style outside-zone run game with heavy use of under-center formations and play-action fakes. It is also an offense that typically features an emphasis on passes to the middle of the field, though this seems to conflict with the preference of QB Jalen Hurts, who threw just 28 times between the hashmarks last season . This was both a career high for Hurts and the fewest amongst QBs who played 14+ games in 2025. Hurts seems to prefer to throw to the sidelines, an area where X-receiver AJ Brown thrived. Brown was traded away in the offseason, but former 1st-round pick DeVonta Smith will try to reprise Brown’s role and become the boundary X. Meanwhile, 2026 1st-round pick Makai Lemon (who battled hamstring injury during training camp, but is now fully healthy) will try to fill that important between-the-hashes role. On defense, the Eagles are in their third year with Vic Fangio at DC. Fangio typically runs a 3-4 front and 2 deep safeties to limit explosive plays. He also typically runs a light box, relying on stout defensive linemen to stop the run, while dropping most of his players back into coverage. It is a defense designed to limit big plays and slowly suffocate offenses into punting. Quite frankly, the Eagles defense is well coached and stacked with good or great players at multiple levels. It will be in contention for best defense in the NFL this year and should be comparable to last year, when it was ranked 13th in yards allowed and 5th in points allowed . However, if it has a weakness, it seems to be at the safety position, which has received little attention in the offseason . I asked Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation five questions to better understand the state of the Eagles and what to look for in this game. 1) Jeff Stoutland was one of the all-time great OL coaches in the NFL and retired this offseason. What does this mean for the Eagles and what do you expect to be different in the Eagles’ OL blocking this year? “Retired.” The Eagles purportedly wanted him back … but only as their offensive line coach and NOT their run game coordinator, which is a title he was granted after the Eagles’ Super Bowl LII win. It would be disingenuous for anyone who previously talked about how great Stout was to now act like it’s no big deal that he’s gone. The Eagles likely downgraded at offensive line coach this offseason. That said, the early returns on his replacement — Chris Kuper — seem to be positive. We saw the Eagles’ run game have success in training camp settings, for whatever that’s worth. The Eagles’ young backup offensive lineman seem to be developing nicely. Multiple Eagles offensive linemen have expressed excitement about the new offense as it relates to making their jobs easier. Lane Johnson has talked about how he’ll have more help now as opposed to almost always being on an island at right tackle. Johnson and Jordan Mailata have also discussed how the new scheme is going to make their offense less predictable. Of course, it’s easy for players and fans to look on the bright side before the games actually start. I do think the Eagles’ offensive line will be better than it was last year because they should be healthier. The entire group isn’t coming off the massive 2024 rushing workload that clearly took a toll on them. Cam Jurgens in particular seems to be removed from the back injury that tanked his 2025 season. I do have some concerns about Landon Dickerson, who doesn’t look back to his Pro Bowl form based on what I saw in training camp, but there are worse starting guards in the league. To be determined if schematic tweaks help or hurt the o-line, if they even make a big difference at all. 2) What will the Eagles offense look like being run by Sean Mannion? How big of a change is that from last year? Great question! It’s not easy to know exactly what to expect, both in terms of aesthetic and the extent to which it is effective. We did see enough in training camp to lead one to believe there will be meaningful differences from the past. There was much more under center play-action usage. There was a good deal of pre-snap motion. Jalen Hurts seemed to throw over the middle of the field more frequently than he has in the past. Do these tweaks guarantee that the offense will be a lot better than it was in 2026? I don’t think they do. But they could certainly help. I mean, it’s hard to get worse than last year’s offense that led the league in three-and-out percentage. But there are still a lot of questions here. Mannion isn’t only a first-time play-caller, he’s entering the third year of his entire coaching career. He’s inexperienced. I already touched on Stoutland above. A.J. Brown is gone, that’s a pretty big loss. It’s also not like the Eagles are the only team trying to reinvent their offense to some degree. Offensive coordinator change has become the norm in the NFL; the longest tenured play-calling OC is from 2025! Most seem to be chasing the Sean McVay/Kyle Shanahan systems, which is where Mannion draws experience from. But while teams understandably covet those influences, it remains to be seen which (if any) disciples can effectively enact their visions. And if these teams might be too late to a trend. The thinking here is that the Eagles’ offense could have some success early on since they begin the season with games against the Commanders and Titans. But things might get bumpy after that and I tend to think that progress might not be linear for this offense. There could be some ups and downs before they hit their stride, if they ever do. 3) What are your thoughts about the Eagles’ trade of AJ Brown and how it will affect the team? I think it’s a bummer because Brown is an awesome player (not was, still is) and Eagles fans should ultimately remember the Super Bowl LIX champion as a big contributor to the most successful sustained stretch in franchise history. But it’s not quite that simple because Brown clearly didn’t put his best foot forward for the Eagles in 2025. Keeping him moving forward clearly wasn’t an option; the Eagles were never going to get the motivated version of Brown in 2026 that the Patriots will be getting. And that’s a shame, for a lot of reasons. I do think the Eagles did reasonably well to get a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick for him. But I also think they’re going to miss Brown. Similar to what I said about Stoutland earlier in this correspondence, I think it’s silly for people to espouse Brown’s greatness during his time in Philly only to then act like replacing him is no big deal. I’m not concerned about DeVonta Smith at all; I think he’s going to have a great season as the Eagles’ undisputed top target. But I do have questions about the other Eagles receivers. Dontayvion Wicks had an encouraging summer and he’s poised to…

title: Which NFL teams have never won a Super Bowl?
summary: Some NFL teams have scored multiple Lombardi trophies, but which franchises have never won the Super Bowl? Check out more information now.
full_text:
It's been 60 years since the NFL and AFL rival football leagues announced their merger and established the Super Bowl, the annual league championship that has been claimed by 20 different franchises since 1967.

 Of the 12 organizations that are still looking to capture the elusive Vince Lombardi Trophy, four of them -- the Cleveland Browns , Detroit Lions , Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars -- have never reached the big game.

 The 2026 NFL season will culminate with Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, the home of the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers . The Rams, who won Super Bowl XXXIV in 2000 and Super Bowl LVI in 2022 (at SoFi Stadium), opened the campaign at +500 odds to win it all .

 Let's take a closer look at the 12 franchises that have never won the big game (along with their number of Super Bowl appearances):

  

 

 Cleveland Browns (0) 

 There was a time when the Browns were the class of the NFL, winning seven championships with three runner-up finishes in their first 10 years as a franchise. However, it's been a different story in the Super Bowl era, particularly over the last three decades . Cleveland reached the AFC Championship Game three times after the 1986, 1987 and 1989 seasons but lost all three to John Elway and the Denver Broncos -- often in heartbreaking fashion . Over the last 30 years, Cleveland has posted more winless seasons (one) than division titles and Super Bowl appearances combined (zero).

 

 Detroit Lions (0) 

 The Lions are one of the NFL's oldest franchises (founded in 1930), yet they have zero Super Bowl appearances and arguably the worst postseason résumé in league history. That's why their 2023 run to the NFC Championship Game was such a big deal for Detroit fans. The Lions won their first playoff game since 1992, ending the NFL's longest active drought (and the fifth-longest all-time, right behind the team's previous 33-year winless run from 1958 to 1991). The Lions seemed poised to make their first Super Bowl appearance, but the San Francisco 49ers erased a 17-point deficit and defeated Detroit to punch their Super Bowl ticket.

 

 Houston Texans (0) 

 The Texans are the newest franchise in the league, having joined as an expansion team in 2002, so Houston's inclusion on this list shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Still, it's been a tough couple of decades for the Texans, who have never reached a conference championship. However, that could change in the coming years, as rookie quarterback C.J. Stroud already looks like a potential superstar, while head coach DeMeco Ryans is a rising star himself and has Super Bowl experience from his time as an assistant coach in San Francisco. Their 45-14 wild-card win over Cleveland during the 2023-24 season helped Texans fans feel hopeful.

 

 Jacksonville Jaguars (0) 

 The Jaguars have had a checkered history across nearly 30 years of existence. Shortly after they joined the NFL in 1995, they found immediate success, making the playoffs four times in their first five seasons -- including two trips to the AFC Championship Game. However, both ended in a lopsided defeat, and Jacksonville reached the playoffs just twice in the next 17 years before making another run to the AFC title game in the 2017 season -- only to blow a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to Tom Brady's Patriots, squandering the team's best shot to reach a Super Bowl so far.

 

 Arizona Cardinals (1) 

 Having been in existence since 1920, the Cardinals are the oldest franchise without a Super Bowl victory, though they did win two league championships (1925, 1947) prior to the Super Bowl era when they were based in Chicago. Arizona came oh-so close to its first Super Bowl victory in 2009, when star receiver Larry Fitzgerald scored a go-ahead touchdown with 2:37 left in Super Bowl XLIII. The Pittsburgh Steelers responded with one of the most impressive game-winning drives in Super Bowl history, scoring in the final seconds to sink the Cardinals' title hopes.

 

 Los Angeles Chargers (1) 

 Few teams have done less with more than the Chargers, who have consistently boasted elite teams that come up short in the postseason. The franchise did reach the Super Bowl once in 1995, falling victim to Joe Montana 's 49ers in a 49-26 rout. The Bolts also reached the AFC title game in the 1980 and 1981 seasons and again in 2007, losing by a touchdown or more in all three. While the Chargers have won 10 or more games six times in the last 20 years, they've won just five playoff games in that stretch, and their 12-19 playoff record ranks fourth-worst all-time. Will new coach Jim Harbaugh be able to end the drought?

 

 Tennessee Titans (1) 

 While other franchises have seen a chance at a championship slip through their grasp, none have come closer than the Titans did in 2000. With six seconds left in Super Bowl XXXIV and Tennessee trailing by seven, receiver Kevin Dyson caught a slant pass over the middle and was wrapped up by St. Louis Rams linebacker Mike Jones near the 1-yard line. Dyson stretched out his arm toward the goal line, but he was inches short. The play, known as "The Tackle" or "One Yard Short," became the enduring image of that game and the Titans' years-long quest for their first Lombardi Trophy.

 

 Atlanta Falcons (2) 

 While other teams on this list have reached more Super Bowls, none blew their chance at hoisting the Lombardi Trophy like the Falcons in 2017. Atlanta held a 28-3 lead over the New England Patriots in the third quarter of Super Bowl LI , when they boasted a win probability as high as 99.7%. That was before Tom Brady launched the defining comeback of his career, leading his team to the biggest comeback in Super Bowl history and the only overtime victory in the game's 57-year history. It was the second title game loss for the Falcons, who got blasted by the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XXXIII . Still, nothing compares to that loss in '17, and the team has reached the playoffs just once in seven seasons since.

 

 Carolina Panthers (2) 

 The Panthers have only been around since 1995, but they've reached the Super Bowl twice in their relatively brief existence. Both times, they were defeated by an all-time great quarterback. In 2004, Brady and the Patriots outlasted Carolina, 32-29, in  Super Bowl XXXVIII . Twelve years later, Peyton Manning led the Broncos to a 24-10 win over the 15-1 Panthers in Super Bowl 50 -- his second Super Bowl victory and the final game of his storied career. Despite those gutting losses, Carolina remains the only team on this list with a winning record in the postseason and one of just 13 teams with multiple Super Bowl appearances this century.

 

 Cincinnati Bengals (3) 

 The Bengals nearly worked their way off this list in 2022, when Joe Burrow led his team to Super Bowl LVI . However, the Bengals came up short against the Los Angeles Rams, 23-20. That marked Cincinnati's first Super Bowl appearance since 1989, when Montana led his 49ers to their second Super Bowl victory over the Bengals in an eight-year span -- with both games decided by five or fewer points. The Bengals were among the title favorites entering the 2023 season before Burrow suffered a season-ending right wrist injury.

 

 Buffalo Bills (4) 

 No team has fallen short more often than the Bills, who lost four consecutive Super Bowls from 1991 to 1994 -- a run memorialized by the ESPN 30 for 30 documentary " Four Falls of Buffalo ." The first was easily the most painful, as kicker Scott Norwood famously missed wide right on a 47-yard field goal in the final seconds to seal a 20-19 loss to the Giants in Super Bowl XXV . It would be the closest Buffalo came to a title, as they lost the next three Super Bowls by a combined 65 points (with none closer than 13 points). The cruelty of those losses is magnified by the fact that the Bills won the two final AFL championships (1964, 1965) before the introduction of the Super Bowl following…

title: Six NFL records that could be broken during the 2026 season
summary: Can a team break the NFL's rushing record? Will we see a new long in field goal kicking? Could there be a new single-season tight end receiving yardage mark?
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is already here. Unfortunately, through two games, no NFL record has been broken. Boring!

 Last time we saw regular-season football, Myles Garrett was setting a single-season sack record (23) and Trey McBride was catching more passes (126) than any tight end in NFL history. With a 17-game season and rules skewed to favor offenses, it feels like more and more records are within reach every year.

 I wanted to find more NFL records that could be broken in 2026, so I went through a long list of candidates. Among them were:

 
 Highest average punt distance for a single season (the Cardinals' Blake Gillikin and Packers' Daniel Whelan both hit 51.7 yards per punt last season, tied for third all time). 
 Most receiving touchdowns in a game (Jerry Rice had five -- if it were four, I would have included it). 
 Most penalized team in NFL history (somehow the 17-game season isn't really affecting total penalty numbers). 
 
 After I ruled those out, I landed on a final six that could reasonably fall this season. There's some statistical reasoning for a few, some schematic considerations considered and some straight vibes rolled in. I want to see a 70-yard field goal. I want to root for a 70-yard field goal. Give me a 70-yard field goal!

 

 But let's start with a new receiving record for tight ends.

 Jump to a record: 
 Most TE receiving yards in a season  
 Most fourth-down conversions in a game 
 Most team rushing yards in a season 
 Longest field goal in NFL history 
 Highest completion percentage in a season 
 Most fumbles forced by a player in a season 

 

 Single-season receiving yards by a tight end 
 Current record holder:  Chiefs tight end  Travis Kelce (1,416 in 2020)

 We have entered a new era of high-volume receiving from tight ends.

 Last season, McBride was the Cardinals' only bright spot when he set a new single-season NFL record for tight end receptions with 126. He broke Zach Ertz 's record of 116 receptions, which Ertz accomplished in a 16-game season (7.25 receptions per game) as a member of the Eagles in 2018. McBride's 126 in a 17-game season was even enough to beat Ertz out on a per-game basis (7.41).

 Tight ends have cracked 100 receptions 13 times, and eight of them have come in the past six years. In 2024, the Raiders' Brock Bowers broke the record for all rookie receptions (not just tight ends) with his 112-catch season. As tight ends become better receivers and coordinators become more clever in featuring them, the inherent reliability of a tight end target lends itself to high reception totals. Just last season, TE targets had a 72% completion rate, while WR targets had a 62% completion rate.

 

 So why bet on the tight end receiving yardage total to be broken? While it is generally the case that tight ends are targeted closer to the line of scrimmage and can't create explosives downfield ... there are a few exceptions to the rule.

 Bears tight end Colston Loveland averaged 12.3 yards per reception over the course of the 2025 season in Ben Johnson's explosive-oriented offense -- that was third among all high-volume tight ends, and it doesn't even include his wild-card round explosion (eight catches, 137 yards) against the Packers. Because Loveland started the season slowly as a rookie coming off injury, he wasn't heavily targeted, accounting for 15.0% of the Bears' team targets relative to McBride's 27.4% with the Cardinals.

 I thought Bowers would be a second excellent candidate to set the arc here, but a late meniscus surgery has him out for at least the next couple of weeks. The good news is that Bowers is far from the only young, exciting tight end looking for a spike in receiving.

 Colts tight end Tyler Warren was on pace for over 1,000 yards last season before Daniel Jones fractured his fibula ahead of Week 12 and the offense suffered . With target sponge Michael Pittman Jr . off the Colts roster, Warren could more than pick up where he left off. Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange has always had the explosiveness (12.3 yards per reception) but never the volume (10.9% of the team's target share) -- but the Jaguars want  more multi-TE sets this year, which should open him up as he takes on fewer blocking assignments. Lions tight end Sam LaPorta now has offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, who was McBride's playcaller when he broke out as a high-volume pass catcher over the past two seasons. And the Cardinals have a new coaching staff as well -- maybe they'll think about McBride's role a little more vertically.

 I'm certain we'll see some candidates challenge the receptions record -- it's just too good of a time to be a pass-catching tight end in the NFL. But ... Kelce's 1,416 yards is a bit trickier to reach. Set in 2020 in the throes of Chiefs hype, Kelce benefitted from the ceiling-lifting speed of Tyreek Hill and the pass-happiness of head coach Andy Reid (and some of the greatest quarterback play in the history of the universe from Patrick Mahomes , of course). Even with an additional game, McBride was almost 200 yards off Kelce's total in 2025 -- he had more targets but he couldn't match Kelce for explosiveness.

 

 Every candidate we've discussed above has a weakness in his profile.

 Loveland should have explosiveness and volume within the Bears' passing game ... but Chicago runs it way more than those 2020 Chiefs did (they had the fifth-highest pass rate over expectation in the past 10 seasons, per NFL Next Gen Stats). LaPorta has the ceiling-lifting speedsters in receiver Jameson Williams and the right scheme for big explosives ... but will he get enough targets sharing time with Williams, receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown  and running back Jahmyr Gibbs ? Bowers should have the scheme, the volume and the big plays ... but will his quarterbacking quality be enough?

 

 If it were easy to break a record, it would happen every year. Of all the receiving records (yards, receptions and touchdowns) across all the positions (running back, receivers and tight ends) I know I want to be betting on tight end records to fall. Bowers broke one in 2024. McBride broke one in 2025. Kelce's total yardage may be the toughest nut to crack at the position, but this new wave of big-play tight ends has the constitution for it.

 
 Single-game fourth-down conversions 
 Current record holder: Los Angeles Chargers (six, 2021) and Dallas Cowboys (six, 2025)

 That's right: Two teams in NFL history have successfully converted on six fourth-down tries in a single game, and one was last season .

 You're forgiven for forgetting the finer details of the Cowboys' 30-23 Christmas Day win over the 4-11 Commanders, who were starting backup quarterback Josh Johnson . You were drowsy on eggnog anyway. But Dallas attempted and converted six fourth downs on the day, tying the 2021 Chargers (coached by Brandon Staley, the straw man of much fourth-down debate over the past several seasons) for the most in NFL history.

 Most of the Cowboys' fourth-down attempts were unspectacular. There was a fourth-and-1 from their own 44-yard-line on the first drive. On their second drive, another fourth-and-1 -- this one at midfield -- was quickly joined by a fourth-and-2 from the Commanders' 23 and a fourth-and-1 from the Commanders' 10. According to ESPN Research, that sequence is just the third drive in the past 45 years to start in the first quarter and have three fourth-down conversions. Two of the three were last season. We live in a different world.

 The Cowboys had another no-man's land conversion (fourth-and-2 from their own 45) late in the fourth quarter, then ended the game on a fourth-and-1 sneak to snag their sixth conversion.

 It took a unique day of near-conversions on third downs for the Cowboys, who never had to attempt a fourth down longer than 2 yards out. These auto-go situations on fourth-and-1s are why the single-game record is easily within reach. Even as teams attempt more fourth downs than ever before (3.3 per game in…

title: NFL Week 1 picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
summary: Josh Allen vs. C.J. Stroud? Jayden Daniels vs. Jalen Hurts? There are 14 games left in Week 1, and we have picks, predictions, key stats, watchability ratings and more.
full_text:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is here! The first kickoff weekend is full of intriguing quarterback showdowns and new team debuts for Jared Verse , Tua Tagovailoa , David Montgomery , Kyler Murray and Kirk Cousins , among others. We have Josh Allen vs. C.J. Stroud . We have Derrick Henry vs. Jonathan Taylor . And we have Packers vs. Vikings and Cowboys vs. Giants.

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, NFL analyst Ben Solak gives one reason to tune into each game (and rates the watchability of the matchup), fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pam Maldonado provides  betting insight. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the rest of the Week 1 slate, which culminates with the "Monday Night Football" matchup between Denver and Kansas City on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

 
 Jump to a matchup: 
 BUF-HOU | BAL-IND | TB-CIN 
 NO-DET | CHI-CAR | ATL-PIT 
 CLE-JAX | NYJ-TEN | GB-MIN 
 WSH-PHI | ARI-LAC | MIA-LV 
 DAL-NYG | DEN-KC 

 Previously played: 
 NE-SEA | SF-LAR 

 
 

 What ESPN Analytics says ... 
 

 

 
 

 Bills at Texans 
 1 p.m. ET | CBS | BUF -1.5 (44.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Bills: Buffalo's reimagined defense has an idea of what to expect from the Texans' offense. "We expect multiple different personnel groupings and for them to try and run the ball," edge Bradley Chubb said. "You look at their offseason additions, they let it be known what they want their offense to be." He's talking about the Texans signing RB  David Montgomery and TE  Foster Moreau and selecting a guard and a tight end in the first two rounds of the draft. What Buffalo's defense will look like under first-time coordinator Jim Leonhard is one of the key early storylines in the AFC. -- Dan Graziano 

 What we're hearing on the Texans: Safety Jalen Pitre said Houston has to "keep [Bills quarterback Josh Allen ] from playing backyard football." But in reality, Allen playing backyard football plays right into Houston's advantage. In the past two matchups against Allen, he is 13-of-34 for 201 passing yards with two interceptions and nine sacks when he holds the ball for longer than 2.5 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 Stat to know: The Texans' five-game home winning streak is tied with the Seahawks' for the longest active streak in the NFL. A win would tie their longest home winning streak in franchise history, including the playoffs. -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction: Bills WR DJ Moore will be held to two or fewer receptions. Perhaps Buffalo's newest playmaker will deliver at some point this season. But I don't think it will be against Derek Stingley Jr . or Kamari Lassiter . -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.8. The Texans and Bills played a great game in primetime last season -- the Texans were victorious on the back of a passionate defensive outing as backup quarterback Davis Mills did just enough to win 23-19 . I bet we see a vengeful Allen (eight sacks, two picks) this time. -- Solak 

 Injuries: Bills | Texans 

 Fantasy nugget: Allen finished with just 8.1 fantasy points in their meeting last season. Houston also gave up the third-fewest fantasy points per game to QBs in 2025. See Week 1 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: Texans unders are 33-18 under DeMeco Ryans, the second-highest rate since 2023 (Chiefs, 34-17). The Texans can pressure Allen and keep numbers in coverage, and Buffalo also consistently started slow despite its offensive abilities. The matchup points toward longer drives and fewer possessions. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Texans 20, Bills 17 
 Moody's pick: Texans 23, Bills 20 
 Walder's pick: Bills 24, Texans 17 
 FPI prediction: BUF, 54.5% (by an average of 1 point)

 

 Matchup must-reads: Big energy, big reward? Brady is full of caffeine and confidence ... Texans' Stroud confident ahead of the biggest season of his life 

 
 

 Ravens at Colts 
 1 p.m. ET | CBS | BAL -3.5 (47.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Ravens: This is QB  Lamar Jackson 's first game with new OC Declan Doyle, but the two-time NFL MVP is familiar with Colts DC Lou Anarumo, who was the longtime coordinator with the Bengals. Jackson has excelled in his past four games against Anarumo's defenses, throwing 10 touchdown passes and two interceptions, while averaging 258.5 passing yards. "He does a pretty good job of being able to keep you off-balance and attack you," Doyle said of Anarumo. "It's very similar to how we try to attack defenses." -- Jamison Hensley 

 What we're hearing on the Colts: Indianapolis enters with significant personnel changes on defense and at least five new starters. How it all comes together, against a Baltimore offense with prolific potential, is anyone's guess. "Anybody would be curious on how everything's going to shake out," said DT  DeForest Buckner , who returns after season-ending neck surgery in 2025. "But all that matters is the trust that you build ... and the chemistry that you build on the field." -- Stephen Holder 

 Stat to know: The Ravens averaged 24.9 points (11th in the NFL) and 333.2 yards (16th) in 2025 -- their fewest YPG in any season since 2017. -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor will record four or more receptions. Last season, no team ran more zone coverage than the Chargers under then-defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. Now, he's coaching the Ravens. And RBs record receptions against zone at a much higher rate than against man. -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.6. There's a lot of intrigue in this one. What does the Minter/Doyle brain trust look like in Baltimore? Just how healthy are QB Daniel Jones and WR Alec Pierce ? And there should be plenty of points.  -- Solak 

 Injuries: Ravens | Colts 

 Fantasy nugget: Zay Flowers is dangerous from both the slot and the outside, and the Colts gave up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to WRs last season. Doyle is incorporating more under-center formations and play-action to maximize Jackson and Flowers, which could lead to more chunk plays. See Week 1 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Colts are 3-14-1 ATS (against the spread) in Week 1 since 2008. The Colts' defense was already one of the league's worst at preventing opponents from moving the ball, and now it has to deal with Jackson, plus an upgraded pass rush on the other side with edge  Trey Hendrickson . Indianapolis has offensive upside, but Jones is returning from an Achilles injury .  Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Ravens 27, Colts 21 
 Moody's pick: Ravens 30, Colts 20 
 Walder's pick: Ravens 21, Colts 14 
 FPI prediction: BAL, 59.8% (by an average of 2.4 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: How Ravens' Henry is driven to rank among NFL's best backs ... Colts' Pierce (ankle) expected to play in Week 1 ...   QB Jones has one box left to check in dramatic return 

 
 

 Buccaneers at Bengals 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | CIN -3.5 (50.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Buccaneers: Coach Todd Bowles called playing QB Joe Burrow a "cat and mouse game" because he is so good at recognizing coverages. "He is outstanding at seeing what you're in." All the more reason they're hoping their remade pass rush -- with first-round draft pick Rueben Bain Jr ., free agents A'Shawn Robinson and Al-Quadin Muhammad , along with standout DT  Vita Vea -- can handle business up front and Bowles can keep as many resources as possible on the backend. Bowles is particularly excited about what they have on the edge. "I feel like I don't have reserves for the first time," he said, feeling as…
