title: Expectations for Saints' Tyler Shough in Year 2? 'Doesn't faze me'
summary: Named a captain this season, the 26-year-old QB is out to prove he can lead New Orleans to the postseason.
full_text:
ON THE FINAL Monday before the Saints' 2026 season opener against the Detroit Lions , the entire team gathered at a local Italian restaurant in Metairie, Louisiana.

 The "Captains' dinner" is an annual tradition for the Saints, a chance to mingle, laugh, and look ahead to the season. It's where the Saints announce their team captains -- in this case, all nine of them.

 "It's kind of that official start of the regular season, Monday night, just having a dinner together," Saints coach Kellen Moore said. "And then we announce the captains, and they have an opportunity to share a message with the rest of the team."

 Zach Wood , Justin Reid , Cameron Jordan and Erik McCoy had all been captains before. Others, such as Chris Rumph II , David Edwards , Kaden Elliss and Chase Young are new.

 Quarterback Tyler Shough , 26, was perhaps the most significant addition. Saints captains are determined by a player vote, and only one year before, the team's 53 players declined to name a quarterback to the captain's group.

 

 Shough, who took over for Spencer Rattler as the starter midway through the 2025 season, has spent this offseason proving he has earned a permanent role. He has immersed himself into the culture of New Orleans, aligned with Saints legends such as Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees and worked to get to know his teammates on-and-off the field. Shough has shown he can be the face of the franchise, and the players' vote of confidence backs up that statement.

 "Everybody in the room knew from OTAs on who the leader of the team was and he's done a really great job," Elliss said. 

 Shough later called being named a captain one of the biggest things he has accomplished in his career so far.

 "The NFL is such a hard business because there's so much fluidity," Shough said. "... I felt like with this business and the guys that come in and out, you have to be really intentional about getting to know all of your teammates ... and it means a lot. But I also know that there's more work to be done."

 As the Saints prepare to face the Lions Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) in their first of two road games to start the season, the true test of his leadership and his abilities start now. For Shough and the rest of the team, the bar has been raised from last season. Can Shough prove he's capable of translating all the momentum from the end of the 2025 season into 2026 and lead the team back to the playoffs for the first time since Brees retired five years ago?

 He's certainly going to try.

 "He's mature beyond his years, especially beyond his years in the league being a quarterback," Elliss said of Shough. "He speaks much more like a Year 6-7 type of guy and he's going to have a great year."

 
 THE LEADUP TO the captains' vote didn't happen overnight.

 Over the past eight months Shough has juggled all the things that come with being a starting quarterback. Once a backup whose sole job was to run the scout team, now Shough is being pulled in different directions. He and his wife Jordan had their first child , son Grayson, in February. More is asked of him off the field from family obligations, to media and appearance requests, and from his coaches and teammates, who look to him to set the tone for the team.

 His time is carefully structured to make sure nothing slips through the cracks.

 "It's very routine based. I've built out a system ... that I try and stick to and have a lot of time, maybe on an off-day to go do charity stuff or maybe a shoot or some family time. But throughout the week it's very much detailed as far as built-in media time, built-in meetings, and obviously have my own time. A lot of time I just get in early to do a lot of prep work and then stay late to do it," Shough said.

 Shough has operated with intentionality and looked for ways to coordinate responsibilities while also connecting with teammates.

 In early February, he rode on a Mardi Gras float with teammates like McCoy. With McCoy's second child being born around the same time as Shough's a weeks later, parenting topics became a common thread between them and Edwards, whose fourth child was also born this past winter.

 

 "Just knowing that we're all kind of in the same season, like, 'Oh, how'd your kids sleep last night? Oh, mine was up at 1, 3, 5, and 7 [a.m.].' It's fun to talk about, and I feel like that gives you a way to bond even just outside of ball," McCoy said during camp.

 Shough didn't take much of a step back once he became a dad. On the contrary, he appeared to be everywhere in the spring. Brees and Shough made a guest appearance during the Savannah Bananas stop in New Orleans . In April, Shough went to the Hondo Rodeo Fest in New Orleans and golfed in the Zurich Classic Celebrity Shootout.

 And during all the engagements, Shough has been a cheerleader for each new Saints player, taking free agents such as Travis Etienne Jr . to dinner and posting on social media his excitement with each new draft pick New Orleans selected.

 "He was the first guy on the team to text me after I signed," Elliss said.

 But the biggest effort -- and the one that further shows the leadership gains the young QB has made -- was when Shough organized a week-long trip to California, offering to pay for his teammates' accommodations to entice them to participate. Some of the attendees included Etienne, running back Audric Estime , tight end Noah Fant , wide receivers Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele . Rookie wideouts Barion Brown and Bryce Lance went as well.

 Shough and tight end Juwan Johnson stayed in the same house that week with their families. The two men have known each other since they played at Oregon and have reconnected since Shough was drafted No. 40 overall by the Saints last year. But the California adventure was another way to strengthen their bond.

 "It was a full house, three kids, two dogs. Oh man, it was a lot, but it was extremely fun," Johnson said. "When you have that camaraderie and you're able to be around people, even staying in the same house, I feel like you learn a lot about people. And that translates on the field, believe it or not."

 Johnson said riding roller coasters or eating breakfast together might not seem like big moments, but it builds friendships that make teammates want to fight for each other.

 "I'm going to do whatever I can to make plays because we took that trip to San Diego or we started throwing routes in February or we went and did some things together. ... You spend time together, you find ways to dig a little deeper because you know that person on a more intimate and deeper level," Johnson said.

 

 
 SHOUGH WOULD BE one of the first people to admit he is still a work in progress. He has described himself as "light years ahead" of where he was at this time last year in training camp, when he was not quite ready to be the starter yet.

 A year ago Shough didn't truly push Rattler in camp until the Saints held scrimmages with "call-it" periods from both coordinators. When the scripted part of practice was taken away to raise the competitive stakes, Shough rose to the challenge.

 In November, with the Saints struggling to a 1-7 start, the coaches felt confident enough in Shough to start him over Rattler based on the progress they'd seen in practice.

 "You always worry about that transition from scout team to playing in games," Saints offensive coordinator Doug Nussmeier said. "But we'd already seen that. We knew his eyes were in the right place. He was seeing things. It just wasn't happening fast enough. But I think probably Week 4 or 5 you really started to see like, OK, he's starting to get it."

 A similar step forward happened this offseason. The Saints' offense didn't automatically gel in the first few weeks of camp. The Saints ran an unscripted red zone session on Aug. 11 in which the defense clearly won, with Shough throwing two interceptions and almost going for a third. Multiple false starts were also an issue for the…

title: Titans, Saleh downplay facing team that fired coach in Jets
summary: Robert Saleh, Titans focused on winning as the coach faces the Jets for the first time.
full_text:
In 2023, Robert Saleh was gearing up for his third season opener as the New York Jets  coach with future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers  set to make his debut for the Green and White.

 It was supposed to be a franchise-altering moment, but it was derailed four offensive snaps into the game. Rodgers was lost for the season with an Achilles injury, and Saleh's third straight losing season would follow.

 With Rodgers back in 2024, expectations were high, but after the Jets opened the season 2-3, Saleh was fired .

 

 Coincidentally, one of Saleh's two wins that season came against the Tennessee Titans , and he's now tasked with turning around that franchise -- which hired him in January -- after back-to-back three-win seasons.

 Each team has a host of ex-players and personnel from the other side, but virtually the entire football operation in New York has changed since Saleh's ouster. Still, there will be familiar faces on the Jets' sideline -- 14 holdovers from his era, including top players like Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall . The defense he built, which peaked in 2022 when it ranked fourth in scoring, was dismantled. Only four players remain, most notably Jamien Sherwood and Will McDonald IV .

 Schedule makers decided to start things off Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) with Saleh's old team versus his new one in Week 1 -- leaving both sides with months of anticipation.

 It's funny how things work out, but now they have to face off. Titans reporter Turron Davenport and Jets reporter Rich Cimini tackle how each team is handling Saleh's much-anticipated debut in Nashville.

 

 A view from the Titans' side 

 Instead of trashing his former team, Saleh is taking the "I want to win every game" approach in his first game as a head coach since being fired by the Jets. He said he isn't harboring any hard feelings toward his former team.

 "New York is still a special place," Saleh said. "They gave me my first opportunity as a head coach. Our desire to win Week 1, to beat the Jets, is because it's Week 1 and nothing more. I'm forever grateful for the opportunity they gave me. I don't hold grudges."

 Joining Saleh's staff as former members of the Jets' organization are cornerbacks coach Tony Oden, safeties coach Marquand Manuel and defensive line coach Aaron Whitecotton. Defensive linemen Jermaine Johnson II , Jacob Martin , Solomon Thomas and  John Franklin-Myers , along with safety Tony Adams , all played for the Jets at some point in their careers as well. Practice squad players Michael Carter and Jalyn Holmes also played in New York before.

 

 Saleh isn't worried about the former Jets-turned-Titans losing composure or trying to be Superman against their former team. His message to them is to stay true to their process and to put their best foot forward.

 "Making a team in New York changed my life altogether," said Adams, who signed with the Jets as an undrafted free agent in 2022. "I'm already a fiery person. So me taking this game personally would cloud my judgment. You take the emotions out of it and just go out there and play ball."

 Johnson was a first-round pick by New York in 2022. He is looking forward to seeing some of his former teammates Sunday and signing autographs for the Jets' fans who travel to Nashville. But once the game starts, he knows they'll be trying to take him out and will be looking to do the same thing. It's nothing personal.

 "The Jets are just another thing in the way of what we want to do," Johnson added.

 While Johnson and Adams are making sure they don't take going against their former team personally, Martin has a different approach. Martin signed a three-year $16.5 million contract with the Jets in 2022 only to get traded to the Denver Broncos later that year.

 "It's always personal for me," Martin said. "You can make any game personal, but I know a lot of guys in this locker room that were with the Jets organization are extra excited to play in this one, myself included."

 Getting another shot at being a head coach has helped ease the sting of being fired for Saleh. He returned to the San Francisco 49ers last season as their defensive coordinator, but it took two hiring cycles to become a head coach again. Now that he's there, Saleh is focused on one thing: starting his tenure in Nashville with a win. It's been six seasons since the Titans won a season opener.

 "Every game you go into you're trying to win," Saleh said. "Starting fast is always good because you never know, you win a couple early and you start getting momentum, you start getting confidence with a young group, and then who knows where it goes." -- Davenport 

 

 Jets talk facing their ex-coach 
 Six months ago, Saleh bumped into a couple of high-ranking Jets officials at a posh cocktail reception during the NFL's annual spring meetings in Phoenix. It was a potentially awkward encounter, but Saleh exchanged hugs and pleasantries with both men. It was a let-bygones-be-bygones moment.

 Owner Woody Johnson wasn't present for the impromptu mini-reunion. That would've been fascinating.

 

 If Saleh harbors ill feelings toward the Jets, they're probably directed at ownership -- not that he'd acknowledged that publicly. One close associate said Saleh's nature is to take the high road, adding that his focus in this game is securing a home win for his new team and new fan base.

 "If he can stick it to the Jets in the process," the associate said, "all the better."

 A former Jets player said, "Saleh will be after their asses."

 Saleh and Woody Johnson never had a close rapport, according to several people familiar with the relationship. The reason, many believe, is because Saleh wasn't hired by Johnson, who was serving the final days of his U.S. ambassadorship in the United Kingdom when the move was made.

 When Saleh was introduced to the media on Jan. 21, 2021, he hadn't yet met or spoken to Johnson, whose younger brother, vice chairman Christopher Johnson, represented ownership during the coaching search.

 Both Johnsons walked into Saleh's office on Oct. 8, 2024, with Woody delivering the news that blindsided the man behind the desk. Johnson later explained to reporters that his decision -- his first in-season firing in 25 years as the owner -- was based on his belief that the team, led by a healthy Rodgers, was underachieving. The Jets were 20-36 overall under Saleh -- the worst winning percentage (.357) of any coach in team history with a minimum of 40 games.

 "I just think we can do better," Johnson said at the time.

 Johnson's bold move, going from Saleh to interim coach Jeff Ulbrich to full-time hire Aaron Glenn in 2025, hasn't worked out. Since the firing, the Jets are 6-23 (.207), the fourth-worst winning percentage in the NFL over that span. Armed with three first-round picks in 2027 and more than $100 million in cap space, they believe they're on the verge of a breakthrough. In case you're wondering, the Titans own the worst winning percentage (5-25, .167).

 One player said he heard Saleh's name come up a couple times this week in locker room conversations with teammates, but that's it. They've remained relatively buttoned up, no doubt heeding Glenn's orders to avoid distractions.

 Speaking of Glenn, he could be in Saleh's crosshairs as well. A year ago, Glenn made frequent references to the penalty problem under the previous staff, also suggesting that certain holdovers -- most notably McDonald -- would flourish in his system. The inference was that McDonald hadn't been coached properly.

 "[Saleh] is going to give it everything he's got to make a statement and get his guys ready to roll," said tight end Jeremy Ruckert , one of the Saleh 14. "I'm not really looking into too much of the past and what's gone down. I just know that he's going to have his guys ready to go. Their defense is going to be flying around, and we have to be ready to match that intensity."

title: Can Saquon Barkley recapture his 2024 dominance?
summary: Philadelphia's heavy under-center, wide zone scheme is largely new to the veteran running back.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- There were moments this summer when running back Saquon Barkley stirred the echoes, flashing a quick burst or a sudden jump cut or a moment of competitive overdrive that brought to the surface what he's done and what he's capable of.

 Day 8 of training camp might have been the highlight. It started when he barreled into the end zone on a deep red zone run and finished the play with a well-spirited shove of cornerback Quinyon Mitchell , helping awake a sagging offense.

 Moments later, with the unit backed up, Barkley hit Jordan Davis with a hop step move that left the defensive tackle chasing wind as Barkley sped through the crease and raced to daylight.

 The days the attack looked best this offseason were the ones when Barkley was featured. This should come as no surprise to anyone who watched their Super Bowl run in 2024, when Barkley set the NFL record for most single-season rushing yards, including playoffs, or saw how the operation fell off last year as the ground game labored to find its footing behind an ailing offensive line.

 But it was a reminder that for all the discussion about quarterback Jalen Hurts and his fit in the new system , so much of the Eagles' fate is actually tied to whether Barkley, in Year 9 and five months away from his 30th birthday, can recapture his NFL Offensive Player of the Year form while acclimating to a new scheme.

 

 "The more productive we are in the run game and stuff feeds off that, we'll see the Saquon of two years ago," Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson  said. "We'll see the big plays, we'll see him flexed out wide at receiver, see him in the screen game."

 Barkley acknowledged he's "going back to like I'm a little kid again" in some respects, working on his steps and techniques to match the new Kyle Shanahan/Sean McVay-like system implemented by offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. This heavy under-center, wide zone scheme is largely new to him.

 "Guys who do really well in outside zone scheme stuff are more like one-cut backs," he said. "I naturally, especially after my ACL [tear in 2020], like to cut off of two, so just prepping myself."

 Barkley is known to study his contemporaries -- players such as  Christian McCaffrey , Bijan Robinson , Jonathan Taylor , Derrick Henry and Jahmyr Gibbs -- as well as the "OGs" to see how he can improve his game. This offseason, he reached out specifically to Todd Gurley , the former Ram great, for advice on how to thrive in this type of system.

 The main difference between inside zone -- which he has majored in since coming to Philly -- and outside zone is that inside zone requires a healthy amount of patience and a strong jump cut, Barkley said, whereas outside zone necessitates a mindset of "attacking it more, stretching them, getting the defense to expand, and when you get the opportunity to put your foot in the ground, do it fast, violent and physical."

 With the offensive line creating wide angles by getting out in space, Johnson likened it to "riding that wave," where if the back can't get to the perimeter, he'll read the backside blocks and choose the gap to shoot through.

 "I feel like it creates a lot more running lanes instead of, we were in more of a narrow style angle last year so it's more sideline to sideline and his ability to cut back," Johnson said.

 As training camp showed, the big-play potential is there.

 That was the bread and butter for the 2024 Eagles offense, as Barkley led all backs with 46 rushes of 10-plus yards. A lot of the credit goes to the offensive front, with Barkley also leading running backs in average yards before contact (4.17). Last season, the yards before contact plummeted to 2.31 yards on average (25th) and he dropped to eighth in runs of 10-plus yards (28). Overall, he ran for 1,140 yards (4.1 YPC) last season compared to 2,005 (5.8 YPC) the season prior.

 The offensive line enters the season largely healthy, offering promise that Barkley will have some big holes to fly through once again.

 

 "I think he's been very excited about being able to run in a new scheme and maybe have some more consistent action to some degree," Hurts said. "I know he's worked his tail off and I have a lot of confidence and excitement for him and his ability and what he's going to do."

 Not only is the offensive line in a better place but Barkley is as well. He shot past his career high in carries (345) during the regular season in 2024 and added 91 more rushes in the postseason. That number fell to 280 last season. And while the wild-card playoff exit against the San Francisco 49ers was disappointing for the Eagles, it gave everyone more of a physical and mental break this offseason, including the 29-year-old Barkley.

 "Huge," said running backs coach Jemal Singleton, on the benefits of the longer layoff. "He could take the time from the offseason and get his rest but then come back and start working. So I feel like he's in a really, really good place now. ... It's going to be exciting to kind of see him go."

 Singleton can see it most in the conditioning part of it where Barkley, who shares a backfield this season with a pair of capable backs in Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley , has stayed on the field for more plays during long drives while looking "explosive."

 Put the fresh legs with a revitalized offensive front in this run scheme, and there is optimism Barkley can ascend to the top of the running back class once again.

 "Being a better playmaker," Barkley said on what he wants to improve from last season. "That's why I was brought here, that's what I feel I'm one of the best in the league [at] and just bringing that back."

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Steelers QB, who is entering his 22nd season in the league, is chasing records, and ESPN will be chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots .

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

 

 That Rodgers is still chasing records in 2026 is somewhat of a surprise after he suggested at times during the 2025 season that he was nearing the end of his career.

 "It's the twilight of my career," he said after beating the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland on Oct. 5, 2025. "I used to say five, six, seven years ago, I was on the back nine. But I'm teeing off on 18 right now."

 In that win, Rodgers made two more noteworthy entries into the record books: most completions of 50-plus yards and second quarterback in NFL history to throw 60 or more touchdown passes against multiple franchises.

 But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that ever-growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Maybe it took him a couple of shots to reach the green, or maybe he took his time finding his shot on the fairway. Either way, the 18th hole is in sight, and Rodgers is crouched in front of his ball, squaring up the putt.

 "I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said on the first day of training camp. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired. And I talked to the wife, and she said you can do one more year. I said, 'We'll see if it works out.' And it kind of all came together."

 Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games, joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. He also needs 3,726 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo and lines up his putt on the 18th green, beginning with Week 1 against the Atlanta Falcons . Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 

 
 Preseason: 0 for 0, 0 yards, 0 interceptions, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1: vs. Atlanta Falcons ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) 
 Rodgers won't eclipse any milestones in Week 1 against the Falcons, but he can make headway in game appearances (287), touchdown passes (572), regular-season games with a touchdown pass (231), regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes (166) and games with at least three touchdown passes (95).

 While the Falcons' pass rush is hampered by James Pearce Jr .'s eight-game suspension and Jalon Walker's ACL tear, the secondary could be a challenge for Rodgers and the Steelers' new-look offense. Led by All-Pro safety  Jessie Bates III , cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. and up-and-coming safety Xavier Watts , who had five interceptions in his rookie campaign, Jeff Ulbrich's unit will be a big Week 1 test for Rodgers and McCarthy's passing attack. Ulbrich should know Rodgers well considering he took over as interim coach in the QB's final year with the Jets after Robert Saleh was fired following a 2-3 start.

title: Seahawks confident in QB Drew Lock amid Sam Darnold's injury
summary: Lock led Seattle to a Week 1 win after Darnold injured his hip and left the game. But can he keep it up against the Cardinals in Week 2 -- and potentially beyond?
full_text:
SEATTLE -- Like most of the NFL's backup quarterbacks, Drew Lock doesn't get regular reps during a game week. But he still has to be able to visualize a play when he hears it in his headset, and his preferred method for doing so -- without being able to get under center in practice -- is to draw out the Xs and Os every day on a whiteboard that he has set up in his bedroom.

 When the Seattle Seahawks ' QB2 is not using it to memorize Brian Fleury's playbook, it's covered in his young son's scribbles.

 "Every day I get home to do that, I have to erase things that were not drawn by me," Lock said. "I think it's a good time-killer for my wife at home with the kiddo. So it's fun. I get to smile right as I start to do it and kind of remember why you're doing it."

 The Lock family whiteboard might get more use than usual in the coming days -- and perhaps weeks -- given the situation with Sam Darnold . The Seahawks' starting quarterback is dealing with a hip injury he suffered in the season opener Wednesday against the New England Patriots . While coach Mike Macdonald said Thursday that test results brought "really good news," a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Darnold is expected to miss time .

 

 That means it will likely be Lock's show to run next Sunday, Sept. 20, when the Seahawks open NFC West play on the road against the Arizona Cardinals  (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox), and potentially beyond. The Seahawks travel to face the Washington Commanders in Week 3 and host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4.

 Unless Darnold's absence is a lengthy one, the way Lock played in the opener should inspire confidence that he can keep the Seahawks' hopes of a Super Bowl repeat afloat in the short-term -- especially with the ample offensive supporting cast and an elite defense that's backing him.

 After taking over for Darnold on Seattle's second possession, Lock went 16-of-22 for 187 yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. His clean performance -- plus three takeaways by Mike Macdonald's defense -- was enough for the Seahawks to rally for a 13-10 win at Lumen Field.

 "He did a phenomenal job," said wide receiver Cooper Kupp , who regularly sits in on Seattle's quarterback meetings. "He basically took no reps with any of the guys that were out there all week. You can see the onus that he puts on himself to be ready, though, when the time comes. There's extra time he spends out there on the field, extra time that he spends with the coaches to make sure.

 "The last thing you want is for Sam to have to not be there, but Drew has done an unbelievable job preparing and did a great job for us today."

 What would have been Lock's first touchdown pass -- a 7-yard throw in the end zone to Kupp -- was nullified by an illegal shift. It was one of seven offensive penalties for the Seahawks, something they have to clean up lest they continually put their backup quarterback in pure passing situations. But even on one such moment Wednesday night, Lock delivered -- hitting  Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 21-yard gain on third-and-22.

 "We've all been saying that Drew has been the best [No. 2 QB] in the NFL for years," said safety Julian Love , who had one of Seattle's three interceptions of Drake Maye . "It was such calm on our sideline defensively that folks didn't realize until ... towards the second half that he was in, because it's just so seamless, he's such a leader, he makes plays all the time in practice. So it's really cool to see him. We just have so much belief, not just in him but anyone who steps in for us. ... That's how we operate."

 

 Seattle's faith in Lock was evident before the outcome was decided against New England. In the fourth quarter of his playcalling debut, Fleury faced a pivotal decision. Instead of calling a tush push with tight end AJ Barner , a play that became a short-yardage asset for the Seahawks last season, Fleury put the ball in Lock's hands.

 The result was a 45-yard touchdown pass to Smith-Njibga that tied the game at 10-10.

 "Drew's a ballplayer," Smith-Njigba said. "He comes in and demands the huddle, and he wants to sling [it], throw the ball around. ... Full confidence in 2."

 Former coach Pete Carroll once described Lock as having some gunslinger to his game. To be sure, he did not simply dink and dunk his way down the field in the opener. The 21-yard completion to Smith-Njigba came on an over-the-middle throw that he fit between defenders. He dropped another throw over Kupp's shoulder for a 24-yard gain. As Macdonald put it, Lock was "aggressive when he needed to be" without putting the ball in jeopardy.

 But with last season's top-ranked scoring defense showing that it remains a dominant force, Seattle will ask Lock to be more game-manager than gunslinger.

 With a much different Seahawks team in 2023, Lock went 1-1 in two fill-in starts while Geno Smith was sidelined with a groin injury. He signed with the New York Giants the following offseason and threw six touchdown passes to five interceptions in five starts. The Giants -- who would finish 3-14 -- lost four of those games, bringing Lock's career record as a starter to 10-18.

 "I've definitely grown," Lock said, comparing the quarterback he is now to when he last saw extensive action. "I've learned a lot about football. But having an opportunity on a team like this can shift your mindset. Knowing the type of defense that we have, there's no rush to push the ball down the field. Let's find ways to get the ball in our guys' hands. Now, when the ones downfield are there, I've never been one to be afraid of those, but having the mindset of taking care of the football, getting it in our guys' hands.

 "You've got the best defense in the world, in my opinion. Let's keep the ball moving forward and see what the scoreboard looks like at the end of this."

 

 Macdonald said Thursday that the Seahawks will have a better sense of Darnold's prognosis when they return to practice on Monday. The quarterback was back at the team's facility that day after spending Wednesday night at the hospital, in part because of how much discomfort he was in. While Macdonald wasn't ready to declare Darnold out for Seattle's next game, he said his early read is that Lock will start against Arizona. 

 "He's been tremendous," Macdonald said of Lock's approach since he returned to Seattle last season. "He operates like a starter does in terms of preparation. The chemistry and the personality of our quarterback room is one that is very supportive of each other and also trying to bring out the best in one another. Drew provides a cool confidence, loose and focusedness to the whole equation, which you need -- you need that.

 "On top of that, since he's got here, I feel like he's just played great football in practice and in the preseason. We saw what he could do last night. If he has to play again, then we expect the same moving forward."

title: ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame inducts all-time leading scorer Tom Brady
summary: Tom Brady retired as fantasy football's all-time leading scorer and is now an ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Famer.
full_text:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame   , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year fantasy football was available on ESPN.com.

 Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 

 Class of 2026 Week 1 Inductee: Tom Brady 

 5,944.36 fantasy points 
89,214 passing yards, 649 passing TDs, 28 rushing TDs 

 The "G.O.A.T.," Brady scored more fantasy points -- nearly 6,000! -- than anyone in history. He was a dominating postseason performer on the gridiron, with seven Super Bowl wins including five MVP awards in those victories, but in fantasy football, he was renowned for his consistency. Brady scored at least 25 fantasy points in a game 66 times and at least 250 in a season 15 times, both NFL records, and between 2001-22 he made a record 333 starts. Like a fine wine, Brady only got better with age. His 1,825.18 fantasy points scored after turning 40 years old are more than double the next-closest player, and represent 31% of his career total.

 
 Tom Brady will be inducted on Sunday during " Fantasy Focus Countdown ," 10 a.m. ET on ESPN2. Tune in each week through Week 16 as we reveal the entire inaugural class.

title: Why Commanders are believing in a Jayden Daniels rebound
summary: Washington offensive coordinator David Blough said Daniels has had his best NFL camp so far.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- For Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels , the season isn't about reminding everyone what he can do. It's not about re-establishing himself among his draft class. Nor is it about proving anyone wrong. Rather, it's just about being on the field and doing what he knows he can do. "I've just got to go out and ... be myself," Daniels said.

 And heading into the season opener at 4:25 p.m. Sunday at Philadelphia (on FOX), the Commanders believe, once again, that will be good enough. When Daniels could be himself in 2024, he led Washington to the NFC Championship Game before losing to the Eagles.

 "He can make any throw and put the ball anywhere and stretch the field for sure," Washington receiver Stefon Diggs said. "He's a young quarterback, but he's a star. He showed in this league he can play at a high level."

 Last season he played only four full games because of injuries. Washington's 5-12 finish led to questions about Daniels and the organization.

 Meanwhile, he watched his fellow 2024 draft class quarterbacks shine. Drake Maye played in the Super Bowl; Bo Nix helped Denver reach the AFC Championship Game before getting hurt, and  Caleb Williams guided Chicago to an 11-6 record and the divisional round.

 But that's not his motivator.

 "I'm happy for them," Daniels said. "We're all chasing a common goal and obviously you want to be the best, you want to win the Super Bowl, and I'm not rooting for them to do bad.

 "There's a lot of stuff that's said of other people in my class and they should get that respect that they earned also. It was a different narrative our rookie year. So every year it's just going to be a flip-flop narrative and we're always going to get compared with each other, especially the top three picks."

 All three of those quarterbacks were starring when Daniels was sidelined for the season with a dislocated left elbow. He last played in Washington's 31-0 loss to Minnesota on Dec. 7, 2025, re-injuring his elbow while attempting to make a tackle after throwing a third-quarter interception. With a 3-10 record after that game, and knowing he had injured that elbow initially in Week 9, the Commanders shut him down. But it's led to a long wait for his return.

 "I'm excited for everyone to see him again," offensive coordinator David Blough said.

 But reminding others of his talent doesn't push Daniels either. He knows what happened as a rookie and what transpired in 2025 doesn't matter anymore.

 "That's what people are going to talk about -- recency biases and all that," he said. "Now we're on to year three. Whatever happens on Sunday, that's what people are going to talk about more than what they talk about year two."

 

 Because of that mindset, he's just doing what he's done in previous years.

 As a rookie, Daniels showed up to spring workouts around 5:45 a.m. During the season he'd arrive at 5:30 for a walk-through with just coaches a half hour later. At the time, offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury would marvel at how Daniels recalled the game plan on Wednesday, having just received it a day earlier.

 That routine hasn't changed -- though Daniels did add weekly film sessions with his receivers in the spring.

 "He's very internally motivated and he's been that way ever since he's been here," Blough said.

 All of this is why he was elected one of five captains for the season.

 But, aside from that, Daniels also had arguably his best training camp of his first three seasons. At one point in August, Blough said Daniels was as "accurate as he's ever been." It wasn't just about completing passes, it was about leading receivers into yards after the catch and throwing passes away from danger -- like an incoming defender.

 "His touch on the deep ball has been great," receiver Terry McLaurin said. "He's always thrown a nice deep ball, but the air he's allowing us to track the ball makes a huge difference for us. His anticipation has been great. His ability to put the ball on the front [shoulder] pad when running crossing routes and we're running away from him. It's hard to gauge every receiver's speed but he gives you a good chance to catch and run."

 "Just the efficiency offensively, the ability for explosive plays," Washington coach Dan Quinn said. "There's certainly going to be some growing as the season goes, new players and playcaller and system. He's in a good place with the system. He's a decisive thinker. You know how important that is. He's able to think quickly, process quickly. That's why he's able to get rid of the ball to the right location, to the right target of where it's going to go."

 Daniels developed a quick connection with Diggs, hooking up for a touchdown in a joint practice vs. Miami and a back-shoulder pass a week after the wideout was signed.

 The coaches liked that Daniels displayed a comfort level in Blough's offense, which requires him to call plays in the huddle for the first time in his NFL career. When listening to audio from practices, the coaches heard Daniels provide extra details to linemen or receivers about what to expect from the defense, and give little reminders on what to do.

 

 "It's his command of everything," McLaurin said. "Blough giving him keys to get us in the right play. It takes a lot of cerebral ability to not only know what the defense is giving you but then getting you in the right play and communicating it to the offense."

 Washington is betting this offense -- which will put Daniels under center more and emphasize play-action -- will result in Daniels' evolving as a quarterback. They also say it will lead to more explosive plays.

 But until the season begins, the focus with Daniels will involve questions. However, Daniels hasn't been deterred by anything said about him.

 "Everybody has an opinion, no matter whether it's good or bad," he said. "It's nothing I can really control. The only thing that matters to me is the people inside that building, my family.

 "Never get too high, never get too low, try to stay even-keeled. They're going to talk about you regardless, good or bad."
